tafsir: They namely mankind will not have the power to intercede save him who has made a covenant with the Compassionate One the covenant being the profession of lā ilāha illā’Llāh wa-lā hawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi’Llāh ‘there is no god but God and there is no power or strength except in God’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَاعَةَ إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَهْداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. None shall have the power of intercession, but such a one as has received permission (or promise) from the Most Gracious (Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they say) i.e. the Jews: (The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son) He has taken Ezra ('Uzayr) as his son.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَلَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 88. And they say: “The Most Gracious (Allāh) has begotten a son (or offspring or children) [as the Jews say: ‘Uzair (Ezra) is the son of Allāh, and the Christians say that He has begotten a son [‘Isā (Jesus) S], and the pagan Arabs say that He has begotten daughters (angels and others.)].”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they say that is the Jews and the Christians and those who claim that the angels are God’s daughters ‘The Compassionate One has taken a son’. But God exalted be He says to them

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَلَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 88. And they say: “The Most Gracious (Allāh) has begotten a son (or offspring or children) [as the Jews say: ‘Uzair (Ezra) is the son of Allāh, and the Christians say that He has begotten a son [‘Isā (Jesus) S], and the pagan Arabs say that He has begotten daughters (angels and others.)].”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Assuredly you utter a disastrous thing) you utter ignominious evil words,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئاً إِدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 89. Indeed you have brought forth (said) a terrible evil thing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly you have uttered something hideous that is a great abomination.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئاً إِدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 89. Indeed you have brought forth (said) a terrible evil thing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Whereby almost the heavens are torn) crack, (and the earth is split asunder and the mountains fall in ruins),

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 90. Whereby the heavens are almost torn, and the earth is split asunder, and the mountains fall in ruins,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The heavens are almost read takādu or yakādu rent read takādu tatafattarna by being torn apart a variant reading has yanfatirna because of it and the earth is almost split asunder and the mountains almost fall down crashing collapsing on top of them because of the fact

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 90. Whereby the heavens are almost torn, and the earth is split asunder, and the mountains fall in ruins,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That ye ascribe unto the Beneficent a son) Ezra,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَلَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 91. That they ascribe a son (or offspring or children) to the Most Gracious (Allāh). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that they have ascribed a son to the Compassionate One. God exalted be He says

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَلَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 91. That they ascribe a son (or offspring or children) to the Most Gracious (Allāh). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When it is not meet for (the Majesty of) the Beneficent that He should choose a son) It does not befit him to take Ezra as a son.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يَنبَغِي لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 92. But it is not suitable for (the Majesty of) the Most Gracious (Allāh) that He should beget a son (or offspring or children)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: when it is not meet for the Majesty of the Compassionate One to take a son that is to say such a thing does not befit Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يَنبَغِي لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 92. But it is not suitable for (the Majesty of) the Most Gracious (Allāh) that He should beget a son (or offspring or children)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There is none in the heavens and the earth but cometh unto the Beneficent as a slave) acknowledging his servitude to the All-Merciful and obedient to Him except, that is, the disbelievers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ آتِي ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَبْداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 93. There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Gracious (Allāh) as a slave..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: There is none in the heavens and the earth but he comes to the Compassionate One as a servant servile submissive on the Day of Resurrection including individuals such as Ezra and Jesus.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ آتِي ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَبْداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 93. There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Gracious (Allāh) as a slave..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Verily He knoweth them) He remembers them (and numbereth them with (right) numbering) and He knows their number.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَاهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 94. Verily, He knows each one of them, and has counted them a full counting..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily He knows their number and has counted them precisely and therefore the knowledge of their total number does not elude Him not even the knowledge of one of them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَاهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 94. Verily, He knows each one of them, and has counted them a full counting..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And each one of them will come unto Him) and each of them will come to Allah (on the Day of Resurrection, alone) without wealth or offspring.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ فَرْداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 95. And everyone of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection (without any helper, or protector or defender)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And each one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection each one alone without wealth or any helper to protect him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ فَرْداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 95. And everyone of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection (without any helper, or protector or defender)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and in the Qur'an (and do good works) between them and their Lord, (the Beneficent will appoint for them love) Allah will love them and make people love them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وُدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 96. Verily, those who believe [in the Oneness of Allāh and in His Messenger (Muḥammad )] and work deeds of righteousness, the Most Gracious (Allāh) will bestow love for them (1) (in the hearts of the believers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly those who believe and perform righteous deeds — for them the Compassionate One shall appoint love between them so that they have mutual love and affection and God exalted be He will love them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وُدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 96. Verily, those who believe [in the Oneness of Allāh and in His Messenger (Muḥammad )] and work deeds of righteousness, the Most Gracious (Allāh) will bestow love for them (1) (in the hearts of the believers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We make (this Scripture) easy in your tongue) We made the recitation of the Qur'an easy for you, ((O Muhammad) only that thou mayst bear good tidings therewith) by means of the Qur'an (unto those who ward off (evil)) disbelief, idolatry and indecency, (and warn therewith) by means of the Qur'an (the froward folk) people who argue by means of falsehood.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنْذِرَ بِهِ قَوْماً لُّدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 97. So, We have made this (the Qur’ān) easy in your own tongue (O Muḥammad ), only that you may give glad tidings to the Muttaqūn (the pious )(2), and warn with it the Ludd (3) (most quarrelsome evil-doer, wicked) people. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We have made it easy namely the Qur’ān in your tongue only that you may bear good tidings therewith to the God-fearing those who will be prosperous because of their faith and warn threaten therewith a folk who are contumacious luddan the accusative plural of aladd in other words extremely disputatious using false arguments — and they are the disbelievers of Mecca.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنْذِرَ بِهِ قَوْماً لُّدّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 97. So, We have made this (the Qur’ān) easy in your own tongue (O Muḥammad ), only that you may give glad tidings to the Muttaqūn (the pious )(2), and warn with it the Ludd (3) (most quarrelsome evil-doer, wicked) people. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And how many a generation) many a bygone nation (before them) before your own people, O Muhammad, (have We destroyed! Canst thou (Muhammad) see a single man of them) after having destroyed them, (or hear from them the slightest sound) after being annihilated and turned into ruins?'

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْنٍ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 98. And how many a genera tion before them have We destroyed! Can you (O Muḥammad ) find a single one of them or hear even a whisper of them?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And how many — in other words many — a generation namely how many a community from among the communities of the past We have destroyed before them for their denial of Our messengers. Can you see can you find so much as one of them or hear from them so much as the faintest sound? No indeed! So just as We destroyed those folk We shall destroy these Meccans.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْنٍ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 98. And how many a genera tion before them have We destroyed! Can you (O Muḥammad ) find a single one of them or hear even a whisper of them?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said upon the explanation of Allah's saying: (Ta. Ha. We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed) We have not revealed the Qur'an to you that you should toil. This verse was revealed when the Prophet (pbuh) used to stand in prayer at night vigil until his feet swelled up, and so Allah alleviated this for him through this verse. He said: Taha, which in the dialect of Mecca means: O man, i.e. O Muhammad, We have not sent Gabriel with the Qur'an for you to toil.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: طه
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Ṭā-Hā. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Tā hā God knows best what He means by these letters.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: طه
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Ṭā-Hā. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said upon the explanation of Allah's saying: (Ta. Ha. We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed) We have not revealed the Qur'an to you that you should toil. This verse was revealed when the Prophet (pbuh) used to stand in prayer at night vigil until his feet swelled up, and so Allah alleviated this for him through this verse. He said: Taha, which in the dialect of Mecca means: O man, i.e. O Muhammad, We have not sent Gabriel with the Qur'an for you to toil.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَآ أَنَزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. We have not sent down the Qur’ān to you (O Muḥammad ) to cause you distress,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We have not revealed the Qur’ān to you O Muhammad (s) that you should be miserable that you should toil because of what you used to do after it was revealed to you in the way of long vigils performing night prayers; in other words so unburden your soul;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَآ أَنَزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. We have not sent down the Qur’ān to you (O Muḥammad ) to cause you distress,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But as a reminder) an admonition (unto him who feareth) unto him who embraces Islam, and We have not revealed it to you in order that you tire yourself,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. But only as a Reminder to those who fear (Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: but We have revealed it only to remind therewith him who fears God;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. But only as a Reminder to those who fear (Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (A revelation) He says: the Qur'an consists of the words spoken (from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens) He raised them one above the other,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِيلاً مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. A revelation from Him (Allāh) Who has created the earth and the high heavens..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: a revelation tanzīlan a substitution standing in place of the conjugated verb derived therefrom which renders it tanzīlan accusative from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens ‘ulā the plural of ‘ulyā similar in pattern to kubrā kubar ‘large’;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِيلاً مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. A revelation from Him (Allāh) Who has created the earth and the high heavens..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The Beneficent One, Who is established on the Throne) it is also said that this means: He filled it; and it is also said that this is a mystery that cannot be explained.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. The Most Gracious (Allāh) rose over (Istawā) the (Mighty) Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He is the Compassionate One presided upon the Throne al-‘arsh in the classical Arabic language denotes a king’s seat a presiding befitting of Him;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. The Most Gracious (Allāh) rose over (Istawā) the (Mighty) Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and whatsoever is between them) of created beings and marvels, (and whatsoever is beneath the sod) that which is beneath the seven earths. This is because the seven earths are above water, and water is above the whale, the whale is above the rock and the rock is above the two horns of the bull and the bull is above the dust, and the dust is moist soil and none knows what is beneath it except Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَهُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and all that is between them, and all that is under the soil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them of creatures and whatever is beneath the soil al-tharā is moist earth meaning whatever is beneath the seven earths since these lie beneath it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَهُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and all that is between them, and all that is under the soil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And if thou speakest aloud) and act openly, (then Lo! He knoweth the secret (thought)) and secret action (and (that which is yet) more hidden) than that which is a secret, whether it has ensued from you or has not yet ensued from you but will in the future. Allah knows all that.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And if you (O Muḥammad ) speak (the invocation) aloud, then verily, He knows the secret and that which is yet more hidden..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And should you be loud in your speech in remembrance of God or supplication then God has no need for this to be spoken loud then indeed He knows the secret and that which is yet more hidden than that secret namely that which the soul whispers to itself and that which occurs to the mind but which you do not speak of to anyone so do not strain yourself to be loud in your speech.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And if you (O Muḥammad ) speak (the invocation) aloud, then verily, He knows the secret and that which is yet more hidden..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Allah! There is no God save Him) alone without any partner. (His are the most beautiful names) His are the most exalted attributes, so call upon Him through them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱللَّهُ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ لَهُ ٱلأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Allāh! Lā ilāhā illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He)! To Him belong the Best Names(1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: God — there is no god save Him. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names the ninety nine Names cited in the hadīth al-husnā is the feminine form of al-ahsan ‘the best’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱللَّهُ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ لَهُ ٱلأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Allāh! Lā ilāhā illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He)! To Him belong the Best Names(1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hath there come unto thee) it had not come to you before, O Muhammad, but has now, (the story of Moses) the event of Moses?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And has there come to you the story of Mūsā (Moses)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Has the story of Moses — indeed it has — come to you?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And has there come to you the story of Mūsā (Moses)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When he saw a fire) on his left side (and said unto his folk: Wait) stay here! (I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom) a brand of fire from there, for that night was very cold, (or may find guidance at the Fire) to show me the way.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ رَأَى نَاراً فَقَالَ لأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوۤاْ إِنِّيۤ آنَسْتُ نَاراً لَّعَلِّيۤ آتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. When he saw a fire, he said to his family: “Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When he caught sight of a fire and said to his family namely to his wife ‘Wait here! — this was when he was leaving Midian heading for Egypt — Indeed I see a fire in the distance. Perhaps I can bring you a brand from it bring you a burning wick or a torch or find at the fire some guidance’ that is someone to guide me by showing me the proper route — for he had lost it in the darkness of the night. He Moses said ‘perhaps’ la‘alla because he could not be certain of fulfilling his promise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ رَأَى نَاراً فَقَالَ لأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوۤاْ إِنِّيۤ آنَسْتُ نَاراً لَّعَلِّيۤ آتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. When he saw a fire, he said to his family: “Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And when he reached it) it was a green tree from which emanated a white fire, (he was called by name: O Moses!)

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّآ أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يٰمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And when he came to it (the fire), he was called by name: “O Mūsā (Moses)!.

tafsir: (Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord. So take off thy shoes) for his shoes were made of the skin of a dead ass, (for Lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa) Tuwa is the name of the valley; it also said that Tuwa means: this valley has been crossed (tawathu) by prophets before you; it is also said that Tuwa is a well which was filled with stones (tuwiyyat bi'l-sakhr) in the valley where he found the tree.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنِّيۤ أَنَاْ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. “Verily, I am your Lord! So take off your shoes; you are in the sacred valley, Ṭuwa..

tafsir: Indeed read as innī if one understands nūdiya ‘he was called’ as meaning qīla ‘it was said’; or read it as annī because of an implied prefixed bā’ I am anā reiterates the first person indicator yā’ of innī used by the direct speaker your Lord. So take off your sandals for lo! you are in the holy meaning either the pure or the blessed valley of Tuwā this is either a substitution or an explicative supplement; read Tuwan with nunation or Tuwā without it is considered declinable on account of it being a location; but alternatively considered indeclinable if taken as considered a feminine proper noun denoting a place name.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنِّيۤ أَنَاْ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى

tafsir: The Hour is assuredly coming. But I will to keep it hidden from mankind — and its nearness in time will manifest itself to them through its signs — so that every soul may be requited thereupon for what it strives for of good or evil.

tafsir: He said ‘It is my staff. I lean I support myself upon it when I leap across something or walk and I beat down leaves I strike the leaves on trees with it so that they fall for my sheep which then consume them; and I have uses for it ma’ārib ‘uses’ is the plural of ma’ruba with the rā’ taking any one of the three vowels sc. ma’ruba ma’raba or ma’riba meaning ‘needs’ in other ways such as using it to carry food supplies and waterskins as well as to drive away undesirable animals. He Moses gives an extensive response to indicate his many needs for it.

tafsir: He said ‘Take hold of it and do not fear it. We will restore it to its former state sīratahā in the accusative because the genitive-operating preposition has been removed. And so he placed his hand in its mouth and it became a staff once again; and it became clear that the place into which he put his hand was the place where it the staff is held between its two prongs. Moses was shown this miracle lest he be terrified when it turns into a snake in the presence of Pharaoh.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلاَ تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلأُولَىٰ

tafsir: (And thrust thy hand within your armpit, it will come forth white) shining (without hurt) it is not touched by leprosy. ((That will be) another token) another sign in addition to the staff.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ آيَةً أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. “And press your (right) hand to your (left) side: it will come forth white (and shining), without any disease as another sign,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And thrust your hand the right one meaning the palm into your flank — that is your left side below the arm into the armpit and then take it out — it will emerge white in contrast to the skin-colour that it was without any fault that is without any sign of leprosy radiating like the rays of the sun blinding to the eyes of onlookers. That is yet another sign āyatan ukhrā this together with baydā’a ‘white’ constitute two circumstantial qualifiers referring to the subject of the verb takhruj ‘it will emerge’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ آيَةً أُخْرَىٰ

tafsir: Saying: Throw him into the ark) put the baby in the ark, (and throw it into the river) and place the ark in the river, (then the river shall throw it on to the bank) of the river, (and there an enemy to Me) as concern Religion, i.e. Pharaoh (and an enemy to him) who intends to kill (shall take him) shall pick him up. (And I endued thee with love from Me) O Moses, such that whoever sees you loves you (that thou mightest be trained according to My will) whatever was done to you was under our very watch,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّي وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِيۤ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. (“Saying:) ‘Put him (the child) into the Tabūt (a box or a case or a chest) and put it into the river (Nile); then the river shall cast it up on the bank, and there, an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his shall take him.’ And I endued you with love from Me, in order that you may be brought up under My Eye..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: “Cast him place him in the ark then cast him while in the ark into the river into the flow of the Nile and then the river shall throw him up onto the shore that is its bank the imperative here fa’l-yulqihi ‘let it throw him’ functions as a predicate; there an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his namely Pharaoh shall take him”. And after he took you I cast upon you love from Me that you may be loved by people; and indeed Pharaoh and all who saw you loved you; and that you might be reared under My eyes be nurtured under My guardianship and My protection of you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّي وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِيۤ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When your sister went) when she entered Pharaoh's palace (and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him) breastfeed him? (and We restored thee) We returned you to your mother (to your mother that her eyes might be refreshed) that she might be comforted (and might not sorrow) thinking that her son may have died upon throwing him in the river. (And thou didst kill a man) a Coptic man (and We delivered thee from great distress) from the distress caused to you by the people, (and tried thee with a heavy trial) We tried again and again. (And thou didst tarry years) ten years (among the folk of Midian. Then comest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses) then you came to face My decree, in that I spoke with you and sent you with a message to Pharaoh,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ تَمْشِيۤ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَىٰ أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُها وَلاَ تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُوناً فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِيۤ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يٰمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. “When your sister went and said: ‘Shall I show you one who will nurse him?’ So, We restored you to your mother, that she might cool her eyes and she should not grieve. Then you did kill a man, but We saved you from great distress and tried you with a heavy trial. Then you stayed a number of years with the people of.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When idh for explanation your sister Maryam walked up to obtain news of you for they had brought wet nurses for you but you would not take to the breast of any of them and she then said “Shall I show you someone who will take care of him?”. Her offer was accepted and so she brought them his mother and he took to her breasts. Thus We restored you to your mother that her eyes might rejoice in seeing you again and not grieve at that point anymore. Then you slew a soul namely the Copt in Egypt — and you became distressed for having slain him because of how Pharaoh would react; whereupon We delivered you from great distress and We tried you with various ordeals We tested you by landing you in some other ordeal and again delivered you from it. Then you stayed for several years ten years among the people of Midian after you had reached it having left Egypt staying with the prophet Shu‘ayb and marrying his daughter. Then you came hither as ordained in My knowledge with the Message that you will deliver — and this was when you were forty years old O Moses!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ تَمْشِيۤ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَىٰ أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُها وَلاَ تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُوناً فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِيۤ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يٰمُوسَىٰ

tafsir: (Go, thou and thy brother) Aaron, (with My tokens) the hand and the staff, (and be not faint in remembrance of Me) do not weaken, wane or slacken in conveying My message to Pharaoh.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. “Go you and your brother with My Āyāt (proofs, evidences, lessons, signs, etc.), and do not, you both, slacken and become weak in My Remembrance..

tafsir: Go you and your brother to the people with My nine signs and do not flag be remiss in remembrance of Me by uttering glorifications and otherwise.

tafsir: (Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds)) he has become arrogant, overweening and a disbeliever.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. “Go, both of you, to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), verily, he has transgressed (all bounds in disbelief and disobedience and behaved as an arrogant and as a tyrant)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Go the two of you to Pharaoh. Truly he has transgressed the bounds in claiming to be the Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. “Go, both of you, to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), verily, he has transgressed (all bounds in disbelief and disobedience and behaved as an arrogant and as a tyrant)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And speak unto him a gentle word) a kind word: “there is no deity except Allah”; it is also said that this means: call him by his agnomen, (that peradventure he may heed) that perhaps he may take admonition (or fear) or surrender [to Allah].

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقُولاَ لَهُ قَوْلاً لَّيِّناً لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. “And speak to him mildly, perhaps he may accept admonition or fear (Allāh).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And speak to him gentle words for him to renounce such claims that perhaps he may be mindful be admonished or fear’ God and so repent — the ‘hope’ for Pharaoh’s repentance is expressed from their perspective for God knows that he was not going to repent.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقُولاَ لَهُ قَوْلاً لَّيِّناً لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. “And speak to him mildly, perhaps he may accept admonition or fear (Allāh).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us) we fear that he may be hasty with us (or that he may play the tyrant) and kill us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالاَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. They said: “Our Lord! Verily, we fear lest he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress (all bounds against us).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The two of them said ‘Our Lord We truly fear that he may forestall us that is by hastening to punish us or become tyrannical’ against us that is be high-handed with us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالاَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. They said: “Our Lord! Verily, we fear lest he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress (all bounds against us).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Allah said to them: (Fear not) being beaten or killed. (Lo! I am with you twain) helping you, (Hearing) what you will be told (and Seeing) what he will do with you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لاَ تَخَافَآ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. He (Allāh) said: “Fear not, verily, I am with you both, hearing and seeing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Do not fear for I shall be with the two of you by providing you with My assistance hearing what he says and seeing what he does.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لاَ تَخَافَآ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. He (Allāh) said: “Fear not, verily, I am with you both, hearing and seeing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So go ye unto him) to Pharaoh (and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord) to you. (So let the Children of Israel go with us) to their homeland, (and torment them not) do not toil them with work, nor kill their men and use their women as servants, because they are free. (We bring thee a token) a sign (from thy Lord) i.e. the sign of the hand, which is the first sign that he showed to Pharaoh (And peace will be for him who follows right guidance) monotheism.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولاۤ إِنَّا رَسُولاَ رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلاَ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. “So go you both to him, and say: ‘Verily, we are Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So go to him and say “Truly we are two messengers of your Lord so let the Children of Israel go with us to Syria and do not continue to chastise them in other words release them from your exploitation of them in those oppressive works of yours such as digging construction and the lifting of heavy objects. We have verily brought you a sign a definitive argument from your Lord as proof of our truthfulness in delivering the Message; and may peace be upon him who follows right guidance that is to say may he be secure from God’s chastisement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولاۤ إِنَّا رَسُولاَ رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلاَ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. “So go you both to him, and say: ‘Verily, we are Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! it hath been revealed unto us that the) continuous (doom will be for him who denieth) God's divine Oneness (and turneth away) from faith.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. “Truly, it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for him who denies [believes not in the Oneness of Allāh, and in His Messengers.], and turns away (from the truth and obedience of Allāh).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed it has been revealed to us that the chastisement shall befall him who denies the truth of what we have brought and turns away” ’ and who rejects it. And so they came to him and said to him all of what has been mentioned.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. “Truly, it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for him who denies [believes not in the Oneness of Allāh, and in His Messengers.], and turns away (from the truth and obedience of Allāh).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Pharaoh) said: Who then is the Lord of you twain, O Moses?)

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يٰمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) said: “Who then, O Mūsā (Moses), is the Lord of you two?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘So who is your Lord O Moses?’ — he Pharaoh restricted this question to him Moses because between him and Aaron he is the principal bearer of God’s Message and also because of his Pharaoh’s having pampered him while he was being reared as a child.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يٰمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) said: “Who then, O Mūsā (Moses), is the Lord of you two?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said: Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its nature) its shape, He gave to humans human progeny, to camels, donkeys and sheep progenies of their own species, (then guided it aright) then He inspired them how to eat, drink and copulate.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِيۤ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Our Lord is He Who gave to everything in creation its peculiar nature through which it is distinguished from another thing and then guided it’ the animal among them to its source of food drink and procreation and in other ways.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِيۤ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Pharaoh said to Moses: (What then is the state of the generations of old?) What is the events of the people of old? How did they perish?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “What about the generations of old?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Pharaoh said ‘So what of the status of the generations the communities of old?’ such as the people of Noah Hūd Lot and Sālih with regard to their having worshipped graven images.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “What about the generations of old?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Moses said: (The knowledge thereof) the knowledge of their destruction (is with my Lord) written down (in a Record) i.e. the Guarded Tablet. (My Lord neither erreth) He does not make mistakes nor is He oblivious to their matter (nor forgetteth) their matter and leave them unpunished,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لاَّ يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلاَ يَنسَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor does He forget.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Said he Moses ‘The knowledge thereof that is the knowledge of their otherworldly status is preserved with my Lord in a Book namely the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz and He shall requite them in accordance with it on the Day of Resurrection. My Lord does not err He is never absent from anything nor does He my Lord forget anything.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لاَّ يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلاَ يَنسَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor does He forget.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads) to use for going and coming (for you therein) in the earth (and hath sent down water) rain (from the sky and thereby) by means of the rain (We have brought forth diverse kinds of vegetation) of different colours,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلأَرْضَ مَهْداً وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلاً وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. Who has made earth for you like a bed (spread out); and has opened roads (ways and paths) for you therein, and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He is the One Who made for you as well as for all creatures the earth a cradle a bed and threaded facilitated for you therein ways roads and sent down from the heaven water rain. God exalted be He says as a complement to Moses’s description of Him and as an address to the people of Mecca and therewith We brought forth various kinds species of plants shattā ‘various’ adjectivally qualifies azwājan ‘kinds’ in other words plants of different colours flavours and different in other ways shattā is the plural of shatīt similar in pattern to marīd plural mardā as may be used in a phrase like shatta al-amr ‘the affair has become divided’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلأَرْضَ مَهْداً وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلاً وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. Who has made earth for you like a bed (spread out); and has opened roads (ways and paths) for you therein, and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Saying): Eat ye) that which you eat (and feed your) grazing (cattle) from its vegetation. (Lo! Herein) in their difference and different colours (verily are portents) signs (for men of thought) for those endowed with intellect among people.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كُلُواْ وَٱرْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لأُوْلِي ٱلنُّهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. Eat and pasture your cattle (therein); verily, in this are Āyāt (proofs and signs) for men of understanding..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Eat thereof and pasture your cattle therein an‘ām ‘cattle’ is the plural of na‘am which are camels cows and sheep; one says ra‘atu’l-an‘āmu ‘the cattle grazed’ or ra‘aytuhā ‘I grazed them’; the imperative here is meant as a permissive and a reminder of God’s grace the sentence being a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb akhrajnā ‘We brought forth’ in other words what is meant is ‘We brought forth the plants permitting you to eat thereof and to graze your cattle thereon’. In that which is mentioned here there are indeed signs indeed lessons for people of sense possessors of intellect al-nuhā the plural of nuhya similar in pattern to ghurfa plural ghuraf. The intellect is called by this term nuhya because it shows a person the sense to refrain from committing vile deeds.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كُلُواْ وَٱرْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لأُوْلِي ٱلنُّهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. Eat and pasture your cattle (therein); verily, in this are Āyāt (proofs and signs) for men of understanding..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thereof) from the earth (We created you) He says We created you from Adam and Adam is from dust, and the dust is from the earth, (and thereunto) to the earth (we return you) He says: We bury you (and thence) from the earth (We bring you forth) He says: from the grave We shall bring you forth (a second time) after death, i.e. for the Resurrection.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. Thereof (the earth) We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out once again..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: From it that is from the earth We created you by creating your father Adam from it and into it We shall restore you when you are interred after death and from it We shall bring you forth at the Resurrection a second time’ in the same way that We brought you forth from it when We initiated your creation.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. Thereof (the earth) We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out once again..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We verily did show him) i.e. Pharaoh (all Our tokens) the hand, the staff, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, blood, drought and lack of harvest, (but he denied them) i.e. the signs and said that they are not from Allah (and refused) to surrender to Allah, rejecting thus all the signs.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. And indeed We showed him [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] all Our Āyāt (signs and evidences), but he denied and refused..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We showed him that is We made Pharaoh see all Our signs all nine but he denied them and claimed that they were the result of sorcery and refused to affirm the Oneness of God exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. And indeed We showed him [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] all Our Āyāt (signs and evidences), but he denied and refused..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) to Moses: (Hast thou come to drive us out from our land) Egypt (by thy magic, O Moses?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يٰمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. He [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Mūsā (Moses)? *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Have you come to us so that you may expel us from our land Egypt and so that kingship over it may be yours by your sorcery O Moses?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يٰمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. He [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Mūsā (Moses)? *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: But we surely can produce magic the like thereof) like the magic you produced; (so appoint a tryst) appoint a time of encounter (between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both)) other than this place; it is also said that this means: a place that is fair to both of us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لاَّ نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلاَ أَنتَ مَكَاناً سُوًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. “Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail to keep, in an open place where both shall have a just and equal chance (and beholders could witness the competition).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Yet We too shall produce for you a sorcery like it one which will counter it. So fix a tryst between us and you for that purpose a tryst which neither we nor you shall fail to keep at a place makānan is in the accusative because the genitive-operator preposition fī ‘at’ has been removed of equal distance read siwān or suwān in other words in the middle equidistant for a person coming from either side.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لاَّ نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلاَ أَنتَ مَكَاناً سُوًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. “Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail to keep, in an open place where both shall have a just and equal chance (and beholders could witness the competition).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Moses) said: Your tryst) the appointed time (shall be the day of the feast) the day of the market, it is also said this means the day of celebration; and it is also said this means the new year's day, (and let the people assemble) from all the townships (when the sun hath risen high) at the time of mid-morning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Said he Moses ‘Your tryst shall be the Day of Adornment — a festive day of theirs on which they adorn themselves and the public assemble — and let the people assemble let the inhabitants of Egypt gather at forenoon’ the time for this tryst to observe what will transpire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then Pharaoh went) to his folk (and gathered his strength) he gathered his advisers and magicians who were 72 in number (and came (to the appointed tryst)) to the appointed time of the gathering.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. So Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) withdrew, devised his plot and then came back..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then Pharaoh withdrew retreated and summoned up his guile that is to say those human elements of his guile from among the sorcerers and then came with them to the tryst.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. So Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) withdrew, devised his plot and then came back..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Moses said unto them) to the magicians: (Woe unto you!) may Allah tighten this worldly life for you (Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you) lest He destroys you (by some punishment) from Him. (He who lieth) about Allah (faileth miserably) loses miserably.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَهُمْ مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لاَ تَفْتَرُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. Mūsā (Moses) said to them: “Woe to you! Invent not a lie against Allāh, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allāh) will fail miserably.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Moses said to them — and there were 72 of them each with a rope and a staff in his hand — ‘Woe to you! meaning may God make you liable to woe. Do not invent a lie against God by ascribing partners to Him lest He annihilate you read fa-yushitakum or fa-yashatakum by some chastisement from Him. For verily he who invents lies against God fails’ he is the loser.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَهُمْ مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لاَ تَفْتَرُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. Mūsā (Moses) said to them: “Woe to you! Invent not a lie against Allāh, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allāh) will fail miserably.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then they debated one with another what they must do) they consulted with one another and decided that if Moses defeats them, they will believe in him, (and they kept their counsel secret) from Pharaoh.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَنَازَعُوۤاْ أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So they disputed their matter among themselves regarding Moses and his brother and kept secret their private counsel that is their conversation regarding the two

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَنَازَعُوۤاْ أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then (They said) openly: (Lo! these are two wizards) i.e. Moses and Aaron are two wizards (who would drive you out from your country) Egypt (by their magic, and destroy your best traditions) your religion and your best men;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُوۤاْ إِنْ هَـٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِّنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. They said: “Verily, these are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with their magic, and to take you away from your superior way (overcome your chiefs and nobles)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said to each other ‘These two men hādhān this form concords with the forms used by those grammarians who use the alif ending for all three cases of the dual person; Abū ‘Amr has the variant reading hādhayn are indeed sorcerers who intend to expel you from your land by their sorcery and do away with your excellent traditions muthlā the feminine form of amthal meaning ‘the noblest’ in other words they will do away with the loyalty of the noblemen among you because these latter will prefer the two of them Moses and Aaron on account of their triumph.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُوۤاْ إِنْ هَـٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِّنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. They said: “Verily, these are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with their magic, and to take you away from your superior way (overcome your chiefs and nobles)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So arrange your plan) your scheming, magic and knowledge, (and come in battle line) all together. (Whoso is uppermost) victorious (this day will be indeed successful).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَجْمِعُواْ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُواْ صَفّاً وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. “So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So summon up your guile in the way of sorcery read fa’jma‘ū from the first form jama‘a meaning ‘he gathered’ or read fa-ajmi‘ū from the fourth form ajma‘a meaning ‘he resolved to do something’ and come in battle-line saffan a circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘standing in rows’. For truly he who is uppermost he who triumphs this day shall be the victor!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَجْمِعُواْ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُواْ صَفّاً وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. “So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said) the magicians said to Moses: (O Moses! Either throw first) either you throw your staff to the ground first, (or let us be the first to throw?)

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ يٰمُوسَىٰ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. They said: “O Mūsā (Moses)! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said ‘O Moses you choose either cast your staff first or we shall be the first to cast’ their staff.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ يٰمُوسَىٰ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. They said: “O Mūsā (Moses)! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Moses said to them: (Nay, do ye throw) you first! And so they threw 72 staffs and 72 ropes. (Then Lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him) to Moses (as though they ran) they moved about.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُواْ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Nay, throw you (first)!” Then behold! Their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Nay you cast!’ and so they cast and lo! their ropes and their staffs ‘isiyyihim derives from ‘isūwwun but the two wāw letters have been changed into two yā’ letters with the kasra vowelling applied to both the ‘ayn and the sād appeared to him by the effect of their sorcery as though they were snakes gliding swiftly on their bellies.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُواْ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Nay, throw you (first)!” Then behold! Their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Moses conceived a fear in his mind) Moses concealed his fear of them. He was afraid that they would kill all those who believed in him, if he failed to defeat them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُّوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. So Mūsā (Moses) con ceived fear in himself..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And Moses sensed fear within himself that is to say he feared that if the effect of their sorcery was of the same kind as his miracle he would become suspect in people’s minds and they would not believe in him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُّوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. So Mūsā (Moses) con ceived fear in himself..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (We said) to Moses: (Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher) you will be victorious over them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْنَا لاَ تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. We (Allāh) said: “Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We said to him ‘Do not be afraid! Indeed you shall have the upper hand over them by triumphing.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْنَا لاَ تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. We (Allāh) said: “Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Throw) to the ground (that which is in thy right hand) O Moses! (It will eat up) it will swallow (that which they have made) that which they have thrown of staffs and ropes. (Lo! that which they have made) that which they have thrown to the ground is (but a wizard's artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful) he shall not be safe nor escape Allah's chastisement or succeed (to whatever point (of skill) he may attain) wherever he is.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوۤاْ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ وَلاَ يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. “And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician’s trick, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may attain.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And cast that which is in your right hand — and this was his staff. It shall swallow up that which they have produced. For what they have produced is only a sorcerer’s trick that is to say a kind thereof and the sorcerer does not succeed wherever he may go’ in his sorcery. So Moses cast his staff and it swallowed up all of that which they had produced.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوۤاْ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ وَلاَ يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. “And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician’s trick, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may attain.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate) their prostration was so quick that one had the impression they were thrown to the ground, (crying) i.e. the magicians: (We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأُلْقِيَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّداً قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. So, the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: “We believe in the Lord of Hārūn (Aaron) and Mūsā (Moses).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thereat the sorcerers cast their heads down prostrating they fell down prostrating to God exalted be He They said ‘We now believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأُلْقِيَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّداً قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. So, the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: “We believe in the Lord of Hārūn (Aaron) and Mūsā (Moses).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Pharaoh) said) to them: (Ye put faith in him before I give you leave) you believed in him before I commanded you to do so. (Lo! he is) i.e. Moses (your chief) the most erudite of you (who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately) the right hand with the left leg, (and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm-trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment) me or the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ آمَنتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَاباً وَأَبْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “Believe you in him [Mūsā (Moses)] before I give you permission? Verily, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So, I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date-palms, and you shall surely know which of us [I (Fir‘aun - Pharaoh) or the Lord of Mūsā (Moses) (Allāh)] can give a more severe and lasting torment.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Said he Pharaoh ‘Do you profess belief read a-āmantum pronouncing both hamzas or with the second changed to an alif in him before I myself give you permission? He is indeed your chief your teacher who taught you sorcery. I shall assuredly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides min khilāfin a circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘alternate hands and feet’ in other words the right hands and the left feet and I shall assuredly crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. And you shall then know which of us — meaning himself and the Lord of Moses — is harsher in inflicting chastisement and which of us is more lasting’ more enduring in sustaining opposition to him Moses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ آمَنتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَاباً وَأَبْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “Believe you in him [Mūsā (Moses)] before I give you permission? Verily, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So, I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of date-palms, and you shall surely know which of us [I (Fir‘aun - Pharaoh) or the Lord of Mūsā (Moses) (Allāh)] can give a more severe and lasting torment.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said) the magicians said to Pharaoh: (We choose thee not) we will not choose worshipping and obeying you (above the clear proofs) of commands, prohibitions, the Scripture, the Messenger and all the signs (that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us) we will choose to worship He who created us. (So decree what thou wilt decree) so proceed to do whatever you wish and sentence us with whatever sentence you wish. (Thou wilt end for us only the life of the world) you will sentence us only in this worldly life but you do not have any power over us in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. They said: “We prefer you not to what have come to us of the clear signs and to Him (Allāh) Who created us. So decree whatever you desire to decree, for you can only decree (regarding) this life of the world..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said ‘We will not choose you over what has come to us of clear signs proving the truthfulness of Moses and over Him Who originated us created us wa’lladhī fatarana either an oath or a supplement to the preceding mā ‘what’. Decree what you will decree that is do what you say. What you decree is only relevant in the life of this world al-hayāta’l-dunyā is in the accusative because the scope of his decree is being indicated in other words ‘you can only decree in it’; yet you will be requited for it in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. They said: “We prefer you not to what have come to us of the clear signs and to Him (Allāh) Who created us. So decree whatever you desire to decree, for you can only decree (regarding) this life of the world..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins) our idolatry (and the magic unto which thou didst force us) the magic which you coerced us to learn. (Allah is better and more lasting) that which is with Allah of reward and favour is better and more lasting that the wealth you give us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ آمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. “Verily, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our faults, and the magic to which you did compel us. And Allāh is better [as regards reward in comparison to your (Fir‘aun’s ― Pharaoh) reward], and more lasting (as regards punishment in comparison to your punishment).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We profess belief in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins in the way of ascribing partners to God and otherwise and the sorcery to which you forced us to learn and to perform in order to oppose Moses. And God is better than you in rewarding if he is obeyed and more enduring’ than you in chastisement if he is disobeyed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ آمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. “Verily, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our faults, and the magic to which you did compel us. And Allāh is better [as regards reward in comparison to your (Fir‘aun’s ― Pharaoh) reward], and more lasting (as regards punishment in comparison to your punishment).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! whoso cometh) on the Day of Judgement (guilty) an idolater (unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die) such that he finds rest (nor live) a beneficial life.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِماً فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لاَ يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يَحْيَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim (criminal, polytheist, sinner, disbeliever in the Oneness of Allāh and His Messengers), then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: God exalted be He says Truly whoever comes to his Lord a criminal a disbeliever like Pharaoh for him there shall be Hell wherein he shall neither die and thus find rest nor live a life of any benefit to him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِماً فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لاَ يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يَحْيَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a Mujrim (criminal, polytheist, sinner, disbeliever in the Oneness of Allāh and His Messengers), then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But whoso cometh unto Him) on the Day of Judgement (a believer) sincere in his faith, (having done good works) secretly between himself and his Lord, (for such are the high stations) in the Gardens;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِناً قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَاتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. But, whoever comes to Him (Allāh) as a believer (in the Oneness of Allāh), and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (in the Hereafter), —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And whoever comes to Him a believer having performed righteous deeds — the obligatory and supererogatory deeds for such shall be the highest degrees al-‘ulā the plural of ‘ulyā the feminine form of a‘lā —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِناً قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَاتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. But, whoever comes to Him (Allāh) as a believer (in the Oneness of Allāh), and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (in the Hereafter), —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then He explained, saying: (Gardens of Eden) this is the Abode of the All-Merciful which He created with His own Hand and power in the middle of the Gardens of Paradise (underneath which) beneath its trees and habitations (rivers) rivers of wine, water, honey and milk (flow, wherein they will abide for ever) living in Paradise, neither to die nor leave it. (That) that Garden and eternity (is the reward of him who groweth) is the reward of he who believes in Allah's divine Oneness and then does good works.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever: such is the reward of those who purify themselves ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: the Gardens of Eden that is to say as a place of residence this jannātu ‘Adnin ‘Gardens of Eden’ is an explication thereof of al-darajātu’l-‘ulā ‘the highest degrees’ underneath which rivers flow abiding therein and that is the reward of him who keeps pure of sins.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever: such is the reward of those who purify themselves ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away) lead (My slaves by night) at the beginning of the night (and strike for them) show them (a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken) by Pharaoh, (neither being afraid (of the sea)) neither being afraid of drowning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لاَّ تَخَافُ دَرَكاً وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. And indeed We revealed to Mūsā (Moses) (saying): “Travel by night with ‘Ibādi (My slaves) and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken [by Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] nor being afraid (of drowning in the sea).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We revealed to Moses saying ‘Lead My servants on a journey by night read as an asri ‘that lead on a journey by night’ from fourth form asrā ‘he travelled by night’; or read as an’isri from first form sarā ‘he travelled by night’ both being alternative forms in other words travel with them by night from the land of Egypt and strike for them make for them by striking your staff a dry path in the sea. So he fulfilled what he had been commanded and God made the ground dry so that they were able to pass through it. Do not fear to be overtaken that is fearing that Pharaoh might catch you and do not be afraid’ of drowning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لاَّ تَخَافُ دَرَكاً وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. And indeed We revealed to Mūsā (Moses) (saying): “Travel by night with ‘Ibādi (My slaves) and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken [by Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] nor being afraid (of drowning in the sea).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then Pharaoh followed with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea) they drowned in the sea.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. Then Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) pursued them with his hosts, but the sea‑water completely overwhelmed them and covered them up..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his hosts with him Pharaoh alongside them and there engulfed them what did engulf them of the sea and it drowned them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. Then Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) pursued them with his hosts, but the sea‑water completely overwhelmed them and covered them up..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Pharaoh led his folk astray) Pharaoh destroyed his people in the sea, (he did not guide them) he did not save them; it is also said that this means: he misguided them regarding Allah's religion and did not guide them to the Truth.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) led his people astray, and he did not guide them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And Pharaoh led his people astray by calling them to worship him and he did not guide them nay he led them to destruction in contrast to what he said to them and I guide you only to the path of rectitude Q. 4029.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) led his people astray, and he did not guide them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (O Children of Israel!) O Children of Jacob (We delivered you from your enemy) from Pharaoh, (and We made a covenant with you on the holy mountain's side) the right side of Moses by giving him the Scripture, (and sent down on you the manna and the quails) in the wilderness,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يٰبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَاكُمْ مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you Al-Manna (1) and quails,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās
