Then We made the sun an indicator of it of the shadow; were it not for the sun the shadow would not have been known.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِناً ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. Have you not seen how your Lord spread the shadow. If He had willed, He could have made it still — But We have made the sun its guide ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then We withdraw it) i.e. the shade (unto Us, a gradual withdrawal) a slight-or as it is said: hidden-withdrawal?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضاً يَسِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Then We withdraw it to Us a gradual concealed withdrawal..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then We retract it the extended shadow to Us by gentle retraction subtle retraction through the rising of the sun.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضاً يَسِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Then We withdraw it to Us a gradual concealed withdrawal..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you) which covers everything, (and sleep repose) for your bodies, (and maketh day a resurrection) a pursuit for your livelihood.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيلَ لِبَاساً وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتاً وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. And it is He Who makes the night a covering for you, and the sleep (as) repose, and makes the day Nushūr ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He it is Who made for you the night as a garment veiling you like a garment and sleep for repose rest for bodies through the temporary cessation of labour and He made the day for rising a time in which all rise to seek their livelihood and so on.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيلَ لِبَاساً وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتاً وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. And it is He Who makes the night a covering for you, and the sleep (as) repose, and makes the day Nushūr ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And He it is Who sendeth the winds, glad tidings heralding His mercy) rain, (and We send down purifying water from the sky) water which purifies and cannot be purified.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْرَاً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And it is He Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His Mercy (rain); and We send down pure water from the sky..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He it is Who sends forth the winds al-riyāha; a variant has al-rīha ‘the wind’ dispersing before His mercy nushuran ‘dispersing’ scattered before the coming of the rain a variant reading has nushran the singular of which is nashūr similar in pattern to rasūl ‘messenger’ plural rusul; another reading has nashran as a verbal noun; and a third variant has bushran in other words the winds function as mubashshirāt ‘bearers of good tidings’ the singular of which is bashīr; and We send down from the heaven purifying water

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْرَاً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And it is He Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His Mercy (rain); and We send down pure water from the sky..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That We may give life thereby to a dead land) a land that has no vegetation, (and We give many beasts and men that We have created to drink thereof.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِّنُحْيِـيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَاماً وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give to drink thereof many of the cattle and men that We had created..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: with which We revive a dead land read maytan in the softened form equally valid for the masculine and the feminine but in the masculine here because of the masculine noun indicating ‘place’ implicit therein and We give it the water as drink to the many cattle camels cows and sheep and humans We have created anāsiyy is the plural of insān properly it the plural should be anāsīn but the final nūn has been replaced with a yā’ with which the other yā’ has been assimilated; or it anāsiyy is simply the plural of insiyy.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِّنُحْيِـيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَاماً وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give to drink thereof many of the cattle and men that We had created..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And verily We have repeated it) the rain (among them) year after year (that they may remember) that they may take heed, (but most of mankind begrudge aught save in gratitude) they refused and stayed firm in ingratitude towards Allah and His blessings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُواْ فَأَبَىٰ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلاَّ كُفُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And indeed We have distributed it (rain or water) amongst them in order that they may remember (the Grace of Allāh), but most men (refuse to accept the Truth or Faith and) accept nothing but disbelief or ingratitude..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We have distributed it the water among them so that they may remember li-yadhdhakkarū should actually be li-yatadhakkarū but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dhāl; a variant reading has li-yadhkurū that is to say so that they may remember therewith the grace of God. But most people are only intent on ingratitude on denial of the grace saying ‘We have received this rain because of such-and-such a storm’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُواْ فَأَبَىٰ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلاَّ كُفُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And indeed We have distributed it (rain or water) amongst them in order that they may remember (the Grace of Allāh), but most men (refuse to accept the Truth or Faith and) accept nothing but disbelief or ingratitude..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (If We willed, We could raise up) We could have sent (a warner) a warning messenger (in every village) to the people of every village. Instead, We have sent you to all mankind as a Messenger so that reward and honour will be all yours.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And had We willed, We would have raised a warner in every town..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And had We willed We could have sent forth in every town a warner to threaten its inhabitants with God’s chastisement; instead We have sent you to the inhabitants of all towns as a warner for your reward to be a great one.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And had We willed, We would have raised a warner in every town..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So obey not the disbelievers) Abu Jahl and his host regarding hat which they ask of you, (but strive against them herewith) by means of the Qur'an (with a great endeavour) by the sword.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهَاداً كَبيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. So, obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them (by preaching) with the utmost endeavour with it (the Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So do not obey the disbelievers in their desires but struggle against them therewith that is through adherence to the Qur’ān with a great endeavour.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهَاداً كَبيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. So, obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them (by preaching) with the utmost endeavour with it (the Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And He it is Who hath given independence to the two seas (though they meet); one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter; and hath set a bar) a barrier between the sweet and the salty (and a forbidding ban between them) preventing either one from transgressing against the other, such as to make the taste of either of them change.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَـٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَـٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. And it is He Who has let free the two seas (kinds of water): this is palatable and sweet, and that is salt and bitter; and He has set a barrier and a complete partition between them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He it is Who merged the two seas letting them flow one adjacent to the other this one palatable sweet and the other saltish bitter; and He set between the two an isthmus so that the one does not mix with the other and a forbidding ban a shield that prevents the two from becoming mixed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَـٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَـٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. And it is He Who has let free the two seas (kinds of water): this is palatable and sweet, and that is salt and bitter; and He has set a barrier and a complete partition between them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And He it is Who hath created man from water) from the water of the male and female, (and hath appointed for him kindred by blood) who are unmarriageable (and kindred by marriage) who are marriageable, whether they are relatives or not; (for thy Lord is) in relation to the lawful and the unlawful which He created (ever Powerful.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَراً فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. And it is He Who has created man from water, and has appointed for him kindred by blood, and kindred by marriage. And your Lord is Ever All-Powerful (to do what He wills)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He it is Who created man from water He created from a sperm-drop a human being and made for him ties of blood and ties of marriage whether it be a male or a female they marry for the purposes of procreation. For your Lord is ever Powerful with the power to do whatever He will.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَراً فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. And it is He Who has created man from water, and has appointed for him kindred by blood, and kindred by marriage. And your Lord is Ever All-Powerful (to do what He wills)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Yet they) the disbelievers of Mecca (worship instead of Allah that which can neither benefit them) in this world or in the next, if they worshipped and obeyed them (nor hurt them) in this world or in the next, if they were to disobey them and abstain from their worship. (The disbeliever) Abu Jahl (was ever a partisan) rebellious (against his Lord) it is also that this means: he is always a helper, through his disbelief, to the disbelievers against his Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. And they (disbelievers, polytheists) worship besides Allāh that which can neither profit them nor harm them; and the disbeliever is ever a helper (of the Satan) against his Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they the disbelievers worship besides God that which neither benefits them when they worship it nor harms them should they refrain therefrom — and these are idols; and the disbeliever is ever a partisan against his Lord an assistant to Satan through his obedience to him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. And they (disbelievers, polytheists) worship besides Allāh that which can neither profit them nor harm them; and the disbeliever is ever a helper (of the Satan) against his Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We have sent thee) O Muhammad to the people of Mecca (only as a bearer of good tidings) Paradise (and a warner) from the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلاَّ مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. And We have sent you (O Muḥammad ) only as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good tidings of Paradise and as a warner a threatener of people with the chastisement of the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلاَّ مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. And We have sent you (O Muḥammad ) only as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) O Muhammad to the people of Mecca: (I ask of you no reward) no payment or provision (for this) for professing Allah's divine Oneness and for the Qur'an, (save that whoso will may choose a way unto his Lord) through faith; it is also said that this means: save for the one who desires to profess Allah's divine Oneness and by means of this profession tread a way back to his Lord whereby he will find his reward.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ مَآ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. Say: “No reward do I ask of you for this (that which I have brought from my Lord and its preaching), except that whosoever wills may take a Path to his Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘I do not ask of you in return for this that is for delivering that Message with which I have been sent any reward except that whoever wishes to follow a way to his Lord should do so’ by expending his wealth for the sake of attaining God’s pleasure exalted be He; then whoever wishes to do so I will not prevent him from doing so.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ مَآ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. Say: “No reward do I ask of you for this (that which I have brought from my Lord and its preaching), except that whosoever wills may take a Path to his Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And trust thou) O Muhammad (in the Living One Who dieth not) and do not trust in those living who die such as Abu Talib or Khadijah, nor trust yet in the dead who have no movement, (and hymn His praise) and pray by His command. (He sufficeth as the Knower of His bondmen's sins) He is aware of the sins of His bondmen,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْحَيِّ ٱلَّذِي لاَ يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. And put your trust (O Muḥammad ) in the Ever Living One Who dies not, and glorify His Praises, and Sufficient is He as the All-Knower of the sins of His slaves, *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And put your trust in the Living One Who does not die and make glorifications ensconced in His praise in other words say subhāna’Llāhi wa’l-hamdu li’Llāh ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God’. And He suffices as One Aware as Knower of the sins of His servants khabīran ‘One Aware’ is semantically connected to bi-dhunūbi ‘of the sins’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْحَيِّ ٱلَّذِي لاَ يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. And put your trust (O Muḥammad ) in the Ever Living One Who dies not, and glorify His Praises, and Sufficient is He as the All-Knower of the sins of His slaves, *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them) of created beings and marvels (in six Days) of the beginning of creation, the length of each day was 1,000 years of the days that you count presently; the first day was Sunday and the last day Friday, (then He mounted the Throne. The Beneficent! Ask any one informed concerning Him) ask those who possess knowledge about Allah, and they will inform you!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days. Then He (Istawā) rose over the Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty). The Most Gracious (Allāh)! Ask Him (O Prophet Muḥammad , concerning His Qualities: His rising over His Throne, His creations, etc.), as He is Khabīr (Well-Acquainted with everything i.e. Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days of the length of the days of this world since there was no sun at that point — had He willed He could have created them in an instant but His not having done so is because He will to teach His creatures to be circumspect — then presided upon the Throne al-‘arsh in the classical language is the seat on which a king sits the Compassionate One al-rahmānu substitutes for the subject of the verb istawā ‘presided’ a presiding befitting of Him; so ask O man about Him about the Compassionate One anyone who is well aware to inform you about His attributes!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days. Then He (Istawā) rose over the Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty). The Most Gracious (Allāh)! Ask Him (O Prophet Muḥammad , concerning His Qualities: His rising over His Throne, His creations, etc.), as He is Khabīr (Well-Acquainted with everything i.e. Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And when it is said unto them) to the people of Mecca: (Adore the Beneficent) submit to the Beneficent through the profession of Allah's divine Oneness! (they say: And what is the Beneficent) we do not know anyone with this name except Musaylimah the liar? (Are we to adore whatever thou (Muhammad) biddest us) a manifest lie? (And it) i.e. the mention of the Beneficent; and it is said: the mention of the Qur'an; and it is said the call of the Prophet (pbuh) (increaseth aversion in them) from faith.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسْجُدُواْ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ قَالُواْ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. And when it is said to them: “Prostrate yourselves to the Most Gracious (Allāh)! they say: “And what is the Most Gracious? Shall we fall down in prostration to that which you (O Muḥammad ) command us?” And it increases in them only aversion..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And when it is said to them to the disbelievers of Mecca ‘Prostrate yourselves before the Compassionate One’ they say ‘And what is the Compassionate One? Should we prostrate ourselves to whatever you bid us’ ta’murunā; or read ya’murunā ‘whatever he bids us’ — in both cases the one bidding is Muhammad (s) — when we do not know who He is? No! And it this that is said to them increases their aversion to faith.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسْجُدُواْ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ قَالُواْ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. And when it is said to them: “Prostrate yourselves to the Most Gracious (Allāh)! they say: “And what is the Most Gracious? Shall we fall down in prostration to that which you (O Muḥammad ) command us?” And it increases in them only aversion..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Blessed be He) He is the Possessor of grace He (Who hath placed in the heaven mansions of the stars) and it is said that this means: mansions, (and hath placed therein) in the heaven (a great lamp) the sun shining during the day for the children of Adam (and a moon giving light) to the Children of Adam during the night!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجاً وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجاً وَقَمَراً مُّنِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. Blessed is He Who has placed in the heaven big stars, and has placed therein a great lamp (sun), and a moon giving light..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: God exalted be He says Blessed magnified is He Who has placed in the heaven constellations twelve of them Aries Taurus Gemini Cancer Leo Virgo al-sunbula Libra Scorpio Sagittarius Capricorn Aquarius and Pisces. They are the mansions for the seven orbiting planets Mars rules Aries and Scorpio Venus Taurus and Libra Mercury Gemini and Virgo the Moon Cancer the Sun Leo Jupiter Sagittarius and Pisces and Saturn Capricorn and Aquarius; and has also placed in it a lamp namely the sun and a shining moon a variant reading for sirājan ‘sun’ has the plural surujan which would mean ‘luminous stars’. The moon is singled out for mention because of its particular merit.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجاً وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجاً وَقَمَراً مُّنِيراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. Blessed is He Who has placed in the heaven big stars, and has placed therein a great lamp (sun), and a moon giving light..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And He it is Who hath appointed night and day in succession) to each other, (for him who desireth to remember) to take admonition in their succession, (or desireth thankfulness) or desires to do righteous works, whatever he left undone at night he does it during the day, and whatever he left undone during the day he does it at night.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ ٱلَّيلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. And He it is Who has put the night and the day in succession, for such who desires to remember or desires to show his gratitude..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He it is Who made the night and day to appear in succession that is one succeeding the other for him who desires to remember read yadhdhakkara or yadhkura as before Q. 2550 — so that if he misses the opportunity to do some good during the one he can do it during the other; or desires to be thankful for the graces of his Lord to him during both of these periods.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ ٱلَّيلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُوراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. And He it is Who has put the night and the day in succession, for such who desires to remember or desires to show his gratitude..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent) the elite of the Beneficent (are they who walk upon the earth modestly) with humility from the fear of Allah, (and when the foolish ones) the disbelievers and sinners (address them answer: Peace) they answer with that which is good and say only nice words;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الجَاهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلاَماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. And the (faithful) slaves of the Most Gracious (Allāh) are those who walk on the earth in humility and sedateness, and when the foolish address them (with bad words) they reply back with mild words of gentleness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the true servants of the Compassionate One ‘ibādu’l-rahmāni is the subject and what comes after it all the way up to ūlā’ika yujzawna ‘they will be rewarded’ of verse 75 below are adjectival qualifiers of this subject with the exception of the parenthetical statements are those who walk upon the earth modestly that is peacefully and humbly and who when the ignorant address them with what they are averse to say words of peace salām in other words words by which they are safe yaslamūna from committing any sin;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الجَاهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلاَماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. And the (faithful) slaves of the Most Gracious (Allāh) are those who walk on the earth in humility and sedateness, and when the foolish address them (with bad words) they reply back with mild words of gentleness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And who spend the night before their Lord) praying, (prostrate and standing) in the night prayer,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَالَّذِينَ يِبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّداً وَقِيَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. And those who spend the night in worship of their Lord, prostrate and standing (1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and who spend the night before their Lord prostrating sujjad is the plural of sājid and standing in worship in other words they spend the night performing prayers;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَالَّذِينَ يِبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّداً وَقِيَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. And those who spend the night in worship of their Lord, prostrate and standing (1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And who say: Our Lord!) O our Lord! (Avert from us the doom of hell; lo! the doom thereof is anguish) binding and persistent;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. And those who say: “Our Lord! Avert from us the torment of Hell. Verily, its torment is ever an inseparable, permanent punishment.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and who say ‘Our Lord avert from us from the chastisement of Hell. Truly its chastisement is abiding that is irrevocable.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. And those who say: “Our Lord! Avert from us the torment of Hell. Verily, its torment is ever an inseparable, permanent punishment.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! it is wretched as abode and station) dwelling;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهَا سَآءَتْ مُسْتَقَرّاً وَمُقَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. Evil indeed it (Hell) is as an abode and as a place to rest in..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is truly a wretched abode and residence!’ in other words it is truly wretched as a place in which to abide and reside.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهَا سَآءَتْ مُسْتَقَرّاً وَمُقَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. Evil indeed it (Hell) is as an abode and as a place to rest in..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then mentioned their spending, saying: (And those who, when they spend, are neither prodigal) they are not prodigal with regard to transgression (nor grudging) they do not withhold that which is right; (and there is ever a firm station) a middle ground (between the two) between prodigality and being miserly;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but hold a medium (way) between those (extremes)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And who when they expend upon their dependants are neither prodigal nor parsimonious read yaqturū or yuqtirū; but between such prodigality and parsimony lies — between the two their expenditure is in — moderation;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but hold a medium (way) between those (extremes)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who cry not unto) worship not (any other god along with Allah) among the idols, (nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden) to kill nor declare it lawful to be killed (save in (course of) justice) through stoning, retaliation or apostasy, (nor commit adultery) nor deem adultery lawful (and whoso doeth this) i.e. deem it lawful (shall pay the penalty) a valley in the Fire; and it is said: a well in the Fire;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا آخَرَ وَلاَ يَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلاَ يَزْنُونَ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. And those who invoke not any other ilāh (god) along with Allāh, nor kill such person as Allāh has forbidden, except for a just cause, nor commit illegal sexual intercourse — and whoever does this shall receive the punishment (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those who do not call on another god along with God nor slay the soul which God has forbidden that it be slain except with due cause and who do not commit fornication — for whoever does that namely whoever does one of these three things shall meet with retribution;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا آخَرَ وَلاَ يَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلاَ يَزْنُونَ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. And those who invoke not any other ilāh (god) along with Allāh, nor kill such person as Allāh has forbidden, except for a just cause, nor commit illegal sexual intercourse — and whoever does this shall receive the punishment (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein) in the doom (disdained) humiliated (for ever;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَاناً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. The torment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide forever therein in disgrace;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: doubled yudā‘af a variant reading has yuda‘‘af will be the chastisement for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will abide therein both verbs may be read in the imperfect apocopated form yudā‘af ‘it will be doubled’ and yakhlud ‘he will abide’ as substitutions or with the indicative damma inflection yudā‘afu and yakhludu to indicate the beginning of a new sentence abased muhānan is a circumstantial qualifier;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَاناً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. The torment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide forever therein in disgrace;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Save him who repenteth) from his disbelief (and believeth) in Allah (and doth righteous work) sincerely after he accepts faith; (as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds) Allah will change them from the state of disbelief to the state of faith, from disobedience to obedience, from the worship of idols to His worship, and from evil to goodness. (Allah is ever Forgiving) He forgives whoever repents, (Merciful) He shows mercy towards whoever dies in a state of repentance.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ مَن تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. Except those who repent and believe (in Islāmic Monothe ism), and do righteous deeds; for those, Allāh will change their sins into good deeds, and Allāh is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (2). And Al-Kalbi said: “Whosoever prays two Rak‘at after the Maghrib (evening) prayer, and four Rak‘at after the ‘Ishā (night) prayer will be considered like those mentioned in this Verse.” (Tafsīr Al-Qurṭubī). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except for him who repents and believes and acts righteously from among them for such God will replace their mentioned evil deeds with good deeds in the Hereafter for God is ever Forgiving Merciful that is He is ever possessed of such attributes;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ مَن تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. Except those who repent and believe (in Islāmic Monothe ism), and do righteous deeds; for those, Allāh will change their sins into good deeds, and Allāh is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (2). And Al-Kalbi said: “Whosoever prays two Rak‘at after the Maghrib (evening) prayer, and four Rak‘at after the ‘Ishā (night) prayer will be considered like those mentioned in this Verse.” (Tafsīr Al-Qurṭubī). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And whosoever repenteth) from sins (and does good) sincerely between him and his Lord, (he verily repenteth towards Allah with true repentance) he will find the reward of this with his Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتاباً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. And whosoever repents and does righteous good deeds; then verily, he repents towards Allāh with true repentance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and whoever repents of his sins from among other than those mentioned and acts righteously indeed turns to God with due repentance that is he returns to God a sincere return and God will requite him with good;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتاباً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. And whosoever repents and does righteous good deeds; then verily, he repents towards Allāh with true repentance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who will not witness vanity) those who do not attend the sessions of false testimony, (but when they pass near senseless play) the assemblies of falsehood, (pass by with dignity) they avoid them out of clemency.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِراماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and if they pass by some evil play or evil talk, they pass by it with dignity..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those who do not give false testimony that is testimony containing mendacity and falsehood and when they come across senseless talk in the way of vile speech and otherwise they pass by with dignity shunning such vanity;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِراماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and if they pass by some evil play or evil talk, they pass by it with dignity..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who, when they are reminded of) admonished about (the revelations of their Lord, fall not deaf) unable to hear (and blind) unable to see while being very capable of hearing and seeing (thereat) the signs of Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّواْ عَلَيْهَا صُمّاً وَعُمْيَاناً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. And those who, when they are reminded of the Āyāt (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those who when they are reminded when they are admonished of the revelations of their Lord that is reminded of the Qur’ān do not fall on them deaf and blind but fall on them listening contemplating benefiting and obedient;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّواْ عَلَيْهَا صُمّاً وَعُمْيَاناً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. And those who, when they are reminded of the Āyāt (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And who say: Our Lord!) O our Lord! (Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring) make our wives and offspring righteous so that we may find comfort in them, (and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil)) make us righteous so that they emulate us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. And those who say: “Our Lord! Bestow on us from our wives and our offspring the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders of the Muttaqūn) (1).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those who say ‘Our Lord! Grant us in our spouses and our offspring read plural dhurriyyātinā or singular dhurriyyatinā a joyful sight for us so that we see them obedient to You and make us paragons of virtue for the God-fearing’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. And those who say: “Our Lord! Bestow on us from our wives and our offspring the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders of the Muttaqūn) (1).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They) those who have such traits (will be awarded the high place) the highest ranks in Paradise (forasmuch as they were steadfast) in obedience of Allah and in bearing poverty and misfortune, (and they will meet therein) in Paradise (with welcome) from Allah (and the word of peace) the angels will meet them in Paradise with greeting and peace from Allah,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ٱلْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةً وَسَلاَماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. Those will be rewarded with the highest place (in Paradise) because of their patience. Therein they shall be met with greetings and the word of peace and respect..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Those they will be rewarded with the sublime abode the highest degree in Paradise forasmuch as they were steadfast in obedience to God and they will be met read yulaqqawna or yalqawna therein in this sublime abode with a greeting and words of peace from the angels;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ٱلْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةً وَسَلاَماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. Those will be rewarded with the highest place (in Paradise) because of their patience. Therein they shall be met with greetings and the word of peace and respect..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Abiding there for ever) they will remain in Paradise for ever, neither to die nor leave. (Happy is it as abode) as habitation (and station!) and dwelling!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرّاً وَمُقَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: Abiding therein forever — excellent it is as an abode, and as a place to rest in.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: abiding therein. Excellent is it as an abode and station as a place of residence for them ūlā’ika ‘those they …’ and what comes after it constitute the predicate to the subject ‘ibādu’l-rahmāni ‘the servants of the Compassionate One’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرّاً وَمُقَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: Abiding therein forever — excellent it is as an abode, and as a place to rest in.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) O Muhammad, to the disbelievers of Mecca: (My Lord would not concern himself with you) what would my Lord do with your bodies and forms (but for your prayer) if He commands you to profess Allah's divine Oneness. (But now ye have denied) you have disbelieved in Muhammad (pbuh) and in the Qur'an, (therefore) this is a threat to them from Allah (there will be judgement) the punishment of the Day of Badr through beating, killing and enslaving them; this is to say: you have disbelieved in your Prophet and, therefore, the chastisement must necessarily befall you'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلاَ دُعَآؤُكُمْ فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. Say (O Muḥammad  to the disbelievers): “My Lord pays attention to you only because of your invocation to Him. But now you have indeed denied (Him). So the torment will be yours forever (insepara ble, permanent punishment).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say O Muhammad (s) to the people of Mecca ‘My Lord would not be concerned with you mā is for negation were it not for your supplications to Him when you are in adversity which He then removes. But why should He be concerned with you when you have denied the Messenger and the Qur’ān and so that the chastisement will remain binding’ permanently bound to you in the Hereafter in addition to what will befall you in this world; and so on the day of Badr seventy of them were slain the response to the conditional lawlā ‘were it not for …’ is indicated the preceding words.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلاَ دُعَآؤُكُمْ فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَاماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. Say (O Muḥammad  to the disbelievers): “My Lord pays attention to you only because of your invocation to Him. But now you have indeed denied (Him). So the torment will be yours forever (insepara ble, permanent punishment).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Ta. Sin. Mim.): '(Ta. Sin. Mim.) He says: Ta stands for His might (tawluh) and power, Sin stands for His majesty (sana'uh), and Mim stands for His dominion (mulkuh); it is also said that (Ta. Sin. Mim.) is an oath by which Allah swore.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: طسۤمۤ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Tā-Sīn-Mīm. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Tā sīn mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: طسۤمۤ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Tā-Sīn-Mīm. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (These are revelations of the Scripture that maketh plain) He says: I swear by this surah, the verses of the Qur'an, which make plain the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and prohibitions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. These are the Āyāt of the manifest Book [(this Qur’ān), which was promised by Allāh in the Taurāt (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel)], makes things clear..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Those namely these signs are the signs of the Manifest Book the Qur’ān the genitive annexation āyātu’l-kitābi conveys the partitive meaning of min the Manifest meaning the one that manifests what is truth from what is falsehood.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. These are the Āyāt of the manifest Book [(this Qur’ān), which was promised by Allāh in the Taurāt (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel)], makes things clear..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (It may be that thou tormentest thyself) it may be that you kill yourself with grief over them (because they believe not) because the Quraysh do not want to become believers. This is because he was very keen for them to become believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلاَّ يَكُونُواْ مُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. It may be that you (O Muḥammad ) are going to kill yourself with grief, that they do not become believers [in your Risalah (Messengership) i.e. in your Message of Islāmic Monotheism](1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Perhaps O Muhammad (s) you might kill yourself out of distress for the reason that they namely the people of Mecca will not become believers la‘alla here expresses sympathy in other words what is meant is ‘have pity on it your self by alleviating the burden of this distress’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلاَّ يَكُونُواْ مُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. It may be that you (O Muḥammad ) are going to kill yourself with grief, that they do not become believers [in your Risalah (Messengership) i.e. in your Message of Islāmic Monotheism](1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (If We will, We can send down on them from the sky a portent) a sign (so that their necks would remain bowed before it) in humiliation.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. If We will, We could send down to them from the heaven a sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: If We will We will send down to them a sign from the heaven before which their necks will remain fa-zallat although grammatically in the past tense is being used in the sense of the imperfect tense bowed in humility and they will believe since ‘necks’ are described as ‘bowed in humility’ a status which in fact refers to those who possess them the adjectival form khādi‘ūn ‘bowed in humility’ used therein is the one normally used for rational beings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. If We will, We could send down to them from the heaven a sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Never cometh there unto them a fresh) i.e. fresh in its coming, in succession (reminder) never did Gabriel bring revelation of the Qur'an to their Prophet (from the Beneficent One, but they turn away from it) except that they disbelieved in the Qur'an.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And never comes there to them a Reminder as a recent revelation from the Most Gracious (Allāh), but they turn away therefrom..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And there would never come to them from the Compassionate One any remembrance any revelation from the Qur’ān that is new muhdathin is an explicative adjective but that they used to disregard it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And never comes there to them a Reminder as a recent revelation from the Most Gracious (Allāh), but they turn away therefrom..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Now they have denied) Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an; (but there will come unto them tidings) the news (of that whereat they used to scoff) of chastisement; it is also said that this means: there will come to them the news of their derision of Muhammad (pbuh) and of the Qur'an.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُواْ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَاءُ مَا كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. So, they have indeed denied (the truth — this Qur’ān), then the news of what they mocked at will come to them. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily then they have denied it; but soon there will come to them the news the consequences of that which they used to deride.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُواْ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَاءُ مَا كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. So, they have indeed denied (the truth — this Qur’ān), then the news of what they mocked at will come to them. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Have they) the disbelievers of Mecca (not seen the earth, how much of every fruitful kind We make to grow therein?)

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Do they not observe the earth — how much of every good kind We cause to grow therein?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have they not contemplated observed the earth how many We have caused to grow therein in other words We have caused to grow therein many of every splendid kind of vegetation of every fair species.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Do they not observe the earth — how much of every good kind We cause to grow therein?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Herein) in the different kinds of fruit (is indeed a portent) a sign and an admonition; (yet most of them are not believers) they were not believers, and all of them were disbelievers, i.e. those who perished at Badr.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Verily, in this is an Āyāh (proof or sign), yet most of them (polytheists, pagans who do not believe in Resurrection) are not believers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Surely in that there is a sign an indication of the perfection of His power exalted be He; but most of them in God’s knowledge are not believers kāna here according to Sībawayhi is extra.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Verily, in this is an Āyāh (proof or sign), yet most of them (polytheists, pagans who do not believe in Resurrection) are not believers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty) in retribution against the disbelievers, (the Merciful) towards the believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And verily, your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And surely your Lord He is the Mighty One Who will exact vengeance from the disbelievers the Merciful Who shows mercy to believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And verily, your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And when thy Lord called Moses) it is also said that this means: and when your Lord commanded Moses, (saying: Go unto the wrong-doing folk) the disbelieving folk,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And (remember) when your Lord called Mūsā (Moses) (saying): “Go to the people who are Ẓālimūn (polytheists and wrong-doers) —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And mention O Muhammad (s) to your people when your Lord called to Moses on the night he saw the fire and the bush saying ‘Go to the wrongdoing folk as a messenger

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And (remember) when your Lord called Mūsā (Moses) (saying): “Go to the people who are Ẓālimūn (polytheists and wrong-doers) —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The folk of Pharaoh. Will they not ward off (evil)) and tell: will they not ward off the worship of other than Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَلا يَتَّقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. “The people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh): Will they not fear Allāh and become righteous?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Pharaoh’s folk to them as well as him — they wronged their souls by disbelieving in God and wronged the Children of Israel by enslaving them — Will they not a-lā the hamza indicates a negation meant as a rebuke show fear?’ of God by being obedient to Him and affirm His Oneness?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَلا يَتَّقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. “The people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh): Will they not fear Allāh and become righteous?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Moses said: (My Lord! Lo! I fear that they will deny me) I fear that they will disbelieve in the message I bring to them,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. He said: “My Lord! Verily, I fear that they will deny me,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Moses said ‘My Lord I fear they will deny me

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. He said: “My Lord! Verily, I fear that they will deny me,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And I shall be embarrassed) because of their denial; it is also said that this means: and my heart will shrink from delivering the message, (and my tongue will not speak plainly) out of awe of him, (therefore send for Aaron (to help me)) send Aaron with me to support me; it is also said that this means: send Gabriel to Aaron so that he helps me.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلاَ يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَارُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. “And my breast straitens, and my tongue expresses not well. So send for Hārūn (Aaron) (to come along with me)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that anguish will constrain my breast because of their denial of me and that my tongue will not utter clearly to deliver the Message because of the knot in it. So give the Mission to my brother Aaron alongside me.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلاَ يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَارُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. “And my breast straitens, and my tongue expresses not well. So send for Hārūn (Aaron) (to come along with me)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they have a crime against me) they may retaliate against me because I killed the Copt, (so I fear that they will kill me) because of this Copt that I killed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. “And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And I have sinned against them by my slaying of the Egyptian man and I fear they will slay me’ for this.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. “And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Allah said: (Nay, verily) I will not set them against you to kill you. (So go ye twain with Our tokens) with Our nine signs: the hand, the staff, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, blood, the lack of foodstuff and drought. (Lo! We shall be with you) We shall help you, (Hearing) what he says to you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ كَلاَّ فَٱذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. (Allāh) said: “Nay! Go you both with Our Signs. Verily, We shall be with you, listening..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Said He exalted be He ‘Certainly not! they shall not slay you. Go both of you you and your brother — this address although in the dual form is predominantly for the person present as opposed to the absent one — with Our signs. We will indeed be with you hearing what you say and what is said to you ma‘akum the two Moses and Aaron are referred to here with the plural pronoun.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ كَلاَّ فَٱذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. (Allāh) said: “Nay! Go you both with Our Signs. Verily, We shall be with you, listening..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And come together unto Pharaoh and say: Lo! we bear a message of the Lord of the Worlds) to you and to your people,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولاۤ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. “And go both of you to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and say: ‘We are the Messengers of the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So the two of you approach Pharaoh and say “Indeed We are — indeed each of the two of us is the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds to you

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولاۤ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. “And go both of you to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and say: ‘We are the Messengers of the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Saying): Let the Children of Israel go with Us) and do not torture them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. “So allow the Children of Israel to go with us.’”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that you should let go forth with us to Syria the Children of Israel” ’. So they approached him and said to him that which has been mentioned.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. “So allow the Children of Israel to go with us.’”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said): Pharaoh looked at Moses and said: (Did we not rear thee among us as a child?) O Moses (And thou didst dwell many years of your life among us) and stayed with us for 30 years,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said [to Mūsā (Moses)]: “Did we not bring you up among us as a child? And you did dwell many years of your life with us..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Pharaoh said to Moses ‘Did we not rear you among us in our homes as a child? as an infant only recently born but weaned and did you not stay with us for years of your life? for thirty years — he would dress from Pharaoh’s clothes and ride chariots of his and was referred to as Pharaoh’s son.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said [to Mūsā (Moses)]: “Did we not bring you up among us as a child? And you did dwell many years of your life with us..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And thou didst that thy deed which thou didst) and you killed the person that you killed, (and thou wast one of the ingrates) and you are now ungrateful for my kindness,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. “And you did your deed, which you did (i.e. the crime of killing a man) while you were one of the ingrates.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And you committed that deed of yours — namely his slaying of the Egyptian — being an ingrate’ a denier of my favours to you in having reared you among us and not enslaved you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. “And you did your deed, which you did (i.e. the crime of killing a man) while you were one of the ingrates.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Moses said: (I did it then, when I was of those who are astray) when I was ungrateful for your kindness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذاً وَأَنَاْ مِنَ ٱلضَّالِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Mūsā (Moses) said: “I did it then, when I was ignorant (as regards my Lord and His Message)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Moses said ‘I did that then when I was astray from the knowledge and the Message which God would later give me.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذاً وَأَنَاْ مِنَ ٱلضَّالِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Mūsā (Moses) said: “I did it then, when I was ignorant (as regards my Lord and His Message)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then I fled from you when I feared you) when I feared that you would kill me, (and my Lord vouchsafed me a command) understanding, knowledge and prophethood (and appointed me (of the number) of those sent (by Him)) He made me a Messenger to you and to your people.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. “So, I fled from you when I feared you. But my Lord has granted me Ḥukm (i.e. religious knowledge, right judgement of the affairs and Prophethood), and made me one of the Messengers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So I fled from you as I was afraid of you. Then my Lord gave me judgement knowledge and made me one of the messengers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. “So, I fled from you when I feared you. But my Lord has granted me Ḥukm (i.e. religious knowledge, right judgement of the affairs and Prophethood), and made me one of the Messengers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And this is the past favour wherewith) with which (thou reproachest me) O Pharaoh, but you do not recall your aloofness towards me: (that thou hast enslaved the Children of Israel.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. “And this is the past favour with which you reproach me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: That is a favour with which you now reproach me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel’ an ‘abbadta banī Isrā’īl is explicative of tilka ‘that’ in other words you have enslaved them but not me there is no favour in that for your enslavement of them is wrong some scholars have reckoned there to be an interrogative hamza of denial at the beginning of this verse a-tilka ni‘matun ‘is that a favour?’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. “And this is the past favour with which you reproach me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Pharaoh said) to Moses: (And what is the Lord of the Worlds) who is the Lord of the Worlds? Is it me you are referring to?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) said: “And what is the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Pharaoh said to Moses ‘And what is “the Lord of the Worlds” ’ the One Whose Messenger you say you indeed are? In other words what exactly is He? And since there is no way for creation to know the true nature of God but only to know Him through an articulation of His attributes Moses blessings and peace be upon him responds to him with mention of some of these attributes

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) said: “And what is the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Moses) said: Lord of the heavens and the earth) the Lord of the Worlds is the Lord of the heavens and the earth (and all that is between them) of created beings and marvels, (if ye had but sure belief) that Allah has created them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ مُّوقِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, if you seek to be convinced with certainty.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in other words the Creator of all that — should you have conviction’ that He exalted be He is their Creator then believe in Him alone.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ مُّوقِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, if you seek to be convinced with certainty.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Pharaoh) said unto those around him) of attendants: (Hear ye not) what Moses says? There were around Pharaoh at that time 250 men wearing attires made of silk brocade plaited with gold. These men were Pharaoh's closest courtiers, and they asked Moses: who is this Lord of the heavens and the earth to whom you are calling us?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ أَلاَ تَسْتَمِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said to those around him: “Do you not hear (what he says)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Pharaoh said to those noblemen among his folk who were around him ‘Did you not hear?!’ his response how it does not correspond to the question I asked?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ أَلاَ تَسْتَمِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said to those around him: “Do you not hear (what he says)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Moses said: (Your Lord) He is your Lord (and the Lord of your fathers.

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Moses said ‘Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers’. Now even though this fact is comprised by what was said before it enrages Pharaoh and therefore

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَآئِكُمُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. [Mūsā (Moses)] said: “Your Lord and the Lord of your ancient fathers!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Pharaoh) said: Lo! your messenger who hath been sent unto you is indeed a madman!) They said: who is this that you are calling us to? And who is this Lord of ours who is also the Lord of our fathers, O Moses?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِيۤ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “Verily, your Messenger who has been sent to you is a madman!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Verily this messenger of yours sent to you is a madman!’

tafsir: (He said) Moses said: (Lord of the East) He is the Lord of the East (and the West) and the Lord of the West (and all that is between them, if ye did but understand) if you did but believe.

tafsir: He Moses said ‘The Lord of the east and the west and all that is between them — should you comprehend’ that He is such a Lord then believe in Him alone.

tafsir: ((Pharaoh) said: If thou choosest) if you worship (a god other than me) O Moses, (I assuredly shall place thee among the prisoners) his prisons were worse than death, for he used to put people in complete isolation, unable to see or hear anyone.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَـٰهَاً غَيْرِي لأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “If you choose an ilāh (god) other than me, I will certainly put you among the prisoners.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Pharaoh said to Moses ‘If you choose any god other than me I will surely make you a prisoner!’. His Pharaoh’s prison was very harsh for a person would be shut up in a dungeon underground alone where he could neither see nor hear anyone else.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَـٰهَاً غَيْرِي لأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ

tafsir: (He said) Moses said: (Even though I show thee) O Pharaoh (something plain) a sign that serves as proof for what I say?

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Moses said to him ‘What would you do this even if I bring you something manifest?’ patent proof of my Mission?

tafsir: ((Pharaoh) said: Produce it then) O Moses, (if thou art of the Truthful) that you are a Messenger to me and to my people!

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Pharaoh said to him ‘Then bring it if you are truthful’ in this.

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then he) Moses (flung down his staff and it became a serpent) a yellow, male serpent (manifest) as huge as any serpent can be,

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So he threw down his staff and lo! it was a manifest serpent a great snake.

tafsir: Pharaoh then said: “this is a manifest sign, do you have any other signs?” (And he drew forth his hand) from his armpit (and lo! it was white to the beholders) his hand had a light like the light of the sun, and whoever looked at it liked it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Pharaoh said to the council around him ‘Surely this man is a cunning sorcerer an expert in the art of magic

meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said to the chiefs around him: “Verily, this is indeed a well-versed sorcerer..

meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. “That we may follow the sorcerers [who were on Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh) religion of disbelief] if they are the winners.”.

tafsir: Moses said to them after they had said to him Either you cast or we shall be the casters Q. 7115 ‘Cast what you have to cast’ — the command to do this signifies an authorisation for them to cast and a means whereby the truth will be made to prevail.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَهُمْ مُّوسَىٰ أَلْقُواْ مَآ أَنتُمْ مُّلْقُونَ

tafsir: Then they threw down their cords and their staves) 72 ropes and 72 staffs (and said) i.e. the wizards said: (By Pharaoh's might, lo! we verily are the winners) against Moses.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. So they threw their ropes and their sticks, and said: “By the might of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), it is we who will certainly win!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So they cast their ropes and their staffs and said ‘By the power of Pharaoh we shall surely be the victors!’

tafsir: the Lord of Moses and Aaron’ for they realised that what they had witnessed in the case of the staff could not have been the result of mere sorcery.

tafsir: (Pharaoh) said, You put your faith in him) you believed in him (before I give you leave) I commanded you to do so. (Lo! He) i.e. Moses (doubtless is your chief) your master wizard (who taught you magic! But verily ye shall come to know) what I will do to you. (Verily I will cut off your hands and your feet alternately) the right hand with the left leg, (and verily I will crucify you everyone) on the bank of the river of Egypt.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ آمَنتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: “You have believed in him before I give you leave. Surely, he indeed is your chief, who has taught you magic! So verily, you shall come to know. Verily, I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Pharaoh said ‘Do you believe a-āmantum read pronouncing both hamzas or replacing the second one with an alif him Moses though I have not given you leave? He is indeed your chief the one who has taught you sorcery — so that he only taught you some tricks and then surpassed you with others. Soon you will know what I will do with you! I will assuredly cut off your hands and legs on opposite sides — in other words the right hand of each one together with his left leg — then I shall surely crucify you all.’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ آمَنتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said: It is no hurt) what you do with us in this worldly life will not harm us in the Hereafter, (for lo! unto our Lord we shall return) we shall return to Allah and His reward.

tafsir: (Lo! we ardently hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins) our idolatry (because we are the first of the believers) in Moses.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. “Verily, we really hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, as we are the first of the believers [in Mūsā (Moses) and in the Monotheism which he has brought from Allāh].”.

tafsir: (And We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night) take by night whoever believes in you from among the Children of Israel, (for ye will be pursued) Pharaoh and his people will catch up with you.

tafsir: And We revealed to Moses after many years which he spent among them calling them to the truth with God’s signs but all of which only increased them in insolence saying ‘Journey with My servants the Children of Israel by night a variant reading for an asri is an isr from the verb sarā one form of asrā go with them by night in the direction of the sea for indeed you will be pursued’. Pharaoh and his armies will pursue you but when they enter the sea in pursuit of you I will deliver you and drown them.
