meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. And he puts forth for Us a parable, and forgets his own creation. He says: “Who will give life to these bones after they are rotten and have become dust?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And he strikes for Us a similitude in this respect and forgets the manner of his creation from a sperm-drop a thing more curious than his similitude; he says ‘Who will revive the bones when they are rot?’ in other words when they have become withered He does not say ramīmatun ‘decayed’ because it ramīmun ‘rot’ is a noun and not an adjective. It is reported that he al-‘Āsī took some withered bones and crushed them into pieces and said to the Prophet s ‘Do you think that God can revive these bones after they have decayed and become rot?’ And so the Prophet s said ‘Yes indeed! And He will also throw you into the Fire’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلاً وَنَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قَالَ مَن يُحيِي ٱلْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. And he puts forth for Us a parable, and forgets his own creation. He says: “Who will give life to these bones after they are rotten and have become dust?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) to him, O Muhammad: (He will revive them Who produced them) Who created them (at the first) from a sperm drop, (for He is Knower of every creation) He is Knower of the creation of everything,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. Say: (O Muḥammad ) “He will give life to them Who created them for the first time! And He is All-Knower of every creation!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘He will revive them Who originated them the first time and He is Knower of all creation of every single creature generally and in detail before and after it has been created —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. Say: (O Muḥammad ) “He will give life to them Who created them for the first time! And He is All-Knower of every creation!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who hath appointed for you fire) other than the Fire of punishment (from the green tree, and behold! Ye) O people of Mecca (kindle from it) you derive from the green tree fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلأَخْضَرِ نَاراً فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْه تُوقِدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. He Who produces for you fire out of the green trees, when behold! you kindle therewith..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Who has made for you and for all human beings fire from the green tree namely from the markh and ‘afār variety or from all trees except for the jujube ‘unnāb and behold from it you kindle’ from it you strike fire this is proof of the power of God to resurrect for in this example of the green tree He has combined the elements of water fire and wood; but neither the water extinguishes the fire nor does the fire ignite the wood.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلأَخْضَرِ نَاراً فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْه تُوقِدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. He Who produces for you fire out of the green trees, when behold! you kindle therewith..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth Able to create) to revive (the like of them? Aye that He is!) He is Able to do so, (for He is the All-Wise Creator) Who will resurrect the dead,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَلَـيْسَ ٱلَذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاواتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلْخَلاَّقُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Is not He, Who created the heavens and the earth, Able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed! He is the All-Knowing Supreme Creator..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth in all their immensity able to create the like of them? namely human beings in all their minuteness? Yes indeed He is able to do this — God Himself replies here. And He is the Creator khallāq means Creator of many things the Knower of all things.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَلَـيْسَ ٱلَذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاواتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلْخَلاَّقُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Is not He, Who created the heavens and the earth, Able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed! He is the All-Knowing Supreme Creator..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But His command) regarding the resurrection, (when He intends a thing) when He wishes the resurrection to take place, (is only that he says unto it: Be! and it is) and the coming of the Hour happens.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيْئاً أَن يَقُولَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. Verily, His Command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, “Be!” — and it is!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: His command His affair when He wills a thing that is when He will to create something is just to say to it ‘Be’ and it is a variant reading for fa-yakūnu has fa-yakūna as a supplement to yaqūla ‘to say’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيْئاً أَن يَقُولَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. Verily, His Command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, “Be!” — and it is!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Therefore glory be to Him) Allah glorified Himself (in Whose hand is the dominion over all things) the stores of all things and the creating of all things! (Unto Him you will be brought back) after death and He will requite you each according to his works'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. So, glorified is He (and exalted above all that they associate with Him), in Whose Hand is the dominion of all things: and to Him you shall be returned..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So glory be to Him in Whose hand is the dominion of all things malakūt means mulk the wāw and tā’ have been added for hyperbole and to Whom you will be returned restored in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. So, glorified is He (and exalted above all that they associate with Him), in Whose Hand is the dominion of all things: and to Him you shall be returned..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (By those who set the ranks in battle order): '(By those who set the ranks in battle order) Allah swore by the angels who are, in heaven, aligned in rows like the rows of the believers in prayer.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلصَّافَّاتِ صَفَّا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By those (angels) ranged in ranks (or rows)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By those who are ranged in ranks — by the angels who range their souls in worship or their wings in the air awaiting their orders;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلصَّافَّاتِ صَفَّا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By those (angels) ranged in ranks (or rows)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who drive away with reproof) He also swore by the angels who drive away the clouds and bring them together.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By those (angels) who drive the clouds in a good way..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the drivers who drive away the angels who drive the clouds;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By those (angels) who drive the clouds in a good way..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who read (the Word) for a reminder) He swore by the angels who recite the Qur'an; it is also said that He swore by the reciters of the Qur'an,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلتَّٰلِيَٰتِ ذِكْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. By those (angels) who bring the Book and the Qur’ān from Allāh to mankind [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those who recite that is to say the readers of the Qur’ān they recite it by way remembrance dhikran is a verbal noun referring to the action of al-tāliyāt ‘those who recite’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلتَّٰلِيَٰتِ ذِكْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. By those (angels) who bring the Book and the Qur’ān from Allāh to mankind [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! thy Lord is surely One) without a son or partner; this oath says: O people of Mecca, your Lord is One, He has no son or partner.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ إِلَـٰهَكُمْ لَوَاحِدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Verily, your Ilāh (God) is indeed One (i.e. Allāh):.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed your God O people of Mecca is certainly One

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ إِلَـٰهَكُمْ لَوَاحِدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Verily, your Ilāh (God) is indeed One (i.e. Allāh):.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lord of the heavens and of the earth) the Creator of the heavens and of the earth (and all that is between them) of created beings and marvels, (and Lord of the sun's risings) the risings of winter and summer.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَشَارِقِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. The Lord of the heavens and of the earth, and all that is between them, and the Lord of every point of the sun’s risings (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them and Lord of the sun’s risings that is as well as the sun’s settings — each day it the sun has a rising and a setting.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَشَارِقِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. The Lord of the heavens and of the earth, and all that is between them, and the Lord of every point of the sun’s risings (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We have adorned the lowest heaven) the first heaven (with an ornament, the planets) He says: the first heaven is adorned with planets:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, We have adorned the near heaven with the stars (for beauty) (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We have indeed adorned the lowest heaven with an adornment the stars that is to say adorned with their light or with them the stars the genitive annexation bi-zīnati’l-kawākib is for explication; similarly explicative is the reading of bi-zīnatin ‘with an adornment’ with nunation the adornment explained as being ‘the stars’;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, We have adorned the near heaven with the stars (for beauty) (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (With security) He says: they are made safe (from every froward devil) from every tough, rebellious devil.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحِفْظاً مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And to guard against every rebellious devil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and to guard wa-hifzan is in the accusative because of an implied verb that is to say ‘We have guarded it with meteors’ from every min kulli is semantically connected to the implied verb any rebellious devil who is a transgressor in rebellion against obedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحِفْظاً مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And to guard against every rebellious devil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They cannot listen) so that they do not listen (to the Highest Chiefs) to the speech of the angels, i.e. the guardian angels, regarding that which is communicated amongst them (for they are pelted from every side) they rise up to,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. They cannot listen to the higher group (angels) for they are pelted from every side. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They namely the devils lā yasma‘ūna this is the beginning of a new sentence cannot listen in — this ‘listening’ of theirs represents that faculty with which they memorise what they hear — on the High Council the angels in the heavens the normally transitive verb al-samā‘ is complemented with the preposition ilā ‘to’ here ‘in on’ because it includes the additional sense of ‘paying attention’ while listening; a variant reading has yassamma‘una which is actually yatasamma‘ūna the tā’ have been assimilated with the sīn for they the devils are pelted with flames from every side from the remotest regions of the heavens

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. They cannot listen to the higher group (angels) for they are pelted from every side. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Outcast) they are driven away from heaven and from listening to the angels, (and theirs is a perpetual torment) by means of the stars; and it is also said that this means: in the Fire;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: دُحُوراً وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ وَاصِبٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Outcast, and theirs is a constant (or painful) torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: to repel them duhūran is a verbal noun from daharahu meaning ‘he repelled him driving him away’; it is an object denoting reason and theirs in the Hereafter is an everlasting chastisement;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: دُحُوراً وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ وَاصِبٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Outcast, and theirs is a constant (or painful) torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save him who snatcheth a fragment) save him who snatches a little of the words of the angels, (and there pursueth him a piercing flame) and is chased by a bright star which burns him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ مَنْ خَطِفَ ٱلْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Except such as snatch away something by stealing, and they are pursued by a flaming fire of piercing brightness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except him who snatches a fragment al-khatfa is the verbal noun that is to say ‘that one time’; the exceptive clause refers to the subject of the verb yasma‘ūna in other words ‘the only devil that is able to listen is the one that hears a word from the angels and snatches it away quickly’ and who is then pursued by a piercing flame shihāb is a meteor that pierces him or burns him or robs him of his senses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ مَنْ خَطِفَ ٱلْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Except such as snatch away something by stealing, and they are pursued by a flaming fire of piercing brightness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then ask them (O Muhammad)) ask the people of Mecca: (Are they stronger as a creation) as a resurrected people, (or those (others) whom We have created) of angels and all other people? (Lo! We created them of plastic) sticking (clay) We created them from Adam and Adam is from clay.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُم مِّن طِينٍ لاَّزِبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Then, ask them (i.e. these polytheists, O Muḥammad ): “Are they stronger as creation, or those (others like the heavens and the earth and the mountains) whom We have created?” Verily, We created them of a sticky clay..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So ask them in other words inquire of the people of Mecca for affirmation or by way of rebuke Are they stronger as a creation or those others whom We created? of angels heavens the two earths and all that is in them the use of man ‘those whom’ in man khalaqnā indicates that the reference is predominantly to other rational creatures. Indeed We created them that is their origin Adam from a viscous clay that sticks to the hand. The intended meaning is that their physical make-up is fragile so let them not behave arrogantly by rejecting the Prophet and the Qur’ān a fact which will result in their — easily accomplished — destruction.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُم مِّن طِينٍ لاَّزِبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Then, ask them (i.e. these polytheists, O Muḥammad ): “Are they stronger as creation, or those (others like the heavens and the earth and the mountains) whom We have created?” Verily, We created them of a sticky clay..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but thou dost) O Muhammad (marvel) their denial of you (when they mock) you and your Scripture.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Nay, you (O Muḥammad ) wondered (at their insolence), while they mock (at you and at the Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay but bal is for effecting a transition from one object to another which in this case is to inform of his state and theirs you marvel ‘ajibta addressing the Prophet s that is you marvel that they deny you while they engage in ridicule at your marvelling

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Nay, you (O Muḥammad ) wondered (at their insolence), while they mock (at you and at the Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And heed not) and take no admonition (when they are reminded) by the Qur'an,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ لاَ يَذْكُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And when they are reminded, they pay no attention..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and even when they are reminded when they are admonished with the Qur’ān they are not mindful they do not heed the admonition

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ لاَ يَذْكُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And when they are reminded, they pay no attention..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And seek to scoff when they) the people of Mecca (behold a portent) a sign such as the splitting of the moon and the eclipse of the sun.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ آيَةً يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And when they see an Āyāh (a sign, or an evidence) from Allāh, they mock at it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and when they see a sign such as the splitting of the moon cf. Q. 541 they make it an object of ridicule they deride it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ آيَةً يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And when they see an Āyāh (a sign, or an evidence) from Allāh, they mock at it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they say: lo! This) which Muhammad (pbuh) brought us (is mere magic) a manifest lie;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُوۤاْ إِن هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. And they say: “This is nothing but evident magic!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they say regarding it ‘This is nothing but manifest sorcery — and they say in denial of the Resurrection —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُوۤاْ إِن هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. And they say: “This is nothing but evident magic!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When we are dead and have become dust and) withered (bones, shall we then, forsooth, be raised (again)) shall we then be brought back to life after we die? Say to them, O Muhammad: indeed you shall.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. “When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we (then) verily be resurrected?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When we are dead and have become dust and bones shall we indeed be resurrected? In both places sc. a-idhā and a-innā either pronounce both hamzas or read without pronouncing the second one and inserting an alif between them in both cases.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. “When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we (then) verily be resurrected?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: They asked: (And our forefathers) shall they be raised again?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَ آبَآؤُنَا ٱلأَوَّلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. “And also our fathers of old?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And our forefathers too?’ read aw ābā’unā indicating a supplement; or read a-wa-ābā’unā as an interrogative effecting the supplement with the wāw; so that what is being supplemented is either the inna together with its subject sc. a-inna la-mab‘ūthūna or the subject of the verb la-mab‘ūthūna in which case the interrogative hamza is a separator.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَ آبَآؤُنَا ٱلأَوَّلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. “And also our fathers of old?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say (O Muhammad): Yea, in truth; and ye) and them (will be brought low) abased and humiliated.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ نَعَمْ وَأَنتُمْ دَاخِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Say (O Muḥammad ): “Yes, and you shall then be humiliated.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘Yes you will be resurrected and you will be utterly humiliated!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ نَعَمْ وَأَنتُمْ دَاخِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Say (O Muḥammad ): “Yes, and you shall then be humiliated.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There is but one Shout) it is but one single blow, which is the blowing of the Resurrection, (and lo!) they emerge from the graves and (they behold) what they will be commanded to do.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَإِذَا هُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. It will be a single Zajrah [shout (i.e. the second blowing of the Trumpet)], and behold, they will be staring!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: For it will be only innamā hiya this hiya is a demonstrative pronoun explained by the following zajratun a single cry and lo! they all creatures will be alive watching to see what will be done with them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَإِذَا هُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. It will be a single Zajrah [shout (i.e. the second blowing of the Trumpet)], and behold, they will be staring!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And say) when they come forth from their graves: (Ah, woe for us! This is the Day of Judgement) this is the Day of Reckoning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ يٰوَيْلَنَا هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. They will say: “Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they the disbelievers will say ‘O yā is for calling attention woe to us!’ O our destruction is here waylanā is a verbal noun without any regular verbal conjugation. And the angels will say to them ‘This is the Day of Retribution’ the Day of Reckoning and Requital.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ يٰوَيْلَنَا هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. They will say: “Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And the angels will say to them: (This is the Day of Separation) the Day of Judgement between you and the believers, (which ye used to deny) in the life of this world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. (It will be said): “This is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘This is the Day of Judgement between all creatures that you used to deny!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. (It will be said): “This is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah would then say to the angels: (Assemble those who did wrong) assemble those who associated partners with Allah, (together with their wives) with their friends and those who are of their calibre from among the jinn, humans and satans (and what they used to worship) of idols

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱحْشُرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. (It will be said to the angels): “Assemble those who did wrong, together with their companions (from the devils) and what they used to worship,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is then said to the angels ‘Gather those who did wrong to their own souls through idolatry together with their mates their associates from among the devils and what they used to worship

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱحْشُرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. (It will be said to the angels): “Assemble those who did wrong, together with their companions (from the devils) and what they used to worship,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Instead of Allah, and lead them to the path to hell) to the middle of hell;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. “Instead of Allāh, and lead them on to the way of flaming Fire (Hell);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: besides God in other words other than Him in the way of graven images and lead them direct them and drive them to the path of Hell the way to the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. “Instead of Allāh, and lead them on to the way of flaming Fire (Hell);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah would also say to the angels: (And stop them) detain them in hell, (for they must be questioned) about this claim; it is also said that this means: they will be questioned about their rejection of “there is no deity except Allah”.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَّسْئُولُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. “But stop them, verily they are to be questioned..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But first stop them detain them on the path for they must be questioned about all their sayings and deeds and it will be said to them in rebuke

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَّسْئُولُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. “But stop them, verily they are to be questioned..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (What aileth you that ye help not one another?) how is it that you do not save yourselves from Allah's chastisement, or help one another to avoid Allah's chastisement?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَنَاصَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. “What is the matter with you? Why do you not help one another (as you used to do in the world)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: “What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?” as was the case with you in this world. And it will be said to them

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَنَاصَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. “What is the matter with you? Why do you not help one another (as you used to do in the world)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but this day) which is the Day of Judgement (they make full submission) the worshipper and the worshipped submitted to Allah and knew that the Truth is with Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ هُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Nay, but that Day they shall surrender..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay but today they offer complete submission they are compliant abased.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ هُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Nay, but that Day they shall surrender..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And some of them draw near unto others) the humans go to the satans and the lowly among people go to the leaders, (mutually questioning) reproaching one another and arguing.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And they will turn to one another and question one another..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And some of them will turn to others questioning each other blaming one another and disputing.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And they will turn to one another and question one another..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They say) i.e. the humans say to the satans: (Lo! ye used to come unto us, imposing, (swearing that ye spoke the Truth)) and enticing us to reject Religion.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. They will say: “It was you who used to come to us from the right side [i.e. from the right side of one of us and beautify for us every evil, enjoin on us polytheism, and stop us from the truth i.e. Islāmic Monotheism and from every good deed].”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They that is the followers among them will say to those whom they followed ‘Indeed you used to approach us from the right’ in other words from that aspect in which we used to trust you for you used to swear that you followed the truth and so we believed you and we followed you — in other words ‘Indeed you have led us astray!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. They will say: “It was you who used to come to us from the right side [i.e. from the right side of one of us and beautify for us every evil, enjoin on us polytheism, and stop us from the truth i.e. Islāmic Monotheism and from every good deed].”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They answer) the satans would answer the humans: (Nay, but ye (yourselves) were not believers) in Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ بَلْ لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ مُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. They will reply: “Nay, you yourselves were not believers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They the ones who were followed say to them the followers ‘On the contrary! You were simply not believers for it would only be true that we led you astray if you had actually been believers in the first place and then rejected faith and followed us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ بَلْ لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ مُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. They will reply: “Nay, you yourselves were not believers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (We had no power over you) we had no reason or proof to win you over, (but ye were wayward folk) but you were disbelievers in Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ بَلْ كُنتُمْ قَوْماً طَاغِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. “And we had no authority over you. Nay! But you were Ṭāghūn (transgressing) people (polytheists, and disbelievers). *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And we did not have any warrant any sway or power over you to compel you to follow us. Nay but you yourselves were a rebellious folk astray like us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ بَلْ كُنتُمْ قَوْماً طَاغِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. “And we had no authority over you. Nay! But you were Ṭāghūn (transgressing) people (polytheists, and disbelievers). *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Now the Word of our Lord) that His chastisement and wrath will be enjoined upon us (hath been fulfilled concerning us. Lo! we are about to taste (the doom)) of the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. “So now the Word of our Lord has been justified against us, that we shall certainly (have to) taste (the torment)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So our Lord’s Words of chastisement — namely His Words ‘Verily I shall fill Hell with jinn and mankind together’ Q. 11119 — have become due against us both. Indeed we shall both taste the chastisement with these Words — which prompts them to say

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. “So now the Word of our Lord has been justified against us, that we shall certainly (have to) taste (the torment)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thus we misled you) from Religion. (Lo! we were (ourselves) astray) from Religion.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَغْوَيْنَاكُمْ إِنَّا كُنَّا غَاوِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. “So, we led you astray because we were ourselves astray.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So we led you astray — the reason for which is given by their saying — indeed we ourselves were astray’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَغْوَيْنَاكُمْ إِنَّا كُنَّا غَاوِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. “So, we led you astray because we were ourselves astray.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then lo! this day) which is the Day of Judgement (they (both) are sharers in the doom) the worshipper and those worshipped.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Then verily, that Day, they will (all) share in the torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: God exalted be He says So they on that day the Day of Resurrection will share in the chastisement for they shared in the error.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Then verily, that Day, they will (all) share in the torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! thus deal We with the guilty) thus We deal with the idolaters.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Certainly, that is how We deal with Al-Mujrimūn (poly the ists, sinners, disbelievers, criminals, the disobedient to Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed so in the same way that We deal with these We deal with sinners other than these in other words We chastise both of them the followers and those who were followed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Certainly, that is how We deal with Al-Mujrimūn (poly the ists, sinners, disbelievers, criminals, the disobedient to Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (For when it was said unto them) in the life of the world, say: (There is no god save Allah, they were scornful) they were too proud to say it

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوۤاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. Truly, when it was said to them: Lā ilāha illallāh “(none has the right to be worshipped but Allāh),” they puffed themselves up with pride(1) (i.e. denied it)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: For truly it was they who in other words it was these sinners who — given the context that follows — when it was said to them ‘There is no god except God’ used to be scornful

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوۤاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. Truly, when it was said to them: Lā ilāha illallāh “(none has the right to be worshipped but Allāh),” they puffed themselves up with pride(1) (i.e. denied it)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And said: Shall we forsake our gods) shall we leave the worship of our gods (for a mad poet) who invents lies? Meaning the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَتَارِكُوۤاْ آلِهَتِنَا لِشَاعِرٍ مَّجْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And (they) said: “Are we going to abandon our ālihah (gods) for the sake of a mad poet?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and would say ‘Are we to abandon our gods for a mad poet?’ that is for the sake of what Muhammad (s) says? as regards the hamzas in a-innā ‘are we’ the same applies as mentioned above.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَتَارِكُوۤاْ آلِهَتِنَا لِشَاعِرٍ مَّجْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And (they) said: “Are we going to abandon our ālihah (gods) for the sake of a mad poet?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but he) Muhammad (pbuh) (brought the Truth) he brought the Qur'an and the profession of Allah's divine Oneness, (and he confirmed those sent (before him)) and he brought a confirmation of the messengers who were sent before him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ جَآءَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَصَدَّقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. Nay! he (Muḥammad ) has come with the truth (i.e. Allāh’s religion — Islāmic Monotheism and this Qur’ān) and he confirms the Messengers (before him who brought Allāh’s religion — Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: God exalted be He says Nay but he has brought them the truth and confirmed the earlier messengers namely those who had also brought this truth which is that there is no god except God.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ جَآءَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَصَدَّقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. Nay! he (Muḥammad ) has come with the truth (i.e. Allāh’s religion — Islāmic Monotheism and this Qur’ān) and he confirms the Messengers (before him who brought Allāh’s religion — Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! (now) verily ye) O people of Mecca (taste the painful doom) in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّكُمْ لَذَآئِقُو ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَلِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. Verily, you (pagans of Makkah) are going to taste the painful torment;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘You shall certainly there is a shift from the third person address to the second here taste the painful chastisement

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّكُمْ لَذَآئِقُو ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلأَلِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. Verily, you (pagans of Makkah) are going to taste the painful torment;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ye are requited) in the Hereafter (naught save what ye did) in the life of the world in your state of idolatry and disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلاَّ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. And you will be requited nothing, except for what you used to do (evil deeds, sins, and Allāh’s disobedience which you used to do in this world) (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and you will only be requited the requital for what you used to do’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلاَّ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. And you will be requited nothing, except for what you used to do (evil deeds, sins, and Allāh’s disobedience which you used to do in this world) (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save single minded slaves of Allah) who are protected from disbelief and idolatry; it is also said that its meaning is: save those who are chosen for worship and for the profession of Allah's divine Oneness;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. Except the chosen slaves of Allāh (i.e. the true believers of Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Except for God’s sincere servants namely the believers the exception clause here is a discontinuous one

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. Except the chosen slaves of Allāh (i.e. the true believers of Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (For them there is a known provision) in measure for the morning and evening of the life of this world, except that over there there is no morning or evening.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أُوْلَئِكَ لَهُمْ رِزْقٌ مَّعْلُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. For them, there will be a known provision (in Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: whose requital is mentioned in His saying For them there will be in Paradise a distinct provision morning and evening —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أُوْلَئِكَ لَهُمْ رِزْقٌ مَّعْلُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. For them, there will be a known provision (in Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Fruits) they have different kinds of fruit. (And they will be honoured) with gifts

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَوَاكِهُ وَهُم مُّكْرَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. Fruits; and they shall be honoured,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: fruits fawākihu either substitutes for rizqun or is an explication thereof here these fruits represent what is eaten for delight and not for the sake of preserving one’s health as in this world for the inhabitants of Paradise are in no need of preserving it given that their bodies will be created to be everlasting — and they will be honoured with God’s reward glory be to Him exalted be He

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَوَاكِهُ وَهُم مُّكْرَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. Fruits; and they shall be honoured,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (In the Gardens of Delight) whose delight is endless,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي جَنَّاتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. In the Gardens of delight (Paradise),.

tafsir: in the Gardens of Bliss

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي جَنَّاتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. In the Gardens of delight (Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (On couches facing one another) upon visitation

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. Facing one another on thrones..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: reclining upon couches facing one another so that they do not see the back of one another;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. Facing one another on thrones..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (A cup) of wine (from a gushing spring) of pure wine (is brought round for them) as service,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِكَأْسٍ مِّن مَّعِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. Round them will be passed a cup of pure wine —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: they are served from all round each one of them is so served with a cup ka’san this denotes the vessel with the drink in it from a spring of wine that flows along the ground like streams of water

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِكَأْسٍ مِّن مَّعِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. Round them will be passed a cup of pure wine —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (White, delicious to the drinkers,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَيْضَآءَ لَذَّةٍ لِّلشَّارِبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. White, delicious to the drinkers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: white whiter than milk delicious to the drinkers in contrast to the wine of this world which is distasteful to drink

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَيْضَآءَ لَذَّةٍ لِّلشَّارِبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. White, delicious to the drinkers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Wherein) in drinking this wine (there is no headache) stomach-ache, drunkenness, harm or sinning (nor are they made mad thereby) because of intoxication; it is also said that this means: they never run out of it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. Neither will they have Ghoul (any kind of hurt, abdominal pain, headache, a sin) from that, nor will they suffer intoxication therefrom..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: wherein there is neither madness nothing to snatch away their minds nor will they be spent by it read yunzafūna or yunzifūna from 1st form nazafa or 4th form anzafa said of one drinking in other words they are not inebriated by it in contrast to the wine of this world

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. Neither will they have Ghoul (any kind of hurt, abdominal pain, headache, a sin) from that, nor will they suffer intoxication therefrom..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And with them) in Paradise (are those of modest gaze) wives who lower their gaze, content with their husbands and wish no man instead of their husband, (with lovely eyes) and beautiful faces,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ عِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And beside them will be Qāṣirāt-aṭ-Ṭarf [chaste females (wives), restraining their glances (desiring none except their husbands)], with wide and beautiful eyes (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and with them will be maidens of restrained glances who reserved their glances exclusively for their spouses and do not look upon any other — because of the beauty they the maidens see in them — with beautiful eyes ‘īn means with large and beautiful eyes

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ عِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And beside them will be Qāṣirāt-aṭ-Ṭarf [chaste females (wives), restraining their glances (desiring none except their husbands)], with wide and beautiful eyes (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (As they were hidden eggs) in their purity, in both heat and cold.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَّكْنُونٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. (Delicate and pure) as if they were (hidden) eggs (well) preserved..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: as if they were in terms of the starkness of their white colour hidden eggs of ostriches sheltered by their feathers from dust the colour being that whiteness with a hint of pallor which is the most beautiful of female complexions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَّكْنُونٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. (Delicate and pure) as if they were (hidden) eggs (well) preserved..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning) conversing with one another.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. Then they will turn to one another, mutually questioning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Some of them some of the inhabitants of Paradise will turn to others questioning each other regarding what they experienced in the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. Then they will turn to one another, mutually questioning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (A speaker of them saith) one of the inhabitants of Paradise, Yehuda the believer, says: (Lo! I had a comrade) whose name was Abu Qutrus, who was actually his brother.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي قَرِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. A speaker of them will say: “Verily, I had a companion (in the world),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: One of them will say ‘Indeed I had a comrade a companion who used to reject the idea of resurrection

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي قَرِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. A speaker of them will say: “Verily, I had a companion (in the world),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who used to say: Art thou in truth of those who put faith (in his words)) do you really believe those messengers?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَقُولُ أَءِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصَدِّقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. Who used to say: “Are you among those who believe (in resurrection after death). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: who used to say to me in reproach “Are you really among those who affirm as truth the Resurrection and

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَقُولُ أَءِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصَدِّقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. Who used to say: “Are you among those who believe (in resurrection after death). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Can we, when we are dead and have become mere dust and) rotten (bones, can we (then) verily be brought to book) because he denied resurrection after death?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. “(That) when we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed (be raised up) to receive reward or punishment (according to our deeds)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that when we are dead and have become dust and bones we shall actually be called to account?” ’ that we shall be requited and reckoned with — he rejects the truth of this as well as regards all three instances of the hamzas sc. a-innaka a-idhā and a-innā what has been mentioned above applies.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. “(That) when we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed (be raised up) to receive reward or punishment (according to our deeds)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He saith) to his brothers in Paradise: (Will ye look) in the Fire that haply you may find out about his state?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ هَلْ أَنتُمْ مُّطَّلِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. (The speaker) said: “Will you look down?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He the one speaking says to his brethren in Paradise ‘Will you have a look?’ together with me into the Fire to see his condition — but they will say ‘No’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ هَلْ أَنتُمْ مُّطَّلِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. (The speaker) said: “Will you look down?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then looketh he and seeth him) and sees his disbelieving brother (in the depth of hell) in the middle of hell.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ فِي سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. So, he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Fire..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then he that speaker will take a look through one of the apertures in Paradise and he will catch sight of him that is he will see his comrade in the centre of Hell in the middle of the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ فِي سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. So, he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Fire..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He saith: By Allah, thou verily didst all but cause my ruin) you almost led me away from Religion and you would have certainly destroyed me if I obeyed you,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرْدِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. He said: “By Allāh! You have nearly ruined me..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He will say to him acknowledging that he the latter deserves his fate ‘By God! You very nearly destroyed me you almost ruined me through your misguidance in this has been softened from the hardened form inna.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرْدِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. He said: “By Allāh! You have nearly ruined me..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And had it not been for the favour of my Lord) Who bestowed faith upon me and protected me from disbelief, (I too had been of those haled forth (to doom)) I too would be tormented with you in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَوْلاَ نِعْمَةُ رَبِّي لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. “Had it not been for the Grace of my Lord, I would certainly have been among those brought forth (to Hell).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And had it not been for the favour of my Lord His grace to me in giving me faith I too would have been of those arraigned’ with you in the Fire. The inhabitants of Paradise will say

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَوْلاَ نِعْمَةُ رَبِّي لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. “Had it not been for the Grace of my Lord, I would certainly have been among those brought forth (to Hell).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then he heard a crier saying: " O people of Paradise death is slain and from now on there is no death ". Upon which he will say to his brothers: (Are we then not to die) after the slaying of death

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. (The dwellers of Paradise will say) “Are we then not to die (any more)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Do we then not die anymore

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. (The dwellers of Paradise will say) “Are we then not to die (any more)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Saving our former death) after our death in the life of the world. They would say to him: “Yes, indeed!” Thereupon he will hear a crier crying: “O people of hell! The fire is now closed; none will enter it or leave it”, and he will say to his brothers: (and are we not to be punished) after the Fire is closed? And their answer will be in the affirmative.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. Except our first death, and we shall not be punished? (after we have entered Paradise).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: aside from our first death that is the one which we suffered in this world and are we not to be chastised?’ — this interrogative statement is one made out of sheer delight and in order to speak at length of the graces of God exalted be He in His granting of everlasting life and refraining from inflicting any punishment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. Except our first death, and we shall not be punished? (after we have entered Paradise).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! this is the Supreme Triumph) this is the ultimate safety; we gained Paradise and all that which is in it and were saved from hell and all that which is in it. The story of these two brothers is the same story of the two brothers mentioned in surah al-Kahf, one of whom was a believer, this is Yehuda, and the other an unbeliever, Abu Qutrus.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. Truly, this is the supreme success!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly this that has mentioned as being the reward for the inhabitants of Paradise is indeed the mighty success.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. Truly, this is the supreme success!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then Allah will say to him: (For the like of this, then) eternity in Paradise and its bliss, (let the workers work) let those who hasten to do righteous works hasten to do them; it is also said that this means: for the like of this let those who compete to spend in the way of Allah spend their wealth; and it is also said that this means: for the like of this let those who strive in seeking knowledge and worship strive.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ ٱلْعَامِلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. For the like of this, let the workers work..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: For the like of this let all the workers work — it is said that this is said to them or it is what they say themselves.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِمِثْلِ هَـٰذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ ٱلْعَامِلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. For the like of this, let the workers work..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Is this) which I have mentioned for the inhabitants of Paradise of food and drink (better as a welcome) better as food, drink and reward for the believers, (or the tree of Zaqqum) for Abu Jahl and his host?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُّزُلاً أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. Is that (Paradise) better entertainment or the tree of Zaqqūm (a horrible tree in Hell)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Is that which is mentioned to them a better hospitality nuzul denotes what is prepared for one who is being received as a guest and so forth or the Zaqqūm tree that is prepared for the inhabitants of the Fire — it is the vilest and most bitter tree of the Tihāma region which God causes to grow in the Fire as will be stated shortly.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُّزُلاً أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. Is that (Paradise) better entertainment or the tree of Zaqqūm (a horrible tree in Hell)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We have appointed it) We mentioned it as (a torment) a trial (for wrong-doers) Abu Jahl and his host, for they said: the Zaqqum is nothing but dates and butter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهَا فِتْنَةً لِّلظَّالِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. Truly, We have made it (as) a trial for the Ẓālimūn (poly theists, disbelievers, wrong-doers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We have indeed made it for that reason sc. its being a tree in the Fire a trial for the wrongdoers? namely for the disbelievers of Mecca for they said ‘Fire consumes trees so how can it make them grow forth?’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهَا فِتْنَةً لِّلظَّالِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. Truly, We have made it (as) a trial for the Ẓālimūn (poly theists, disbelievers, wrong-doers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! it is a tree that springeth) grows (in the heart of hell) in the middle of hell.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِيۤ أَصْلِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. Verily, it is a tree that springs out of the bottom of Hell‑fire,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed it is a tree that comes forth from the very source of Hell in other words from the depths of Hell with its branches extending up through all its different levels.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِيۤ أَصْلِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. Verily, it is a tree that springs out of the bottom of Hell‑fire,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Its crop) its fruit (is as it were the heads of devils) the heads of snakes which resemble devils. This kind of snakes is found near Yemen.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. The shoots of its fruit-stalks are like the heads of Shayāṭīn (devils);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Its spathes likened to the spathes of a date-palm are like the heads of devils as vile-looking snakes.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. The shoots of its fruit-stalks are like the heads of Shayāṭīn (devils);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! They) i.e. the people of Mecca as well as all the disbelievers (verily must eat thereof) of the tree of Zaqqum, (and fill (their) bellies therewith) and fill their bellies of it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّهُمْ لآكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. Truly, they will eat thereof and fill their bellies therewith..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed they the disbelievers will eat of it despite its vileness because of the severity of their hunger and will fill their bellies from it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّهُمْ لآكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. Truly, they will eat thereof and fill their bellies therewith..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And afterward, lo! thereupon they have a drink of boiling water) to go with the Zaqqum.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْباً مِنْ حَمِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. Then, on the top of that, they will be given boiling water to drink, so that it becomes a mixture (of boiling water and Zaqqūm in their bellies)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then lo! on top of it they will have a brew of boiling water which they drink and which mixes with what they have eaten and becomes a brew thereof.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْباً مِنْ حَمِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. Then, on the top of that, they will be given boiling water to drink, so that it becomes a mixture (of boiling water and Zaqqūm in their bellies)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And afterward, lo! their return) their destination (is surely unto hell) the middle of hell.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لإِلَى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. Then, thereafter, verily, their return is to the flaming fire of Hell..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then indeed their return shall be to Hell-fire — this suggests that they exit from it only to drink the boiling water which is located outside it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لإِلَى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. Then, thereafter, verily, their return is to the flaming fire of Hell..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They indeed found their fathers) in the life of this world (astray) from the Truth and guidance,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْاْ آبَآءَهُمْ ضَآلِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. Verily, they found their fathers on the wrong path;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lo! they found their fathers to be astray

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْاْ آبَآءَهُمْ ضَآلِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. Verily, they found their fathers on the wrong path;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But they make haste (to follow) in their footsteps) they hasten to follow their religion, and do as they did.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. So, they (too) hastened in their footsteps!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and so they are also now hurrying in their footsteps they shall be prodded to follow them and they end up hurrying towards it Hell-fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. So, they (too) hastened in their footsteps!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily most of the men of old) of past generations, (went astray before them) before your folk, O Muhammad.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ أَكْثَرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. And indeed most of the men of old went astray before them;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily most of the ancients of past communities went astray before them

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ أَكْثَرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. And indeed most of the men of old went astray before them;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We sent among them warners) but they disbelieved in them and, as a result, We destroyed them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِمْ مُّنذِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. And indeed We sent among them warners (Messengers);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and We certainly had sent among them warners in the way of messengers to threaten them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِمْ مُّنذِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. And indeed We sent among them warners (Messengers);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then see) O Muhammad (the nature of the consequence for) the requital of (those warned) of those who were warned by the messenger, but chose to disbelieve, how we destroyed them,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. Then, see what was the end of those who were warned (but heeded not)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So behold how was the consequence for them who were warned namely the disbelievers in other words the sequel for them was that they ended up in the chastisement;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. Then, see what was the end of those who were warned (but heeded not)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then made an exception, saying: (Save singled minded slaves of Allah) who are protected from disbelief and idolatry; and it is said that this means according to a variant reading: except those chosen for worship and the profession of Allah's divine Oneness. The latter did not disbelieve and therefore We did not destroy them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. Except the chosen slaves of Allāh (faithful, obedient, and true believers of Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: all except God’s sincere servants namely the believers who are saved from chastisement because they were sincere in their worship mukhlisīna; or if one reads mukhlasīna because God has made them sincerely devoted to such worship.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. Except the chosen slaves of Allāh (faithful, obedient, and true believers of Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Noah verily prayed unto Us) Noah prayed against his folk, saying: (My Lord! Leave not one of the disbelievers in the land…) [Noah, 71: 26-27], (and gracious was the Hearer of his prayer) by destroying his folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ نَادَانَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. And indeed Nūḥ (Noah) invoked Us, and We are the Best of those who answer (the request)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily Noah called to Us when he said ‘My Lord I have been overcome so help me Q. 5410 and how excellent were the Hearers of the prayer for him were We in other words he invoked Us against his people so We destroyed them by drowning them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ نَادَانَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. And indeed Nūḥ (Noah) invoked Us, and We are the Best of those who answer (the request)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We saved him and his household) and all those who believed in him (from the great distress) i.e. drowning,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. And We rescued him and his family from the great distress (i.e. drowning),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We delivered him and his family from the great distress which was the drowning

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. And We rescued him and his family from the great distress (i.e. drowning),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And made his seed the survivors) until the Day of Judgement. Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Yapheth. Shem is the father of the Arabs and those people surrounding them; Ham is the father the Abyssinians, Berbers and inhabitants of Sind; and Yapheth is the father of the rest of people,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. And, his progeny, them We made the survivors (i.e. Shem, Ham and Japheth)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and made his descendants the survivors thus all human beings are descended from him peace be upon him. He had three sons Shem Sām the ancestor of the Arabs the Persians and the Byzantines; Ham Hām the ancestor of the Negroes; and Japheth Yāfith the ancestor of the Turks the Khazar and the peoples of Gog and Magog and the inhabitants of such regions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. And, his progeny, them We made the survivors (i.e. Shem, Ham and Japheth)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And left for him) for Noah good praise (among the later folk) who remained after him:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلآخِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. And left for him (a goodly remembrance) among the later generations:.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We left We preserved for him fair praise among posterity among the prophets and communities after him until the Day of Resurrection which is

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلآخِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. And left for him (a goodly remembrance) among the later generations:.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Peace be unto Noah) safety and happiness from Us unto Noah (among the peoples) of his time!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. “Salām (peace) be upon Nūḥ (Noah) (from Us) among the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Peace from Us be to Noah among the worlds!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. “Salām (peace) be upon Nūḥ (Noah) (from Us) among the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! thus do We reward the good) in words and works by bestowing upon them good praise and safety.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. Verily, thus We reward the Muḥsinūn (good-doers)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thus indeed in the way that We requited them We requite the virtuous.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. Verily, thus We reward the Muḥsinūn (good-doers)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Verily, he [Nūḥ (Noah)] was one of Our believing slaves..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He was indeed one of Our faithful servants.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Verily, he [Nūḥ (Noah)] was one of Our believing slaves..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then We did drown the others) those who remained after him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلآخَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. Then We drowned the others (disbelievers and polytheists)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then We did drown the others the disbelievers from among his folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلآخَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. Then We drowned the others (disbelievers and polytheists)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! of his persuasion) of Noah's persuasion; and it is also said this means: of Muhammad's persuasion (verily was Abraham) He says: Abraham followed the religion and way of Noah and Muhammad (pbuh) followed Abraham's religion and way.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِ لإِبْرَاهِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. And, verily, among those who followed his [Nūḥ’s (Noah)] way (Islāmic Monotheism) was Ibrāhīm (Abraham)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And truly of his adherents that is of those who agreed with him on the fundaments of religion was Abraham despite the fact that there was a long interval between them 2640 years and between them came the prophets Hūd and Sālih.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِ لإِبْرَاهِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. And, verily, among those who followed his [Nūḥ’s (Noah)] way (Islāmic Monotheism) was Ibrāhīm (Abraham)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When he came unto his Lord) He says: when Abraham betook himself to worshipping his Lord (with a whole heart) with a heart free from any blemish;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ جَآءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 84. When he came to his Lord with a pure heart [attached to Allāh Alone and none else, worshipping none but Allāh Alone — true Islāmic Monotheism, pure from the filth of polytheism]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When he came to his Lord in other words he continued to follow Him upon coming to Him with a heart that was pure of any doubt or the like

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ جَآءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 84. When he came to his Lord with a pure heart [attached to Allāh Alone and none else, worshipping none but Allāh Alone — true Islāmic Monotheism, pure from the filth of polytheism]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When he said unto his father) Azar (and his folk) the idol worshippers: (What is it that you worship) beside Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 85. When he said to his father and to his people: “What is it that which you worship?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: when he said while still in this continuous state of his to his father and his folk in reproach ‘What do — what is it that — you worship?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 85. When he said to his father and to his people: “What is it that which you worship?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: They replied: " we worship idols " , to which Abraham said: (Is it a falsehood gods beside Allah that ye desire) do you then worship false deities?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَإِفْكاً آلِهَةً دُونَ ٱللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 86. “Is it a falsehood — ālihah (gods) other than Allāh — that you desire?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Is it a calumny a-ifkan as regards the two hamzas the same applies as mentioned before — gods other than God — that you desire? ifkan is an object denoting reason; ālihatan is the direct object of turīdūna ‘you desire’; ifk denotes the worst kind of lie. In other words do you worship any other than God?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَإِفْكاً آلِهَةً دُونَ ٱللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 86. “Is it a falsehood — ālihah (gods) other than Allāh — that you desire?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (What then is your opinion of the Lord of the Worlds) what do you think He will do to you if you worship other than Him?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَا ظَنُّكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. “Then what think you about the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn, and all that exists)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: What then is your supposition regarding the Lord of the Worlds?’ having worshipped other than Him do you think that He will leave you without punishment? No! They were a people of astrologers. On one occasion they went out to celebrate a festival of theirs and left their food behind with their idols claiming that they were securing thereby blessings for it and that they would eat it upon their return. They had said to the lord Abraham ‘Come out with us’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَا ظَنُّكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. “Then what think you about the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn, and all that exists)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he glanced a glance at the stars) it is also said that this means: he reflected for a while,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةً فِي ٱلنُّجُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 88. Then, he cast a glance at the stars,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās
