meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. We made his kingdom strong and gave him Al-Ḥikmah (Prophethood) and sound judge ment in speech and decision..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee?) Then came to you the story of the opponents of David. (How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And has the news of the litigants reached you? When they climbed over the wall into (his) Miḥrāb (a praying place or a private room);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And has there come to you O Muhammad (s) the purpose of the interrogative indicated by hal here is to provoke curiosity and a desire to listen to what will follow the tale of the disputants when they scaled the sanctuary? David’s sanctuary that is his place of prayer for they had been prohibited from entering by the front gates because of his being engaged in worship in other words has it come to you their tale and their account?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And has the news of the litigants reached you? When they climbed over the wall into (his) Miḥrāb (a praying place or a private room);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: How they burst in upon David, and he) David (was afraid of them. They) i.e. the two angels who entered in on David (said: Be not afraid (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefore judge aright) justly (between us; be not unjust) do not be partial and transgress not; (and show us the fair way) show us what is right.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُودَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُواْ لاَ تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَٱحْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلاَ تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. When they entered in upon Dāwūd (David), he was terrified of them. They said: “Fear not! (We are) two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, therefore judge between us with truth, and treat us not with injustice, and guide us to the Right Way. *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When they entered upon David and he was frightened by them. And they said ‘Do not fear; we are two disputants some say that this means ‘two groups’ in order to agree with the plural person of the verb dakhalū ‘they entered’; others say ‘two individuals’ with the plural person actually denoting these two; al-khasm may refer to a one or more individuals. These two were angels who had come in the form of two disputants between whom there was supposed to have occurred the situation mentioned — but only hypothetically — in order to alert David peace be upon him to what he had done he had ninety nine women but desired the woman of a man who had only her and no other. He David had married her and consummated the marriage. One of us has infringed upon the rights of the other so judge justly between us and do not transgress do not be unjust and guide us direct us to the right path’ the correct way.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُودَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُواْ لاَ تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَٱحْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلاَ تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. When they entered in upon Dāwūd (David), he was terrified of them. They said: “Fear not! (We are) two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, therefore judge between us with truth, and treat us not with injustice, and guide us to the Right Way. *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes) meaning 99 wives (while I had one ewe) i.e. one wife; (and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech) this is a similitude which they struck for David in order for him to understand what he did to Uriah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ هَذَآ أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِي نَعْجَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلْخِطَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Verily, this my brother (in religion) has ninety-nine ewes, while I have (only) one ewe, and he says: “Hand it over to me, and he overpowered me in speech.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Behold this brother of mine in other words my fellow co-religionist has ninety-nine ewes — here used to represent the women — while I have a single ewe; yet he said “Entrust it to me” in other words make me in charge of it and he overcame me in speech’ in other words in the argument; so the latter conceded charge of it to him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ هَذَآ أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِي نَعْجَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلْخِطَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Verily, this my brother (in religion) has ninety-nine ewes, while I have (only) one ewe, and he says: “Hand it over to me, and he overpowered me in speech.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe) in taking your ewe (in addition to his ewes) even though he has many ewes, (and lo! many partners) and brothers (oppress one another) transgress against one another, (save such as believe) in Allah (and do good works) between them and their Lord, (and they are few) those who do not transgress. And the two went out from whence they came. (And David guessed) he knew and was certain (that We had tried him) because of the sin he committed, (and he sought forgiveness of his Lord) from his sin, (and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented) feeling remorse for what he did.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِ وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِيۤ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُودُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّاهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعاً وَأَنَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. [Dāwūd (David)] said (immediately without listening to the opponent): “He has wronged you in demanding your ewe in addition to his ewes. And, verily, many partners oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous good deeds, and they are few.” And Dāwūd (David) guessed that We have tried him and he sought Forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down prostrate and turned (to Allāh) in repentance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘He has certainly wronged you by asking for your ewe that he may add it to his sheep. And indeed many associates infringe upon the rights of one another except such as believe and perform righteous deeds but few are they!’ mā emphasises the ‘fewness’. As the two angels were ascending to the heaven one said to the other ‘He has certainly passed judgement on himself!’ David was thus alerted to his deed. God exalted be He says And David thought in other words he became certain that We had indeed tried him that We had caused him to fall into a trial that is a test through his love for that woman. So he sought forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing in other words prostrate and repented.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِ وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِيۤ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُودُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّاهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعاً وَأَنَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. [Dāwūd (David)] said (immediately without listening to the opponent): “He has wronged you in demanding your ewe in addition to his ewes. And, verily, many partners oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous good deeds, and they are few.” And Dāwūd (David) guessed that We have tried him and he sought Forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down prostrate and turned (to Allāh) in repentance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So We forgave him that) sin; (and lo! he had access to Our presence) he is close in rank (and a happy journey's end) in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. So, We forgave him that, and verily, for him is near access to Us, and a good place of (final) return (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So We forgave him that and indeed he has a station of nearness with Us that is even more good things in this world and a fair return in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. So, We forgave him that, and verily, for him is near access to Us, and a good place of (final) return (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a vicegerent in the earth) We appointed you a prophet king for the Children of Israel; (therefore judge aright between mankind) judge justly between people, (and follow not desire) that as you did regarding Bathseba, the wife of Uriah, who was also David's cousin (that it beguile thee from the way of Allah) from the obedience of Allah. (Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah) from the obedience of Allah (have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning) because they forsake working for the Day of Reckoning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يٰدَاوُودُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَٱحْكُمْ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلاَ تَتَّبِعِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدُ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. O Dāwūd (David)! Verily, We have placed you as a successor on the earth; so judge you between men in truth (and justice) and follow not your desire — for it will mislead you from the Path of Allāh. Verily, those who wander astray from the Path of Allāh (shall) have a severe torment, because they forgot the Day of Reckoning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘O David! We have indeed made you a vicegerent on the earth managing the affairs of people; so judge justly between people and do not follow desire that is the desires of the soul that it then lead you astray from the way of God that is to say from the proofs that indicate the truth of His Oneness. Truly those who go astray from the way of God in other words from belief in God — for them there will be a severe chastisement because of their forgetting the Day of Reckoning’ as a result of their having neglected faith. For had they been certain of the truth of the Day of Reckoning they would have first been believers in this world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يٰدَاوُودُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَٱحْكُمْ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلاَ تَتَّبِعِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدُ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. O Dāwūd (David)! Verily, We have placed you as a successor on the earth; so judge you between men in truth (and justice) and follow not your desire — for it will mislead you from the Path of Allāh. Verily, those who wander astray from the Path of Allāh (shall) have a severe torment, because they forgot the Day of Reckoning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them) of created beings and marvels (in vain) for nothing, without ordaining commands and prohibitions. (That is the opinion of those who disbelieve) that is the denial of those who disbelieve in resurrection after death. (And woe) severe chastisement is (unto those who disbelieve) in resurrection after death, (from the Fire) in the Fire!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَاطِلاً ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them without purpose! That is the consideration of those who disbelieve! Then woe to those who disbelieve (in Islāmic Monotheism) from the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in vain frivolously. That namely the creation of what has been mentioned as being for no particular purpose is the supposition of those who disbelieve from among the people of Mecca. So woe — a valley in hell-fire — to the disbelievers from the Fire!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَاطِلاً ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them without purpose! That is the consideration of those who disbelieve! Then woe to those who disbelieve (in Islāmic Monotheism) from the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Shall We treat those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and in the Qur'an (and do good works) and perform acts of obedience between themselves and their Lord; the reference here is to 'Ali Ibn Abi Talib, Hamzah Ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and 'Ubaydah Ibn al-Harth (as those who spread corruption) as the idolaters (in the earth) i.e. 'Utbah and Shaybah the sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid Ibn 'Utbah; (or shall We treat the Pious) who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecent acts, i.e. 'Ali and his two fellow believers (as the wicked) as the disbelievers: 'Utbah and Shaybah the sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid Ibn 'Utbah? Each one of these three had, on the Day of Badr, a dual with 'Ali, Hamzah and 'Ubaydah, respectively; 'Ali killed al-Walid Ibn 'Utbah, Hamzah killed 'Utbah Ibn Rabi'ah and 'Ubaydah killed Shaybah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ كَٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلْفُجَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Shall We treat those who believe (in the Oneness of Allāh — Islāmic Monotheism) and do righteous good deeds as the Mufsidūn (those who associate partners in worship with Allāh and commit crimes) on earth? Or shall We treat the Muttaqūn (the pious — See V.2:2) as the Fujjār (criminals, disbelievers, the wicked)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or shall We treat those who believe and perform righteous deeds like those who cause corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the God-fearing like the profligate? This was revealed when the Meccan disbelievers said to the believers ‘In the Hereafter we will receive the same reward as that which you will receive’ am ‘or’ contains the rhetorical hamza of denial.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ كَٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلْفُجَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Shall We treat those who believe (in the Oneness of Allāh — Islāmic Monotheism) and do righteous good deeds as the Mufsidūn (those who associate partners in worship with Allāh and commit crimes) on earth? Or shall We treat the Muttaqūn (the pious — See V.2:2) as the Fujjār (criminals, disbelievers, the wicked)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto you) We have sent with Gabriel to you, (full of blessing) wherein there is forgiveness and mercy for those who believe in it, (that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding) and that those possessed of intellects among people (may reflect) take heed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوۤاْ آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. (This is) a Book (the Qur’ān) which We have sent down to you, full of blessings, that they may ponder over its Verses, and that men of understanding may remember..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: A Book kitābun the predicate of a missing subject namely hādhā ‘this is’ that We have revealed to you full of blessing that they may contemplate yaddabbarū is actually yatadabbarū but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dāl its signs that they may reflect upon its meanings and become believers and that they may remember that they may be admonished — those people of pith those possessors of intellect.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوۤاْ آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. (This is) a Book (the Qur’ān) which We have sent down to you, full of blessings, that they may ponder over its Verses, and that men of understanding may remember..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We bestowed on David, Solomon. How excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (towards Allah)) he is ever betaking himself to Allah and engaged in His obedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُودَ سُلَيْمَانَ نِعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. And to Dāwūd (David) We gave Sulaimān (Solomon). How excellent a slave! Verily, he was ever oft-returning in repentance (to Us)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We bestowed on David Solomon his son — what an excellent servant! that is Solomon. Truly he was a penitent soul always returning to God with glorification and remembrance at all times.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُودَ سُلَيْمَانَ نِعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. And to Dāwūd (David) We gave Sulaimān (Solomon). How excellent a slave! Verily, he was ever oft-returning in repentance (to Us)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When there were shown to him at eventide) after the Zuhr (light footed coursers) pure, Arab horses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِٱلْعَشِيِّ ٱلصَّافِنَاتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, well trained horses of the highest breed [for Jihād (holy fighting in Allāh’s Cause)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When one evening — which is the period after midday — there were displayed before him the prancing steeds al-sāfināt ‘horses’ is the plural of sāfina which denotes a horse standing on three legs with the fourth supported on the edge of the hoof and derives from the verb safana yasfinu sufūnan; al-jiyād is the plural of jawād which is a ‘racer’; the meaning is that these horses are such that when they are halted they stand still and when they run they surpass others in speed. One thousand horses were displayed before him after he had performed the midday prayer for he had wanted to use them in a holy struggle jihād against an enemy. But when the display reached the nine-hundredth horse the sun set and he had not performed the afternoon prayer. So he was greatly distressed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِٱلْعَشِيِّ ٱلصَّافِنَاتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, well trained horses of the highest breed [for Jihād (holy fighting in Allāh’s Cause)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he said: Lo! I have preferred the good things (of the world)) I have preferred the wealth of this world (to the remembrance of my Lord) to the obedience of my Lord; (till they were taken out of sight behind the curtain) until the sun disappeared behind the mountain of Qaf.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَالَ إِنِّيۤ أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. He said: “I did love the good (these horses) instead of remembering my Lord (in my ‘Aṣr prayer)” till the time was over, and (the sun) had hidden in the veil (of night)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Lo! I have loved I have desired the love of worldly good things that is of horses over the remembrance of my Lord’ that is over the afternoon prayer until it that is the sun disappeared behind the night’s veil until it was concealed by that which veils it from sight.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَالَ إِنِّيۤ أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. He said: “I did love the good (these horses) instead of remembering my Lord (in my ‘Aṣr prayer)” till the time was over, and (the sun) had hidden in the veil (of night)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Then he said): Bring them back to me) bring back whatever was shown to me, (and fell to slashing (with his sword their) legs and necks) it is also said that he began slashing their necks and legs until the sun disappeared and he missed the 'Asr prayer; this is why he did what he did.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلأَعْنَاقِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Then he said “Bring them (horses) back to me.” Then he began to pass his hand over their legs and their necks (till the end of the display)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Bring them back to me! that is the horses that were displayed; and they so brought them back. Then he set about slashing with his sword their legs al-sūq is the plural of sāq and necks in other words he slaughtered them and cut off their legs as an offering of atonement to God exalted be He for having been distracted by them from the prayer. He gave all the meat thereof as voluntary alms and so God compensated him what was better and faster that these horses and this was the wind which blew at his command as he wished.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلأَعْنَاقِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Then he said “Bring them (horses) back to me.” Then he began to pass his hand over their legs and their necks (till the end of the display)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We tried Solomon) by the loss of his kingdom for 40 days, the number of days in which the idols were worshipped in his house, (and set upon his throne a (mere) body) a devil. (Then did he repent) then did he return to his kingdom and to the obedience of his Lord and repented from his sin.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. And indeed, We did try Sulaimān (Solomon) and We placed on his throne Jasad (a devil, so he lost his kingdom for a while) and he did return (to Allāh with obedience and.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We certainly tried Solomon We tested him by wresting his kingdom from him because he had married a woman solely out of his desire for her. She used to worship idols in his own home without his knowledge. Now control of his kingdom lay in his ring. On one occasion needing to withdraw to relieve himself he took it off and left it with this woman of his whose name was al-Amīna as was his custom; but a jinn disguised in the form of Solomon came to her and seized it from her. And We cast upon his throne a lifeless body which was that very jinn and he was the one known as Sakhr — or it was some other jinn; he sat upon Solomon’s throne and so as was the case with Solomon the birds and other creatures devoted themselves to him in service. When Solomon came out of his palace having seen him the jinn upon his throne he said to the people ‘I am Solomon not him!’ But they did not recognise him. Then he repented — Solomon returned to his kingdom many days later after he had managed to acquire the ring. He wore it and sat upon his throne again.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. And indeed, We did try Sulaimān (Solomon) and We placed on his throne Jasad (a devil, so he lost his kingdom for a while) and he did return (to Allāh with obedience and.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said: My Lord! Forgive me) my sin (and bestow on me sovereignty such shall not belong to any after me) it is also said that this means: that will not be taken from me as the first time. (Lo! Thou art the Bestower) of sovereignty and prophethood to whomever you will.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكاً لاَّ يَنبَغِي لأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِيۤ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. He said: “My Lord! Forgive me, and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me: Verily, You are the Bestower.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘My Lord! Forgive me and grant me a kingdom that shall not belong to anyone after me in other words other than me this use of min ba‘dī to mean ‘other than me’ is similar to Q. 4523 fa-man yahdīh min ba‘di’Llāh ‘who will guide him other than God?’. Truly You are the Bestower’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكاً لاَّ يَنبَغِي لأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِيۤ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. He said: “My Lord! Forgive me, and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me: Verily, You are the Bestower.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So We made the wind subservient unto him) after that, (setting fair) setting gently (by his command) and it is said: by Allah's command (whithersoever he intended) wherever he wished.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. So, We subjected to him the wind; it blew gently by his order whithersoever he willed,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So We disposed for him the wind which blew softly gently at his command wherever he intended.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. So, We subjected to him the wind; it blew gently by his order whithersoever he willed,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And) also made subservient (the unruly) the devils, (every builder and diver) into the bottom of the sea,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّآءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And also the Shayāṭīn (devils) from the jinn (including) every kind of builder and diver,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the devils also We disposed every builder building marvellous edifices and diver in the sea bringing up pearls

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّآءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And also the Shayāṭīn (devils) from the jinn (including) every kind of builder and diver,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And others) and other than these (linked together in chains) in iron chains; these are the rebellious devils who were never entrusted with any work except that they rebelled,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي ٱلأَصْفَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. And also others bound in fetters..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and others too from among them bounded together in fetters in shackles with their hands tied to their necks.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي ٱلأَصْفَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. And also others bound in fetters..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Saying): This is Our gift) this is Our sovereignty, O Solomon. We made you a sovereign over the devils, (so bestow thou) favour whom you will among the rebellious and relieve them from their chains, (or withhold) or keep them chained, (without reckoning) without taking anyone to task or incur a sin as a result.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. [Allāh said to Sulaimān (Solomon)]: “This is Our gift: so spend you or withhold, no account will be asked (of you).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We said to him ‘This is Our gift. So bestow grant thereof to whomever you wish or withhold from giving without any reckoning’ in other words without your being called to account for any of this.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. [Allāh said to Sulaimān (Solomon)]: “This is Our gift: so spend you or withhold, no account will be asked (of you).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! he hath favour) close rank (with Us, and a happy journey's end) and a happy return in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And verily, for him is near access to Us, and a good (final) return (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed he has a station of nearness with Us and a fair resort — a similar statement has already appeared in another verse above.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And verily, for him is near access to Us, and a good (final) return (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And make mention (O Muhammad) of Our bondman) mention to the disbelievers of Mecca the event of Our bondman (Job, when he cried) when he prayed (unto his Lord (saying): Lo! the devil doth afflict me) I am afflicted because You set Satan on me (with distress) toil and tiredness (and torment) trial and sickness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And remember Our slave Ayyūb (Job), when he invoked his Lord (saying): “Verily, Shaiṭān (Satan) has touched me with distress (by ruining my health) and torment (by ruining my wealth)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And mention also Our servant Job when he called out to his Lord saying ‘Lo! Satan has afflicted me with hardship harm and suffering’ pain he attributes all this to Satan even though all things are from God to show reverence in his call to Him exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And remember Our slave Ayyūb (Job), when he invoked his Lord (saying): “Verily, Shaiṭān (Satan) has touched me with distress (by ruining my health) and torment (by ruining my wealth)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then Gabriel said to him: O Job! (Strike the ground with thy foot) when he did so, a spring gushed out. Gabriel said to him: (This (spring) is a cool bath), take a bath in it. When he took a bath his wounds healed. Gabriel asked him to strike the ground with his foot again and another spring gushed out. Gabriel said: (and a refreshing drink) this is cool, sweet water, drink from it! When he drank, his inside ailment was cured.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هَـٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌ بَارِدٌ وَشَرَابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. (Allāh said to him): “Strike the ground with your foot: This is (a spring of) water to wash in, cool and a (refresh- ing) drink.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And it was said to him ‘Stamp your foot on the ground — and he stamped it and a spring of water gushed forth and it was said This is a cool bath cool water for you to wash with and a drink’ for you to drink of. So he washed himself and drank from it whereat every ailment that had affected him internally and externally disappeared.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هَـٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌ بَارِدٌ وَشَرَابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. (Allāh said to him): “Strike the ground with your foot: This is (a spring of) water to wash in, cool and a (refresh- ing) drink.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We bestowed on him (again) his household) which We made to perish (and therewith the like thereof) in the life of this world and it is said in the Hereafter, (a mercy from Us) a blessing from Us to him, (and a memorial) an admonition (for men of understanding) for those possessed of intellect among people.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا وَذِكْرَىٰ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. And We gave him (back) his family, and along with them the like thereof, as Mercy from Us, and a Reminder for those who understand..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We gave him back his family along with others like them that is God brought back to life all the children of his that had died and provided him with as many in addition to them as a mercy a grace from us and a reminder an admonition to people of pith possessors of intellect.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا وَذِكْرَىٰ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. And We gave him (back) his family, and along with them the like thereof, as Mercy from Us, and a Reminder for those who understand..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand) O Job (a branch) of 100 spikes of grain (and smite therewith) and smite with it your wife, Rahmah the daughter of the Prophet Joseph, (and break not thine oath) this is because he vowed before that if Allah were to cure him, he would flog his wife 100 lashes because she said something which did not please Allah. (Lo! We found him steadfast) in trial, (how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord)) he is ever obedient to Allah and betaking himself to Allah's obedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً فَٱضْرِب بِّهِ وَلاَ تَحْنَثْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِراً نِّعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. “And take in your hand a bundle of thin grass and strike therewith (your wife), and break not your oath(1). Truly, We found him patient. How excellent a slave! Verily, he was ever oft-returning in repentance (to Us)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We said to him ‘Take in your hand a bunch of twigs or some blades of grass and smite therewith your wife — for he had sworn to smite her a hundred times on one occasion when she was late in coming to him — and do not break your oath’ by not smiting her so he took a hundred rushes and smote her with them once and that sufficed to fulfil his oath. Truly We found him to be steadfast. What an excellent servant! was Job. Indeed he was a penitent soul always returning to God exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً فَٱضْرِب بِّهِ وَلاَ تَحْنَثْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِراً نِّعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. “And take in your hand a bundle of thin grass and strike therewith (your wife), and break not your oath(1). Truly, We found him patient. How excellent a slave! Verily, he was ever oft-returning in repentance (to Us)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And make mention of our bondmen, Abraham) the friend of the Beneficent, (Isaac and Jacob, men of parts) men of strength in the worship of Allah (and vision) regarding Religion.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي وَٱلأَبْصَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And remember Our slaves, Ibrāhīm (Abraham), Isḥāq (Isaac), and Ya‘qūb (Jacob), (all) owners of strength (in worship ping Us) and (also) of religious understand ing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And mention also Our servants Abraham and Isaac and Jacob — men of fortitude vigorous in their worship and insight deep understanding of religion a variant reading for ‘ibādanā ‘Our servants’ has singular ‘abdanā ‘Our servant’ with Ibrāhīma as the explication thereof and what follows as being a supplement to ‘abdanā ‘Our servant’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي وَٱلأَبْصَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And remember Our slaves, Ibrāhīm (Abraham), Isḥāq (Isaac), and Ya‘qūb (Jacob), (all) owners of strength (in worship ping Us) and (also) of religious understand ing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We purified them with a pure thought) We selected them, (remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter) for the remembrance of Allah and the remembrance of the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Verily, We did choose them by granting them (a good thing, — i.e.) the remembrance of the Home ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly We purified them with an exclusive thought namely the remembrance of the Abode of the Hereafter in other words to always remember it and to work for it a variant reading for bi-khālisatin dhikrā’l-dār has the genitive construction bi-khālisati dhikrā’l-dār making this dhikrā al-dār ‘remembrance of the Abode’ the explicative thereof.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Verily, We did choose them by granting them (a good thing, — i.e.) the remembrance of the Home ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent) they are selected in the life of the world for prophethood and Islam and they are excellent in Allah's sight on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُمْ عِندَنَا لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصْطَفَيْنَ ٱلأَخْيَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. And they are with Us, verily, of the chosen and the best!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed in Our sight they are of the elect the excellent akhyār is the plural of khayyir.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُمْ عِندَنَا لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصْطَفَيْنَ ٱلأَخْيَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. And they are with Us, verily, of the chosen and the best!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha) the cousin of Ilyas (and Dhu'l-Kifl) who appointed himself as a guarantor of a few things which belonged to some people and kept his word; it is also said that he took charge of 100 prophets and he fed them until Allah saved them from death. However, he was a righteous man and not a prophet. (All are of the chosen) in Allah's sight.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلأَخْيَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And remember Ismā‘īl (Ishmael), Alyasa‘ (Elisha), and Dhul-Kifl (Isaiah), all are among the best..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And mention also Our servants Ishmael and Elisha who was a prophet the lām here in al-Yasa‘ is extra and Dhū’l-Kifl — there is disagreement over whether he was a prophet; it is said that he was so called because he looked after kafala a hundred prophets who had sought refuge with him from being killed. Each that is every one of them was among the excellent akhyār is the plural of khayyir.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلأَخْيَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And remember Ismā‘īl (Ishmael), Alyasa‘ (Elisha), and Dhul-Kifl (Isaiah), all are among the best..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (This is a reminder) this is a remembrance of the righteous; it is also said that this means: this Qur'an contains the events of the people of old as well as of future generations. (And lo! for those who ward off (evil)) disbelief, idolatry and indecent acts (is a happy journey's end) a happy return in the Hereafter,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. This is a Reminder. And verily, for the Muttaqūn (the pious)(2) is a good final return (Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: This is a remembrance of them made by the mention of fair praise of them here; and indeed for the God-fearing who comprise them there will truly be a fair return in the Hereafter —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. This is a Reminder. And verily, for the Muttaqūn (the pious)(2) is a good final return (Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah explained where they will dwell in the Hereafter, saying: (Gardens of Eden) the source of prophets and righteous, (whereof the gates are opened for them) on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُّفَتَّحَةً لَّهُمُ ٱلأَبْوَابُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), whose doors will be opened for them. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Gardens of Eden jannāti ‘Adnin is either a substitution for or an explicative supplement to husna ma’ābin ‘a fair return’ whose gates are flung open for them;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُّفَتَّحَةً لَّهُمُ ٱلأَبْوَابُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (everlasting Gardens), whose doors will be opened for them. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Wherein, reclining) sitting on couches in curtained canopies, enjoying comfort in Paradise, (they call) they ask in Paradise (for plenteous fruit) for different kinds of fruit (and cool drink) and different kinds of drink ((that is) therein) in Paradise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. Therein they will recline; therein they will call for fruits in abundance and drinks;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: reclining therein on couches; therein they call for plenteous fruit and drink.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. Therein they will recline; therein they will call for fruits in abundance and drinks;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And with them are those of modest gaze) wives who are content with their husbands, (companions) who are of the same age.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ أَتْرَابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. And beside them will be Qāṣirāt-aṭ-Ṭarf [chaste females (wives) restraining their glances (desiring none except their husbands)], (and) of equal ages..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And with them there will be maidens of restrained glances restricting their eyes to their spouses of a like age of the same age girls who are thirty three years of age atrāb is the plural of tirb.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ أَتْرَابٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. And beside them will be Qāṣirāt-aṭ-Ṭarf [chaste females (wives) restraining their glances (desiring none except their husbands)], (and) of equal ages..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah will say to them: (This it is that ye are promised) you were promised in the life of the world (for the Day of Reckoning) on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. This it is what you (Al-Muttaqūn — the pious)(1) are promised for the Day of Reckoning!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘This that is mentioned is what you are promised by way of the unseen there is a shift in the address away from the third to the second person for the Day of Reckoning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. This it is what you (Al-Muttaqūn — the pious)(1) are promised for the Day of Reckoning!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! this in truth is Our provision) this is the food and bliss We have for them, (which will never waste away) which will never cease or be interrupted.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِن نَّفَادٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. (It will be said to them): Verily, this is Our Provision which will never finish..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: This is indeed Our provision which will never be exhausted’ in other words one which will never cease this last sentence mā lahu min nafādin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to rizqunā ‘Our provision’; or it is a second predicate of inna ‘indeed’ meaning that it will be ‘everlasting’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِن نَّفَادٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. (It will be said to them): Verily, this is Our Provision which will never finish..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (This) is for the believers. (And lo! for the transgressors) for the disbelievers: Abu Jahl and his host (there will be an evil journey's end) an evil return in the Hereafter,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. This is so! And for the Ṭāghūn  will be an evil final return (Fire)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: That which is mentioned will be the reward for the believers is so; but for the insolent this is a new sentence there will surely be an evil place of return —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. This is so! And for the Ṭāghūn  will be an evil final return (Fire)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hell, where they will burn) on the Day of Judgement, (an evil resting place) the Fire is an evil abode for them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ ٱلْمِهَادُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. Hell! Where they will burn, and worst (indeed) is that place to rest!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Hell which they will enter — an evil resting place!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ ٱلْمِهَادُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. Hell! Where they will burn, and worst (indeed) is that place to rest!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Here is) for the disbelievers (a boiling and an ice cold draught) which burns them just as fire does, (so let them taste it) let them taste the torment of Gehenna,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. This is so! Then let them taste it — a boiling fluid and dirty wound discharges..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: This chastisement — inferred as so by what follows — let them then taste it burning hot water and pus read ghasāq or ghassāq the festering matter excreted by the inhabitants of the Fire;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. This is so! Then let them taste it — a boiling fluid and dirty wound discharges..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And other (torment) of the kind) of burning heat and ice cold draught (in pairs (the two extremes)!) different kinds of torment. Allah will cast them in the Fire one after another, in order of merit, whenever a generation of people enters it, they curse those who entered the Fire before them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَآخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. And other (torments) of similar kind — all together!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and other ākhar may be plural or singular kinds of torment resembling it in other words like the boiling water and pus mentioned in pairs of all sorts in other words their chastisement will consist of various kinds.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَآخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. And other (torments) of similar kind — all together!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah will say to the first generation of people who entered the Fire: (Here is an army) a group of people (rushing blindly with you) into the Fire. Those who entered hell first will say to those who entered it after them: (No word of welcome for them) may Allah not make it spacious for them. (Lo! they will roast at the Fire) they will abide in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا فَوْجٌ مُّقْتَحِمٌ مَّعَكُمْ لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. This is a troop entering with you (in Hell), no welcome for them! Verily, they shall burn in the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And it will be said to them as they enter the Fire with their followers ‘This is a horde about to plunge to enter with you into the Fire violently — at which point those who used to be followed say no welcome is there for them here! in other words they will find no comfort for them here. They will indeed roast in the Fire’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا فَوْجٌ مُّقْتَحِمٌ مَّعَكُمْ لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. This is a troop entering with you (in Hell), no welcome for them! Verily, they shall burn in the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They say) those who entered the Fire afterward will say: (Nay, but ye (misleaders), for you there is no word of welcome) may Allah not make it spacious for you. (You prepared) you prescribed (this for us) i.e. the religion which we followed you on. (Now hapless is the plight) evil is the abode for both of us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ بَلْ أَنتُمْ لاَ مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ أَنتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنَا فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرَارُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. They (The followers of the misleaders) will say: “Nay, you (too)! No welcome for you! It is you (misleaders) who brought this upon us (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They the followers say ‘Nay but for you there is no welcome! You prepared this that is disbelief for us. So what an evil abode!’ for us and for you is the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ بَلْ أَنتُمْ لاَ مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ أَنتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنَا فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرَارُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. They (The followers of the misleaders) will say: “Nay, you (too)! No welcome for you! It is you (misleaders) who brought this upon us (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They say) the first to enter the Fire and the last say: (Our Lord!) O our Lord! (Whoever did prepare) whoever prescribed (this) religion; meaning here Satan and all the leaders of error (for us), oh, give him double portion of the Fire) double than what we have!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَاباً ضِعْفاً فِي ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. They will say: “Our Lord! Whoever brought this upon us, add to him a double torment in the Fire!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They also say ‘Our Lord whoever prepared this for us give him double his chastisement that is give him in addition the like of his chastisement for his disbelief in the Fire!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَاباً ضِعْفاً فِي ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. They will say: “Our Lord! Whoever brought this upon us, add to him a double torment in the Fire!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they say: What aileth us that we behold not) in the Fire (men) meaning the poor among the believers (whom we were wont to count among the wicked) whom we counted among the lowly and paupers?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ مَا لَنَا لاَ نَرَىٰ رِجَالاً كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَشْرَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. And they will say: “What is the matter with us that we see not men whom we used to count among the bad ones?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they the disbelievers of Mecca say while they are in the Fire ‘What is the matter with us that we do not see here men whom we used to count in the world among the wicked?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ مَا لَنَا لاَ نَرَىٰ رِجَالاً كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَشْرَارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. And they will say: “What is the matter with us that we see not men whom we used to count among the bad ones?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Did we take them (wrongly) for a laughing stock) we made them subservient to us in the life of the world, (or have our eyes missed them) and we did not see them?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيّاً أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ ٱلأَبْصَار
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. Did we take them as an object of mockery, or have (our) eyes failed to perceive them?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Did we treat them mockingly? read sukhriyyan or sikhriyyan did we use to deride them in the life of the world the final yā’ in sikhriyyā is attributive. In other words are they missing? Or have our eyes missed them here?’ so that we have not caught sight of them. Such men were the poor among the Muslims like ‘Ammār b. Yāsir Bilāl al-Habashī Suhayb al-Rūmī and Salmān al-Fārisī.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيّاً أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ ٱلأَبْصَار
meta_data.ayah_translation: 63. Did we take them as an object of mockery, or have (our) eyes failed to perceive them?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! That) which I have mentioned of the event of the inhabitants of the Fire (is the very truth) is true: (the wrangling of the dwellers in the Fire) this is how the dwellers of the Fire argue with each other.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. Verily, that is the very truth — the mutual dispute of the people of the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly that is true such a scene will necessarily take place which is the wrangling of the inhabitants of the Fire — as shown above.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ ٱلنَّارِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 64. Verily, that is the very truth — the mutual dispute of the people of the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) to the people of Mecca, O Muhammad: (I am only a warner) a warning messenger, (and there is no God save Allah) He has no son or partner, (the One, the Absolute) Superior over His creation,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَاْ مُنذِرٌ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَاحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. Say (O Muḥammad ): “I am only a warner and there is no Ilāh (God) except Allāh (none has the right to be worshipped but Allāh) the One, the Irresistible,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say O Muhammad (s) to the disbelievers of Mecca ‘I am only a warner to threaten disbelievers with punishment in the Fire. And there is no god except God the One the All-Compelling of all His creatures;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَاْ مُنذِرٌ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَاحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 65. Say (O Muḥammad ): “I am only a warner and there is no Ilāh (God) except Allāh (none has the right to be worshipped but Allāh) the One, the Irresistible,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lord of the heavens and the earth) the Creator of the heavens and the earth (and all that is between them) of created beings and marvels, (the Mighty) in retribution against those who disbelieve in Him, (the Pardoning) He pardons those who repent and believe in Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفَّارُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. “The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the All-Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them the Mighty Whose way always prevails the ever Forgiving’ of His friends.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفَّارُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 66. “The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the All-Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) O Muhammad: (It) i.e. the Qur'an (is tremendous tidings) it is blessed and exalted and contains the events of the people of old as well as the events of future generations of people.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. Say: “That (this Qur’ān) is great news,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say to them ‘It is a tremendous tiding

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 67. Say: “That (this Qur’ān) is great news,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Whence you turn away) whence you disbelieve and abandon!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. “From which you turn away!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: from which you are turning away namely the Qur’ān of which I have informed you and in which I have brought you what can only be known by revelation and that is God’s saying

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 68. “From which you turn away!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (I had no knowledge of the Highest Chiefs) i.e. of the angels, if it was not Allah Who sent me (when they disputed) when they spoke and said: (Wilt Thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. “I had no knowledge of the chiefs (angels) on high when they were disputing and discussing (about the creation of Adam)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: I had no knowledge of the High Council that is to say of the angels when they disputed in the matter of Adam when God exalted be He said to them ‘I am appointing on earth a vicegerent’ to the end of the verse Q. 230.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 69. “I had no knowledge of the chiefs (angels) on high when they were disputing and discussing (about the creation of Adam)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: It is revealed unto me only that I may be a plain warner) a warning messenger addressing you in a language that you understand.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِن يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ إِلاَّ أَنَّمَآ أَنَاْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. “Only this has been revealed to me, that I am a plain warner.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: All that is revealed to me is that I am just a plain warner’ one whose warning is clear.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِن يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ إِلاَّ أَنَّمَآ أَنَاْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 70. “Only this has been revealed to me, that I am a plain warner.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then Allah explained the argument of the angels, saying: mention to them, O Muhammad (When thy Lord said unto the angels: lo! I am about to create a mortal out of mire) i.e. Adam,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلاَئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَراً مِّن طِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. (Remember) when your Lord said to the angels: “Truly, I am going to create man from clay”..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Mention when your Lord said to the angels ‘Indeed I am about to create a human being out of clay and this was Adam.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلاَئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَراً مِّن طِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 71. (Remember) when your Lord said to the angels: “Truly, I am going to create man from clay”..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And when I have fashioned him) and when I have gathered his creation (and breathed into him of My spirit) and placed in him My spirit, (then fall down before him prostrate) then prostrate before him,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. So, when I have fashioned him and breathed into him (his) soul created by Me, then you fall down prostrate to him.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So when I have proportioned him completed him and breathed in him when I have caused to flow therein My spirit so that he becomes a living being — the addition of ‘the spirit’ to Adam is an honour for him; the ‘spirit’ is a subtle body that gives life to a human being by permeating him — then fall down in prostration before him!’ — a prostration of salutation that is actually a bow.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 72. So, when I have fashioned him and breathed into him (his) soul created by Me, then you fall down prostrate to him.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The angels fell down prostrate, every one) before Adam.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ كُـلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them:.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thereat the angels prostrated all of them together there are two emphases here kulluhum and ajma‘ūn;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ كُـلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 73. So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them:.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Saving Iblis, he was scornful) he was too proud to prostrate before Adam (and became one of the disbelievers) because of disobeying Allah's command.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ ٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. Except Iblīs (Satan): he was proud(1) and was one of the disbelievers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except Iblīs the father of the jinn who was among the audience of angels; he was disdainful and he was one of the disbelievers according to God’s knowledge exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ ٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 74. Except Iblīs (Satan): he was proud(1) and was one of the disbelievers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Allah said to him: (O Iblis!) O wicked one! (What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands) what prevented you from prostrating before that which I have shaped with My hands? (Art thou too proud) to prostrate before Adam (or art thou of the high) or are you of those who disobey My command?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ يٰإِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْعَالِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. (Allāh) said: “O Iblīs (Satan)! What prevents you from prostrating yourself to one whom I have created with Both My Hands (2). Are you too proud (to fall prostrate to Adam) or are you one of the high exalted?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘O Iblīs! What prevents you from prostrating before that which I have created with My own hands? in other words whose creation I Myself have undertaken. This in itself is an honour for Adam as God has Himself undertaken the unmediated creation of all creatures. Are you being arrogant now in refraining from prostrating an interrogative meant as a rebuke; or are you of the exalted?’ of the proud and have therefore disdained to prostrate yourself because you are one of them?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ يٰإِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْعَالِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 75. (Allāh) said: “O Iblīs (Satan)! What prevents you from prostrating yourself to one whom I have created with Both My Hands (2). Are you too proud (to fall prostrate to Adam) or are you one of the high exalted?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire, whilst him Thou didst create of clay) and the Fire consumes clay; this is why I did not prostrate before him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَنَاْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. [Iblīs (Satan)] said: “I am better than him. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَنَاْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. [Iblīs (Satan)] said: “I am better than him. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Allah said to him: (Go forth from hence) leave the angelic form; and it is also said this means: leave the earth, (for lo! thou art outcast) you are accursed and banished from My mercy and beneficence,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. (Allāh) said: “Then get out from here; for verily you are outcast..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Then begone hence that is from Paradise — or it is said begone from the heavens — for you are indeed accursed outcast.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. (Allāh) said: “Then get out from here; for verily you are outcast..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! My curse) My wrath and chastisement; it is also said that Allah banished him to the isles of the sea and, hence, he goes to the land only in the form of a thief, wearing tattered clothes, and scaring people (is on you till the Day of Judgement) until the Day of Reckoning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِيۤ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. “And verily, My Curse is on you till the Day of Recom pense.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed My curse shall be on you until the Day of Judgement’ the Day of Requital.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِيۤ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. “And verily, My Curse is on you till the Day of Recom pense.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Iblis said: (My Lord!) O my Lord! (Reprieve me) give me a respite (till the day when they are raised) from the graves. The wicked one wanted to escape the taste of death.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِيۤ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. [Iblīs (Satan)] said: “My Lord! Give me then respite till the Day the (dead) are resurrected.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘My Lord then reprieve me until the day when they mankind will be raised’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِيۤ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. [Iblīs (Satan)] said: “My Lord! Give me then respite till the Day the (dead) are resurrected.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Allah said: (Lo! thou art of those reprieved) you are given a respite

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. (Allāh) said: “Verily, you are of those allowed respite.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Then you will indeed be among the reprieved

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. (Allāh) said: “Verily, you are of those allowed respite.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Until the day of the time appointed) until the first blow of the Trumpet.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Till the Day of the time appointed.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: until the day of the known time’ the time of the First Blast.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Till the Day of the time appointed.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said: Then, by Thy might) and favour, (I surely will beguile them every one) I will mislead all of them from Your religion and obedience,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. [Iblīs (Satan)] said: “By Your Might, then I will surely mislead them all, (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘Now by Your might I shall surely pervert them all

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. [Iblīs (Satan)] said: “By Your Might, then I will surely mislead them all, (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save Thy single minded slaves) save those slaves who are protected from me (among them) among the children of Adam.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. “Except Your chosen slaves amongst them (i.e. faithful, obedient, true believers of Islāmic Monotheism).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except those servants of Yours among them who will be saved’ namely the believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. “Except Your chosen slaves amongst them (i.e. faithful, obedient, true believers of Islāmic Monotheism).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He said) Allah said to him: (The Truth is) I am the Truth, (and the Truth I speak,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 84. (Allāh) said: “The Truth is — and the Truth I say —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘So the truth is — and the truth I always speak read both words in the accusative fa’l-haqqa wa’l-haqqa; or with the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative because of the verb aqūlu ‘I speak’ that follows. As for reading the first one in the accusative this would be on account of the mentioned verb qāla ‘he said’; but it is also said to be on account of its being a verbal noun the sense being uhiqqu l-haqqa ‘I establish the truth’; or it is in the accusative by implication if the particle for the oath fa is removed. It the first haqq could also be in the nominative because of its being the subject of a missing predicate as in fa’l-haqqu minnī ‘truth comes from Me’. It is also said that the sentence means fa’l-haqqu qasamī ‘the truth is this oath from Me’ the response to which is the following la-amla’anna … —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 84. (Allāh) said: “The Truth is — and the Truth I say —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: That I shall fill hell with thee) and with your offspring (and with such of them as follow thee) of the Children of Adam, (together) all those who obey your way.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 85. That I will fill Hell with you [Iblīs (Satan)] and those of them (mankind) that follow you, together.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: I shall assuredly fill Hell with you by way of filling it with your progeny and with whoever of them follows you that is of mankind all together’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 85. That I will fill Hell with you [Iblīs (Satan)] and those of them (mankind) that follow you, together.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) O Muhammad, to the people of Mecca: (I ask of you no fee) no payment or provision (for this) for belief in Allah's divine Oneness and in the Qur'an, (and I am no impostor) and I am not inventing anything.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ مَآ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَمَآ أَنَآ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 86. Say (O Muḥammad ): “No wage do I ask of you for this (the Qur’ān), nor am I one of the Mutakallifūn (those who pretend and fabricate things which do not exist)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘I do not ask of you in return for this for delivering the Message to you any reward any fee; nor am I an impostor so as to make up the Qur’ān myself.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ مَآ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَمَآ أَنَآ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 86. Say (O Muḥammad ): “No wage do I ask of you for this (the Qur’ān), nor am I one of the Mutakallifūn (those who pretend and fabricate things which do not exist)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! It) i.e. the Qur'an (is naught else than a reminder) an admonition (for all peoples) for the jinn and human beings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. “It (this Qur’ān) is only a Reminder for all the ‘Ālamīn (mankind and jinn)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is only in other words the Qur’ān is only a reminder an admonition for all worlds those of humans jinn and other rational beings but excluding the angels.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. “It (this Qur’ān) is only a Reminder for all the ‘Ālamīn (mankind and jinn)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And ye will come in time to know the Truth thereof) you will know the Truth of the Qur'an and that which it contains of promises and threats after you believe; and it is also said: after death. Some came to know after they accepted faith: these are the believers; and some came to know after death and these are the disbelievers. Both came to know that what Allah said in the Qur'an is the Truth'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 88. “And you shall certainly know the truth of it after a while”..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And you will assuredly come to know O disbelievers of Mecca its tiding the news of its truth in due time’ that is to say on the Day of Resurrection ‘ilm ‘knowing’ is here being used in the sense of ‘urf ‘experience’; the prefixed lām in la-ta‘lamunna ‘you will assuredly know’ is for an implicit oath in other words what is meant is wa’Llāhi la-ta‘lamunna ‘By God you will assuredly know’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 88. “And you shall certainly know the truth of it after a while”..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying: (The revelation of the Scripture): '(The revelation of the Scripture is) He says: this Scripture is an address (from Allah, the Mighty) in retribution against those who disbelieve in Him, (the Wise) in His command and decree; He commanded that none should be worshipped except Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The revelation of this Book (the Qur’ān) is from Allāh, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The revelation of the Book the Qur’ān tanzīlu’l-kitābi the subject is from God mina’Llāhi its predicate the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His handiwork.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The revelation of this Book (the Qur’ān) is from Allāh, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We have revealed the Scripture unto thee (Muhammad)) We have sent Gabriel to you with the Scripture (with truth) not with falsehood; (so worship Allah, making religion pure for Him (only)) making worship and the profession of Allah's divine Oneness sincere to Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Verily, We have sent down the Book to you (O Muḥammad ) in truth: So worship Allāh (Alone) by doing religious deeds sincerely for Allāh’s sake only..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We have revealed to you O Muhammad (s) the Book with the truth bi’l-haqqi is semantically connected to anzalnā ‘We have revealed’; so worship God devoting your religion purely to Him pure of any idolatry in other words affirming His Oneness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Verily, We have sent down the Book to you (O Muḥammad ) in truth: So worship Allāh (Alone) by doing religious deeds sincerely for Allāh’s sake only..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Surely Pure religion is) sincerity in religion is enjoined upon people (for Allah only. And those who choose) and those who worship (protecting friends) deities: al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat (beside Him) beside Allah, i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ((say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah) near to Allah in rank and intercession.
