meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَاثاً وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Man (the disbeliever) does not get tired of asking good (things from Allāh); but if an evil touches him, then he gives up all hope and is lost in despair To Allāh belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female (offspring) upon whom He wills, and bestows male (offspring) upon whom He wills..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He will; He gives to whomever He will in the way of children females and He gives to whomever He will males.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَاثاً وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Man (the disbeliever) does not get tired of asking good (things from Allāh); but if an evil touches him, then he gives up all hope and is lost in despair To Allāh belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female (offspring) upon whom He wills, and bestows male (offspring) upon whom He wills..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or He mingleth them, males and females) as was the case with the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) (and He maketh barren whom He will) as was the case with the Prophet John the son of Zachariah. (Lo! He is Knower, Powerful) regarding that which He gives of males or females.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَاناً وَإِنَاثاً وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيماً إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And truly, if We give him a taste of mercy from Us, after some adversity (severe poverty or disease, etc.) has touched him, he is sure to say: “This is due to my (merit); I think not that the Hour will be established. But if I am brought back to my Lord, surely, there will be for me the best (wealth) with Him. Then, We verily, will show to the disbelievers what they have done, and We shall make them taste a severe torment Or He bestows both males and females, and He renders barren whom He wills. Verily, He is All-Knower and is Able to do all things..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or He combines them that is to say or He makes them males and females; and He makes whomever He will infertile such that she is unable to conceive or he cannot have a child. Surely He is Knower of what He creates Powerful in bringing about whatever He will.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَاناً وَإِنَاثاً وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيماً إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And truly, if We give him a taste of mercy from Us, after some adversity (severe poverty or disease, etc.) has touched him, he is sure to say: “This is due to my (merit); I think not that the Hour will be established. But if I am brought back to my Lord, surely, there will be for me the best (wealth) with Him. Then, We verily, will show to the disbelievers what they have done, and We shall make them taste a severe torment Or He bestows both males and females, and He renders barren whom He wills. Verily, He is All-Knower and is Able to do all things..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And it was not (vouchsafed)) it was not permissible (to any mortal that Allah should speak to him) directly without a veil (unless (it be) by revelation) in dream (or from behind a veil) as when He spoke with Moses (pbuh) (or (that) He sendeth a messenger) i.e. Gabriel, such as when He sent him to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) (to reveal what He will) of commands and prohibitions (by His leave) by His command. (Lo! He is Exalted) more exalted than all created beings, (Wise) in His command and decree.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ وَحْياً أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولاً فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ مَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّهُ عَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And when We show favour to man, he withdraws and turns away; but when evil touches him, then he has recourse to long supplications It is not given to any human being that Allāh should speak to him unless (it be) by Revelation, or from behind a veil, or (that) He sends a Messenger to reveal what He wills by His Leave. Verily, He is Most High, All-Wise (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And it is not possible for any human that God should speak to him except that He should reveal to him by revelation in sleep or by inspiration or except from behind a veil where He makes the person able to hear His speech but without seeing Him — as was the case with Moses peace be upon him; or except that He should send a messenger an angel such as Gabriel and he the messenger then reveals to the person to whom he has been sent that is to say and then he speaks to him with His permission that is God’s whatever He God will. Truly He is Exalted above the attributes of created beings Wise in His actions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ وَحْياً أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولاً فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ مَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّهُ عَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And when We show favour to man, he withdraws and turns away; but when evil touches him, then he has recourse to long supplications It is not given to any human being that Allāh should speak to him unless (it be) by Revelation, or from behind a veil, or (that) He sends a Messenger to reveal what He wills by His Leave. Verily, He is Most High, All-Wise (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And thus have We inspired in thee (Muhammad) a Spirit of Our command) i.e. We sent you Gabriel with the Qur'an. (Thou knewest not what the Scripture was) you did not know what the Qur'an was before the coming of Gabriel to you nor did you know how to recite the Qur'an before it came to you, (nor what the Faith) nor did you know the call to Allah's divine Oneness. (But We have made it) i.e. the Qur'an (a light) an exposition of commands and prohibitions, the lawful and unlawful, the Truth and falsehood (whereby) by means of the Qur'an (We guide whom We will) whoever deserves it (of Our bondmen. And lo! thou verily dost guide) do call (unto a right path) a straight, true religion.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحاً مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِي مَا ٱلْكِتَابُ وَلاَ ٱلإِيمَانُ وَلَـٰكِن جَعَلْنَاهُ نُوراً نَّهْدِي بِهِ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِيۤ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. Say: “Tell me, if it (the Qur’ān) is from Allāh, and you disbelieve in it? Who is more astray than one who is in opposition far away (from Allāh’s Right Path and His obedience) And thus We have sent to you (O Muḥammad ) Rūḥ (a Revelation, and Mercy) of Our Command. You knew not what is the Book, nor what is Faith? But We have made it (this Qur’ān) a light wherewith We guide whosoever of Our slaves We will. And verily, you (O Muḥammad ) are indeed guiding (mankind) to a Straight Path (i.e. Allāh’s Religion of Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And thus in the same way that We have revealed to messengers other than you have We revealed to you O Muhammad (s) a Spirit namely the Qur’ān by which hearts are revived from Our command that command which We reveal to you. You did not know before revelation came to you what the Book was what the Qur’ān was nor faith that is its ordinances and ritual ceremonies the negation comments in place of the verb on the action and what has come after it constitutes two direct objects; but We have made it namely the Spirit — or the Qur’ān — a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants. And verily you guide you are summoning people by means of what is revealed to you to a straight path a straight way the religion of Islam

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحاً مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِي مَا ٱلْكِتَابُ وَلاَ ٱلإِيمَانُ وَلَـٰكِن جَعَلْنَاهُ نُوراً نَّهْدِي بِهِ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِيۤ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. Say: “Tell me, if it (the Qur’ān) is from Allāh, and you disbelieve in it? Who is more astray than one who is in opposition far away (from Allāh’s Right Path and His obedience) And thus We have sent to you (O Muḥammad ) Rūḥ (a Revelation, and Mercy) of Our Command. You knew not what is the Book, nor what is Faith? But We have made it (this Qur’ān) a light wherewith We guide whosoever of Our slaves We will. And verily, you (O Muḥammad ) are indeed guiding (mankind) to a Straight Path (i.e. Allāh’s Religion of Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The path of Allah) the religion of Allah, (unto Whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings. (Do not all things reach Allah at last?) the consequence of things in the Hereafter reach to the Wise Sovereign'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: صِرَاطِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَلاَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلأُمُورُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. We will show them Our Signs in the universe, and in their own selves, until it becomes manifest to them that this (the Qur’ān) is the truth. Is it not sufficient in regard to your Lord that He is a Witness over all things? The Path of Allāh to Whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. Verily, all matters in the end go to Allāh (for decision). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: the path of God to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth as possessions creatures and servants. Surely with God all matters end their journey all matters return.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: صِرَاطِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَلاَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلأُمُورُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. We will show them Our Signs in the universe, and in their own selves, until it becomes manifest to them that this (the Qur’ān) is the truth. Is it not sufficient in regard to your Lord that He is a Witness over all things? The Path of Allāh to Whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. Verily, all matters in the end go to Allāh (for decision). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said in the interpretation of Allah's saying (Ha. Mim.): '(Ha. Mim.) He says: He has already decreed that which will happen, i.e. He has shown it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حـمۤ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Ḥā-Mīm. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Hā mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حـمۤ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Ḥā-Mīm. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (By the Scripture which maketh plain) he says: and I swear by the Scripture which makes plain the lawful and unlawful, the commands and prohibitions that that which will happen has already been decreed; it is also said Allah swore by the (Ha) and (Mim) and also by the Scripture which makes plain the commands and prohibitions, the lawful and unlawful,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By the manifest Book (i.e. this Qur’ān that makes things clear)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By the Book the Qur’ān that clarifies the one that manifests the path of guidance and what one needs of the prescriptions of the Law.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By the manifest Book (i.e. this Qur’ān that makes things clear)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We have appointed it) We have spoken it, i.e. the Qur'an (a Lecture in Arabic) in the Arabic usage, hence the oath, (that haply ye may understand) so that you may know what is in the Qur'an of the lawful and unlawful, commands and prohibitions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Verily, We have made it a Qur’ān in Arabic that you may be able to understand (its meanings and its admonitions)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lo! We have made it We have brought the Book into existence as an Arabic Qur’ān in the language of the Arabs that perhaps you O people of Mecca may understand that you may comprehend its meanings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Verily, We have made it a Qur’ān in Arabic that you may be able to understand (its meanings and its admonitions)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! in the Source of Decrees) in the Guarded Tablet, (which We possess) where it is written, (it) i.e. the Qur'an (is indeed sublime) exalted, noble and glorious, (decisive) in explaining the lawful and the unlawful,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And verily, it (this Qur’ān) is in the Mother of the Book (i.e. Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ) with Us, indeed exalted, full of wisdom..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And it is indeed fixed in the Mother Book the source of all the scriptures namely the Preserved Tablet which is with Us ladaynā substitutes for fī ummi’l-kitābi ‘in the Mother Book’ and it is indeed exalted above all the scriptures that came before it wise containing excellent wisdoms.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And verily, it (this Qur’ān) is in the Mother of the Book (i.e. Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ) with Us, indeed exalted, full of wisdom..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Shall We utterly ignore you) shall We remove from you, O people of Mecca, the revelation and the Messenger? Or shall We leave you uncared for, without commands or prohibitions (because ye are a wanton folk) because you are idolatrous folk who do not believe in Allah, as is in His foreknowledge?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّسْرِفِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Shall We then (warn you not and) take away the Reminder (this Qur’ān) from you, because you are a people Musrifūn (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Shall We turn away shall We withhold from you the Remembrance the Qur’ān utterly an utter withholding so that you are then neither commanded nor forbidden because you are a profligate an idolatrous folk? No!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّسْرِفِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Shall We then (warn you not and) take away the Reminder (this Qur’ān) from you, because you are a people Musrifūn (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (How many a Prophet did We send) did We send before you, O Muhammad, (among the men of old) among bygone nations; We knew that they would not believe, but We nonetheless did not leave them without messengers and Scriptures!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن نَّبِيٍّ فِي ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And many a Prophet We have sent amongst the men of old..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And how many a prophet did We send among the ancients!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن نَّبِيٍّ فِي ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And many a Prophet We have sent amongst the men of old..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And never came there unto them) i.e. to these past nations (a Prophet but they used to mock him) i.e. they used to mock the Prophet.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ نَّبِيٍّ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And never came there a Prophet to them but they used to mock at him. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And never did a prophet come to them but that they used to deride him in the same way that your people deride you — this statement is intended to comfort the Prophet s.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ نَّبِيٍّ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And never came there a Prophet to them but they used to mock at him. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then we destroyed men mightier than these) mightier than the people of Mecca (in prowess) in strength and power; (and the example of the men of old hath gone (before them)) i.e. they were destroyed when they disbelieved in their messengers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَهْلَكْنَآ أَشَدَّ مِنْهُم بَطْشاً وَمَضَىٰ مَثَلُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Then We destroyed men stronger (in power) than these — and the example of the ancients has passed away (before them)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So We destroyed those who were mightier than them — than your people — in prowess strength and already there passed there has been mentioned in previous verses the example of the ancients the description of how they were destroyed and thus the sequel for your people will be the same.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَهْلَكْنَآ أَشَدَّ مِنْهُم بَطْشاً وَمَضَىٰ مَثَلُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Then We destroyed men stronger (in power) than these — and the example of the ancients has passed away (before them)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And if thou (Muhammad) ask them) i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca: (Who created the heavens and the earth, they) i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca (will surely answer: The Mighty) in His dominion and sovereignty, (the Knower) of His providence and created beings (created them);

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And indeed if you ask them, “Who has created the heavens and the earth?” They will surely say: “The All-Mighty, the All-Knower created them.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you ask them ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say the indicative nūn has been omitted because of the other nūn coming after it and likewise the wāw replaced by the damma in -lunna because of two unvowelled consonants coming together ‘The Mighty the Knower created them’ — this would have to be their eventual response that is to say God created them Lord of Might and Knowledge. God exalted be He adds

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And indeed if you ask them, “Who has created the heavens and the earth?” They will surely say: “The All-Mighty, the All-Knower created them.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah says: yes, He created them Him (Who made the earth a resting place for you, and placed roads for you therein, that haply ye may find your way) by means of the roads;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلأَرْضَ مَهْداً وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلاً لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Who has made for you the earth like a bed, and has made for you roads therein, in order that you may find your way..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He Who made the earth a cradle for you a flat resting-place like a child’s cradle and placed for you therein ways routes that perhaps you may be guided to your destinations during your travels;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلأَرْضَ مَهْداً وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلاً لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Who has made for you the earth like a bed, and has made for you roads therein, in order that you may find your way..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And who sendeth down water) rain (from the sky in (due) measure) according to the knowledge of the storer, (and We revive a dead land therewith) and We revive through it a barren land that had hitherto no vegetation. (Even so will ye be brought forth) Even so you will be revived and brought forth from the graves as We revive the barren land and bring forth from it vegetation;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَنشَرْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً كَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And Who sends down water (rain) from the sky in due measure, then We revive a dead land therewith, and even so you will be brought forth (from the graves)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Who sent down water from the heaven in measure that is to say in the measure that you require thereof and did not send it down in a deluge and We revived with it a dead land. Thus — like this revivification — will you be brought forth from your graves alive;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَنشَرْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً كَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And Who sends down water (rain) from the sky in due measure, then We revive a dead land therewith, and even so you will be brought forth (from the graves)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He Who created all the pairs) all the different kinds of created beings, (and appointed for you) and created for you (ships and cattle whereupon ye ride.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْفُلْكِ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And Who has created all the pairs and has appointed for you ships and cattle on which you ride:.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Who created the pairs the species all of them and made for you ships and cattle such as camels on which you ride the referential pronoun has been omitted here for brevity; it is genitive in the case of the first that is fīhi sc. tarkabūna fīhi ‘you ride in them’ and accusative in the case of the second sc. tarkabūnahā ‘you ride them’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْفُلْكِ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And Who has created all the pairs and has appointed for you ships and cattle on which you ride:.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: That ye may mount upon their backs) i.e. the backs of camels, (and may remember your Lord's favour) for making them subdued for you (when ye mount thereon, and may say: Glorified be He Who hath subdued these) camels (unto us, and we were not capable (of subduing them)) and we were not capable of owning them or making them subdued;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ إِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَتَقُولُواْ سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. In order that you may mount on their backs, and then may remember the Favour of your Lord when you mount thereon, and say: “Glory to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could have never had it (by our efforts)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that you may sit that you may find a firm position upon their backs He has made the suffixed pronoun a masculine plural and rendered zahr ‘back’ plural because of the particle mā and its plural import; and then remember your Lord’s grace when you are settled on them and say ‘Glory be to Him Who has disposed this for us and we by ourselves were no match for it not capable of it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ إِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَتَقُولُواْ سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. In order that you may mount on their backs, and then may remember the Favour of your Lord when you mount thereon, and say: “Glory to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could have never had it (by our efforts)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! unto our Lord we are returning) after we die.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And verily, to Our Lord we indeed are to return!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed it is to our Lord that we shall return’ to Him that we shall depart.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And verily, to Our Lord we indeed are to return!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they allot to Him) they ascribe to Him (a portion of His bondmen) i.e. the angels! They claimed, i.e. Banu Malih, that the angels were Allah's daughters. (Lo! Man) i.e. the Banu Malih (is verily a mere ingrate) a disbeliever in Allah whose disbelief is quite apparent.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلُواْ لَهُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ جُزْءًا إِنَّ ٱلإنسَانَ لَكَفُورٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Yet, they assign to some of His slaves a share with Him . Verily, man is indeed a manifest ingrate!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they assign to Him from among His own servants a part when they say that the angels are God’s daughters — for a child is a part of its parent — even though the angels are like them servants of His exalted be He. Man such as the one who says the above-mentioned words is verily a manifest ingrate one whose ungratefulness is manifest and clear.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلُواْ لَهُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ جُزْءًا إِنَّ ٱلإنسَانَ لَكَفُورٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Yet, they assign to some of His slaves a share with Him . Verily, man is indeed a manifest ingrate!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or chooseth He daughters of all that He hath created) i.e. of the angels, (and honours) and choose (He you) i.e. the Banu Malih (with sons?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ بَنَاتٍ وَأَصْفَاكُم بِٱلْبَنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Or has He taken daughters out of what He has created, and He has selected for you sons?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or am has the significance of the hamza of denial; the ‘saying’ is implied in other words a-taqūlūna ‘or do you say that …’ He has adopted from all that He has created daughters for Himself and preferred you privileged you with sons? — that which is the necessary inference from what you claim and which by itself is an abomination.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ بَنَاتٍ وَأَصْفَاكُم بِٱلْبَنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Or has He taken daughters out of what He has created, and He has selected for you sons?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And if one of them) one of the Banu Malih (hath tidings of that which he likeneth) of that which he ascribes (to the Beneficent One) i.e. daughters, (his countenance becometh black) of grief (and he is full of inward rage) would you then, O Banu Malih, like for Allah that which you do not like for yourselves?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِمَا ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مَثَلاً ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. And if one of them is informed of the news of (the birth of a girl) that which he sets forth as a parable to the Most Gracious (Allāh), his face becomes dark, and he is filled with grief !.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And when one of them is given the good tidings of that which he has attributed to the Compassionate One of that which he has likened to Him by the ascription to Him of daughters — for a child is likened to its parent; in other words when one of them is informed that a daughter has been born to him his face becomes darkened transformed into one laden with anguish and he chokes inwardly filled with anguish so how can such a person then attribute daughters to Him? Exalted be He high above such claims.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِمَا ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مَثَلاً ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. And if one of them is informed of the news of (the birth of a girl) that which he sets forth as a parable to the Most Gracious (Allāh), his face becomes dark, and he is filled with grief !.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Liken they then to Allah) that which is bred up in outward show) in ornaments of gold and silver, (and in dispute) in speech (cannot make itself plain) whose argument is not strong, i.e. women, how could they be the daughters of Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي ٱلْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. (Like they then for Allāh) a creature who is brought up in adornments (wearing silk and gold ornaments, i.e. women), and who, in dispute, cannot make herself clear?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: What! a-wa contains both the hamza of denial and the conjunctive waw ‘and’ in other words ‘do they ascribe to God …’ one that is brought up amid trinkets ornaments and is incoherent in a dispute? unable to argue clearly because of an inherent inability in this respect as a result of that person belonging to the female sex.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي ٱلْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. (Like they then for Allāh) a creature who is brought up in adornments (wearing silk and gold ornaments, i.e. women), and who, in dispute, cannot make herself clear?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they make the angels, who are the slaves of the Beneficent, females) the daughters of Allah. (Did they witness their creation) when they were created for them to know that they are females? They said: “no, O Muhammad, we did not witness their creation but we heard our fathers saying so”. Allah will say: “O Muhammad!” (Their testimony will be recorded) that they lie against Allah when they claim that the angels are Allah's daughters (and they will be questioned) about this claim on the Day of Judgement. In other words, when they claimed that the angels are Allah's daughters, they were asked: “did you witness their creation?” They said: “No!” “How did you then come to the conclusion that the angels are females and Allah's daughters?” They said: “We heard this from our fathers”. Allah said that their claim about the angels will be recorded and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلُواْ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ إِنَاثاً أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ سَتُكْتَبُ شَهَادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْأَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And they make the angels who themselves are slaves of the Most Gracious (Allāh) females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they have made the angels who are themselves servants of the Compassionate One females. Did they witness were they present at their creation? Their testimony to the effect that they are females will be written down and they will be questioned about it in the Hereafter wherefore punishment will ensue for them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلُواْ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ إِنَاثاً أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ سَتُكْتَبُ شَهَادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْأَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And they make the angels who themselves are slaves of the Most Gracious (Allāh) females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they) i.e. the Banu Malih (say: If the Beneficent One had (so) willed) if the Beneficent one had repelled and warned us, (we should not have worshipped them) they said this out of mockery, “but He commanded us to worship them and never warned us against such a worship”. (They have no knowledge whatsoever of that) they have no proof or warrant for what they say. (They do but guess) they do but lie against Allah because they were forbidden from worshipping them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ مَا عَبَدْنَاهُمْ مَّا لَهُم بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَخْرُصُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And they said: “If it had been the Will of the Most Gracious (Allāh), we would not have worshipped them (false deities).” They have no knowledge whatsoever of that. They do nothing but lie!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they say ‘Had the Compassionate One so willed we would not have worshipped them’ the angels therefore our worship of them happens by His will and so He must be satisfied with it. God exalted be He says They do not have any knowledge of that which is said of His being satisfied with the worship of these angels; and they are only surmising inventing lies in this respect and so punishment will befall them as a result thereof.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ مَا عَبَدْنَاهُمْ مَّا لَهُم بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَخْرُصُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And they said: “If it had been the Will of the Most Gracious (Allāh), we would not have worshipped them (false deities).” They have no knowledge whatsoever of that. They do nothing but lie!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or have We given them any Scripture before) this Qur'an (so that they are holding fast thereto) so that they take such a belief from this Scripture?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ كِتَاباً مِّن قَبْلِهِ فَهُم بِهِ مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Or have We given them any Book before this (the Qur’ān) to which they are holding fast?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or have We brought them a scripture before that is before the Qur’ān that they should worship other than God so that they are holding fast to it? In other words this never happened.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ كِتَاباً مِّن قَبْلِهِ فَهُم بِهِ مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Or have We given them any Book before this (the Qur’ān) to which they are holding fast?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: They said: “We do not have, O Muhammad, any other Scripture; but we found our fathers on this belief”. Allah said: (Nay, for they say only: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footprints) and we are following their religion and actions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ءَاثَارِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. Nay! They say: “We found our fathers following a certain way and religion, and we guide ourselves by their footsteps.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay but they say ‘Lo! we found our fathers following a certain creed and we are indeed proceeding in their footsteps to be guided’ by them for they used to worship other than God.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ءَاثَارِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. Nay! They say: “We found our fathers following a certain way and religion, and we guide ourselves by their footsteps.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And even so) just as your own folk said (We sent not a warner) a warning prophet (before thee (Muhammad) into any township) to the inhabitants of any township (but its luxurious ones) the tyrants among them (said: Lo! We found our fathers following a religion) following this religion, (and we are following their footprints) and we are emulating their religion and actions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَذَلِكَ مَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلاَّ قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ءَاثَارِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. And similarly, We sent not a warner before you (O Muḥammad ) to any town (people) but the luxurious ones among them said: “We found our fathers following a certain way and religion, and we will indeed follow their footsteps.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And thus We never sent a warner before you into any city without that its affluent folk those of comfortable means said the like of what your people say ‘Lo! we found our fathers following a certain creed and so we are indeed following in their footsteps’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَذَلِكَ مَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلاَّ قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ءَاثَارِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. And similarly, We sent not a warner before you (O Muḥammad ) to any town (people) but the luxurious ones among them said: “We found our fathers following a certain way and religion, and we will indeed follow their footsteps.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) to them, O Muhammad: (What! Even though I bring you better guidance) a truer religion (than that ye found your fathers following) would you not accept it? (They answered: Lo! in what ye bring) of Scripture (we are disbelievers) we are deniers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَٰلَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمْ عَلَيْهِ آبَآءَكُمْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. (The warner) said: “Even if I bring you better guidance than that which you found your fathers following?” They said: “Verily, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say to them ‘What! Will you follow them even if I bring you a better means to guidance than what you found your fathers following?’ They say ‘Lo! we disbelieve in what you and those before you are sent with’. God exalted be He says to them as a threat to them

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَٰلَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمْ عَلَيْهِ آبَآءَكُمْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. (The warner) said: “Even if I bring you better guidance than that which you found your fathers following?” They said: “Verily, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So We requited them) by sending punishment upon them when they denied the messengers and Scriptures. (Then see the nature of the consequence for the rejecters) then see the ultimate end of the deniers of Scriptures and messengers!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. So We took revenge on them, then see what was the end of those who denied (Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So We took vengeance on them that is to say on those who denied the messengers before you; behold then how was the sequel for the deniers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. So We took revenge on them, then see what was the end of those who denied (Islāmic Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And when Abraham said unto his father) Azar (and his folk) when He was sent to them: (Lo! I am innocent of what ye worship

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And (remember) when Ibrāhīm (Abraham) said to his father and his people: “Verily, I am innocent of what you worship,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And mention when Abraham said to his father and his people ‘Surely I am innocent of that which you worship

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And (remember) when Ibrāhīm (Abraham) said to his father and his people: “Verily, I am innocent of what you worship,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Save Him Who did create me) except He Whom I worship, He Who created me, (for He will surely guide me) He will preserve me on His religion and obedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. “Except Him (i.e. I worship none but Allāh Alone) Who did create me; and verily, He will guide me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except Him Who originated created me; for He will indeed guide me’ He will show me the way to His religion.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. “Except Him (i.e. I worship none but Allāh Alone) Who did create me; and verily, He will guide me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he made It) i.e. “there is no deity except Allah” (a word enduring) firm (among his seed) the offspring of Abraham, (that haply they might return) that his folk may return from their disbelief to the belief in Allah's divine Oneness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. And he made it [i.e. Lā ilāha illallāh (none has the right to be worshipped but Allāh Alone-True Monotheism)] a Word lasting among his offspring, that they may turn back (i.e. to repent to Allāh or receive admonition)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And he made it namely the statement of the affirmation of God’s Oneness understood from his words I shall indeed depart to my Lord; He will guide me Q. 3799 a word enduring among his posterity his descendants and thus there still remains among them those who affirm the Oneness of God; that perhaps they that is the people of Mecca might recant what they follow and return to the religion of their forefather Abraham.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. And he made it [i.e. Lā ilāha illallāh (none has the right to be worshipped but Allāh Alone-True Monotheism)] a Word lasting among his offspring, that they may turn back (i.e. to repent to Allāh or receive admonition)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but I let these) the people of Mecca (and their fathers) before them (enjoy life (only) till there should come unto them the Truth) the Scripture (and a messenger making plain) who explains the Truth to these people in a language they understand.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ وَآبَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Nay, but I gave (the good things of this life) to these (polytheists) and their fathers to enjoy, till there came to them the truth (the Qur’ān), and a Messenger (Muḥammad ) making things clear..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay but I have let these idolaters and their fathers enjoy life without hastening to punish them until there came to them the truth the Qur’ān and a messenger who makes things clear one who manifests to them the stipulations of the Law — and this messenger is Muhammad (s).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ وَآبَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُّبِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Nay, but I gave (the good things of this life) to these (polytheists) and their fathers to enjoy, till there came to them the truth (the Qur’ān), and a Messenger (Muḥammad ) making things clear..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And now that the Truth) the Scripture and Messenger (hath come unto them they say: This) i.e. this Scripture (is mere magic) is a mere lie, (and lo! we are disbelievers therein) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ قَالُواْ هَـٰذَا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِ كَافِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. And when the truth (this Qur’ān) came to them, they (the disbelievers in this Qur’ān) said: “This is magic, and we disbelieve therein.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But when the truth the Qur’ān came to them they said ‘This is sorcery and we are indeed disbelievers in it’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ قَالُواْ هَـٰذَا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِ كَافِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. And when the truth (this Qur’ān) came to them, they (the disbelievers in this Qur’ān) said: “This is magic, and we disbelieve therein.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they) i.e. the people of Mecca: al-Walid and his host (say: If only this Qur'an had been revealed to some great man of the two towns) i.e. to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah and Abu Mas'ud al-Thaqafi from Mecca and Ta'if respectively?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. And they say: “Why is not this Qur’ān sent down to some great man of the two towns (Makkah and Tā’if)?” *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they said ‘If only this Qur’ān had been revealed to some great man from the inhabitants of the two towns!’ in other words from either of the two; such as al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra at Mecca or ‘Urwa b. Mas‘ūd al-Thaqafī at Tā’if.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. And they say: “Why is not this Qur’ān sent down to some great man of the two towns (Makkah and Tā’if)?” *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Is it they who apportion their Lord's mercy) i.e. your Lord's prophethood and Scriptures, such that they give it to whoever they will? (We have apportioned among them their livelihood) their wealth and children (in the life of the world, and raised some of them above others in rank) and We raised the merits of some above others in relation to wealth and offspring (that some of them may take labour from others) that some may use others in the capacity of servants and slaves; (and the mercy of thy Lord) i.e. prophethood and Scripture; and it is also said that this means: Paradise for the believers (is better than (the wealth) that they amass) is better than what the disbelievers amass of wealth and adornment in the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضاً سُخْرِيّاً وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. Is it they who would portion out the Mercy of your Lord? It is We Who portion out between them their livelihood in this world, and We raised some of them above others in ranks, so that some may employ others in their work. But the Mercy (Paradise) of your Lord (O Muḥammad ) is better than the (wealth of this world) which they amass..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? the mercy being prophethood. We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world making some of them wealthy and others poor and raised some of them in wealth above others by degrees so that some of them who are wealthy may take others who are poor in service disposed to work for them in return for a wage the final yā’ in sukhriyyā is attributive; a variant reading has sikhriyyan; and the mercy of your Lord that is Paradise is better than what they amass in this world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضاً سُخْرِيّاً وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. Is it they who would portion out the Mercy of your Lord? It is We Who portion out between them their livelihood in this world, and We raised some of them above others in ranks, so that some may employ others in their work. But the Mercy (Paradise) of your Lord (O Muḥammad ) is better than the (wealth of this world) which they amass..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And were it not that mankind would have become one community) i.e. follow one religion, the religion of disbelief, (We might well have appointed, for those who disbelieve in the Beneficent, roofs) the roofs of their houses (of silver for their houses and stairs (of silver) whereby to mount) whereby to climb,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. And were it not that mankind would have become one community (all disbelievers desiring worldly life only), We would have provided for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious (Allāh), silver roofs for their houses, and elevators whereby they ascend,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And were it not for the danger that mankind would be one community following disbelief We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Compassionate One roofs read saqfan or plural suqufan of silver for their houses li-buyūtihim substitutes for li-man ‘for those who’ and stairs such as steps also of silver by which they ascend by which they go up to the roof;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. And were it not that mankind would have become one community (all disbelievers desiring worldly life only), We would have provided for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious (Allāh), silver roofs for their houses, and elevators whereby they ascend,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And for their houses doors (of silver) and couches of silver whereon to recline) to sleep,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْوَاباً وَسُرُراً عَلَيْهَا يَتَّكِئُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. And for their houses, doors (of silver), and thrones (of silver) on which they could recline,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and doors of silver for their houses and We would have made for them couches of silver surur ‘couches’ is the plural of sarīr on which they recline

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْوَاباً وَسُرُراً عَلَيْهَا يَتَّكِئُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. And for their houses, doors (of silver), and thrones (of silver) on which they could recline,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And ornaments of gold) and all the gold and silver utensils of their houses. (Yet all that would have been but a provision of the life of the world) yet all that would be but the stuff of the life of the world. (And the Hereafter) i.e. Paradise (with your Lord would have been for those who keep from evil) for those who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies; this is much better than the stuff of the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَزُخْرُفاً وَإِن كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. And adornments of gold. Yet all this (i.e. the roofs, doors, stairs, elevators, thrones of their houses) would have been nothing but an enjoyment of this world. And the Hereafter with your Lord is (only) for the Muttaqūn (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and ornaments gold in other words were it not for fear that a believer might disbelieve as a result of Our giving the disbeliever what has been mentioned We would have given him such luxuries since the affairs of this world represent no danger to Us and he the disbeliever would then have no share in the Bliss of the Hereafter. Yet surely wa-in in is softened from the hardened form inna all that would be nothing read lamā with the mā as extra; or read lammā to mean ‘but’ making the particle in for negation but the transient enjoyment of the life of this world enjoyed during it but then perishes and the Hereafter Paradise with your Lord is for the God-fearing.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَزُخْرُفاً وَإِن كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. And adornments of gold. Yet all this (i.e. the roofs, doors, stairs, elevators, thrones of their houses) would have been nothing but an enjoyment of this world. And the Hereafter with your Lord is (only) for the Muttaqūn (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he whose sight is dim to the remembrance of the Beneficent) and he who is blind to the declaration of the divine Oneness and Scripture of the Beneficent, (We assign unto him a devil who becometh his comrade) in the life of the world and in the Fire;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And whosoever turns away blindly from the remembrance of the Most Gracious (Allāh) (i.e. this Qur’ān and worship of Allāh), We appoint for him Shaiṭān (Satan - devil) to be a companion to him. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And whoever withdraws from whoever is oblivious to the Remembrance of the Compassionate One namely the Qur’ān We assign We produce for him a devil and he becomes his companion never leaving his side.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And whosoever turns away blindly from the remembrance of the Most Gracious (Allāh) (i.e. this Qur’ān and worship of Allāh), We appoint for him Shaiṭān (Satan - devil) to be a companion to him. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! They) i.e. the devils (surely turn them from the way of Allah) from the Truth and guidance, (and yet they deem that they are rightly guided) to the Truth and guidance;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And verily, they (Satans / devils) hinder them from the Path (of Allāh), but they think that they are guided aright!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed they that is the devils bar them the blind from the way from the path of guidance while they suppose that they are rightly guided the plural muhtadūna takes into account the potentially plural sense of man ‘whoever’ of the previous verse

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And verily, they (Satans / devils) hinder them from the Path (of Allāh), but they think that they are guided aright!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Till, when he) i.e. the son of Adam along with his comrade the devil, tied to one chain (cometh unto Us, he saith) unto his devil comrade: (Ah, would that between me and thee there were the distance of the two horizons, an evil comrade) and friend!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرِينُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. Till, when (such a one) comes to Us, he says to his companion) “Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts (or the east and west)” — a worst (type of) companion (indeed)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: until when he comes to Us such a blind one together with his companion on the Day of Resurrection he says to him ‘O yā is for calling attention would that there were between me and you the distance of the two easts!’ that is to say like the distance between the east and the west What an evil companion then! you are for me. God exalted be He says

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرِينُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. Till, when (such a one) comes to Us, he says to his companion) “Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts (or the east and west)” — a worst (type of) companion (indeed)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And it profiteth you not) Allah says: it profits you not (this day) such talk, (because ye did wrong) because you disbelieved in the life of the world, (that ye will be sharers in the doom) the devils and the children of Adam.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. It will profit you not this Day (O you who turn away from Allāh’s remembrance and His worship) as you did wrong, (and) that you will be sharers (you and your Qarīn) in the punishment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And it your wishes or your remorse will not benefit you blind ones this day given that you did wrong that is to say given that it has become clear to you that you were wrongdoers through your idolatry in this world that you together with your companions will be sharing in the chastisement this constitutes the justification on the basis of an implied lām sc. li-annakum … for the ‘lack of benefit’; idh substitutes for al-yawma ‘this day’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. It will profit you not this Day (O you who turn away from Allāh’s remembrance and His worship) as you did wrong, (and) that you will be sharers (you and your Qarīn) in the punishment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Canst thou) O Muhammad (make the deaf to hear) make the one who pretends to be deaf hear the Truth and guidance, (or canst thou guide the blind) or guide the disbeliever to see the Truth and guidance (or him who is in error manifest) whom you cannot guide to the guidance?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَأَنتَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ أَوْ تَهْدِي ٱلْعُمْيَ وَمَن كَانَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. Can you (O Muḥammad ) make the deaf hear, or can you guide the blind or him who is in manifest error?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Can you then make the deaf hear or can you guide the blind and one who is in manifest error? in other words such individuals will not believe.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَأَنتَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ أَوْ تَهْدِي ٱلْعُمْيَ وَمَن كَانَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. Can you (O Muḥammad ) make the deaf hear, or can you guide the blind or him who is in manifest error?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And if We take thee away) if We make you die, (We surely shall take vengeance on them) by punishing them,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And even if We take you (O Muḥammad ) away, We shall indeed take vengeance on them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So if fa-immā the conditional particle in has been assimilated herein with an extra mā We take you away by making you die before chastising them then We will take vengeance on them in the Hereafter;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And even if We take you (O Muḥammad ) away, We shall indeed take vengeance on them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or (if) We show thee that wherewith We threaten them) on the Day of Badr; (for lo! We have complete command of them) We are able to punish them before your death and after it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ ٱلَّذِي وَعَدْنَاهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُّقْتَدِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. Or (if) We show you that wherewith We threaten them: then verily We have perfect command over them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: or We show you during your lifetime that which We have promised them in the way of chastisement for surely We have power over surely We are able to chastise them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ ٱلَّذِي وَعَدْنَاهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُّقْتَدِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. Or (if) We show you that wherewith We threaten them: then verily We have perfect command over them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So hold thou fast to) act upon (that which is inspired in you) i.e. the Qur'an. (Lo! thou) O Muhammad (art on a right path) are on an established religion with which Allah is pleased.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْتَمْسِكْ بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. So, hold you (O Muḥammad ) fast to that which is revealed to you. Verily, you are on a Straight Path..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you namely the Qur’ān; surely you are on a straight path a straight way.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْتَمْسِكْ بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. So, hold you (O Muḥammad ) fast to that which is revealed to you. Verily, you are on a Straight Path..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo!) i.e. the Qur'an (is in truth a Reminder for thee) an honour for you (and for thy folk) the Quraysh because it is revealed in their own language; (and ye will be questioned) about the gratitude which is owed to such an honour.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ وَسَوْفَ تُسْأَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. And verily, this (the Qur’ān) is indeed a Reminder for you (O Muḥammad ) and your people (Quraish people, or your followers), and you will be questioned (about it)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And it is indeed a Reminder an honour for you and for your people as it has been revealed in their language. And you will eventually be questioned about the extent of your fulfilling your duty towards it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ وَسَوْفَ تُسْأَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. And verily, this (the Qur’ān) is indeed a Reminder for you (O Muḥammad ) and your people (Quraish people, or your followers), and you will be questioned (about it)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And ask those of Our messengers) such as Jesus, Moses and Abraham; this was on the night when he was taken up to heaven and he led in prayer 70 prophets, among whom were Abraham, Moses and Jesus. Allah commanded His Prophet, saying: ask them (whom We sent before thee) O Muhammad: (Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped beside the Beneficent) did We command that any other deity beside the Beneficent be worshipped? It is also said that this means: ask those unto whom We sent the messengers before you, i.e. the people of Book, did We appoint any other deities beside the Beneficent to be worshipped? And it is also said that this means: ask them, did the messengers bring anything other than the profession of Allah's divine Oneness; the Prophet did not have to ask because he was certain that Allah did not appoint any other deities to be worshipped beside Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And ask (O Muḥammad ) those of Our Messengers whom We sent before you: “Did We ever appoint ālihāh (gods) to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious (Allāh)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you Did We ever appoint besides the Compassionate One that is to say any other than Him gods to be worshipped? It is said that this is to be understood literally in other words that God gathered for him all the messengers on the Night of the Journey; but it is also said that this meant that he should ask any communities belonging to either of the two Peoples of the Scripture. According to one of the two opinions he never asked anyone since the point of this command to ask is to affirm to the idolaters of Quraysh that no messenger or scripture ever came from God with the command to worship any other than God.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And ask (O Muḥammad ) those of Our Messengers whom We sent before you: “Did We ever appoint ālihāh (gods) to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious (Allāh)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We sent Moses with Our revelations) the hand and the staff (unto Pharaoh and his chiefs) and his folk the Copts, (and he said: I am a messenger of the Lord of the Worlds) to you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِآيَـٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلإِيْهِ فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. And indeed We did send Mūsā (Moses) with Our Āyāt (proofs, evidences, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) and his chiefs (inviting them to Allāh’s religion of Islām) He said: “Verily, I am a Messenger of the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his council namely the Egyptians al-Qibt and he said ‘I am indeed the messenger of the Lord of the Worlds’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِآيَـٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلإِيْهِ فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. And indeed We did send Mūsā (Moses) with Our Āyāt (proofs, evidences, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) and his chiefs (inviting them to Allāh’s religion of Islām) He said: “Verily, I am a Messenger of the Lord of the ‘Ālamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But when he) Moses (brought them Our tokens) the hand and the staff, (behold! they laughed at them) they were first amazed but then mocked these signs, refusing thus to believe in them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِآيَاتِنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَضْحَكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. But, when he came to them with Our Āyāt (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations) behold, they laughed at them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But when he brought them Our signs those proving his mission from God behold! they laughed at them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِآيَاتِنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَضْحَكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. But, when he came to them with Our Āyāt (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations) behold, they laughed at them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And every token) sign (that We showed them was greater than its sister (token)) that We sent before it, even so they refused to believe, (and we grasped them with the torment) with the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, shortage of foodstuffs and years of drought, (that haply they might turn again) that haply they might desist from their disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا نُرِيِهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ إِلاَّ هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا وَأَخَذْنَاهُم بِٱلْعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And not an Āyah (sign, etc.) We showed them but it was greater than its fellow, and We seized them with torment, in order that they might turn [from their polytheism to Allāh’s religion (Islāmic Monotheism)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We never showed them a sign from among the signs of chastisement such as the flood which was when the waters of the Nile penetrated their dwellings and for seven days rose as high as their throats as they sat or the chastisement of the locusts but it was greater than the one before it the one immediately preceding it. And We seized them with chastisement that perhaps they might recant their disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا نُرِيِهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ إِلاَّ هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا وَأَخَذْنَاهُم بِٱلْعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And not an Āyah (sign, etc.) We showed them but it was greater than its fellow, and We seized them with torment, in order that they might turn [from their polytheism to Allāh’s religion (Islāmic Monotheism)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they said: O wizard) O knowledgeable wizard, as a form of respect, because magicians were venerated amongst them; (Entreat thy Lord for us by the pact that He hath made with thee) ask your Lord by the pact Allah made with you-the pact was that if they believed He will remove His punishment from them-this is why they asked him by the pact that Allah had made. (Lo! we verily will walk aright) we will believe in you and in that which you brought.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ يَٰأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. And they said [to Mūsā (Moses)]: “O you sorcerer! Invoke your Lord for us accord ing to what He has covenanted with you. Verily, We shall guide ourselves (aright).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they said to Moses upon seeing the chastisement ‘O sorcerer! — that is to say ‘O knowledgeable perfect one’ since for them sorcery was an awesome form of knowledge — supplicate your Lord for us by the covenant that He has made with you to the effect that He would relieve us from chastisement if we believe. Assuredly we will be guided’ that is to say we will become believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالُواْ يَٰأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهْتَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. And they said [to Mūsā (Moses)]: “O you sorcerer! Invoke your Lord for us accord ing to what He has covenanted with you. Verily, We shall guide ourselves (aright).”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But when We eased them of the torment) when We removed the torment from them, (behold! they broke their word) they broke their undertaking and refused to believe.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. But when We removed the torment from them, behold, they broke their covenant (that they will believe if We remove the torment from them)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But as soon as We relieved them by the supplication of Moses from the chastisement behold! they had broken their pledge reneging on their covenant and persisting in their disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. But when We removed the torment from them, behold, they broke their covenant (that they will believe if We remove the torment from them)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Pharaoh caused a proclamation to be made among his people) Pharaoh delivered a sermon to his people, the Copts, (saying: O my people! Is not mine the sovereignty of Egypt) which is 40 square parasangs (and these rivers flowing under me) around me; it is also said what he meant here is: and these horses run around me? (Can ye not then discern?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَادَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ أَلَيْسَ لِي مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْهَارُ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِيۤ أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) proclaimed among his people (saying): “O my people! Is not mine the dominion of Egypt, and these rivers flowing underneath me. See you not then?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And Pharaoh proclaimed boastfully among his people ‘O my people does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me and these rivers of the Nile flowing beneath me? that is to say beneath my palaces. Do you not perceive? my magnificence.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَادَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ أَلَيْسَ لِي مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْهَارُ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِيۤ أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) proclaimed among his people (saying): “O my people! Is not mine the dominion of Egypt, and these rivers flowing underneath me. See you not then?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: I am surely better than this fellow, who is despicable) physically weak, (and can hardly make (his meaning) plain) his argument plain!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. “Am I not better than this one [Mūsā (Moses)] who is despicable and can scarcely express himself clearly?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or do you perceive in which case am I not better than this one namely Moses who is contemptible feeble and lowly and who can scarcely speak clearly? who can scarcely articulate his speech because of his lisp — which was the result of his accidentally placing a hot coal in his mouth when he was a child.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. “Am I not better than this one [Mūsā (Moses)] who is despicable and can scarcely express himself clearly?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Why, then, have armlets of gold not been set upon him) as you yourselves are wearing, (or angels sent along with him) to help him and affirm the message with which he is sent?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. “Why then are not golden bracelets bestowed on him, or angels sent along with him?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Why then if he were being truthful have bracelets of gold asāwira is the plural of aswira which is the plural of siwār similar in pattern to ghurāb aghriba not been cast on him — as according to their custom with those whom they made their leaders dressing them with gold bracelets and gold necklaces — or the angels not come with him one after the other?’ in succession to testify to his truthfulness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. “Why then are not golden bracelets bestowed on him, or angels sent along with him?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thus he persuaded his people) the Copts (to make light (of Moses), and they obeyed him) in what he said. (Lo! they were a wanton folk) they were disbelieving folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ فَأَطَاعُوهُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَوْماً فَاسِقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. Thus he [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] befooled (and misled) his people, and they obeyed him. Verily, they were ever a people who were Fāsiqūn (rebellious, disobedient to Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thus did he Pharaoh persuade incite his people and they obeyed him in his wish that Moses be denied. They were truly an immoral folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ فَأَطَاعُوهُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَوْماً فَاسِقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. Thus he [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] befooled (and misled) his people, and they obeyed him. Verily, they were ever a people who were Fāsiqūn (rebellious, disobedient to Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So, when they angered Us) when they angered Our Prophet Moses, and tended to anger Us, (We punished them and drowned them every one) in the sea.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. So when they angered Us, We punished them, and drowned them all..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So when they had angered Us We took vengeance on them and drowned them all.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. So when they angered Us, We punished them, and drowned them all..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We made them a thing past) by means of the punishment, (and an example) and a lesson (for those after (them)) for those who remained after them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً وَمَثَلاً لِّلآخِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. And We made them a precedent (as a lesson for those coming after them), and an example to later generations..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We made them a thing past salaf is the plural of sālif similar in pattern to khādim khadam that is to say a precedent as a lesson and an example for others after them that they posterity might take their predicament as a lesson and so not engage in actions similar to theirs.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً وَمَثَلاً لِّلآخِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. And We made them a precedent (as a lesson for those coming after them), and an example to later generations..
