meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَاهَا وَزَيَّنَّاهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Have they not looked at the heaven above them, how We have made it and adorned it, and there are no rifts in it?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the earth have We spread out) over water, (and have flung firm hills) firm mountains so that it does not sway (therein) on the earth, (and have caused of every lovely kind to grow thereon) and have caused of every kind of seemly appearance to grow thereon,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And the earth! We have spread it out, and set thereon mountains standing firm, and have produced therein every kind of lovely growth (plants)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the earth wa’l-arda is a supplement to the position of the words ilā l-samā’i ‘at the heaven’ how We have spread it out how We have rolled it across the face of the water and cast in it firm mountains to fix it in place and caused every delightful kind every delightful specimen causing delight by its very beauty to grow in it

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And the earth! We have spread it out, and set thereon mountains standing firm, and have produced therein every kind of lovely growth (plants)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (A vision) so that you may see (and a reminder) a lesson so that you may learn from it; it is also said “a vision” means an admonition and “reminder” means reflection (for every penitent slave) who turns to Allah and His obedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُّنِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. An insight and a Reminder for every slave who turns to Allāh in repentance ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: as an insight tabsiratan is a direct object denoting reason that is to say We did this to give an insight from Us and a reminder for every penitent servant who returns to obedience of Us.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُّنِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. An insight and a Reminder for every slave who turns to Allāh in repentance ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We send down from the sky blessed water) rain blessed with vegetation and benefit from which all things derive life (whereby We give growth unto gardens and the grain of crops) all kinds of grain that are harvested,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً مُّبَٰرَكاً فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ جَنَّٰتٍ وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And We send down blessed water (rain) from the sky, then We produce therewith gardens and grain (every kind of harvests) that are reaped..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We send down from the heaven blessed water containing much blessing with which We cause to grow gardens orchards and the grain that is harvested

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً مُّبَٰرَكاً فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ جَنَّٰتٍ وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And We send down blessed water (rain) from the sky, then We produce therewith gardens and grain (every kind of harvests) that are reaped..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lofty date-palms with ranged clusters,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And tall date‑palms, with ranged clusters..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the date-palms that stand tall bāsiqātin is an implied future circumstantial qualifier with piled spathes one cluster of dates sitting on top of the other

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And tall date‑palms, with ranged clusters..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Provision (made) for men) food for people, i.e. the grains; (and therewith) i.e. through water (We quicken a dead land) a land with no vegetation. (Even so will be the resurrection of the dead) this is how they will be brought back to life and raised forth from the graves through water on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رِّزْقاً لِّلْعِبَادِ وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً كَذَلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. A provision for (Allāh’s) slaves. And We give life therewith to a dead land. Thus will be the resurrection (of the dead)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: as provision for Our servants rizqan li’l-‘ibādi is a direct object denoting reason; and with it We revive a dead land baldatan may be followed equally by the masculine maytan or the feminine adjective maytatan. So like that manner of reviving shall be the rising from the graves so how can you deny it? the interrogative is meant as an affirmative; the meaning then is that they have indeed observed all of these things and are aware of what has been mentioned yet they disbelieve.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رِّزْقاً لِّلْعِبَادِ وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً كَذَلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. A provision for (Allāh’s) slaves. And We give life therewith to a dead land. Thus will be the resurrection (of the dead)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The folk of Noah denied) denied Noah (before them) before your folk, O Muhammad, (and (so did) the dwellers at al-Rass) al-Rass is a well close to al-Yamamah; the dwellers of al-Rass are the people of Shu'ayb who denied Shu'ayb (and (the tribe of) Thamud) the people of Salih,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Denied before them (i.e. these pagans of Makkah) the people of Nūḥ (Noah), and the Dwellers of Ar‑Rass, and Thamūd;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The people of Noah denied before them kadhdhabat has a feminine person inflection because of the feminine gender of the import of qawm ‘people’ and so did the dwellers at al-Rass — this was the name of a well around which they dwelt together with their livestock; they worshipped idols and it is said that their prophet was one Hanzala b. Safwān; but some say that he was some other person — and Thamūd the people of Sālih

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Denied before them (i.e. these pagans of Makkah) the people of Nūḥ (Noah), and the Dwellers of Ar‑Rass, and Thamūd;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (the tribe of) 'Aad) the people of Hud denied Hud, (and Pharaoh) and his folk denied Moses, (and the brethren of Lot) and the folk of Lot denied Lot,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعَادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوَانُ لُوطٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And ‘Ād, and Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and the brethren of Lūṭ (Lot);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and ‘Ād the people of Hūd and Pharaoh the brethren of Lot

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَعَادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوَانُ لُوطٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And ‘Ād, and Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and the brethren of Lūṭ (Lot);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the dwellers in the wood) the people of Shu'ayb denied Shu'ayb, (and the folk of Tubba') Tubba' was the king of Himyar. His name was As'ad Ibn Malkikarb, and his agnomen was Abu Karb and he was called Tubba' because of the huge number of his followers (atba'); he was also a person who surrendered to Allah: (every one) of these folk (denied their messengers) just as your folk, the Quraysh, denied you, (therefore My threat took effect) and therefore My punishment and torment were enjoined upon them when they denied the messengers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُّبَّعٍ كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And the Dwellers of the Wood, and the people of Tubba‘. Everyone of them denied (their) Messengers, so My Threat took effect..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the dwellers in the wood a small forest — the people of Shu‘ayb — and the people of Tubba‘ — a king who ruled in Yemen; he had submitted to God and had summoned his people to the same submission to God but they denied him. Each of those mentioned denied the messengers as your tribe Quraysh have and so My threat became due the sending down of chastisement on all of them became incumbent so do not be anguished by Quraysh’s disbelieving in you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُّبَّعٍ كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And the Dwellers of the Wood, and the people of Tubba‘. Everyone of them denied (their) Messengers, so My Threat took effect..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Were We then worn out by the first creation) such that We will be worn out by their second creation when We create them for resurrection after death? (Yet they) i.e. the Quraysh (are in doubt about a new creation) after death.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلأَوَّلِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Were We then tired with the first creation? Nay, they are in confused doubt about a new creation (i.e. Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Were We then wearied by the first creation? that is to say We were not wearied by it and likewise We will not be wearied by restoring it. Nay yet they are in doubt about a new creation which will be at the Resurrection.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلأَوَّلِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Were We then tired with the first creation? Nay, they are in confused doubt about a new creation (i.e. Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (We verily created a man) the child of Adam; and it is said this means: Abu Jahl (and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him) We are more aware of him and have more power over him (than his jugular vein) and there is nothing closer to man than this jugular vein.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. And indeed We have created man, and We know what his ownself whispers to him. And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein (by Our Knowledge)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We created man and We know wa-na‘lamu is a circumstantial qualifier with an implicit preceding nahnu what mā relates to the verbal action his soul whispers to him what it speaks to him the bi- of bihi ‘him’ is extra or it is required for the intransitive verb to become transitive and take a direct object; the suffixed personal pronoun in bihi ‘him’ refers to man; and We are nearer to him in knowing him than his jugular vein habli’l-warīdi the genitive annexation is explicative; al-warīdān are two principal veins on either side of the neck.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. And indeed We have created man, and We know what his ownself whispers to him. And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein (by Our Knowledge)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When the two Receivers receive (him)) when the two angels write, (seated on) one sitting on one side and the other on another side (the right hand) the right hand of the child of Adam (and on the left) the left hand of the child of Adam,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى ٱلْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. (Remember) that the two receivers (recording angels) receive (each human being),(1) one sitting on the right and one on the left (to note his or her actions)(2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When idh is dependent because of an implied udhkur ‘mention’ the two Receivers the two angels charged with recording a person’s deeds receive when they observe and record seated that is while both of them are sitting qa‘īdun ‘seated’ is the subject the predicate of which is the preceding clause on the right and on the left hand side of him —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى ٱلْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. (Remember) that the two receivers (recording angels) receive (each human being),(1) one sitting on the right and one on the left (to note his or her actions)(2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He uttereth no word) the slave utters no good or evil word (but there is with him an observer ready) to record either that which is in his advantage or disadvantage.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إِلاَّ لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Not a word does he (or she) utter but there is a watcher by him ready (to record it)(3)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: he does not utter a word but that there is beside him a watcher a guardian who is ready present both raqībun ‘watcher’ and ‘atīdun ‘ready’ are meant to indicate the dual.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إِلاَّ لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Not a word does he (or she) utter but there is a watcher by him ready (to record it)(3)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the agony of death) the pangs of death (cometh in truth) heralding either damnation or felicity. (This) child of Adam (is that which thou wast wont to shun) and dislike.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And the stupor of death will come in truth: “This is what you have been avoiding!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the agony of death its throes and distress arrives with the truth of the Hereafter such that the one who denied it sees it with his own eyes — and this is the distress itself. That namely death is what you used to shun what you used to flee from and be terrified by.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And the stupor of death will come in truth: “This is what you have been avoiding!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the trumpet is blown) this is the blowing of the resurrection. (This is the threatened Day) the threatened Day of the first and latter nations.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْوَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And the Trumpet will be blown — that will be the Day whereof warning (had been given) (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the Trumpet will be blown for resurrection. That namely the day of the blast is the Day of the Promised Threat of chastisement for the disbelievers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْوَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And the Trumpet will be blown — that will be the Day whereof warning (had been given) (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And every soul cometh, along with it a driver) leading it to its Lord; this driver is the angel who recorded the evil deeds it had committed (and a witness) before its Lord; this is the angels who recorded its good deeds; and it is also said that this witness is man's works.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَآءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And every person will come forth along with an (angel) to drive (him) and an (angel) to bear witness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And thereat every soul will come to the site for the Gathering accompanied by a driver an angel to drive it there and a witness to testify to its deeds namely the hands and the feet and others; and it will be said to the disbeliever

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَآءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And every person will come forth along with an (angel) to drive (him) and an (angel) to bear witness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thou wast) O child of Adam (in heedlessness) in ignorance and oblivion (of this) Day. (Now We have removed from thee your covering) your works, that which was concealed from you in the life of the world, (and piercing is your sight this day) and it is also said that this means: your knowledge is thorough this day.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّقَدْ كُنتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. (It will be said to the sinners): “Indeed, you were heedless of this. Now We have removed from you your covering, and sharp is your sight this Day!” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Verily in the world you were oblivious of this that has befallen you on this day; So now We have removed from you your covering We have done away with your oblivion by what you witness on this day and so your sight on this day is acute’ it is sharp able to perceive what you used to reject in the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّقَدْ كُنتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. (It will be said to the sinners): “Indeed, you were heedless of this. Now We have removed from you your covering, and sharp is your sight this Day!” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (unto the evil-doer) his comrade) the angel who recorded his good deeds; and it is said: the angel who recorded his evil works (saith: This is that which I have) this is that which with you have entrusted me (ready (as testimony)).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُ هَـٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. And his companion (angel) will say: “Here is (this Record) ready with me!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And his companion the angel charged with him will say ‘This is what I have ready with me as testimony’ whereupon it will be said to Mālik the Keeper of the Fire

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُ هَـٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. And his companion (angel) will say: “Here is (this Record) ready with me!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And Allah would say to him: (Do ye twain hurl to hell each rebel) who turns away from faith (ingrate) and who disbelieves in Allah, i.e. al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. (Allāh will say to the angels): “Both of you throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever (in the Oneness of Allāh, in His Messengers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Cast into Hell alqiyā meaning either alqi alqi ‘cast cast …’ to denote repetition or the emphatic form alqiyan ‘cast!’ which is the reading of al-Hasan al-Basrī in other words the final nūn has been changed into an alif every obdurate disbeliever obstinate to the truth

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. (Allāh will say to the angels): “Both of you throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever (in the Oneness of Allāh, in His Messengers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hinderer of good) i.e. Islam, he hindered his sons and his grandchildren and brother's children and family, relatives and kinsfolk, (transgressor) oppressor, (doubter) whose doubt is quite manifest and who further lies against Allah,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ مُّرِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. “Hinderer of good, transgressor, doubter,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: hinderer of good such as the payment of alms transgressor wrongdoer skeptic a doubter of his religion

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ مُّرِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. “Hinderer of good, transgressor, doubter,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who setteth up another god along with Allah) who claims that Allah has a son and a partner. (Do ye twain hurl him to the dreadful doom) Allah would say to the angels who recorded his deeds: cast him in the severe torment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهاً آخَرَ فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلشَّدِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. “Who set up another ilāh (god) with Allāh. Then both of you cast him in the severe torment.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: who has set up alongside God another god! alladhī ja‘ala ma‘a’Llāhi ilāhan ākhara is the subject with an implicitly conditional import the predicate of which is the following. Cast him then into the severe chastisement’ the explanation of this dual form of the verb alqiyāhu ‘cast him’ is as above.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهاً آخَرَ فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلشَّدِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. “Who set up another ilāh (god) with Allāh. Then both of you cast him in the severe torment.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (His comrade) the angel who recorded his evil deeds (saith: Our Lord! I did not cause him to rebel) “I did not hasten to record his evil deeds nor did I record that which he has never said or done”; this will be said when the disbeliever will claim that the angel hastened to write his evil deeds and recorded that which he never said or did. it is also said that his comrade is his devil who will plead with Allah that he did not cause him to rebel or err (but be was (himself) far gone in error) far from the Truth and guidance.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ قرِينُهُ رَبَّنَا مَآ أَطْغَيْتُهُ وَلَـٰكِن كَانَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ بَعِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. His companion (Satan — devil)] will say: “Our Lord! I did not push him to transgression, (in disbelief, oppression, and evil deeds), but he was himself in error far astray.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And his companion Satan will say ‘Our Lord! I did not make him a rebel I did not lead him astray but he himself was in extreme error’ and so when I invited him to disobedience he heeded my call — for this one had said ‘he Satan made me a rebel’ by way of his Satan’s invitation to him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ قرِينُهُ رَبَّنَا مَآ أَطْغَيْتُهُ وَلَـٰكِن كَانَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ بَعِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. His companion (Satan — devil)] will say: “Our Lord! I did not push him to transgression, (in disbelief, oppression, and evil deeds), but he was himself in error far astray.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He saith) Allah says to them: (Contend not in My presence, when I had already proffered unto you the warning) I have informed you in the Scripture with which the Messenger was sent about this Day.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لاَ تَخْتَصِمُواْ لَدَيَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُم بِٱلْوَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Allāh will say: “Dispute not in front of Me, I had already in advance sent you a warning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He exalted be He will say ‘Do not dispute in My presence in other words disputing is of no use here for I had already given you in the life of the world the threat of chastisement in the Hereafter should you not believe and so it is now inevitable.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ لاَ تَخْتَصِمُواْ لَدَيَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُم بِٱلْوَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Allāh will say: “Dispute not in front of Me, I had already in advance sent you a warning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The sentence that cometh from Me cannot be changed) My words cannot be changed through lying; and it is also said that this means: My decree concerning My salves will not be changed this Day; and it is also said that this means: words cannot be twisted in My presence, (and I am in nowise a tyrant unto the slaves) such that I would punish them without them having committed a crime.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ وَمَآ أَنَاْ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. The Sentence that comes from Me cannot be changed, and I am not unjust to the slaves.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The word that comes from Me in this respect cannot be altered and I am not unjust to servants’ that I should chastise them without any guilt on their part zallām means dhū zulm ‘one of injustice’ because of His words There will be no injustice today Q. 4017;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ وَمَآ أَنَاْ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. The Sentence that comes from Me cannot be changed, and I am not unjust to the slaves.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (On the day) this is the Day of Judgement (when We say unto hell: Art thou filled) as I have promised? (and it saith: Can there be more to come?) and it will have more; and it is also said that hell will say: I am quite full, I do not have room even for one extra man.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ ٱمْتَلأَتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. On the Day when We will say to Hell: “Are you filled?” It will say: “Are there any more (to come)?” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: on the day yawma is in the accusative because of zallām ‘unjust’ when We will say naqūlu may also be read yaqūlu ‘He will say’ to Hell ‘Are you now full?’ this interrogative is for confirmation of His promise to fill it with mankind and jinn and it will say by way of an interrogative such as a question ‘Are there any more?’ that is to say ‘I Hell only have capacity for what I have been filled with’ in other words ‘I am full!’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ ٱمْتَلأَتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. On the Day when We will say to Hell: “Are you filled?” It will say: “Are there any more (to come)?” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the Garden is brought nigh for those who kept from evil) those who warded off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies, (no longer distant) from them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. And Paradise will be brought near to the Muttaqūn (the pious)(2), not far off. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing to a place not far anymore from them and so they see it whereupon it will be said to them

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. And Paradise will be brought near to the Muttaqūn (the pious)(2), not far off. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((And it is said): That) reward and honour (is that which ye were promised) in the life of the world. ((It is) for every penitent) who turns to Allah and His obedience (and heedful one) observant of Allah's command in his private moment; and it is also said: in his prayers,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. (It will be said): “This is what you were promised — (it is) for those oft-returning (to Allāh) in sincere repentance, and those who preserve their covenant with Allāh ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘This that you see is what you were promised read tū‘adūna or third person plural yū‘adūna ‘they were promised’ in the world and what follows substitutes for li’l-muttaqīna ‘for the God-fearing’ — it is for every penitent one for every person reverting after sin to obedience of God who is mindful mindful of the bounds of God’s religion

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. (It will be said): “This is what you were promised — (it is) for those oft-returning (to Allāh) in sincere repentance, and those who preserve their covenant with Allāh ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who feareth the Beneficent in secret) who strives for the Beneficent even he has not seen Him (and cometh with a contrite heart) sincere in his worship and profession of Allah's divine Oneness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّنْ خَشِيَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَجَآءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُّنِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. “Who feared the Most Gracious (Allāh) in the Ghaib (Unseen) and came with a heart turned in repentance (to Him and absolutely free from each and every kind of polytheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: who fears the Compassionate One while He is in the Unseen the one who fears Him without having seen Him and comes with a penitent heart’ a heart eagerly applying itself to obedience of Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّنْ خَشِيَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَجَآءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُّنِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. “Who feared the Most Gracious (Allāh) in the Ghaib (Unseen) and came with a heart turned in repentance (to Him and absolutely free from each and every kind of polytheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah will say to them: (Enter it) i.e. Paradise (in peace) in safety from Allah's chastisement. (This is the day of immortality) the day when the dwellers of Paradise will enter Paradise to abide therein for eternity.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلاَمٍ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلُخُلُودِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. “Enter you therein in peace and security — this is the Day of eternal life!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It will also be said to the God-fearing ‘Enter it in peace! that is to say secure from every fear or it means enter it with a greeting that is to say greet yourselves and enter. That day in which this entry takes place is the day of immortality’ of everlastingness in Paradise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلاَمٍ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلُخُلُودِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. “Enter you therein in peace and security — this is the Day of eternal life!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There) in Paradise (they have all that they desire, and there is more with Us) i.e. beholding Allah's Countenance; and it is said that this means: in every hour and in every day, they have with Us an increase in honour and reward.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. There they will have all that they desire — and We have more (for them, i.e. a glance at the All-Mighty, All-Majestic B)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Therein they will have whatever they wish; and with Us there is yet more as extra for what they did and for what they will request.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. There they will have all that they desire — and We have more (for them, i.e. a glance at the All-Mighty, All-Majestic B)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And how many a generation) past generation (We destroyed before them) before your folk, (who were mightier than these) than your folk (in prowess) in physical strength (so that they overran the lands!) they moved about and travelled for their trade (Had they any place of refuge) or escape from Our chastisement? And it is also said this means: is there anyone of them left?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُم بَطْشاً فَنَقَّبُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And many a generation We have destroyed before them who were stronger in power than they. And (when Our Torment came), they ran for a refuge in the land! Could they find any place of refuge (for them to save themselves from destruction)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And how many a generation We destroyed before them that is before the disbelievers of Quraysh We destroyed many generations of disbelievers who were mightier than these in prowess and who then searched throughout the land wondering is there any escape? for them and others from death but they found none.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُم بَطْشاً فَنَقَّبُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And many a generation We have destroyed before them who were stronger in power than they. And (when Our Torment came), they ran for a refuge in the land! Could they find any place of refuge (for them to save themselves from destruction)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Therein) in that which was done with them (verily is a reminder) for your folk (for him who hath a heart) a living heart, (or giveth ear) or listens to the Qur'an (with full intelligence) with focus and not absentmindedly.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. Verily, therein is indeed a reminder for him who has a heart or gives ear while he is heedful..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly there is in that which is mentioned a reminder an admonition for him who has a heart a mind or gives ear or listens to admonitions in full witness present in heart and mind.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. Verily, therein is indeed a reminder for him who has a heart or gives ear while he is heedful..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them) of created beings and marvels, (in six Days) of the days of the beginning of the life of the world, each day the equivalent of 1,000 years of present days, the first day being Sunday and the last Friday, (and naught of weariness touched Us) We were not tired as claimed by the Jews who said: when Allah finished the creation of the heavens and earth, he put one leg on the other and rested on Saturday. The enemies of Allah have lied against Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. And indeed We created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six Days and nothing of fatigue touched Us..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days the first of which was Sunday and the last of which was Friday and no weariness no fatigue touched Us this was revealed as a refutation of the Jews’ claim that God rested on the Saturday and lay down upon the Throne. The preclusion of weariness in His case is absolute on account of His transcending of the attributes of creatures and the non-existence of any contiguity between Him and other beings His command when He wills a thing is just to say to it ‘Be’ and it is Q. 3682.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. And indeed We created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six Days and nothing of fatigue touched Us..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Therefore) O Muhammad (bear with what they say) bear with the lies of the Jews; it is also said this means: bear with what the deriders say; these are five people whom we have already mentioned somewhere else: (and hymn the praise of thy Lord) pray by the command of your Lord (before the rising) this is the morning prayer (and before the setting of the sun) these are the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ ٱلْغُرُوبِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. So bear with patience (O Muḥammad ) all that they say, and glorify the Praises of your Lord, before the rising of the sun and before (its) setting (i.e. the Fajr, Ẓuhr, and ‘Aṣr prayers)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So endure patiently addressing the Prophet s what they the Jews and others say in the way of anthropomorphic comparisons and denials and glorify with praise of your Lord perform prayers with praise of Him before the rising of the sun in other words perform the morning prayer and before the sunset that is to say perform both the midday and the afternoon prayers;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ ٱلْغُرُوبِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. So bear with patience (O Muḥammad ) all that they say, and glorify the Praises of your Lord, before the rising of the sun and before (its) setting (i.e. the Fajr, Ẓuhr, and ‘Aṣr prayers)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in the night time hymn His praise) pray for Him the prayers of Maghrib and 'Isha' or the prayer of tahajjud: (And after the (prescribed) prostrations) two units of prayer after the Maghrib.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ ٱلسُّجُودِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And during a part of the night (also) glorify His praises (i.e. Maghrib and ‘Isha prayers) and (so likewise) after the prayers [As-Sunnah, Nawāfil — optional and additional prayers. And also glorify, praise and magnify Allāh — Subḥān Allāh, Alḥamdu lillāh, Allāhu-Akbar]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and glorify Him at some part of the night that is to say perform the two evening prayers and after prostrations read adbār as the plural of dubur or idbār as the verbal noun from adbara ‘to pass’ in other words perform supererogatory prayers as prescribed by the Sunna after the obligatory ones; it is also said to mean the actual uttering of glorifications at these times with continuous praise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ ٱلسُّجُودِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And during a part of the night (also) glorify His praises (i.e. Maghrib and ‘Isha prayers) and (so likewise) after the prayers [As-Sunnah, Nawāfil — optional and additional prayers. And also glorify, praise and magnify Allāh — Subḥān Allāh, Alḥamdu lillāh, Allāhu-Akbar]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And listen on) O Muhammad, so that you can hear the description of it; it is also said that this means: strive, O Muhammad, for the day when the angel blows the Trumpet (the day when the crier crieth from a near place) close to heaven, from the dome of Jerusalem, which is the closest spot on earth to heaven by about 12 miles; and it is also said this means: from a close distance from which they can hear from beneath their feet.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And listen, on the Day when the caller will call from a near place..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And listen — O addressee to My words — on the day when the caller namely the archangel Isrāfīl calls out from a place that is near to the heaven this is the Rock of the Holy House of Jerusalem the place on earth that is the nearest to the heaven. He Isrāfīl will say ‘O withered bones severed limbs torn flesh and scattered hairs! God verily commands you to come together for the passing of judgement’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And listen, on the Day when the caller will call from a near place..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth) coming forth from the graves. (That is the day of coming forth (from the graves)) which is the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيْحَةَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْخُرُوجِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. The Day when they will hear Aṣ-Ṣaiḥah (shout) in truth: that will be the Day of coming out (from the graves, i.e. the Day of Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: On the day yawma substitutes for the previous yawma when they that is all creatures hear the Call of truth of the Resurrection — this will be Isrāfīl’s second blast and it may precede or follow his initial call — that day of the call and the hearing is the day of coming forth from the graves yawma ‘on the day is in the accusative because of an implied yunādī ‘when he will call’ that is to say they will come to know the consequence of their denial.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيْحَةَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْخُرُوجِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. The Day when they will hear Aṣ-Ṣaiḥah (shout) in truth: that will be the Day of coming out (from the graves, i.e. the Day of Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We it is Who quicken) for the resurrection (and give death) in the life of the world, (and unto Us is the journeying) after death.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِـي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا ٱلْمَصِيرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. Verily, We it is Who give life and cause death; and to Us is the final return. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed it is We Who give life and bring death and to Us is the journey’s end.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِـي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا ٱلْمَصِيرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. Verily, We it is Who give life and cause death; and to Us is the final return. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (On the day when the earth spliteth asunder from them, hastening forth (they come)) out of the graves. (That is a gathering easy for Us (to make).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعاً ذَلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. On the Day when the earth shall be cleft, from them, (they will come out) hastening forth. That will be a gathering, quite easy for Us..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: On the day when yawma substitutes for the previous yawma with the intervening statement being a parenthetical the earth is split asunder read tashaqqaqu or tashshaqqaqu where the original second tā’ of tatashaqqaqu has been assimilated with it the shīn from them they will come hastening forth sirā‘an sirā‘ the plural of sarī‘ a circumstantial qualifier referring to an implied clause that is to say together they would read fa-yakhrujūna musri‘īna ‘they come forth hastening’. That is an easy gathering for Us dhālika hashrun ‘alaynā yasīr there is here a separation of the noun from its adjective by what is semantically connected to it for the purpose of specification — which is rhetorically unobjectionable; dhālika ‘that’ is meant to point out the signification of the ‘gathering’ which itself is also predicated by this demonstrative particle and this signification is the bringing back to life after extinction and the assembly for the exposition and the reckoning before God.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعاً ذَلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. On the Day when the earth shall be cleft, from them, (they will come out) hastening forth. That will be a gathering, quite easy for Us..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: We are best aware of what they say) concerning the resurrection; and it is said: of what they say in the life of the world, (and thou) O Muhammad (art in nowise a compeller over them) such that you force them to accept faith; but later on Allah commanded him to fight them. (But warn) admonish (by the Qur'an him who feareth My threat) for only he who fears My chastisement in the Hereafter will accept your admonition'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِٱلْقُرْآنِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. We know best what they say. And you (O Muḥammad ) are not the one to force them (to Belief). But warn by the Qur’ān him who fears My warning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We know best what they the disbelievers of the Quraysh say and you are not to be a coercer of them so as to coerce them to embrace faith — but this was revealed before the command to struggle against these disbelievers. So admonish by the Qur’ān those who fear My threat namely believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِٱلْقُرْآنِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. We know best what they say. And you (O Muḥammad ) are not the one to force them (to Belief). But warn by the Qur’ān him who fears My warning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said in the interpretation of Allah's saying (By those that winnow with a winnowing): '(By those that winnow with a winnowing) He says: Allah swears by the blowing winds and that which they carry into the homes of people,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْواً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By (the winds) that scatter dust..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By the scatterers the winds that scatter dust and other things that scatter dharwan is a verbal noun; one may also say tadhrīhi dharyan ‘it blows it sweeping it away’;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْواً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By (the winds) that scatter dust..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those that bear the burden (of the rain)) and He swears by the heavy clouds which carry rain,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْحَامِلاَتِ وِقْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And (the clouds) that bear heavy weight of water..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those that bear the clouds that bear moisture as a burden wiqran is the direct object of al-hāmilat ‘those that bear’;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْحَامِلاَتِ وِقْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And (the clouds) that bear heavy weight of water..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those that glide with ease (upon the sea)) and He swears by the ships which easily sail on the sea,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And (the ships) that float with ease and gentleness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those that run the ships that run upon the surface of the water with ease yusran is a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial qualifier that is to say muyassaratan;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And (the ships) that float with ease and gentleness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who distribute (blessings) by command) and swears by the angels Gabriel, Michael, Seraphiel and the angel of death who apportion [provisions] for people: Allah swore by all these,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And those (angels) who distribute (provisions, rain, and other blessings) by (Allāh’s) Command..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those that apportion by command the angels who distribute provisions and the rains and other things across the lands and to all servants

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And those (angels) who distribute (provisions, rain, and other blessings) by (Allāh’s) Command..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! that wherewith ye are threatened) regarding the resurrection (is indeed true) will indeed take place,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَصَادِقٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Verily, that which you are promised (i.e. Resurrection in the Hereafter and receiving the reward or punishment of good or bad deeds) is surely true..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: assuredly what you are promised mā ‘what’ relates to the verbal action in other words the promise given to them of resurrection and other matters is true is indeed a true promise

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَصَادِقٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Verily, that which you are promised (i.e. Resurrection in the Hereafter and receiving the reward or punishment of good or bad deeds) is surely true..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! the judgement) reckoning, judgement and retaliation in it (will indeed befall) and happen.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَٱقِعٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And verily, the Recompense is sure to happen..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and assuredly judgement requital after the reckoning will take place! without doubt.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَٱقِعٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And verily, the Recompense is sure to happen..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (By the heaven full of paths) this is another oath; Allah swears by the seemly and beautiful heaven that has paths; it is also said that full of paths means: it has stars, the sun, the moon; and it is also said that full of paths means: full of waves like those of water upon being hit by the wind, or like the waves of sand upon being blown by the wind, or like the waves of curly hair or the waves of armour made of iron; and it is also said this refers to the seven heaven by which Allah has sworn.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. By the heaven full of paths,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And by the heaven with all its tracks hubuk is the plural of habīka similar in pattern and meaning to turuq tarīqa ‘paths’ that is to say by the heaven that is created with tracks similar to tracks made in the sand

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. By the heaven full of paths,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Ye) O people of Mecca, (forsooth, are of various opinion (concerning the Truth)) some of you believe in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an and some of you disbelieve in them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُّخْتَلِفٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Certainly, you have different ideas (about Muḥammad  and the Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: indeed you O people of Mecca with regard to the matter of the Prophet s and the Qur’ān are of differing opinions some say of the Prophet that he is ‘a poet’ ‘a sorcerer’ or ‘a soothsayer’ and of the Qur’ān that it is ‘poetry’ ‘sorcery’ or ‘soothsaying’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُّخْتَلِفٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Certainly, you have different ideas (about Muḥammad  and the Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He is made to turn away from it) he is made to turn away from Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (who is (himself) averse) who is barred from the Truth and guidance, i.e. al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, Abu Jahl Ibn Hisham, Ubayy Ibn Khalaf, Umayyah Ibn Khalaf and Munbih and Nabih the sons of al-Hajjaj. They turned people away from Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an and so Allah cursed them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Turned aside therefrom (i.e. from Muḥammad  and the Qur’ān) is he who is turned aside (by the Decree and Preordainment of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He is turned away therefrom from the Prophet s and the Qur’ān that is turned away from believing therein who has deviated who has been turned away from guidance in God’s exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Turned aside therefrom (i.e. from Muḥammad  and the Qur’ān) is he who is turned aside (by the Decree and Preordainment of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah said: (Accursed be the conjecturers) accursed are the liars of the Banu Makhzum: al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah and his host

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُتِلَ ٱلْخَرَّاصُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Cursed be the liars.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Perish the conjecturers accursed be the liars those of differing opinions

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُتِلَ ٱلْخَرَّاصُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Cursed be the liars.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who are careless) oblivious to believing in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (in an abyss!) in ignorance and blindness concerning the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ سَاهُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Who are under a cover of heedlessness (think not about the gravity of the Hereafter),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: who are in a stupor in ignorance that has stupefied them heedless oblivious of the matter of the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ سَاهُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Who are under a cover of heedlessness (think not about the gravity of the Hereafter),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They) the Banu Makhzum (ask) you, O Muhammad: (When is the Day of Judgement) in which we will be chastised?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَسْأَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. They ask: “When will be the Day of Recompense?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They ask the Prophet asking him derisively ‘When is the Day of Judgement?’ in other words ‘when will it come?’ and the response given to them is that it will come

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَسْأَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. They ask: “When will be the Day of Recompense?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah said: ((It is) the day) the Day of Judgement (when they will be tormented at the Fire) they will be burnt in the Fire; it is also said this means: they will be made to roast in the Fire; and it is also said that this means: they will be dragged into the Fire,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. (It will be) a Day when they will be tried (punished i.e. burnt) over the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: on the day when they will be tormented in the Fire that is to say chastised in it and it will be said to them during the chastisement

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. (It will be) a Day when they will be tried (punished i.e. burnt) over the Fire!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: The angels of the Fire will say to them: (Taste your torment. This) chastisement (is what ye sought to hasten) in the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ذُوقُواْ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. “Taste you your trial (punishment i.e. burning)! This is what you used to ask to be hastened!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Taste this torment of yours this chastisement of yours. This chastisement is what you sought to hasten on!’ in the world in derision.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ذُوقُواْ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. “Taste you your trial (punishment i.e. burning)! This is what you used to ask to be hastened!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then Allah explained the abode of the believers, like Abu Bakr and his fellow believers, saying: (Lo! those who keep from evil) those who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies (will dwell amid Gardens and watersprings) of pure water.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Verily, the Muttaqūn (the pious)(1). will be in the midst of Gardens and Springs (in Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly the God-fearing will be amid gardens orchards and springs flowing therein

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Verily, the Muttaqūn (the pious)(1). will be in the midst of Gardens and Springs (in Paradise),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Taking) content and pleased with (that which their Lord giveth them) in the Garden and it is also said that this means: they act upon that which their Lord commands them in the life of the world; (for lo! aforetime) before they were given this reward and honour (they were doers of good) they were good in their speech and action in the life of the world;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: آخِذِينَ مَآ آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Taking joy in the things which their Lord has given them. Verily, they were before this Muḥsinūn (good-doers) (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: receiving ākhidhīna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the predicate of inna ‘truly’ what their Lord has given them of reward for indeed formerly before their entering Paradise they had been virtuous in the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: آخِذِينَ مَآ آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Taking joy in the things which their Lord has given them. Verily, they were before this Muḥsinūn (good-doers) (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They used to sleep but little of the night) He says: they hardly slept at night,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً مِّن ٱللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. They used to sleep but little by night [invoking their Lord (Allāh) and praying, with fear and hope]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Little of the night did they use to sleep mā is extra; yahja‘ūna is the predicate of kānū; qalīlan ‘little’ is an adverb in other words they used to sleep for a small portion of the night and perform prayers during most of it

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً مِّن ٱللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. They used to sleep but little by night [invoking their Lord (Allāh) and praying, with fear and hope]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And ere the dawning of each day would seek forgiveness) and at dawn they would pray,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَبِٱلأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. And in the hours before dawn, they were (found) asking (Allāh) for forgiveness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and at dawns they used to seek forgiveness they used say ‘Our Lord! Forgive us’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَبِٱلأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. And in the hours before dawn, they were (found) asking (Allāh) for forgiveness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in their wealth the beggar) who asks from people (the outcast) he who does not beg from people nor is he given and nor do people realise he is in need; it is also said that the outcast means: the one whose wage and spoils are denied; and it is said that this means: the one who has a trade but whose life is hard and cannot earn his day's sufficiency (had due share) had an acknowledged right.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِيۤ أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لَّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And in their properties there was the right of the Sā’il (the beggar who asks) and the Mahrūm (the poor who does not ask others) (3)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and there was a share in their wealth assigned for the beggar and the deprived the latter being the one who does not beg because of his self-restraint.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِيۤ أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لَّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And in their properties there was the right of the Sā’il (the beggar who asks) and the Mahrūm (the poor who does not ask others) (3)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in the earth are portents) signs and lessons, like the trees, beasts, mountains and seas (for those whose faith is sure) for those who have certainty in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And on the earth are signs for those who have Faith with certainty..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And in the earth in the way of mountains seas trees fruits plants and other things there are signs indications of God’s power glory be to Him exalted be He and of His Oneness for those who know with certainty

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And on the earth are signs for those who have Faith with certainty..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (also) in yourselves) there are signs and lessons such as pain, sickness and misfortune. A person for example administers his food and drink from one place but they come out from two different places. (Can ye then not see?) Do you then not perceive such that you reflect upon that which Allah has created?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And also in your ownselves. Will you not then see?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and in your souls there are also signs from the beginning of your creation to its end and in the marvelous aspects of your creation. Will you not then perceive? all that and thus infer therefrom the Creator of it and His power.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And also in your ownselves. Will you not then see?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in the heaven is your providence) and from the heaven comes your provision, i.e. rain (and that which ye are promised) i.e. the Garden; your provision is upon the Lord of heaven just as what you are promised of reward and punishment is upon Allah;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And in the heaven is your provision, and that which you are promised. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And in the heaven is your provision that is the rain from which results the vegetation that is your provision and there is also what you are promised in the way of the ultimate return reward and punishment in other words all of this is foreordained in the heaven.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And in the heaven is your provision, and that which you are promised. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And by the Lord of the heavens and the earth) Allah swore by Himself, (it) that which I have related to you concerning provision (is the Truth) it will surely happen, (even as (it is true) that ye speak) even as you say: there is no deity except Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Then, by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth (i.e. what has been promised to you), just as it is the truth that you can speak..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth it that which you are promised is as assuredly true as the fact that you have power of speech read mithlu in the nominative as an adjective with the mā being extra; or read mithla in the accusative as being a compound with mā that is to say it is as true as your speech is in reality that is in your knowing it to be true necessarily by its issuing from you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Then, by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth (i.e. what has been promised to you), just as it is the truth that you can speak..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hath the story of Abraham's honoured guests) has the event of the guests of Abraham who were honoured by being offered a calf to eat (reached thee) O Muhammad?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. Has the story reached you, of the honoured guests [three angels; Jibrā’īl (Gabriel) along with another two] of Ibrāhīm (Abraham)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Has the story reached you — addressing the Prophet s — of Abraham’s honoured guests? — these were said to be either twelve ten or three angels one of whom was Gabriel.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. Has the story reached you, of the honoured guests [three angels; Jibrā’īl (Gabriel) along with another two] of Ibrāhīm (Abraham)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When they) Gabriel and two other angels with him; and it is also said: Gabriel and 12 other angels with him (came in unto him) to Abraham (and said: Peace!) they gave the greetings of peace to Abraham (he answered, Peace!) Abraham answered their greetings of peace, ((and thought): Folk unknown (to me)) he did not recognize them and did not see that their greeting of peace was unknown at the time and place where he was.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. When they came in to him and said: “Salām, (peace be upon you)!” He answered: “Salām, (peace be upon you),” and said: “You are a people unknown to me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When idh is an adverbial qualifier of hadīthu dayfi ‘the story of the guests’ they entered upon him and said ‘Peace!’ — in other words they said these very words. He said ‘Peace!’ — also these very words — These are an unfamiliar folk whom we do not know — he said this to himself qawmun munkarūna is the predicate of an implicit subject such as hā’ūlā’i ‘these are’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. When they came in to him and said: “Salām, (peace be upon you)!” He answered: “Salām, (peace be upon you),” and said: “You are a people unknown to me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then he went apart unto his housefolk so that they brought a fatted calf) a roasted, fatted calf to his guests;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Then, he turned to his household, and brought out a roasted calf [as the property of Ibrāhīm (Abraham) was mainly cows]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then he went aside to his family secretly and brought a fat calf — in sūrat Hūd it is said a roasted calf Q. 1169 —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Then, he turned to his household, and brought out a roasted calf [as the property of Ibrāhīm (Abraham) was mainly cows]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he set it before them) but when he saw that they did not reach to it, (saying: Will ye not eat) the food?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلاَ تَأْكُلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And placed it before them, (saying): “Will you not eat?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and he placed it near them saying ‘Will you not eat?’ he invited them to eat but they did not respond.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلاَ تَأْكُلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And placed it before them, (saying): “Will you not eat?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then he conceived a fear of them) Abraham concealed his fear of them when they did not eat his food. He thought they were thieves. This is because, in his time, to eat of the food of another person was a sign of coming with a good intention. When the angels realised his fear. (They said: Fear not!) Fear us not, O Abraham! We are the messengers of your Lord (and gave him tidings of (the birth of) a wise son) a son who is wise in his childhood, great when he grows older: this is Isaac.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُواْ لاَ تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلاَمٍ عَلِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Then he conceived a fear of them (when they ate not). They said: “Fear not.” (1) And they gave him glad tidings of a son having knowledge (about Allāh and His religion of True Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then he conceived he kept secret in himself a fear of them. They said ‘Do not be afraid!’ we are messengers from your Lord. And they gave him good tidings of the birth of a knowledgeable boy one endowed with much knowledge and this was Isaac as mentioned in sūrat Hūd Q. 1171.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُواْ لاَ تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلاَمٍ عَلِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Then he conceived a fear of them (when they ate not). They said: “Fear not.” (1) And they gave him glad tidings of a son having knowledge (about Allāh and His religion of True Monotheism)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then his wife came forward) his wife Sarah came, (making moan) and wailing, (and smote her face) she gathered the extremities of her fingers and hit her face and forehead, (and cried: A barren old woman!) A barren old woman giving birth, how is this possible?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Then his wife came forward with a loud voice: she smote her face, and said: “A barren old woman!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then his wife Sarah came forward clamouring shouting fī sarratin is a circumstantial qualifier that is to say she came shouting and smote slapped her face and said ‘A barren old woman!’ who has never given birth to a child aged ninety-nine with Abraham being one hundred years old; or alternatively he was a hundred and twenty years old and she was ninety years old.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Then his wife came forward with a loud voice: she smote her face, and said: “A barren old woman!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said) Gabriel and the angels with him said: (Even so) just as we have said to you, O Sarah, (saith thy Lord. Lo! He is the Wise) He decrees the birth of children from those who are barren and those who are not, (the Knower) what will come out of both you in the future.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ كَذَلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. They said: “Even so says your Lord(1). Verily, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knower.” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said ‘So just like what we have said with regard to the good tiding has your Lord said. Indeed He is the Wise in His actions the Knower’ of His creatures.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ كَذَلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. They said: “Even so says your Lord(1). Verily, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knower.” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((Abraham) said: And (afterward) what is your errand) what is happening and why have you come, (O ye sent (from Allah)?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. [Ibrāhīm (Abraham)] said: “Then for what purpose you have come, O Messengers?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He said ‘So what is your business O you who have been sent by God?’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. [Ibrāhīm (Abraham)] said: “Then for what purpose you have come, O Messengers?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said: Lo! we are sent unto a guilty folk) idolatrous folk who brought ruin upon themselves because of engaging in an abominable act; referring here to the folk of Lot,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. They said: “We have been sent to a people who are Mujrimūn (polytheists, sinners, criminals, disbelievers in Allāh).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said ‘Lo! we have been sent to a guilty folk disbelievers — these were the people of Lot —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. They said: “We have been sent to a people who are Mujrimūn (polytheists, sinners, criminals, disbelievers in Allāh).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That we may send upon them stones of clay) cooked like bricks,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً مِّن طِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. To send down upon them stones of baked clay..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that we may unleash upon them stones of clay baked in fire

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً مِّن طِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. To send down upon them stones of baked clay..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Marked) black in red (by thy Lord) these stones will come from your Lord (for (the destruction of) the wanton) for the destruction of the idolatrous folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Marked by your Lord for the Musrifūn ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: marked bearing the name of the person at whom it will be hurled by your Lord ‘inda rabbika is an adverbial qualifier of musawwamatan ‘marked’ for the destruction of the prodigal’ for coming unto males in addition to their disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Marked by your Lord for the Musrifūn ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (You We brought forth) from the townships of Lot's folk (such believers as were there) who believed in Allah's divine Oneness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. So, We brought out from therein the believers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So We brought forth those in them that is in the towns of the people of Lot who were believers in order to destroy the disbelievers;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. So, We brought out from therein the believers..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But We found there) in the townships of Lot's folk (but one house) but the inhabitants of one house (of those surrendered (to Allah)) of those close to Allah: Lot and his two daughters, Za'ura and Raytha.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. But, We found not there any household of the Muslims except one [of Lūṭ (Lot) and his two daughters]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: but We did not find therein other than one house of those who had submitted to God these were Lot and his two daughters. They have been described here with the terms ‘belief’ and ‘submission’ because they had affirmed faith in their hearts and used their limbs to perform acts of obedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. But, We found not there any household of the Muslims except one [of Lūṭ (Lot) and his two daughters]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We left behind therein) in the townships of Lot's folk (a portent) a sign and lesson (for those who fear a painful doom) in the Hereafter such that they do not emulate their abominable act.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ آيَةً لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلأَلِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And We have left there a sign (i.e. the place of the Dead Sea(1) in Palestine) for those who fear the painful torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We left therein after destroying the disbelievers a sign an indication of their destruction for those who fear the painful chastisement so that they may not do what these sinners did.
