meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And was at a distance of two bows’ length or (even) nearer..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And He revealed unto His slave) Gabriel (that which He revealed) to His slave Muhammad (pbuh); and it is said this means: and He revealed to His slave Muhammad (pbuh) that which He revealed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ مَآ أَوْحَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. So (Allāh) revealed to His slave [Muḥammad  through Jibrā’īl (Gabriel) S] whatever He revealed..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: whereat He God exalted be He revealed to His servant Gabriel what he Gabriel revealed to the Prophet s; the thing being revealed is not mentioned explicitly in exaltation of its great status.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ مَآ أَوْحَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. So (Allāh) revealed to His slave [Muḥammad  through Jibrā’īl (Gabriel) S] whatever He revealed..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The heart) of Muhammad (pbuh) (lied not (in seeing) what it saw) when he saw his Lord with his heart; it is also said that he saw his Lord with his eyes. This is why Allah made His oath.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا كَذَبَ ٱلْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. The (Prophet’s) heart lied not about what he (Muḥammad ) saw..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The heart the heart of the Prophet did not deny read khadhaba or kadhdhaba what he saw with his own eyes of the image of Gabriel.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا كَذَبَ ٱلْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. The (Prophet’s) heart lied not about what he (Muḥammad ) saw..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: When the Prophet (pbuh) informed them of what he saw, they disbelieved him. And so Allah said: (Will ye then dispute with him concerning) will you then disbelieve (what he seeth) what Muhammad (pbuh) saw?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَىٰ مَا يَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Will you then dispute with him (Muḥammad ) about what he saw [during the Mi‘rāj (Ascent of the Prophet  to the seven heavens)] (1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Will you then dispute with him will you then argue with him and hope to overwhelm him concerning what he saw? — an address to the idolaters who denied the Prophet’s s vision of Gabriel.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَىٰ مَا يَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Will you then dispute with him (Muḥammad ) about what he saw [during the Mi‘rāj (Ascent of the Prophet  to the seven heavens)] (1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily he saw him) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) saw Gabriel; and it is said he saw his Lord with his heart; and it is said he saw his Lord with his eyes, (yet another time) other than the time about which he informed you,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And indeed he (Muḥammad ) saw him [Jibrā’īl (Gabriel)] at a second descent (i.e. another time)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily he saw him in his true image another time

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And indeed he (Muḥammad ) saw him [Jibrā’īl (Gabriel)] at a second descent (i.e. another time)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (By the lote tree of the utmost boundary) at which point every close angel and sent prophet stops; it is also said that this means: the knowledge of every close angel and sent prophet and firm-footed scholar stops at this point,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عِندَ سِدْرَةِ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Near Sidrat-ul-Muntahā (a lote-tree of the utmost boundary over the seventh heaven beyond which none can pass)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: by the Lote-tree of the Ultimate Boundary when he was carried on the night journey up through the heavens — this lote-tree is a nabk thorn-tree that lies to the right of the Throne ‘arsh the tree beyond which no angel or any other being pass;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عِندَ سِدْرَةِ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Near Sidrat-ul-Muntahā (a lote-tree of the utmost boundary over the seventh heaven beyond which none can pass)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nigh unto which is the Garden of Abode) wherein the spirits of martyrs abide.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عِندَهَا جَنَّةُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Near it is the Paradise of Abode..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: near which is the Garden of the Retreat to which the angels the spirits of martyrs and the pious retreat;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عِندَهَا جَنَّةُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Near it is the Paradise of Abode..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When that which shroudeth did enshroud the lote tree) when the angels enshroud the lote tree; and it is said this means: when the light enshrouds the lote tree; and it is also said that this means: when a canopy of gold enshrouds the lote tree,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ يَغْشَىٰ ٱلسِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَىٰ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: when there shrouded the Lote-tree that which shrouded it of flying creatures and other beings idh ‘when’ is operated by ra’āhu ‘he saw him’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذْ يَغْشَىٰ ٱلسِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. When that covered the lote-tree which did cover it! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The eye turned not aside) the sight of Muhammad (pbuh) did not turn right or left because of what he saw (nor yet was overbold) due to what he saw; he saw that Gabriel had 600 wings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا زَاغَ ٱلْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: The sight (of Prophet Muḥammad ) turned not aside (right or left), nor it transgressed beyond the limit (ordained for it).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The eye did not swerve on the part of the Prophet s nor did it go beyond the bounds that is to say his gaze did not turn away from the object of vision designated for it nor did it go beyond that object on that night.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا زَاغَ ٱلْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: The sight (of Prophet Muḥammad ) turned not aside (right or left), nor it transgressed beyond the limit (ordained for it).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Verily he) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) (saw one of the greater revelations of his Lord) he saw one of the greatest marvels of his Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَقَدْ رَأَىٰ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Indeed, he (Muḥammad ) did see of the Greatest Signs of his Lord (Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily he saw in it some of the greatest signs of his Lord some of the most awesome of these signs. He thus saw from among the marvels of the Realm malakūt a green drape rafraf that obscured the entire horizon of the heaven and Gabriel with his six hundred wings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَقَدْ رَأَىٰ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Indeed, he (Muḥammad ) did see of the Greatest Signs of his Lord (Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Have ye) O people of Mecca (thought upon al-Lat and al-'Uzza

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ ٱللاَّتَ وَٱلْعُزَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Have you then considered Al-Lāt, and Al-‘Uzzā (two idols of the pagan Arabs)(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have you considered al-Lāt and al-‘Uzzā

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ ٱللاَّتَ وَٱلْعُزَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Have you then considered Al-Lāt, and Al-‘Uzzā (two idols of the pagan Arabs)(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And Manat, the third, the other) will benefit you in the Hereafter? It will not benefit them. It is also said that the verse means: do you deem that your worship of al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat in the life of the world will benefit you in the Hereafter. No, it will surely not benefit you. As for al-Lat it was an idol which was worshipped in Thaqif; al-'Uzza was a tree in Batn al-Nakhlah which Ghatafan worshipped; while Manat was an idol in Mecca which was worshipped beside Allah by Hudhayl and Khuza'ah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَنَاةَ ٱلثَّالِثَةَ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And Manāt (another idol of the pagan Arabs), the other third?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Manāt the third of the preceding two the other? al-ukhrā a derogatory qualification of the third one. These were stone idols which the idolaters worshipped and which they claimed interceded for them with God the first direct object of a-fa-ra’aytum ‘have you seen’ is al-Lāt and what has been supplemented thereto; the second direct object has been omitted. The meaning then is ‘Inform Me do these idols have the power over anything such that you worship them besides God Who has the power over all that has been mentioned?’ And because of their assertion also that the angels were God’s daughters despite their aversion to daughters the following was revealed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَنَاةَ ٱلثَّالِثَةَ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And Manāt (another idol of the pagan Arabs), the other third?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Are yours the males) O people of Mecca, whom you are pleased to have for yourselves (and His the females) despite the fact that you dislike them and will not be pleased to have them for yourselves?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَكُمُ ٱلذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ ٱلأُنْثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Is it for you the males and for Him the females?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Are you to have males and He females?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَكُمُ ٱلذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ ٱلأُنْثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Is it for you the males and for Him the females?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That indeed were an unfair division!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تِلْكَ إِذاً قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. That indeed is a division most unfair!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: That then would indeed be an unfair division! dīzān ‘unfair’ derives from dāzahu yadīzuhu to mean ‘he wronged him’ ‘he was unjust to him’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تِلْكَ إِذاً قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. That indeed is a division most unfair!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: They are) i.e. al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat (but names) idols (which ye have named ye and your fathers) you have appointed them as deities; it is also said that this means: you and your forefathers have made them, (for which Allah hath revealed) regarding their worship or naming (no warrant) no Scripture wherein is found your proof. (They follow) they do not worship al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat or that which they call deities (but a guess) except through surmise and have no certainty about their worship (and that which (they) themselves desire) and they also worship them because they follow their own desires. (And now the guidance from their Lord) the explanation in the Qur'an that Allah has no son or partner (hath come unto them) to the people of Mecca.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ أَسْمَآءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَآبَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَانٍ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى ٱلأَنفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. They are but names which you have named — you and your fathers — for which Allāh has sent down no authority. They follow but a guess and that which they themselves desire, whereas there has surely come to them the Guidance from their Lord!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: These that is the mentioned deities are nothing but names which you have named by which you have named you and your fathers idols that you worship. God has not revealed any warrant any proof or evidence for them that is to say for the worship of them. They follow nothing but conjecture in their worship of them and that which ignoble souls desire of that which Satan adorned for them that they may intercede for them before God exalted be He even though guidance has already come to them from their Lord by the tongue of the Prophet s with definitive proof; yet they do not desist from their ways.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ أَسْمَآءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَآبَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَانٍ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى ٱلأَنفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. They are but names which you have named — you and your fathers — for which Allāh has sent down no authority. They follow but a guess and that which they themselves desire, whereas there has surely come to them the Guidance from their Lord!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or shall man) the people of Mecca (have what he coveteth) i.e. that the idols and angels will intercede for them?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لِلإِنسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. Or shall man have what he wishes?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or shall man that is shall every human being among them have whatever he wishes for? such as their wish that the idols intercede for them. No! It is not so.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لِلإِنسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. Or shall man have what he wishes?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But Unto Allah belongeth the after (life)) through the bestowal of reward, honour and intercession, (and the former) by giving knowledge and success.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلِلَّهِ ٱلآخِرَةُ وٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. But, to Allāh belongs the last (Hereafter) and the first (the world)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Yet to God belong the Hereafter and the former life that is to say the life of the world and so nothing comes to pass in them except what He exalted wills.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلِلَّهِ ٱلآخِرَةُ وٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. But, to Allāh belongs the last (Hereafter) and the first (the world)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And how many angels are in the heavens) whom you claim are Allah's daughters (whose intercession availeth naught) who intercede for no one (save after Allah giveth leave) except after Allah commands them to intercede (to whom He chooseth) to whoever deserves it from among the believers (and accepteth) them through the profession of Allah's divine Oneness!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ مِّن مَّلَكٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لاَ تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئاً إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرْضَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allāh has given leave for whom He wills and is pleased with..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And how many an angel that is to say many an angel there is in the heavens and how honoured they are in God’s sight but whose intercession cannot avail in any way except after God gives permission to them for this intercession for whomever He wills of His servants and with whom He is satisfied because of His saying and they do not intercede except for him with whom He is satisfied Q. 2128. It is also well-known that it intercession cannot be forthcoming from them except after permission for it has been granted who is there that shall intercede with Him save with His leave Q. 2255.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَمْ مِّن مَّلَكٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لاَ تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئاً إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرْضَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allāh has given leave for whom He wills and is pleased with..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! it is those who disbelieve in the Hereafter) in resurrection after death, i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca (who name the angels with the names of females) they make them Allah's daughters.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ ٱلأُنْثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. Verily, those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names. (1) *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly those who do not believe in the Hereafter give the angels the names of females for they say ‘They are God’s daughters’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ ٱلأُنْثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. Verily, those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names. (1) *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they have no knowledge thereof) they have no proof or elucidation about what they say. (They follow but a guess) they lie out of surmise and do not have any certainty, (and lo! a guess) and worship based on guess and claims based on guess (can never take the place of the Truth) cannot spare one from Allah's chastisement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لاَ يُغْنِي مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْئاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. But, they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and verily, guess is no substitute for the truth..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But they do not have any knowledge thereof of this claim. They follow in this respect nothing but conjecture which they have conjured up and indeed conjecture can never substitute for the truth that is to say when it comes to acquiring knowledge of that which one is required to have knowledge of.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لاَ يُغْنِي مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْئاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. But, they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and verily, guess is no substitute for the truth..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then withdraw) then turn your face, O Muhammad, (from him who fleeth) from him who turns away (from Our remembrance) from Our divine Oneness and Scripture (and desireth) of his works (but the life of the world) but that which is in the life of the world, i.e. Abu Jahl and his host.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَعْرِضْ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلاَّ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Therefore withdraw (O Muḥammad ) from him who turns away from Our Reminder (this Qur’ān) and desires nothing but the life of this world..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So shun him who turns away from Our Remembrance that is from the Qur’ān and desires nothing but the life of this world — this was revealed before the command to struggle against the disbelievers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَعْرِضْ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلاَّ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Therefore withdraw (O Muḥammad ) from him who turns away from Our Reminder (this Qur’ān) and desires nothing but the life of this world..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Such is their sum of knowledge) such is the extent at which their knowledge, intellect and opinion end, since they claimed that the angels are Allah's daughters and that there is no Hereafter. (Lo! thy Lord) O Muhammad (is best aware of him who strayeth) from His religion, in reference here to Abu Jahl, (and He is best aware of him who goeth right) to His religion, in reference here to Abu Bakr.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. That is what they could reach of knowledge. Verily, your Lord it is He Who knows best him who goes astray from His Path, and He knows best him who receives guidance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: That namely the desire of this world is the full extent of their knowledge that is the limit of their knowledge namely that they have preferred this life to that of the Hereafter. Truly your Lord knows best those who have strayed from His way and He knows best those who are rightly guided He has knowledge of both and will requite both.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. That is what they could reach of knowledge. Verily, your Lord it is He Who knows best him who goes astray from His Path, and He knows best him who receives guidance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens) of creation (and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings; they are all slaves of Allah, (that He may reward those who do evil) those ascribe partners to Allah (with that which they have done) in their state of idolatry, (and reward those who do good) those who believe in Allah's divine Oneness (with goodness) with the Garden.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَاءُواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَيَجْزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ بِٱلْحُسْنَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. And to Allāh belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, that He may requite those who do evil with that which they have done (i.e. punish them in Hell), and reward those who do good, with what is best (i.e. Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth that is He owns all of that among which also are the misguided one and the rightly guided one leading astray whomever He will and guiding whomever He will that He may requite those who do evil for what they have done by way of idolatry and otherwise and reward those who are virtuous by their affirmation of God’s Oneness and other acts of obedience with the best reward namely Paradise. He points out ‘the virtuous’ as being

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَاءُواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَيَجْزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ بِٱلْحُسْنَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. And to Allāh belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, that He may requite those who do evil with that which they have done (i.e. punish them in Hell), and reward those who do good, with what is best (i.e. Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then showed their works in the life of the world, saying: (Those who avoid enormities of sin) i.e. idolatry and the major sins (and abominations) adultery and transgressions, (save the unwilled offences) except a furtive look, a taunt, a censure which they then blame themselves for committing and repent of doing; it is also said that this means: except marrying ((for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy) towards he who repents of major and minor sins. (He is best aware of you) than your own selves (when He created you from the earth) He created you from Adam and Adam is from dust and dust is from the earth, (and when ye were) small (hidden in the bellies of your mothers) Allah knew in these circumstances what will ensue from you. (Therefore ascribe not purity unto yourselves) do not absolve yourselves from committing sins. (He is best aware of him who wardeth off (evil)) transgression and does good.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَاحِشَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنشَأَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ فَلاَ تُزَكُّوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. Those who avoid great sins and Al-Fawāḥish (great sins and illegal sex) except the small faults, — verily, your Lord is of Vast Forgiveness. He knows you well when He created you from the earth (Adam), and when you were fetuses in your mothers’ wombs. So, ascribe not purity to yourselves. He knows best him who fears Allāh and keeps his duty to Him [i.e. those who are Al-Muttaqūn (the pious) (1)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Those who avoid grave sins and abominations excepting lesser offences that is minor sins such as a look a kiss or a touch this constitutes a discontinuous exception in other words the meaning is but lesser offences are forgiven by the avoidance of grave sins. Truly your Lord is of vast forgiveness for such lesser sins and for accepting repentance. The following was revealed regarding those who used to say ‘What of our prayers our fasting and our pilgrimage!’. He knows you best from the time when He produced you from the earth that is to say when He created your father Adam from dust and when you were hidden fetuses ajinna is the plural of janīn in the bellies of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves do not praise yourselves that is in admiration; but if it is done in recognition of God’s grace then that is fine. He knows best those who are God-fearing.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَاحِشَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنشَأَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ فَلاَ تُزَكُّوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. Those who avoid great sins and Al-Fawāḥish (great sins and illegal sex) except the small faults, — verily, your Lord is of Vast Forgiveness. He knows you well when He created you from the earth (Adam), and when you were fetuses in your mothers’ wombs. So, ascribe not purity to yourselves. He knows best him who fears Allāh and keeps his duty to Him [i.e. those who are Al-Muttaqūn (the pious) (1)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Didst thou (O Muhammad) observe him who turned away) from spending and giving alms to the poor among the Companions of the Prophet (pbuh)

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Did you (O Muḥammad ) observe him who turned away (from Islām). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Did you see him who turned away from faith — that is the one who recanted when he was derided for it. He said ‘But I fear the punishment of God!’. But when the one deriding him guaranteed him that he would bear God’s chastisement for him provided that he reverted to his former idolatry and he then gave him a stated sum money he reverted —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Did you (O Muḥammad ) observe him who turned away (from Islām). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And gave a little) for the sake of Allah, (then was grudging) then stopped his spending and almsgiving in the way of Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلاً وَأَكْدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. And gave a little, then stopped (giving)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and gave a little of the stated sum of money and was then grudging? refrained from giving the remainder akdā derives from al-kudya earth that is hard as rock and which prevents the well-digger from digging through when he hits it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلاً وَأَكْدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. And gave a little, then stopped (giving)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hath he knowledge of the Unseen) the Guarded Tablet (so that he seeth) his doing in it that it is indeed as he did? This verse was revealed about 'Uthman Ibn 'Affan who was of the habit of spending a great deal on, and gives alms to, the Companions of the Prophet (pbuh) but then he met 'Abdullah Ibn Sa'd Ibn Abi Sarh. The latter said to him: " I see that you spend a great deal on these, and I fear that you may be left with nothing ". 'Uthman said to him: " I have faults and sins which I want to expiate and I also want to obtain Allah's good pleasure ". 'Abdullah said: " Give me the halter of your camel and I will bear your sins and faults in this life and in the Hereafter ". As a result, he gave him the halter of his camel and confided himself to spending on him. It is because of this that this verse was revealed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَعِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. Is with him the knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Does he possess knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees? and therefore from among such knowledge he is able to know that another person may bear the chastisement of the Hereafter for him? No! This was al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra or someone else the sentence beginning with a-‘indahu ‘does he possess’ is the second object of the a-ra’ayta ‘have you seen’ which has the significance of ‘inform Me!’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَعِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. Is with him the knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or hath he not had news) has he not been informed in the Qur'an (of what is in the books of Moses) He says: in the Torah and the scrolls of Abraham.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. Or is he not informed with what is in the Pages (Scripture) of Mūsā (Moses),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or am means bal has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses the books of the Torah or scrolls before it

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. Or is he not informed with what is in the Pages (Scripture) of Mūsā (Moses),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Abraham who paid his debt) i.e. he conveyed the message of his Lord and acted upon that which Allah had commanded him; it is also said that this means: he did as he was told in his dream vision:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلَّذِي وَفَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And of Ibrāhīm (Abraham) who fulfilled (or conveyed) all that (Allāh ordered him to do or convey):.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the scrolls of Abraham who fulfilled his summons he who completed what he had been charged with as in And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words and he fulfilled them Q. 2124 the explication of mā ‘what’ is the following

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلَّذِي وَفَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And of Ibrāhīm (Abraham) who fulfilled (or conveyed) all that (Allāh ordered him to do or convey):.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That no laden one shall bear another's load) that no bearer shall bear the sins of another; it is also said that this means: no soul shall be tormented for the sins of another soul,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلاَّ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. That no burdened person (with sins) shall bear the burden (sins) of another..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that no burdened soul shall bear the burden of another an ‘that’ has been softened in place of the hardened form in other words no soul shall bear responsibility for the sins of another;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلاَّ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. That no burdened person (with sins) shall bear the burden (sins) of another..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that man) on the Day of Judgement (hath only that for which he maketh effort) he has only that which he has earned of good or evil in the life of the world,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سَعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. And that man can have nothing but what he does (good or bad) (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that wa-an to be understood as wa-annahu man shall have only what he himself strives for of good deeds and so he shall not have anything of the reward for good deeds striven for by another;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سَعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. And that man can have nothing but what he does (good or bad) (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that his effort will be seen) and that his works will be seen,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And that his deeds will be seen..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that his endeavour will be seen it will be inspected in the Hereafter

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And that his deeds will be seen..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And afterward he will be repaid for it with fullest payment) good with good and evil with evil;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ ٱلْجَزَآءَ ٱلأَوْفَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. Then he will be recom pensed with a full and the best recompense(2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: then he will be rewarded for it with the fullest reward the most perfect reward one may say jazaytuhu sa‘yahu or jazaytuhu bi-sa‘yihi to mean the same thing

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ ٱلْجَزَآءَ ٱلأَوْفَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. Then he will be recom pensed with a full and the best recompense(2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that thy Lord, He is the goal) to your Lord is the return of all created beings after they die and their destination will be to Him in the Hereafter;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. And that to your Lord (Allāh) is the End (Return of everything)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that read wa-anna as a supplement; it is also read wa-inna as the beginning of a new sentence; and the same applies to what comes after it in which case according to this second reading these inna statements no longer form part of the content of all that is ‘in the scrolls’ the ultimate end the return and the destination after death is toward your Lord whereat He will requite them;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. And that to your Lord (Allāh) is the End (Return of everything)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He it is Who maketh laugh) the people of the Garden when they see what pleases them in terms of the honour that is bestowed upon them, (and maketh weep) the people of the Fire when they see what grieves them in terms of humiliation,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. And that it is He (Allāh) Who makes (whom He wills) laugh, and makes (whom He wills) weep..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that it is He Who makes to laugh whomever He will He makes joyous and makes to weep whomever He will He makes him sorrowful

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. And that it is He (Allāh) Who makes (whom He wills) laugh, and makes (whom He wills) weep..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He it is Who giveth death) in the life of the world (and giveth life) for the resurrection; it is also said that this means: He gives death to fathers and life to sons;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. And that it is He (Allāh) Who causes death and gives life..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that it is He Who brings death in this world and gives life for resurrection

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. And that it is He (Allāh) Who causes death and gives life..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He createth the two spouses) a pair, (the male and the female,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And that He (Allāh) creates the pairs, male and female, (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that He Himself creates the two spouses the two kinds the male and the female

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And that He (Allāh) creates the pairs, male and female, (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: From a drop (of seed) when it is poured forth) in the womb of the woman; it is also said that this means: when it is created;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. From Nuṭfah (drops of semen — male and female discharges) when it is emitted..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: from a drop of semen once it is emitted once it is poured forth into the womb

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. From Nuṭfah (drops of semen — male and female discharges) when it is emitted..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He hath ordained the second bringing forth) the other creation after the resurrection;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. And that upon Him (Allāh) is another bringing forth (Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that with Him rests the second genesis read al-nashā’ata or al-nash’ata the other creation for the Resurrection after the first creation

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. And that upon Him (Allāh) is another bringing forth (Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He it is Who enricheth) He made Himself independent of the need for created beings (and contenteth) and He made His slaves needy for Him; it is also said that this means: He made some rich with gold and silver and others content with the possession of camels, bovines and sheep.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And that it is He (Allāh) Who gives much or a little (of wealth and contentment).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that it is He Who enriches people by granting them sufficient wealth and grants possessions He Who gives that wealth that is enjoyed as property

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. And that it is He (Allāh) Who gives much or a little (of wealth and contentment).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He it is Who is the Lord of Sirius) which was worshipped by Khuza'ah;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلشِّعْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. And that He (Allāh) is the Lord of Sirius (the star which the pagan Arabs used to worship)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that it is He Who is the Lord of Sirius — this is a star lying beyond the constellation of Gemini which was worshipped in the time of pagandom jāhiliyya;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلشِّعْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. And that He (Allāh) is the Lord of Sirius (the star which the pagan Arabs used to worship)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And that He destroyed the former (tribe of) 'Aad) the folk of Hud,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَاداً ٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And that it is He (Allāh) Who destroyed the former ‘Ād (people),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that He destroyed former ‘Ād ‘Ādan al-ūlā a variant reading elides the nunation with the following lām sc. ‘Āda’l-ūlā; this former one refers to the people of ‘Ād while the second ‘Ād is that of the people of Sālih

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَاداً ٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And that it is He (Allāh) Who destroyed the former ‘Ād (people),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (the tribe of) Thamud) the folk of Salih (He spared not) a single one of them;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَثَمُودَ فَمَآ أَبْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And Thamūd (people): He spared none of them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Thamūd wa-Thamūda may be declined as the name of their forefather or left as a diptote being the name of the tribe; it is a supplement to ‘Ādan sparing not a single one of them;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَثَمُودَ فَمَآ أَبْقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And Thamūd (people): He spared none of them..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the folk of Noah) and He also destroyed the folk of Noah (aforetime) before the folk of Salih, (lo! They) i.e. the folk of Noah (were more unjust) more intense in their disbelief (and more rebellious) in their transgression and sinning;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. And the people of Nūḥ (Noah) aforetime. Verily, they were more unjust and more rebellious and transgressing [in disobeying Allāh and His Messenger Nūḥ (Noah) S]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the people of Noah before that that is to say before ‘Ād and Thamūd We also destroyed them; indeed they were more unjust and more insolent than ‘Ād and Thamūd because of the long time that Noah remained among them and he remained among them a thousand-less-fifty years Q. 2914 for they despite their disbelief in him would still harm him and assault him;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. And the people of Nūḥ (Noah) aforetime. Verily, they were more unjust and more rebellious and transgressing [in disobeying Allāh and His Messenger Nūḥ (Noah) S]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And al-Mu'tafikah He destroyed) and He destroyed the townships of the folk of Lot: Sodom, Sadum, Gomorrah and Sawa'im; al-Mu'tafikat means those that were swallowed up by the earth.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. And He destroyed the over thrown cities [of Sodom to which Prophet Lūṭ (Lot) was sent]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the Deviant cities namely the cities of the people of Lot He overturned He hurled them down to the earth after lifting them up to the heaven upside down by commanding Gabriel to do this;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. And He destroyed the over thrown cities [of Sodom to which Prophet Lūṭ (Lot) was sent]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So that there covered them that which did cover) i.e. stones covered them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. So there covered them that which did cover (i.e. torment with stones)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: so that there covered them of rocks afterwards that which covered them this is purposely left vague in order to inspire terror; in sūrat Hūd it is stated We made their uppermost the nethermost and We rained upon them stones of baked clay Q. 1182.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. So there covered them that which did cover (i.e. torment with stones)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Concerning which then, of the bounties of thy Lord) which of the blessings of your Lord, O man-this refers to all human beings except Muhammad (pbuh)-(canst thou dispute) can you deny that it is not from your Lord?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. Then which of the Graces of your Lord (O man!) will you doubt?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then which of the bounties of your Lord which of His graces graces which indicate His Oneness and power do you dispute? do you have doubt about O man or deny?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. Then which of the Graces of your Lord (O man!) will you doubt?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (This is a warner) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) is a warning Messenger (of the warners of old) like the earlier messengers whom We sent to their folks; it is also said that this means: this is a messenger among the messengers of old whom it is written, in the Guarded Tablet, that We would sent to their folks.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا نَذِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنُّذُرِ ٱلأُوْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. This (Muḥammad ) is a warner (Messenger) of the (series of) warners (Messengers) of old (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: This Muhammad (s) is a warner in the tradition of the warners of old of their kind that is to say he is a messenger like messengers before him sent to you just as they were sent to their peoples.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَـٰذَا نَذِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنُّذُرِ ٱلأُوْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 56. This (Muḥammad ) is a warner (Messenger) of the (series of) warners (Messengers) of old (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The threatened Hour is nigh) the advent of the Hour is close.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَزِفَتِ ٱلآزِفَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. The Day of Resurrection draws near. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The Impending Hour is imminent the Resurrection is near at hand.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَزِفَتِ ٱلآزِفَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 57. The Day of Resurrection draws near. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (None beside Allah can disclose it) none except Allah can reveal its advent and exact time.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. None besides Allāh can avert it (or advance it or delay it)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: None no soul besides God can disclose it that is to say only He can disclose it and manifest it as where He says He alone shall reveal it at its proper time Q. 7187.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 58. None besides Allāh can avert it (or advance it or delay it)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Marvel ye then at this statement) He says: are you mocking-and it is said: are you denying-this Qur'an which Muhammad (pbuh) recites to you, O people of Mecca,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَمِنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. Do you then wonder at this recitation (the Qur’ān)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Do you then marvel in denial at this discourse the Qur’ān

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَمِنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 59. Do you then wonder at this recitation (the Qur’ān)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And laugh) at out of derision (and not weep) because of what it contains of rebuke, threats and warning,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلاَ تَبْكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. And you laugh at it and weep not,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and laugh mockingly and not weep when you hear its Promise and Threat

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلاَ تَبْكُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 60. And you laugh at it and weep not,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (While ye amuse yourselves) while you are heedless of it and disbelieve in it?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. Wasting your (precious) lifetime in pastime and amusements (singing, etc.)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: while you remain oblivious? unmindful and heedless of what is required of you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 61. Wasting your (precious) lifetime in pastime and amusements (singing, etc.)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Rather prostrate yourselves before Allah) rather submit to Him through declaring His divine Oneness and also by repenting (and serve Him) and testify that there is only one God Who has no partner, solely for Allah's sake, for the Hour is nigh'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ وَٱعْبُدُواْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. So fall you down in prostration to Allāh and worship Him (Alone)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So prostrate to God Who created you and worship Him! and do not prostrate to idols nor worship them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ وَٱعْبُدُواْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 62. So fall you down in prostration to Allāh and worship Him (Alone)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said in the interpretation of Allah's saying (The hour drew nigh): '(The hour drew nigh) He says: the coming of the Hour drew nigh by the advent of Muhammad (pbuh) and the coming down of the smock (and the moon was rent in twain) this is also another sign of the closeness of the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱقْتَرَبَتِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been cleft asunder  (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The Hour has drawn near the Resurrection is close at hand and the moon has split it broke in two at Mount Abū Qubays and Qu‘ayqa‘ān as a sign for the Prophet s for it had been demanded of him and when it took place he said ‘Bear witness now!’ — as reported by the two Shaykhs al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱقْتَرَبَتِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been cleft asunder  (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And if they behold a portent) like the splitting of the moon (they turn away) they deny the sign (and say:) this sign is nothing but (Prolonged illusion) which will vanish.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِن يَرَوْاْ آيَةً يُعْرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحْرٌ مُّسْتَمِرٌّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And if they see a sign, they turn away, and say: “This is continuous magic.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And if they the disbelievers among Quraysh see a sign a miracle of the Prophet s they turn away and say this is ‘A powerful sorcery!’ mustamirr ‘powerful’ derives from al-mirra meaning ‘strength’; or it mustamirr means ‘incessant’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِن يَرَوْاْ آيَةً يُعْرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحْرٌ مُّسْتَمِرٌّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And if they see a sign, they turn away, and say: “This is continuous magic.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They denied) the sign and the coming of the Hour (and followed their own lusts) in denying the sign, the coming of the Hour and worshipping idols. (Yet everything will come to a decision) every word from Allah or His Messenger regarding promise, threat, tidings of Paradise or hell, mercy or punishment is true, some of this will happen in the life of the world, for all to see, and some of it will happen in the Hereafter and everything there will be manifest. It is also said that this means: every action and word that ensue from the slaves has a reality and this reality is in the heart.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَذَّبُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُوۤاْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. They denied (the Verses of Allāh — this Qur’ān), and followed their own lusts. And every matter will be settled ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they denied the Prophet s and followed their own desires as regards their falsehood; and every matter that is good or evil will be settled with that person who is responsible for it either by his ending up in Paradise or in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكَذَّبُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُوۤاْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. They denied (the Verses of Allāh — this Qur’ān), and followed their own lusts. And every matter will be settled ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And surely there hath come unto them) unto the people of Mecca in the Qur'an (news) of the nations of old, how they were destroyed when they disbelieved (whereof the purport should deter) and take admonition,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلأَنبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And indeed there has come to them news (in this Qur’ān) wherein there is (enough warning) to check (them from evil),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily there has come to them such tidings stories about the destruction of communities which denied their messengers as contain a deterrent to them muzdajar is a verbal noun or a noun of place; the dāl of muzdajar replaces the tā’ of the 8th form ifta‘ala; one may say izdajartuhu or zajartuhu to mean ‘I forbade him sternly’; mā ‘such as’ either indicates a relative clause or it is qualified by an adjective;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلأَنبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And indeed there has come to them news (in this Qur’ān) wherein there is (enough warning) to check (them from evil),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Effective) is the (wisdom) of the Qur'an; it is wisdom from Allah which they were conveyed on behalf of Allah; (but warnings) i.e. the messengers (avail not) the people who disbelieve in Allah as it is in His preeternal knowledge.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حِكْمَةٌ بَالِغَةٌ فَمَا تُغْنِ ٱلنُّذُرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Perfect wisdom (this Qur’ān), but (the preaching of) warners benefit them not. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: wisdom hikmatun is the predicate of an omitted subject or a substitution for mā ‘such as’ or for muzdajar ‘deterrent’ that is far-reaching complete; but warnings nudhur is the plural of nadhīr functioning in the agent sense of mundhir ‘a warner’ that is to say ‘those matters which warn them’; mā is either for negation or it is an interrogative of denial in which case it stands as a preceding direct object are of no avail warnings are of no use with them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حِكْمَةٌ بَالِغَةٌ فَمَا تُغْنِ ٱلنُّذُرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Perfect wisdom (this Qur’ān), but (the preaching of) warners benefit them not. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So withdraw from them) so turn away from them, O Muhammad-but he was later commanded to fight them-(on the day) which is the Day of Judgement (when the Summoner summoneth unto a painful thing) a tremendous and frightful thing whereby the dwellers of Paradise will be taken to Paradise and the dwellers of hell to hell.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ يَدْعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَيْءٍ نُّكُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. So (O Muḥammad ) withdraw from them. The Day that the caller will call (them) to a terrible thing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So turn away from them! this is the import of the preceding statement and it completes what is being said. On the day when the Summoner namely Isrāfīl yawma ‘the day’ is rendered accusative by yakhrujūna ‘they will emerge’ next verse summons to an awful thing read nukur or nukr in the sense of munkar ‘disagreeable’ a thing which the souls will find awful and this is the Reckoning;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ يَدْعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَيْءٍ نُّكُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. So (O Muḥammad ) withdraw from them. The Day that the caller will call (them) to a terrible thing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (With downcast eyes) humbled, (they come forth from the graves) upon the first blow of the Trumpet (as they were locusts spread abroad) He says: they fall on each other like locusts,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خُشَّعاً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلأَجْدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. They will come forth, with humbled eyes from (their) graves as if they were locusts spread abroad,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: with their downcast khāshi‘an a variant reading has khushsha‘an humiliated looks absāruhum is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb yakhrujūna ‘they will emerge’ they that is mankind will emerge from the graves as though they were scattered locusts not knowing where to go out of fear and perplexity this sentence ka’annahum jarādun muntashirun is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb yakhrujūna ‘they will emerge’ and so is His saying muhti‘īna

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خُشَّعاً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلأَجْدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. They will come forth, with humbled eyes from (their) graves as if they were locusts spread abroad,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hastening towards the Summoner) to find out about what he is going to command them; (the disbelievers say) on the Day of Judgement: (This is a hard day) on them, that is.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُّهْطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِ يَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُونَ هَـٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Hastening towards the caller. The disbelievers will say: “This is a hard Day.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: scrambling hastening with their necks stretched out toward the Summoner. The disbelievers among them will say ‘This is a hard day!’ a difficult one for disbelievers — as is stated in sūrat al-Muddaththir a day of hardship for the disbelievers Q. 749-10.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُّهْطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِ يَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُونَ هَـٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Hastening towards the caller. The disbelievers will say: “This is a hard Day.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The folk of Noah denied) Noah (before them) before your folk, O Muhammad, (yea, they denied Our slave) Noah (and said: A madman) bewitched; (and he was repulsed) he was deterred from what he brought to them, crying in his face: " you have lost your mind! ".

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُواْ عَبْدَنَا وَقَالُواْ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. The people of Nūḥ (Noah) denied (their Messenger) before them. They rejected Our slave, and said: “A madman!” and he was insolently rebuked and threatened..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The people of Noah denied kadhdhabat has feminine inflection on account of the import referring to a feminine noun qawm ‘tribe’ before them before Quraysh. Thus they denied Our servant Noah and said ‘A madman!’ and he was reviled they repulsed him with insults and in other ways.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُواْ عَبْدَنَا وَقَالُواْ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. The people of Nūḥ (Noah) denied (their Messenger) before them. They rejected Our slave, and said: “A madman!” and he was insolently rebuked and threatened..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So he cried unto his Lord, saying: I am vanquished) I am oppressed, (so give help) by punishing them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فَٱنتَصِرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Then he invoked his Lord (saying): “I have been overcome, so help (me)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And so he invoked his Lord saying ‘I have been annī to be understood as bi-annī overcome so help me!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فَٱنتَصِرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. Then he invoked his Lord (saying): “I have been overcome, so help (me)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then opened We the gates of heaven) for 40 days (with pouring water) with pouring rain.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَابَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَاءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. So We opened the gates of the heaven with water pouring forth..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then We opened read fa-fatahnā or fa-fattahnā the gates of the heaven with torrential waters waters pouring down intensely

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَابَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَاءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. So We opened the gates of the heaven with water pouring forth..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And caused the earth to gush forth springs) for 40 days, (so that the waters) of the heaven and the earth (met for a predestined purpose) met for a measure that We have appointed: the rain of heaven and the water of springs; it is also said that this means: the waters met for a decreed purpose to destroy the folk of Noah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلأَرْضَ عُيُوناً فَالْتَقَى ٱلمَآءُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth. So the waters (of the heaven and the earth) met for a matter predestined..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and We made the earth burst forth with springs that flowed forth and the waters the waters of the heaven and the earth met for a purpose a circumstance that was preordained a matter which had been decreed since pre-eternity namely their destruction by drowning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلأَرْضَ عُيُوناً فَالْتَقَى ٱلمَآءُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth. So the waters (of the heaven and the earth) met for a matter predestined..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And We carried him) i.e. Noah and those who believed in him (upon a thing of planks and nails) an ark,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحَمَلْنَاهُ عَلَىٰ ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And We carried him on a (ship) made of planks and nails,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And We bore him that is Noah on one a ship made of planks and nails dusur is what boards are fastened down with of nails and the like; the singular is disār similar in pattern to kutub kitāb ‘book’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحَمَلْنَاهُ عَلَىٰ ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And We carried him on a (ship) made of planks and nails,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That ran (upon the waters) in Our sight) under Our protection, (as a reward for him who was rejected) He says: this is as a reward for the folk of Noah as a result of their disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Floating under Our Eyes: a reward for him who had been rejected!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: sailing before Our eyes that is in Our sights in other words it was being protected as retaliation jazā’an is in the accusative because of the implied verbal clause that is to say ‘they were drowned by way of revenge’ for the sake of him who was rejected namely Noah peace be upon him a variant reading for passive kufira has kafara ‘him who disbelieved’ in other words they were drowned as a punishment for them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Floating under Our Eyes: a reward for him who had been rejected!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We left it as a token) as a sign for people, i.e. We left the ark of Noah, after the death of Noah, as a sign for people; it is also said that this means: We left the similitude of Noah as a sign for people; (but is there any that remembereth) is there any that will take admonition from what was done to the folk of Noah and, hence, desist from transgression?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ تَّرَكْنَاهَا آيَةً فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. And indeed, We have left this as a sign. Then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We left it We preserved this deed as a sign for whomever might be admonished by it in other words the news of this deed became widely-known and endured. So is there anyone who will remember? anyone who will take heed from or be admonished by it? muddakir is actually mudhtakir but the tā’ has been replaced with a dāl likewise the dhāl and it the dāl has been assimilated with it the other dāl.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ تَّرَكْنَاهَا آيَةً فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. And indeed, We have left this as a sign. Then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings!) See, O Muhammad, how My punishment of these folk and how the state of those warned became, when Noah warned them but they rejected faith.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: How dreadful then were My chastisement and My warnings? this is an interrogative meant as an affirmative; kayfa ‘how’ is the predicate of kāna ‘was’ and it is here being used to inquire about a ‘state’; the intention is to prompt those who are being addressed to affirm the fact that God’s chastisement of those who denied Noah was fully deserved.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember) recite and write; it is also said that this means: We have made the recitation of the Qur'an easy; (but is there any that remembereth) is there any that seeks knowledge and hence be helped to acquire it?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. And We have indeed made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any who will remember (or receive admonition)? *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember We have facilitated its memorisation and disposed it to serve as a source of remembrance. So is there anyone who remember? anyone who will be admonished by it and memorise it? the interrogative here is intended as an imperative in other words memorise it and be admonished by it; none of God’s scriptures is memorised by heart other than it the Qur’ān.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. And We have indeed made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any who will remember (or receive admonition)? *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((The tribe of) 'Aad rejected warnings) the folk of Hud denied Hud. (Then how dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings) see, O Muhammad, how the state of those warned by Hud became when they disbelieved in him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. ‘Ād (people) denied (their Prophet, Hūd); then how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Ād denied their prophet Hūd and so they were chastised. How then were My chastisement and My warnings? how then was My warning them of the chastisement before it was sent down? In other words it was justified and He explains this chastisement by saying

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. ‘Ād (people) denied (their Prophet, Hūd); then how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We let loose on them a raging wind) a cold wind, which is the west wind (on a day of constant calamity) a day of continuous calamity upon the young and the old,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Verily, We sent against them a furious wind screaming on a day of evil omen and continuous calamity..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We unleashed upon them a clamorous wind intensely noisy on a day of prolonged ill fortune nahsin mustamirr means either one of continuous ill fortune or one of severe ill fortune — and this was the last Wednesday of the month —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Verily, We sent against them a furious wind screaming on a day of evil omen and continuous calamity..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Sweeping men away as though they were uprooted trunks of palm-trees.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Plucking out men as if they were uprooted stems of date-palms..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: tearing people away wrenching them from the holes in the ground in which they had been embedded and flinging them down to the ground head first thereby crushing their necks and severing their heads from their bodies as if they were while lying in this mentioned state trunks of uprooted palm-trees severed and thrown on the ground — they are likened to palm-trees because of their tallness nakhlun ‘palm-trees’ is masculine here but feminine in sūrat al-Hāqqa nakhlun khāwiya ‘fallen down or hollow palm-trees’ Q. 697 in order to harmonise with the end-rhyme of the verses in both instances.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Plucking out men as if they were uprooted stems of date-palms..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings!) See, O Muhammad, how was My punishment of them, and how was the state of those who were warned by Hud but did not believe him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: How then were My chastisement and My warnings?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember) and to recite; (but is there any that remembereth) is there any that takes admonition from what was done to the people of Hud and therefore abstain from transgression?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And We have indeed made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who will remember?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And We have indeed made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((The tribe of) Thamud) the folk of Salih (rejected warnings) disbelieved in Salih as well as in all the messengers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Thamūd (people also) denied the warnings..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thamūd denied the warnings nudhur is the plural of nadhīr with the sense of mundhir that is to say they denied those matters which their prophet Sālih warned them of if they refused to believe in him and to follow him

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Thamūd (people also) denied the warnings..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (For they said: Is it a mortal man) he is a human being like us, (alone among us, that we are to follow) his matter and religion? (Then) if we follow him (indeed we should fall into error) in manifest error (and madness) tiredness and toil.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَالُوۤاْ أَبَشَراً مِّنَّا وَاحِداً نَّتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّآ إِذاً لَّفِي ضَلاَلٍ وَسُعُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. And they said: “A man, alone among us — shall we follow him? Truly, then we should be in error and distress (or madness)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and they said ‘Is it a mortal basharan is in the accusative because it is governed by a succeeding verb alone among us minnā wāhidan are both adjectives of basharan that we are to follow? nattabi‘uhu this explains the verb which renders it basharan ‘mortal’ accusative; the interrogative is meant as a negative in other words why should we follow him when there are many of us and he is only one among us and not a king? That is to say we will not follow him. Then indeed if we were to follow him we would be in error a parting with reason and insanity!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَالُوۤاْ أَبَشَراً مِّنَّا وَاحِداً نَّتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّآ إِذاً لَّفِي ضَلاَلٍ وَسُعُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. And they said: “A man, alone among us — shall we follow him? Truly, then we should be in error and distress (or madness)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hath the remembrance) prophethood (been given unto him alone among us) when we are nobler than him? (Nay, but he is a rash liar) Salih is a vain liar who lies against Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَءُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِن بَيْنِنَا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. “Is it that the Reminder is sent to him [Prophet Ṣāliḥ S ] alone from among us? Nay, he is an insolent liar!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Has the Reminder the revelation been cast read a-ulqiya pronouncing both hamzas or by not pronouncing the second one but in both cases inserting an intervening alif or leaving this insertion out upon him alone from among us? in other words nothing has been revealed to him. Nay but he is a conceited an arrogant and insolent liar in his saying that the mentioned has been revealed to him. God exalted be He says

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَءُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِن بَيْنِنَا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. “Is it that the Reminder is sent to him [Prophet Ṣāliḥ S ] alone from among us? Nay, he is an insolent liar!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Salih said to them: (Tomorrow) on the Day of Judgement (they will know who is the rash liar) who is the vain liar who lies against Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً مَّنِ ٱلْكَذَّابُ ٱلأَشِرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Tomorrow they will come to know who is the liar, the insolent one!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘They will know tomorrow in the Hereafter who is the conceited liar and it is them for they will be chastised for having denied their prophet Sālih.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً مَّنِ ٱلْكَذَّابُ ٱلأَشِرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Tomorrow they will come to know who is the liar, the insolent one!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then Allah said to Salih: (Lo! We are sending the she-camel) We shall bring forth the she-camel from the rock (as a test for them) as a trial for your folk; (so watch them) wait until the she-camel is brought forth (and have patience) for the harm coming to you and for the killing of the she-camel;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا مُرْسِلُواْ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَّهُمْ فَٱرْتَقِبْهُمْ وَٱصْطَبِرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. Verily, We are sending the she-camel as a test for them. So watch them [O Ṣāliḥ], and be patient!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lo! We are sending the She-camel We will bring it forth out of the mountain the rock as they demanded as a trial a test for them that We may try them. So watch them O Sālih await to see what they will do and what will be done with them and remain patient istabir the tā’ here has replaced the tā’ of the 8th form ifta‘ala in other words endure their harm.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا مُرْسِلُواْ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَّهُمْ فَٱرْتَقِبْهُمْ وَٱصْطَبِرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. Verily, We are sending the she-camel as a test for them. So watch them [O Ṣāliḥ], and be patient!.
