meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And inform them that the water) of the well (is to be shared between (her and) them) one day for her and one day for them. (Every drinking will be witnessed) Salih informed them of this. They agreed to comply and observed this for a while but then their wretchedness overtook them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُّحْتَضَرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them, each one’s right to drink being established (by turns)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And inform them that the water is to be divided between them and the She-camel one day for them and the next for it every drinking every portion of water will be attended’ by the people drawing water on their designated day and by the She-camel on its day. They adhered to this regime but eventually became impatient with it and decided to slaughter the She-camel.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُّحْتَضَرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them, each one’s right to drink being established (by turns)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But they called their comrade) he called Masda' and Qudar Ibn Salif after Masda' Ibn Dahr shot her with an arrow (and he took) and Qudar took another arrow (and hamstrung (her)) killing the she-camel and dividing her meat.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَنَادَوْاْ صَاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. But they called their comrade and he took (a sword) and killed (her)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But they called their companion Qudār to slay it so he took he drew his sword and he hamstrung with it the She-camel in other words he slew her in compliance with their wish.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَنَادَوْاْ صَاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. But they called their comrade and he took (a sword) and killed (her)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then see) O Muhammad (how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings!) and how was the state of those warned by Salih but who rejected faith

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: How then were My chastisement and My warnings? My warning them of chastisement before it was sent down? In other words it was justified. He explains it their chastisement by saying

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Then, how (terrible) was My Torment and My Warnings?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We sent upon them one Shout) the shout of Gabriel three days after the killing of the she-camel, (and they became as the dry twigs (rejected by) the builder of a cattle fold) they became like the things in the cattle fold on which the cattle step.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. Verily, We sent against them a single Ṣaiḥah (torment — awful cry), and they became like the stubble of a fold-builder..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We unleashed upon them a single Cry and they became like the chaff of a corral builder al-muhtazir is one who makes a pen from dried tree-branches and thorns for his sheep to protect them from wolves and beasts of prey; the fallen parts which they tread are called hashīm.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. Verily, We sent against them a single Ṣaiḥah (torment — awful cry), and they became like the stubble of a fold-builder..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember) easy to take admonition from, and easy to memorise and recite; (but is there any that remembers) but is there any that takes admonition from what was done to the folk of Salih and, as a result, desist from transgression? It is also said that this means: is there any that seeks knowledge such that he is helped to acquire it?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَد يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. And indeed, We have made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who will remember?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَد يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. And indeed, We have made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The folk of Lot rejected warnings) they rejected Lot as well as all the messengers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. The people of Lūṭ (Lot) denied the warnings..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The people of Lot denied the warnings they denied those issues of which they were warned by his Lot’s tongue.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. The people of Lūṭ (Lot) denied the warnings..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We sent a storm of stones upon them (all) save the family of Lot) save Lot and his two daughters: Za'ura and Raytha, (whom We rescued in the last watch of the night) We rescued them at dawn,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حَاصِباً إِلاَّ آلَ لُوطٍ نَّجَّيْنَاهُم بِسَحَرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Verily, We sent against them a violent storm of stones (which destroyed them all), except the family of Lūṭ (Lot), We saved them in the last hour of the night,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We unleashed upon them a squall of pebbles a wind hurling at them pebbles namely small stones a single one of these being no larger than the palm of the hand and they were destroyed; all except the family of Lot namely his two daughters together with him whom We delivered at dawn from among the dawns the morning time of an unspecified day had a specific day been meant for that mentioned dawn it sahar would have been treated as a diptote instead of the declined form saharin being a definite noun derived from al-sahar for with definite nouns one ought to use the preceding definite article al. So was the squall unleashed at first with the family of Lot still there? There are two opinions regarding this in the case of the former that it was unleashed upon them including the family of Lot the exception is understood as a continuous one while in the case of the latter opinion that they were delivered before the squall the exception is understood as a discontinuous one even if it ‘the family of Lot’ is actually subsumed by the collective noun ‘the people of Lot’ and so they were delivered as a kindness from God;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حَاصِباً إِلاَّ آلَ لُوطٍ نَّجَّيْنَاهُم بِسَحَرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Verily, We sent against them a violent storm of stones (which destroyed them all), except the family of Lūṭ (Lot), We saved them in the last hour of the night,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (As grace from Us) as mercy from Us. (Thus We reward him who gives thanks) thus We save he who believes in Our divine Oneness and gives thanks for Our bounty.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نِّعْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي مَن شَكَرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. As a Favour from Us. Thus do We reward him who gives thanks (by obeying Us)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: as a grace ni‘matan is a verbal noun that is to say in‘āman ‘an act of grace’ from Us. So like that requital do We requite him who gives thanks for Our graces and is a believer or it means him who is a believer in God and His messenger and is obedient to both.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نِّعْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي مَن شَكَرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. As a Favour from Us. Thus do We reward him who gives thanks (by obeying Us)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he) Lot (indeed had warned them of Our blow) of Our chastisement, (but they did doubt the warnings) but they rejected what Lot said to them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَنذَرَهُمْ بَطْشَتَنَا فَتَمَارَوْاْ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And he [Lūṭ (Lot)] indeed had warned them of Our Seizure (punishment), but they did doubt the warnings!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily he had warned them Lot had threatened them of Our strike Our seizing them with chastisement but they disputed they contested and denied the warnings his warning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَنذَرَهُمْ بَطْشَتَنَا فَتَمَارَوْاْ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. And he [Lūṭ (Lot)] indeed had warned them of Our Seizure (punishment), but they did doubt the warnings!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They even asked of him his guests for an ill purpose) they wanted his guests, Gabriel and the angels who were with him, for their abominable deed. (Then We blinded their eyes) Gabriel blinded their eyes ((and said): Taste now My punishment after My warnings!) And I said to them: taste now My punishment and the warning of My warners!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَاوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنَآ أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And they indeed sought to shame his guests (by asking to commit sodomy with them). So, We blinded their eyes, (saying) “Then taste you My Torment and My Warnings.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they had even solicited of him his guests that he should let them have their own way with those who had come to him as guests that they may do wicked things with them — and these guests were angels. So We blotted out their eyes We blinded them and made them without slits so that they were continuous folds of skin like the rest of the face by having Gabriel smack them with his wing. ‘So taste now so We said to them taste My chastisement and My warnings’ that is to say taste the effects and the substance of My warning and My threat.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَاوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنَآ أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. And they indeed sought to shame his guests (by asking to commit sodomy with them). So, We blinded their eyes, (saying) “Then taste you My Torment and My Warnings.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in truth the punishment decreed befell them early in the morning) and this punishment is connected with the punishment of the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُم بُكْرَةً عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. And verily, an abiding torment seized them early in the morning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily there greeted them in the early morning the morning time of an unspecified day an abiding chastisement a permanent chastisement continuous with the chastisement of the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُم بُكْرَةً عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. And verily, an abiding torment seized them early in the morning..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Now taste My punishment after My warnings!) And I said to them: taste My punishment and the warning of My warners; those whom Lot warned but did not believe him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. “Then taste you My Torment and My Warnings.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘So taste now My chastisement and My warnings!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. “Then taste you My Torment and My Warnings.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember) to memorise, recite and write down; (but is there any that remembereth) but is there any that takes admonition from what was done to the folk of Lot and, hence, desist from transgression?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And indeed, We have made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We have made the Qur’ān easy to remember. So is there anyone who will remember?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. And indeed, We have made the Qur’ān easy to understand and remember; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And warnings came in truth unto the house of Pharaoh) Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and his folk

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ ٱلنُّذُرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And indeed, warnings came to the people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) [through Mūsā (Moses) and Hārūn (Aaron)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily there came to Pharaoh’s folk his people together with him the warnings the warning by the tongue of Moses and Aaron but they did not believe.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ ٱلنُّذُرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. And indeed, warnings came to the people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) [through Mūsā (Moses) and Hārūn (Aaron)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who denied Our revelations, every one) of the nine signs. (Therefore We grasped them with the grasp of the Mighty) by means of punishment, (the Powerful) to inflict punishment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبُواْ بِئَايَاتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ أَخْذَ عِزِيزٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. They denied all Our Signs, so We seized them with a Seizure of the All-Mighty, All-Capable (Omnipotent)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Rather They denied Our signs all nine of them which were given to Moses. So We seized them by way of chastisement with the seizing of One Who is Mighty Strong Omnipotent Powerful Whom nothing can thwart.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبُواْ بِئَايَاتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ أَخْذَ عِزِيزٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. They denied all Our Signs, so We seized them with a Seizure of the All-Mighty, All-Capable (Omnipotent)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Are your disbelievers) O Muhammad; and it is said: O people of Mecca (better than those) We related to you, (or have ye some immunity in the Scriptures) from punishment?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَكُفَّٰرُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أُوْلَٰئِكُمْ أَمْ لَكُم بَرَآءَةٌ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. Are your disbelievers (O Quraish!) better than these [nations of Nūḥ (Noah), Lūṭ (Lot), Ṣāliḥ, and the people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) who were destroyed]? Or have you an immunity (against Our Torment) in the Divine Scriptures?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Are your disbelievers O Quraysh better than those? mentioned beginning from the people of Noah to those of Pharaoh which is why they have not been chastised? Or have you O disbelievers of Quraysh been granted some immunity from chastisement in the Scriptures? the Books? the interrogative in both instances is meant as a denial in other words it is not so.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَكُفَّٰرُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أُوْلَٰئِكُمْ أَمْ لَكُم بَرَآءَةٌ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 43. Are your disbelievers (O Quraish!) better than these [nations of Nūḥ (Noah), Lūṭ (Lot), Ṣāliḥ, and the people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) who were destroyed]? Or have you an immunity (against Our Torment) in the Divine Scriptures?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or say they) i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca: (We are a host victorious) and immune from punishment?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. Or say they: “We are a great multitude, victorious.?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or do they the disbelievers of Quraysh say ‘We are a host that will be helped to victory’? against Muhammad (s)? When Abū Jahl on the day of Badr said ‘We are a host that will be helped to victory’ the following was revealed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. Or say they: “We are a great multitude, victorious.?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The hosts) the hosts of the disbelieving (will all be routed) on the Day of Badr (and will turn and flee) defeated; this refers to Abu Jahl and his host, some of whom were killed on the Day of Badr and others defeated.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. Their multitude will be defeated, and they will show their backs..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The host will truly be routed and turn its back to flee and so they were defeated at Badr and God’s Messenger s was granted victory over them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. Their multitude will be defeated, and they will show their backs..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but the Hour (of doom)) the advent of the Hour (is their appointed tryst) of punishment, (and the Hour) of punishment (will be more wretched) more tremendous (and more bitter) than the punishment they suffered on the Day of Badr.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Nay, but the Hour is their appointed time (for their full recompense), and the Hour will be more grievous and more bitter..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay but the Hour is their tryst for chastisement and the Hour that is the chastisement thereat will be more calamitous greater in affliction and more bitter than the chastisement of this world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Nay, but the Hour is their appointed time (for their full recompense), and the Hour will be more grievous and more bitter..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! the guilty) the idolaters: Abu Jahl and his host (are in error) in manifest error in the life of the world (and madness) toil and tiredness in hell.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ وَسُعُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. Verily, the Mujrimūn (polytheists, disbelievers, sinners, criminals) are in error (in this world) and will burn (in the Hell-fire in the Hereafter)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed the guilty are in error in the destruction of being killed in this world and in a blazing fire a fire that has been set ablaze musa‘‘ara that is fiercely ignited in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ وَسُعُرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. Verily, the Mujrimūn (polytheists, disbelievers, sinners, criminals) are in error (in this world) and will burn (in the Hell-fire in the Hereafter)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (On the day) which is the Day of Judgement (when they are dragged into the Fire) the angels of the Fire will drag them (upon their faces) and these angels will say to them: (Feel the touch of hell) taste the punishment of the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. The Day they will be dragged on their faces into the Fire (it will be said to them): “Taste you the touch of Hell!” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The day when they are dragged into the Fire on their faces in the Hereafter and it is said to them ‘Taste now the touch of Saqar’ Hell’s affliction of you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. The Day they will be dragged on their faces into the Fire (it will be said to them): “Taste you the touch of Hell!” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! We have created every thing) of your works (by measure) by you rejected this. This verse was revealed about those who argued about destiny.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Verily, We have created all things with Qadar . (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly everything read inna kulla shay’in is in the accusative as a dependent clause because of a verb governing it have We created in a measure by ordainment bi-qadarin ‘in a measure’ is a circumstantial qualifier referring to kulla ‘every’ in other words ‘already predetermined’; a variant reading for kulla has nominative kullu as the subject the predicate of which is khalaqnāhu ‘We have created’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Verily, We have created all things with Qadar . (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Our commandment) concerning the coming of the Hour (is but one (commandment)) is but one word, (as the twinkling of an eye) in its swiftness. It is also said that (We have created every thing) means: We have created for everything something similar to it and also that which agrees with it of clothes and things.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِٱلْبَصَرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And Our Commandment is but one as the twinkling of an eye..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And Our command for a thing which We want to bring into existence is but a single word like the twinkling of an eye in terms of speed and this is the saying of kun ‘Be’ whereat it comes into existence. His command when He wills a thing is just to say to it ‘Be’ and it is Q. 3682.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِٱلْبَصَرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. And Our Commandment is but one as the twinkling of an eye..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily We have destroyed your fellows) We have destroyed the like of you and those who followed your religion, O people of Mecca; (but is there any that remembereth) is there any that takes admonition from what was done with them and, thus, desist from transgression?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَآ أَشْيَاعَكُمْ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And indeed, We have destroyed your likes; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily We have destroyed the likes of you the likes of you in terms of disbelief from among past communities. So is there anyone who will remember? this is an interrogative meant as an imperative that is to say ‘Remember and be admonished!’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَآ أَشْيَاعَكُمْ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And indeed, We have destroyed your likes; then is there any that will remember (or receive admonition)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And every thing they did) of transgression in their state of idolatry and opposition of the prophets (is in the Scriptures) written down; and it is said this means: it is written in the Guarded Tablet. This also was revealed about those who disputed about fate.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. And everything they have done is noted in (their) Records (of deeds)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And everything they that is servants have done is recorded in the scrolls the books of the Guardian Angels al-hafaza

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. And everything they have done is noted in (their) Records (of deeds)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And every small and great thing) of good or evil (is recorded) in the Guarded Tablet; this was revealed about the people who disputed about fate and who denied that everything is recorded in the Guarded Tablet.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. And everything, small and big, is written down (in Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ already beforehand i.e. before it befalls, or is done by its doer: ) 1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and every small and great sin or deed is inscribed is recorded in the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 53. And everything, small and big, is written down (in Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ already beforehand i.e. before it befalls, or is done by its doer: ) 1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! the righteous) those who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies (will dwell among Gardens and rivers) many rivers; and it is said: in vast meadows,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. Verily, The Muttaqūn (the pious)(2), will be in the midst of Gardens and Rivers (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly the God-fearing will be amid gardens orchards and rivers the collective noun is meant here; a variant reading for nahar has the plural nuhur similar in form to asad ‘lion’ plural usud the meaning being that they will drink from its rivers water milk honey and wine;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 54. Verily, The Muttaqūn (the pious)(2), will be in the midst of Gardens and Rivers (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Firmly established) they are in an honoured place in Paradise (in the favour of a Mighty King) Who is able to dispense both reward and punishment to His slaves'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. In a seat of truth (i.e. Paradise), near the Omnipotent King (Allāh, the One, the All‑Blessed, the Most High, the Owner of Majesty and Honour). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: in an abode of truth a place of truth wherein there is no idle talk or cause for sin — the collective noun maq‘ad is meant here; a variant reading has maqā‘id ‘abodes’ in other words they are in congregations in Paradise that are free from idle talk and cause for sin in contrast to the congregations of this world which are rarely free from such things syntactically this statement is considered a second predicate and also a substitution; it the ‘abode’ may be understood as being ‘one of truth’ regardless of whether one reads the substitution as being of the part for the whole or otherwise; before a King malīk this form is hyperbolic that is to say One of a mighty and vast kingdom Who is Omnipotent Powerful Whom nothing can thwart namely God exalted be He ‘inda indicates glorious rank and closeness to His bounty exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 55. In a seat of truth (i.e. Paradise), near the Omnipotent King (Allāh, the One, the All‑Blessed, the Most High, the Owner of Majesty and Honour). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said: “When the verse (Say (unto mankind): Cry unto Allah, or cry unto the Beneficent) [17:111] was revealed, the disbelievers of Mecca-Abu Jahl, al-Walid, 'Utbah and Shaybah and their hosts-said: we know no one called the Beneficent except Musaylimah the liar who lives in Yamamah. So he is this Beneficent one, O Muhammad?” And so Allah revealed this: (The Beneficent

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The Most Gracious (Allāh)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The Compassionate One God exalted be He

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The Most Gracious (Allāh)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Hath made known the Qur'an) to Gabriel and the latter to Muhammad, and Muhammad to his nation. Allah sent Gabriel with the Qur'an to Muhammad (pbuh) and the Prophet taught it to his nation.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. He has taught (you mankind) the Qur’ān (by His Mercy)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: has taught whomever He will the Qur’ān.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. He has taught (you mankind) the Qur’ān (by His Mercy)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He hath created man) i.e. Adam from the surface of the earth.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He created man..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He created man the species mankind

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He created man..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He hath taught him utterance) Allah inspired him with the exposition of everything as well as with the names of every beast on the surface of the earth.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَّمَهُ ٱلبَيَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. He taught him eloquent speech..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: teaching him the coherent speech utterance.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَّمَهُ ٱلبَيَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. He taught him eloquent speech..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The sun and the moon are made punctual) their orbits are measured; and it is also said that this means: they are suspended half way between heaven and earth; and it is also said that this means: they both will be taken to task and have a lifespan like the lifespan of human beings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. The sun and the moon run on their fixed courses (exactly) calculated with measured out stages for each (for reckoning)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The sun and the moon follow a reckoning they move according to a strict calculation

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. The sun and the moon run on their fixed courses (exactly) calculated with measured out stages for each (for reckoning)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The najm and the trees adore) the stars and the trees prostrate to the Beneficent; and it is also said that najm refers to vegetation that has no stalks.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلنَّجْمُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And the herbs (or stars) and the trees both prostrate themselves (to Allah) (1). (Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the grass all stalkless vegetation and the trees that vegetation which possesses stalk prostrate comply with what is required of them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلنَّجْمُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And the herbs (or stars) and the trees both prostrate themselves (to Allah) (1). (Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the sky He hath uplifted) above everything; such that nothing touches it; (and He hath set the measure) on the earth; He explained fair measure through the scale,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And the heaven: He has raised it high, and He has set up the Balance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He has raised the heaven and set up the balance He has established justice

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And the heaven: He has raised it high, and He has set up the Balance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That ye exceed not the measure) that you do not transgress or be unjust in measure,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ فِي ٱلْمِيزَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. In order that you may not transgress (due) balance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: declaring that you should not contravene that is to say so that you may not do wrong with regard to the balance that instrument with which one weighs.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ فِي ٱلْمِيزَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. In order that you may not transgress (due) balance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But observe the measure strictly) keep the balance of the scale justly; and it is also said that this means: observe your tongues by saying only the Truth, (nor fall short thereof) do not weigh less for the people such that you take away their rights.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلاَ تُخْسِرُواْ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And observe the weight with equity and do not make the balance deficient..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And observe the weights with justice fairly and do not skimp the balance do not decrease the value of what is being weighed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلاَ تُخْسِرُواْ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And observe the weight with equity and do not make the balance deficient..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the earth hath He appointed) He spread it on the water (for (His) creatures) for all created beings whether dead or alive,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلأَنَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And the earth: He has put down (laid) for the creatures..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the earth He placed it He fixed it in place for all creatures man jinn and others.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلأَنَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And the earth: He has put down (laid) for the creatures..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Wherein) in the earth (are fruit) different kind of fruits (and sheathed palm-trees) which has foreskin or shells, or anything that has not sprouted up.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَٱلنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ ٱلأَكْمَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Therein are fruits, and date‑palms producing sheathed fruit-stalks (enclosing dates). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: In it are fruits and the familiar date-palms with sheaths the spathes containing its flowers

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَٱلنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ ٱلأَكْمَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Therein are fruits, and date‑palms producing sheathed fruit-stalks (enclosing dates). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Husked grain) all kind of grain (and scented herb) spikes of grain and fruits.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْحَبُّ ذُو ٱلْعَصْفِ وَٱلرَّيْحَانُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And also corn, with (its) leaves and stalk for fodder, and sweet-scented plants..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: (Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny) and claim that they are not from Allah, O jinn and humans? This is addressed to all human beings except Muhammad (pbuh).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So which of your Lord’s favours graces will you deny? tukadhdhibān is mentioned thirty one times; the interrogative is meant to be understood as an affirmative judging by what al-Hākim al-Naysābūrī reported by way of an isnād from Jābir b. ‘Abd Allāh al-Ansārī who said ‘The Messenger of God s was reciting surāt al-Rahmān to us and when he completed it he said “What is wrong with you that you have been silent throughout? Verily the jinn are more responsive than you. Not once did I recite this verse to them — So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny? — but that they said ‘Not one of your graces our Lord do we deny for all praise belongs to You’ ”.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He created man) i.e. Adam (of clay like the potter's) out of which pottery is made,

meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. He created man (Adam) from sounding clay like the clay of pottery..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He created man Adam of dry clay salsāl a dry hollow mud producing an echo if tapped resembling the potter’s fakhkhār clay that has been baked

meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. He created man (Adam) from sounding clay like the clay of pottery..

tafsir: (And the jinn) the father of the jinn and satans (did He create of smokeless fire.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lord of the two Easts) the East of winter and the East of summer, (and Lord of the two Wests) the West of winter and the West of summer! There are two Easts and two Wests. The East of winter and the East of summer have 180 phases just as the two Wests and the moon have 180 phases. It is also said that the Easts of summer and winter have 177 phases and the Wests of summer and winter as well as the moon have 177 phases. The sun rises throughout the year two days in the same phase and it also sets two days in the same phase.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. (He is) the Lord of the two easts (places of sunrise during early summer and early winter) and the Lord of the two wests (places of sunset during early summer and early winter)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lord of the two Easts the points of the winter sunrise and the summer sunrise and Lord of the two Wests likewise the two points of sunset.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ

tafsir: He hath loosed the two seas) the sweet and the salty. (They meet) without mixing.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. He has let loose the two seas (the salt and fresh water) meeting together..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He has loosed the two waters the sweet and the salty; and so they meet in the perception of the eye.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. He has let loose the two seas (the salt and fresh water) meeting together..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There is a barrier) from Allah (between them) between the sweet and salty seas. (They encroach not (one upon the other)) nor does any one of them change the taste of the other.

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Between them there is a barrier by His power exalted be He. They do not overstep neither of the two encroaches upon the other to become mixed with it.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: There cometh forth from both of them) but especially from the salty one (the pearl) big in size (and coral stone) small in size.

tafsir: From both of them from the point at which they seem to meet — but which is actually from only one of the two and that is the salt water — is brought forth yukhraju passive may also be read as active yakhruju ‘emerge’ the pearl and the coral marjān these are red pieces of shell or small pearls.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا ٱلُّلؤْلُؤُ وَٱلمَرْجَانُ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: His are the crafted ships that sail in the sea appearing like landmarks like mountains in their tremendous size and height.

tafsir: Everyone that is thereon) on the face of the earth (will pass away) will die; it is also said that this means: everyone upon it will vanish; and it is also said that this means: every act that is done for other than Allah will perish;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Whatsoever is on it (the earth) will perish..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Everyone who is on it that is on the earth of animal beings will perish man ‘who’ is used to indicate predominance of rational beings;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. Whatsoever is on it (the earth) will perish..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There remaineth but the Countenance of thy Lord) dies not; and it is also said that this means: the righteous works which are performed for the sake of Allah's Countenance will not perish (of Might) Who possesses might and sovereignty (and Glory) and who also possesses forgiveness and beneficence.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلاَلِ وَٱلإِكْرَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And the Face of your Lord full of Majesty and Honour will remain forever..

meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And the Face of your Lord full of Majesty and Honour will remain forever..

meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: All that are in the heavens) among the angels (and the earth) among the believers. The inhabitants of the earth ask Him forgiveness, success, preservation from sin, bestowal of honour and provision (entreat Him. Every day He exerciseth (universal) power) He gives life, He takes life, He raises, He abases, He brings into the world a new born baby, He releases a prisoner; and the things He exercises are beyond count.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَسْأَلُهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Whosoever is in the heavens and on earth begs of Him (its needs from Him). Every day He is (engaged) in some affair (such as giving honour or disgrace to some, life or death to some, etc.)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: All that is in the heavens and the earth implore Him either by way of speech or by their very state of dependence on Him for the strength which they require for worship for provision forgiveness and other things. Every day all the time He is upon some matter something that He manifests in accordance with what He has decreed since pre-eternity such as the giving of life the bringing of death exalting and abasing individuals giving abundantly and withholding responding to a supplicating person and giving the one requesting something and so on and so forth.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Whosoever is in the heavens and on earth begs of Him (its needs from Him). Every day He is (engaged) in some affair (such as giving honour or disgrace to some, life or death to some, etc.)!.

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny) which of the blessings of your Lord, O men and jinn-here to the exception of Muhammad (pbuh)-do you reject and claim that it is not from Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. Then, which of the Blessings of your Lord will you both (jinn and men) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Blessed be the Name of thy Lord) your Lord is the Possessor of grace and Mercy; and it is said: Allah exonerates Himself from having a son or partner, (Mighty) the Possessor of might and sovereignty (and Glorious) and the Possessor of forgiveness and beneficence upon the advent of the Day of Judgement!'

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبَارَكَ ٱسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي ٱلْجَلاَلِ وَٱلإِكْرَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. Blessed is the Name of your Lord (Allāh), the Owner of Majesty and Honour. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Blessed be the Name of your Lord He of Majesty and Munificence as explained above; the word ism is extra.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبَارَكَ ٱسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي ٱلْجَلاَلِ وَٱلإِكْرَامِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. Blessed is the Name of your Lord (Allāh), the Owner of Majesty and Honour. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (When the event befalleth): '(When the event befalleth) He says: when the Day of Judgement comes.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا وَقَعَتِ ٱلْوَاقِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. When the Event (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) befalls..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When the imminent Event comes to pass when the Resurrection takes place

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا وَقَعَتِ ٱلْوَاقِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. When the Event (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) befalls..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There is no denying that it will befall) its coming cannot be repulsed, delayed or contain any ambiguity.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And there can be no denial of its befalling..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: there will be no denying its coming to pass there is no soul to deny it by repudiating it as it did in this world

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And there can be no denial of its befalling..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Abasing (some)) due to their own works and, thus, sends them to the Fire, (exalting (others)) due to their own works and, thus, sends to the Garden. It is also said it is called the Event because of its sound which will be heard by the near and the far;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Bringing low (some — those who will enter Hell), Exalting (others — those who will enter Paradise). [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr].
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: it will be abasing some exalting others that is it will manifest the abasing of some people by virtue of their admission into the Fire and manifest the exalting of others by their admission into Paradise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Bringing low (some — those who will enter Hell), Exalting (others — those who will enter Paradise). [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr].
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When the earth is shaken with a shock) when the earth is shaken with such an earthquake that every mountain and building in it will be obliterated and turn into rubble.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا رُجَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ رَجّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. When the earth will be shaken with a terrible shake..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When the earth is shaken with a violent shock

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا رُجَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ رَجّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. When the earth will be shaken with a terrible shake..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the hills are ground to powder) and it is also said: and the hills are made to move like the passing of the clouds; and it is also said that this means: when the hills are uprooted from their spots.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And the mountains will be powdered to dust,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the mountains are pulverised to tiny pieces

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And the mountains will be powdered to dust,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So that they become a scattered dust) like the dust which sticks to the hooves of beasts or the atoms of dust which can be seen when the rays of the sun emerge from a hole in a house or a crack in a door,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَانَتْ هَبَآءً مُّنبَثّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. So that they will become floating dust particles..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: so that they become a scattered dust the second idh ‘when’ is a substitution for the first idh

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَانَتْ هَبَآءً مُّنبَثّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. So that they will become floating dust particles..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And ye will be) on the Day of Judgement (three kinds:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُنتُمْ أَزْوَاجاً ثَلاَثَةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And you (all) will be in three groups..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and you will be at the Resurrection three kinds categories

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَكُنتُمْ أَزْوَاجاً ثَلاَثَةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And you (all) will be in three groups..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (First) those on the right hand) these are the inhabitants of the Garden who will be given their scrolls in their right hands; they are the ones about whom Allah said: " These are destined for Paradise, and I care not " ; (what of those on the right hand) arousing by this expression the wonder of His Prophet: and what do you know, O Muhammad, about the bliss, happiness and honour of the people of the Garden?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. So those on the Right Hand (i.e. those who will be given their Records in their right hands) — how (fortunate) will be those on the Right Hand! (As respect for them, because they will enter Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Those of the right hand those who are given their record of deeds in their right hand fa-ashābu’l-maymanati is the subject the predicate of which is the following mā ashābu’l-maymanati — what of those of the right hand? — a glorification of their status on account of their admittance into Paradise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. So those on the Right Hand (i.e. those who will be given their Records in their right hands) — how (fortunate) will be those on the Right Hand! (As respect for them, because they will enter Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (then) those on the left hand) these are the dwellers of the Fire who will be given their scrolls in their left hands; they are the ones about whom Allah said: “These are destined for hell, and I care not”; (what of those on the left hand) again arousing the wonder of His Prophet: and what do you know, O Muhammad, about the humiliation, punishment and chastisement suffered by the dwellers of hell?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And those on the Left Hand (i.e. those who will be given their Records in their left hands) — how (unfortunate) will be those on the Left Hand! (As disgrace for them, because they will enter Hell)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And those of the left hand al-mash’ama means al-shimāl ‘left’ each of whom is given his record of deeds in their left hands — what of those of the left hand? — an expression of contempt for their status on account of their admittance into the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And those on the Left Hand (i.e. those who will be given their Records in their left hands) — how (unfortunate) will be those on the Left Hand! (As disgrace for them, because they will enter Hell)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the foremost in the race) and the forerunners in the life of the world towards faith, migration, jihad, the utterance of the first “Allahu akbar” [Allah is the greatest] as well as towards all good things, these are (the foremost in the race) the forerunners in the Hereafter towards the Garden:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلسَّابِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And the foremost ones [(in Islāmic Faith of Monotheism and in performing righteous deeds) in the life of this world on the very first call for to embrace Islām] will be the foremost (in Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And the foremost in the race to do good namely the prophets al-sābiqūna is a subject the foremost this repetition is to emphasise their exalted status; the predicate is the following ūlā’ika’l-muqarrabūna

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلسَّابِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And the foremost ones [(in Islāmic Faith of Monotheism and in performing righteous deeds) in the life of this world on the very first call for to embrace Islām] will be the foremost (in Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Those are they who will be brought nigh) to Allah

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. These will be the nearest (to Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: they are the ones brought near to God

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. These will be the nearest (to Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (In Gardens of Delight) whose delight is eternal;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي جَنَّاتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. In the Gardens of Delight (Paradise).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: in the Gardens of Bliss

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي جَنَّاتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. In the Gardens of Delight (Paradise).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (A multitude of those of old) a group of people from the earlier nations before the community of Muhammad (pbuh)

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. A multitude of those (foremost) will be from the first generations (who embraced Islām)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: a multitude from the former generations thullatun mina’l-awwalīna the subject that is to say a group of individuals from communities of old

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. A multitude of those (foremost) will be from the first generations (who embraced Islām)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And a few of those of later time) and a group from the later nations, which is the community of Muhammad (pbuh). It is also said that both groups are from the community of Muhammad (pbuh). When Allah's saying (A multitude of those of old), the Prophet (pbuh) and his Companions were aggrieved because of it, until Allah revealed (And a few of those of later time).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنَ ٱلآخِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And a few of those (foremost) will be from the later generations..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and a few from the later ones from among the community of Muhammad (s) being the foremost from among the communities of old and this community the predicate is the following ‘alā sururin mawdūnatin

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنَ ٱلآخِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And a few of those (foremost) will be from the later generations..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (On lined couches) sitting on couches linked to each other by branches of gold and silver, weaved with pearls and sapphires,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. (They will be) on thrones woven with gold and precious stones..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: will be upon encrusted couches their linings woven onto rods of gold and jewels

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. (They will be) on thrones woven with gold and precious stones..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Reclining) in comfort (therein) on couches (face to face) upon visitation.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُّتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْهَا مُتَقَابِلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Reclining thereon, face to face..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: reclining on them face to face muttaki’īna ‘alayhā mutaqābilīna constitute two circumstantial qualifiers referring to the subject person of the predicate ‘they’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مُّتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْهَا مُتَقَابِلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Reclining thereon, face to face..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (There wait on them) for service (immortal youths) servants; it is also said that these are the children of the disbelievers who are made servants for the people of Paradise. Another way of reading this verse is (There wait on them youths, and they are immortal): i.e. they will never die nor leave the Garden.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Immortal boys will go around them (serving),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They will be waited on by immortal youths resembling young boys never ageing;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Immortal boys will go around them (serving),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: The youth will go round (With bowls and ewers and a cup from a pure spring) of pure running wine

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ وَكَأْسٍ مِّن مَّعِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. With cups, and jugs, and a glass of flowing wine,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: with goblets akwāb are drinking-vessels without handles and ewers abārīq are vessels that have handles and spouts and a cup ka’s is the vessel for drinking wine from a flowing spring in other words wine flowing from a spring that never runs out

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ وَكَأْسٍ مِّن مَّعِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. With cups, and jugs, and a glass of flowing wine,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Wherefrom they get no aching of the head) from drinking (nor any madness) nor get intoxicated; it is also said that this means, according to another reading: their drinking is continuous,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْهَا وَلاَ يُنزِفُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Wherefrom they will get neither any aching of the head, nor any intoxication..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: wherefrom they suffer no headache nor any stupefaction read yanzafūna or yanzifūna respectively derived from nazafa or anzafa al-shāribu ‘the drinker became inebriated’ in other words they do not get a headache from it nor do they lose their senses in contrast to the case with the wine of this world;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْهَا وَلاَ يُنزِفُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Wherefrom they will get neither any aching of the head, nor any intoxication..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And fruit) different kinds of fruit (that they prefer) that they desire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَاكِهَةٍ مِّمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And with fruit that they may choose..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and such fruits as they prefer

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَاكِهَةٍ مِّمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And with fruit that they may choose..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And flesh of fowls that they desire) and different types of birds' meat that they desire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَحْمِ طَيْرٍ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And with the flesh of fowls that they desire..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and such flesh of fowls as they desire for themselves to enjoy

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَحْمِ طَيْرٍ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And with the flesh of fowls that they desire..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And (there are) fair ones with wide, lovely eyes,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحُورٌ عِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And (there will be) Ḥūr (fair females) with wide, lovely eyes (as wives for Al-Muttaqūn-the pious-) (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and houris maidens with intensely black eyes set against the whiteness of their irises with wide eyes ‘īn the ‘ayn here is inflected with a kasra instead of a damma because it the kasra better harmonises with the yā’; the singular is ‘aynā’ similar in pattern to hamrā’; a variant reading for wa-hūrun ‘īn has the genitive case wa-hūrin ‘īn

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحُورٌ عِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And (there will be) Ḥūr (fair females) with wide, lovely eyes (as wives for Al-Muttaqūn-the pious-) (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Like unto hidden pearls) hidden from heat and cold,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَأَمْثَالِ ٱللُّؤْلُؤِ ٱلْمَكْنُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Like the preserved pearls..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: resembling hidden guarded pearls

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَأَمْثَالِ ٱللُّؤْلُؤِ ٱلْمَكْنُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Like the preserved pearls..

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And indeed it the swearing by these setting-places of stars is a tremendous oath if you only knew — if you were people of deep knowledge you would realise the magnitude of this oath.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 76. And verily that is indeed a great oath, if you but know. (1) Tafsīr Al-Qurṭubī. (2).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That (this) is indeed a noble Qur'an) a noble and bounteous Qur'an

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 77. That (this) is indeed an honourable recitation (the Noble Qur’ān)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: This namely what is being recited to you is indeed a noble Qur’ān

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي كِتَابٍ مَّكْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. In a Book well-guarded (with Allāh in the heaven i.e. Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ)..

tafsir: in a Book inscribed guarded preserved and this is the Mushaf;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي كِتَابٍ مَّكْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 78. In a Book well-guarded (with Allāh in the heaven i.e. Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Which none toucheth) i.e. the Guarded Tablet (save the purified) from ritual impurities and sins, i.e. the angels; it is also said that this means: none acts upon the Qur'an except those who are given success,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يَمَسُّهُ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُطَهَّرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 79. Which (that Book with Allāh) none can touch but the purified (i.e. the angels)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: which none touch lā yamassuhu is a predicate functioning as a prohibitive command except the purified those who have purified themselves of ritual impurities 5680 a revelation revealed by the Lord of the Worlds.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَّ يَمَسُّهُ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُطَهَّرُونَ

tafsir: (A revelation) a speech (from the Lord of the Worlds) unto Muhammad (pbuh).

meta_data.ayah_translation: 80. A Revelation (this Qur’ān) from the Lord of the ‘Alamīn (mankind, jinn and all that exists)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Do you then belittle do you take lightly and deny this discourse? the Qur’ān.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنزِيلٌ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ

tafsir: (Is it this Statement) is it this Qur'an which Muhammad (pbuh) recites to you, O people of Mecca, (that ye scorn) that you deny, and claim that there is no Paradise or hell, resurrection or reckoning, as the Prophet says,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَبِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَنتُمْ مُّدْهِنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 81. Is it such a talk (this Qur’ān) that you (disbelievers) deny?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And for your livelihood in the way of rain that is to say the thanks for it you offer your denial? of God’s granting it to you by saying ‘We have rain because of this or that storm’?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَبِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَنتُمْ مُّدْهِنُونَ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And make denial thereof your livelihood) and say about the rain that you are given: we were given rain because of such-and-such a storm?

meta_data.ayah_translation: 82. And instead (of thanking Allāh) for the provision He gives you, you deny (Him by disbelief)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. Then why do you not (intervene) when (the soul of a dying person) reaches the throat?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Why then when it the spirit during the throes of death reaches the dying person’s throat hulqūm is the passage for food

meta_data.ayah_translation: 83. Then why do you not (intervene) when (the soul of a dying person) reaches the throat?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And ye) O people of Mecca (are at that moment looking) when his soul will come out

meta_data.ayah_translation: 84. And you at the moment are looking on,.

tafsir: and you are O you attending the dying person at that moment looking at him —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 84. And you at the moment are looking on,.

tafsir: (And We are nearer unto him) the angel of death and his aids are closer to the dying person (than ye are) than his own family, (but ye see not) the angel of death and his aids.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنكُمْ وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُبْصِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 85. But We (i.e. Our angels who take the soul) are nearer to him than you, but you see not, (Tafsīr Aṭ-Ṭabarī).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and We are nearer to him than you are to know of his state but you do not perceive tubsirūna derives from al-basīra ‘perception’ that is to say you do not realise this —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنكُمْ وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تُبْصِرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 85. But We (i.e. Our angels who take the soul) are nearer to him than you, but you see not, (Tafsīr Aṭ-Ṭabarī).

tafsir: why then if you are not going to face a reckoning if you are not going to be requited by your being resurrected in other words why then if you are not going to be resurrected as you claim

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَوْلاَ إِن كُنتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 86. Then why do you not — if you are exempt from the reckoning and recompense (punishment) —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Do ye not force it back) force the soul back to the body, (if ye are truthful) that you are not legally bound?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَرْجِعُونَهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. Bring back the soul (to its body), if you are truthful?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: do you not bring it back why do you not restore the spirit to the body after it has reached the throat if you are truthful? in what you claim the second law-lā ‘why … if’ is repeated to emphasise the first one; idhā ‘when’ is an adverbial particle qualifying tarji‘ūna ‘bring it back’ to which both conditions are semantically connected. The meaning is ‘Why do you not bring it back when in repudiating resurrection you are being truthful in this repudiation?’ That is to say ‘Let death also be repudiated as impossible in its case just as you claim that resurrection is impossible’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَرْجِعُونَهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 87. Bring back the soul (to its body), if you are truthful?.

tafsir: (Then breath of life) then rest for them in the grave; and it is also said that this means: then there is mercy for them, (and plenty) when they come out of the grave; and it is also said this means: and provision, (and a Garden of Delight) on the Day of Judgement whose delight is perpetual.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ وَجَنَّتُ نَعِيمٍ

tafsir: (Therefore (O Muhammad) praise the name of thy Lord, the Tremendous) therefore pray by the command of your Lord, the Mighty; and it is also said that this means: remember the divine Oneness of your Lord, the Mighty, Who is more tremendous than all there is'.

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying's (All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Allah): 'He says: (All that is in the heavens) of creation (and the earth) of created beings (glorifieth Allah) pray to Allah; and it is said this means: makes remembrance of Allah, (and He is the Mighty) in retribution against those who disbelieve in Him, (the Wise) in His command and decree: He commanded that none should be worshipped save Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَبَّحَ للَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allāh, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God that is to say all things exalt Him as being transcendent thus the lām of li’Llāhi is extra; mā ‘all that’ is used instead of min ‘all who’ in order to indicate what is the predominant sc. non-rational beings; and He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His actions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَبَّحَ للَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allāh, and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (His is the Sovereignty) His are the stores (of the heavens) i.e. rain (and the earth) i.e. vegetation; (He quickeneth) for the resurrection (and He giveth death) in the life of the world; (and He is Able to do things) of giving life and death.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَهُ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يُحْيِـي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. It is He Who gives life and causes death, and He is Able to do all things..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; He gives life through His act of creation and He brings death thereafter and He has power over all things.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَهُ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يُحْيِـي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. It is He Who gives life and causes death, and He is Able to do all things..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He is the First) before the appearance of all things, (and the Last) after the disappearance of all things, (and the Outward) above all things (and the Inward) in all things; (and He is Knower of all things) that is to say, He is the First means: He is the Living, the preeternal; He was before all that which Allah gave life to; the Last means: He is the Living and Eternally subsistent and will remains after He takes life from all that which Allah has given life to; the Outward means: He is the Conqueror and there is none that can conquer Him; while the Inward means: He is the One Who has knowledge of the inward and outward without there being anyone to inform Him; and it is also said that this means: He is the One Who puts ahead any that is first and the One Who puts last any that is last, before He created any creation; and He will subsist after the annihilation of everything He created, and He is the Living, the Subsistent Who will never die or be annihilated, and He is Aware of all things from first to last, inward or outward.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هُوَ ٱلأَوَّلُ وَٱلآخِرُ وَٱلظَّاهِرُ وَٱلْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He is the First (nothing is before Him) and the Last (nothing is after Him), the Most High (nothing is above Him) and the Most Near (nothing is nearer than Him). And He is All-Knower of every thing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He is the First preceding everything but without His having any beginning and the Last succeeding everything but without His having any end and the Manifest through the proofs for Him and the Hidden from the perception of the senses and He has knowledge of all things.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هُوَ ٱلأَوَّلُ وَٱلآخِرُ وَٱلظَّاهِرُ وَٱلْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He is the First (nothing is before Him) and the Last (nothing is after Him), the Most High (nothing is above Him) and the Most Near (nothing is nearer than Him). And He is All-Knower of every thing..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days) of the days of the beginning of the life of the world whereby one day is 1,000 years of the days we know, the first day being Sunday and the last Friday; (then He mounted the Throne) He established Himself on the Throne and it is said He filled it. Before He created the heavens and the earth, Allah was established on the Throne without any modality (bila-kayf). (He knoweth all that entereth the earth) of rain, treasures and dead created beings, (and all that emergeth therefrom) from the earth of dead created beings, vegetation, water and treasures (and all that cometh down from the sky) of provision, rain, angels and misfortunes (and all that ascendeth therein) of angels, the angels who record people's actions and works; (and He is with you) and He is Aware of you (wheresoever ye may be) on land or at sea. (And Allah is Seer of what ye do) of good or evil.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days and then rose over (Istawā) the Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty). He knows what goes into the earth and what comes forth from it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends thereto. And He is with you (by His Knowledge) wheresoever you may be. And Allāh is All-Seer of what you do..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is He Who created the heavens and the earth in six days of the days of this world the first of which being Sunday and the last of which Friday then presided upon the Throne ‘arsh denotes the kursī a presiding that was befitting of Him. He knows what enters the earth of rain and dead creatures and what issues from it of vegetation and minerals and what comes down from the heaven in the way of mercy and chastisement and what ascends in it of righteous deeds and evil ones. And He is with you by virtue of His knowledge wherever you may be; and God is Seer of what you do.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days and then rose over (Istawā) the Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty).
