tafsir: Say ‘Have you considered If God destroys me and those with me of believers by His chastisement as you would have it or has mercy on us and does not chastise us who then will protect the disbelievers from a painful chastisement?’ in other words they will have no protector from it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَهْلَكَنِيَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِيَ أَوْ رَحِمَنَا فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Say (O Muḥammad ): “Tell me! If Allāh destroys me, and those with me, or He bestows His Mercy on us — who can save the disbelievers from a painful torment?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Say) to them, O Muhammad: (He is the Beneficent) Who will save us and show mercy towards us. (In Him we believe) truly (and in Him we put our trust) and we rely on Him. (And you will soon know) when the chastisement comes down (who it is that is in error manifest) who it is that is in manifest disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ هُوَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ آمَنَّا بِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Say: “He is the Most Gracious (Allāh), in Him we believe, and in Him we put our trust. So you will come to know who is it that is in manifest error.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘He is the Compassionate One; we believe in Him and in Him we put our trust. And assuredly you will soon know sa-ta‘lamūna is also read sa-ya‘lamūna ‘they will know’ upon seeing the chastisement with your own eyes who is in manifest error’ is it us or yourselves or them?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ هُوَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ آمَنَّا بِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. Say: “He is the Most Gracious (Allāh), in Him we believe, and in Him we put our trust. So you will come to know who is it that is in manifest error.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Say) to them, O Muhammad: (Have ye thought) O people of Mecca: (If (all) your water) i.e. Zamzam (were to disappear into the earth) out of your reach, (who then could bring you gushing water) within your reach? It is also said that this means: who could bring you gushing water save the Creator of the whale and the pen'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْراً فَمَن يَأْتِيكُمْ بِمَآءٍ مَّعِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Say (O Muḥammad ): “Tell me! If (all) your water were to sink away, who then can supply you with flowing (spring) water?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘Have you considered If your water were to sink deep into the earth who then will bring you running water?’ which hands and buckets would be able to reach like they do your water in other words none but God exalted be He would be able to bring it so how can you reject that He will resurrect you? It is commendable for one to say Allāhu rabbu’l-‘ālamīna ‘God Lord of the Worlds!’ after ma‘īn ‘running water’ as is stated in a hadīth. This verse was recited before a certain tyrant who then replied ‘Hatchets and pickaxes will bring it!’ whereupon the water of his eyes dried up and he became blind. We seek refuge with God against that we should be insolent towards Him or His verses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْراً فَمَن يَأْتِيكُمْ بِمَآءٍ مَّعِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Say (O Muḥammad ): “Tell me! If (all) your water were to sink away, who then can supply you with flowing (spring) water?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Nun): '(Nun) He says: Allah swears by the Nun, which is the whale that carries the earths on its back while in Water, and beneath which is the Bull and under the Bull is the Rock and under the Rock is the Dust and none knows what is under the Dust save Allah. The name of the whale is Liwash, and it is said its name is Lutiaya'; the name of the bull is Bahamut, and some say its name is Talhut or Liyona. The whale is in a sea called 'Adwad, and it is like a small bull in a huge sea. The sea is in a hollowed rock whereby there is 4,000 cracks, and from each crack water springs out to the earth. It is also said that Nun is one of the names of the Lord; it stands for the letter Nun in Allah's name al-Rahman (the Beneficent); and it is also said that a Nun is an inkwell. (By the pen) Allah swore by the pen. This pen is made of light and its height is equal to the distance between Heaven and earth. It is with this pen that the Wise Remembrance, i.e. the Guarded Tablet, was written. It is also said that the pen is one of the angels by whom Allah has sworn, (and that which they write (therewith)) and Allah also swore by what the angels write down of the works of the children of Adam,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نۤ وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Nūn. [These letters (Nūn, etc.) are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]. By the pen and by what they (the angels) write (in the Records of men)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nūn one of the letters of the alphabet God knows best what He means by it. By the Pen with which He has inscribed the records of all creatures in the Preserved Tablet and what they inscribe that is the angels of good and righteousness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نۤ وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Nūn. [These letters (Nūn, etc.) are one of the miracles of the Qur’ān, and none but Allāh (Alone) knows their meanings]. By the pen and by what they (the angels) write (in the Records of men)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thou art not) O Muhammad, (for your Lord's favour) for the prophethood and Islam bestowed (unto thee, a madman) bewitched. This is the reason why Allah made the above oath.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. You (O Muḥammad ), by the Grace of your Lord, are not mad..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: You are not O Muhammad (s) by the grace of your Lord a madman that is to say madness is precluded in your case on account of your Lord’s grace to you by way of His assigning to you prophethood and in other ways — this was a refutation of their saying that he was a madman.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. You (O Muḥammad ), by the Grace of your Lord, are not mad..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! thine) O Muhammad (verily will be a reward) in the Garden for the prophethood and Islam bestowed upon you (unfailing) undiminished, unspoilt and blameless.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لأَجْراً غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And Verily, for you (O Muḥammad ) will be an endless reward..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And assuredly you will have an unfailing reward.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لأَجْراً غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And Verily, for you (O Muḥammad ) will be an endless reward..

tafsir: (And lo! thou art) O Muhammad (of a tremendous nature) following a noble religion which is honoured by Allah; it is also said this means: you have great character traits with which Allah has honoured you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And Verily, you (O Muḥammad ) are on an exalted (standard of) character..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And assuredly you possess a magnificent nature a magnificent religion.

meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And Verily, you (O Muḥammad ) are on an exalted (standard of) character..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Which of you is the demented) which of you is mad.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بِأَييِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Which of you is afflicted with madness..

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بِأَييِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Which of you is afflicted with madness..

tafsir: (Lo! thy Lord) O Muhammad (is best aware of him who strayeth from His way) from His religion, i.e. Abu Jahl and his host, (and He is best aware of those who walk aright) and He is best aware of those who are guided to His religion, i.e. Abu Bakr and his fellow believers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Verily, your Lord is the Best Knower of him who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Knower of those who are guided..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly your Lord knows best those who stray from His way and He knows best those who are guided to Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Verily, your Lord is the Best Knower of him who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Knower of those who are guided..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Therefore obey not thou) O Muhammad (the rejecters) the disbelievers in Allah, His Scripture and His Messenger, i.e. the leaders of the people of Mecca

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. So (O Muḥammad ) obey you not the deniers [(of Islāmic Monotheism — those who deny the Verses of Allāh), the Oneness of Allāh, and the Messengership of Muḥammad ].
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So do not obey the deniers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. So (O Muḥammad ) obey you not the deniers [(of Islāmic Monotheism — those who deny the Verses of Allāh), the Oneness of Allāh, and the Messengership of Muḥammad ].
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who would have had you) who would wish you to (compromise, that they may compromise) i.e. who would wish that you lean towards them so that they would lean towards you; it is also said that this means: who would wish that you agree with them so that they agree with you and that you flatter them so that they would flatter you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَدُّواْ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. They wish that you should compromise (in religion out of courtesy) with them: so they (too) would compromise with you..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They desire they yearn that law relates to the verbal action you should be pliable that you should yield to them so that they may be pliable towards you so that they may yield to you fa-yudhinūna is a supplement to tudhinu ‘you should be pliable’ but if it is understood to be the response to the optative clause of waddū ‘they yearn’ then a free standing pronoun hum should be read as implied before it after the fā’ sc. fa-hum yudhinūna.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَدُّواْ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. They wish that you should compromise (in religion out of courtesy) with them: so they (too) would compromise with you..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Neither obey thou) O Muhammad (each feeble) with regard to the religion of Allah (oath monger) who lies against Allah. This refers to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلاَّفٍ مَّهِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And (O Muḥammad ) obey you not everyone who swears much and is a liar? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And do not obey any mean despicable oath-monger given to frequent swearing by falsehood

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلاَّفٍ مَّهِينٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And (O Muḥammad ) obey you not everyone who swears much and is a liar? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Detractor) who slanders and curses people right and left, (spreader abroad of slanders) who is a talebearer in order to cause mischief between people?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَمَّازٍ مَّشَّآءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. A slanderer, going about with calumnies,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: backbiting faultfinder that is to say calumniator scandal-monger spreading evil talk among people in order to sow dissension between them

meta_data.ayah_arabic: هَمَّازٍ مَّشَّآءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. A slanderer, going about with calumnies,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hinderer of the good) hinderer of Islam, for he prevented his sons and relatives from embracing Islam, (transgressor) he transgressed, O Muhammad, against the Truth and wronged them, (malefactor) sinful

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Hinderer of the good, trans gressor, sinful,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: hinderer of good niggardly with his wealth against deserving causes sinful transgressor wrongdoer

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Hinderer of the good, trans gressor, sinful,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Greedy therewithal) he eats and drinks much and has a strong body and a large belly; it is also said that this means: he is extreme in arguing in favour of falsehood and lies, (intrusive) he is stuck with the folk while he is not of them; it is also said that this means: he is well known for his disbelief, idolatry, indecency, sinfulness and evil; it is also said that this means: he is known for his meanness just as a young donkey is known to have a pendant on its ear.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Cruel, and moreover base-born (of illegitimate birth)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: coarse-grained crude moreover ignoble an adopted son of Quraysh — namely al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra whose father claimed him after eighteen years; Ibn ‘Abbās said ‘We know of no one whom God has described in the derogatory way in which He describes him blighting him with ignominy that will never leave him the adverbial qualifier ba‘da dhālika ‘moreover’ is semantically connected to zanīm ‘ignoble’ —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Cruel, and moreover base-born (of illegitimate birth)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (It is because he is possessed of wealth and children) He says: do not obey him even if he has wealth and children. This man had 9,000 measures of silver and ten children

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. (He was so) because he had wealth and children..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: only because an should be understood as li-an ‘because’ and it is semantically connected to that meaning which it is indicating he has wealth and sons.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. (He was so) because he had wealth and children..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That, when Our revelations) the Qur'an, detailing the commands and prohibitions (are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old) this is just the talk and lies of the men of old.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. When Our Verses (of the Qur’ān) are recited to him, he says: “Tales of the men of old!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When Our signs — the Qur’ān — are recited to him he says that they are merely ‘Fables of the ancients!’ in other words he denies them in arrogance on account of the mentioned things which We have bestowed on him out of Our grace a variant reading for an of the previous verse has the interrogative a-an.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. When Our Verses (of the Qur’ān) are recited to him, he says: “Tales of the men of old!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (We shall brand him on the nose) We shall hit him on the nose; and it is said this means: We shall hit him on the face; and it is also said this means: his face will be darkened.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. We shall brand him on the snout (nose)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We shall brand him on the snout We shall leave a distinguishing mark upon his nose one by which he will be reviled for as long as he lives; and so his nose was chopped off by a sword at Badr.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. We shall brand him on the snout (nose)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! we have tried them) We have tried the people of Mecca with death, captivity and defeat on the Day of Badr because they refrained from asking forgiveness and We tried them with hunger and drought for a period of seven years because the Prophet, Allah bless him and give peace, prayed against them on the Day of Badr (as We tried) with hunger and the burning of the gardens (the owners of the garden) the owners of the fields: the Banu Darwan (when they vowed) when they swore by Allah (they would pluck its fruit next morning) at the break of dawn.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُواْ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Verily, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden, when they swore to pluck the fruits of the (garden) in the morning,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed We have tried them We have tested the people of Mecca with drought and famine just as We tried the owners of the garden the orchard when they vowed that they would pluck that they would pick its fruits in the morning so that the poor folk would not notice them and so that they would not then have to give them of it that portion which their father used to give them of it by way of charity.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُواْ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Verily, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden, when they swore to pluck the fruits of the (garden) in the morning,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And made no exception (for the will of Allah)) they forgot to say: Allah willing;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يَسْتَثْنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Without saying: Inshā’ Allāh (If Allāh wills)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they did not make any exception to their vow for God’s will the sentence is a new syntactically independent one in other words and that was their condition.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يَسْتَثْنُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. Without saying: Inshā’ Allāh (If Allāh wills)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then a visitation) a punishment from your Lord (came upon it) upon the garden (while they slept) and was burned.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Then there passed by on it (the garden) a visitation (fire) from your Lord (at night and burnt it) while they were asleep..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then a visitation from your Lord visited it that is a fire consumed it during the night while they slept.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Then there passed by on it (the garden) a visitation (fire) from your Lord (at night and burnt it) while they were asleep..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in the morning it was as if plucked) it was like a dark night.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. So, the (garden) became black by the morning, like a pitch dark night (in complete ruins). (1) Tafsīr Aṭ-Ṭabarī..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So by the morning it was like the darkness of night in other words black.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. So, the (garden) became black by the morning, like a pitch dark night (in complete ruins). (1) Tafsīr Aṭ-Ṭabarī..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they cried out one unto another in the morning) at the break of dawn,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَنَادَوْاْ مُصْبِحِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Then they called out, one to another as soon as the morning broke..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They then called out to one another in the morning

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَتَنَادَوْاْ مُصْبِحِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Then they called out, one to another as soon as the morning broke..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit)) before the needy ones come to know about it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنِ ٱغْدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَارِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. Saying: “Go to your tilth in the morning, if you would pluck the fruits.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: saying ‘Go forth early to your tillage your produce ani’ghdū ‘alā harthikum constitutes an explication of the import of tanādaw ‘they called out to one another’; otherwise an relates to the verbal action to be understood as being bi-an if you are going to pluck’ if your intention is to pick the fruits the response to the conditional is indicated by what preceded it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَنِ ٱغْدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَارِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. Saying: “Go to your tilth in the morning, if you would pluck the fruits.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So they went off) towards the fields, (saying one unto another in low tones:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱنطَلَقُواْ وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. So, they departed, con versing in secret low tones (saying):.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So off they went whispering to one another talking secretly

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱنطَلَقُواْ وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. So, they departed, con versing in secret low tones (saying):.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: No needy man shall enter it) i.e. the garden (today against you.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن لاَّ يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّسْكِينٌ

tafsir: ‘No needy person shall today come to you in it’ this constitutes the explication of the preceding verse; or else an relates to the verbal action to be understood to mean bi-an.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن لاَّ يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّسْكِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. “No Miskīn (needy man) shall enter upon you into it today.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: They went betimes) they went to their fields holding rancour, (strong in (this) purpose) to pluck their fruits.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَغَدَوْاْ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. And they went in the morning with strong intention, thinking that they have power (to prevent the poor taking anything of the fruits therefrom)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they went forth early supposing themselves able to prohibit to prevent the poor folk from enjoying the fruit.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَغَدَوْاْ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. And they went in the morning with strong intention, thinking that they have power (to prevent the poor taking anything of the fruits therefrom)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But when they saw it) when they saw the fields burned down, (they said: Lo! we are in error!) we have taken a wrong turn; thinking that they were not their fields

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. But when they saw the (garden), they said: “Verily, we have gone astray.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But when they saw it blackened and charred they said ‘Assuredly we have strayed!’ from it that is to say this is not the one. Then when they recognised it they said

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. But when they saw the (garden), they said: “Verily, we have gone astray.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then they said: (Nay, but we are desolate!) We have been denied the benefit of the garden because of our ill intentions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. (Then they said): “Nay! Indeed we are deprived of (the fruits)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘Nay but we have been deprived!’ of its fruits by our denying it to the poor folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. (Then they said): “Nay! Indeed we are deprived of (the fruits)!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The best among them) in intellect and opinion; and it is also said this means: the older one of them; and it is also said: the most upright among them (said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)) why not say: Allah willing? He said this when they made their vow.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَّكُمْ لَوْلاَ تُسَبِّحُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. The best among them said: “Did I not tell you: why say you not: Inshā’ Allāh (If Allāh wills)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The most moderate the best one among them said ‘Did I not say to you “Why do you not glorify?” ’ God repenting to Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَّكُمْ لَوْلاَ تُسَبِّحُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. The best among them said: “Did I not tell you: why say you not: Inshā’ Allāh (If Allāh wills)?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said: Glorified be our Lord!) We ask forgiveness of our Lord. (Lo! we have been wrong-doers) we harmed ourselves by our transgression and intention to deprive the needy ones and also by failing to say “Allah willing”.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. They said: “Glory to Our Lord! Verily, we have been Ẓālimūn (wrong-doers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said ‘Glory be to God our Lord. Verily we have been wrongdoers’ by denying the poor folk what is their due.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. They said: “Glory to Our Lord! Verily, we have been Ẓālimūn (wrong-doers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching) reproaching one another.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَلاَوَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Then they turned one against another, blaming..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They then turned to one another blaming each other.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَلاَوَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Then they turned one against another, blaming..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (They said) in unison: (Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous) we were sinful by depriving the needy ones.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ يٰوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. They said: “Woe to us! Verily, we were Ṭāghūn (trans gressors and disobedient).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They said ‘O yā is for calling attention to something woe to us! O destruction of ours. We have indeed been unjust.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قَالُواْ يٰوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. They said: “Woe to us! Verily, we were Ṭāghūn (trans gressors and disobedient).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (It may be) and “may be” when used in connection with Allah denotes necessity (that our Lord will give us) in the Hereafter in exchange (better than this in place thereof) better than this garden. (Lo! we beseech our Lord) our desire is with Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْراً مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. We hope that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this. Truly, we turn to our Lord (wishing for good that He may forgive our sins and reward us in the Hereafter)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It may be that our Lord will give us in its place read yubaddilanā or yubdilanā one that is better than it. Truly we turn humbly to our Lord’ that He might accept our repentance and give us back a garden that is better than our garden — it is reported that they were indeed given a better one in its place.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْراً مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. We hope that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this. Truly, we turn to our Lord (wishing for good that He may forgive our sins and reward us in the Hereafter)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Such was the punishment) in the life of the world for the one who refrains from giving Allah's due from his wealth, just as Allah burnt their garden and exposed them to hunger; it is also said that this means: such is the punishment of the life of the world as happened to the people of Mecca who were exposed to hunger and death. (And verily the punishment of the Hereafter) for he who does not repent (is greater) than the punishment of the life of the world (if they did but know) if the people of Mecca did but knew, but they do not know nor do they believe in this.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَلِكَ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Such is the punishment (in this life), but truly the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they but knew..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Such that is to say like the chastisement for these people will be the chastisement for those disbelievers of Mecca and others who contravene Our command; and the chastisement of the Hereafter is assuredly greater did they but know its chastisement they would not have contavened Our command. When they said ‘If we are resurrected we shall be given better than what you have been given the following was revealed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَلِكَ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 33. Such is the punishment (in this life), but truly the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they but knew..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! for those who keep from evil) for those who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies (are Gardens of Bliss) whose bliss is continuous and eternal (with their Lord) in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Verily, for the Muttaqūn (the pious)(1) are Gardens of delight (Paradise) with their Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily for the God-fearing there will be the Gardens of Bliss near their Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 34. Verily, for the Muttaqūn (the pious)(1) are Gardens of delight (Paradise) with their Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: 'Utbah Ibn Rabi'ah said: “if what Muhammad (pbuh) says to his Companions about Paradise and its bliss is true, we will surely be better than them in the Hereafter as we are better than them in the life of this world”, and so Allah revealed: (Shall We then treat those who have surrendered) shall We then make the reward of the Muslims in Paradise (as We treat the guilty) as the reward of the idolaters who are the owners of the Fire?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَنَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ كَٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. Shall We then treat the Muslims (believers of Islamic Monotheism, doers of righteous deeds) like the Mujrimūn (crimi nals, polytheists and disbelievers, etc.)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Are We then to treat those who submit to Us as We treat the sinners? that is to say as belonging with them in terms of reward?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَنَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ كَٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 35. Shall We then treat the Muslims (believers of Islamic Monotheism, doers of righteous deeds) like the Mujrimūn (crimi nals, polytheists and disbelievers, etc.)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (What aileth you) O people of Mecca? (How foolishly ye judge!) Evil is what you judge for yourselves!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. What is the matter with you? How judge you?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: What is wrong with you? How do you judge? with such corrupt judgement?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 36. What is the matter with you? How judge you?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or have ye a Scripture wherein you learn) wherein you recite

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتَابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. Or have you a Book wherein you learn,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or am lakum means a-lakum do you have a Scripture revealed wherein you learn wherein you read

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتَابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 37. Or have you a Book wherein you learn,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That you shall indeed have) in this Scripture (all that ye choose) all you desire in Paradise in the Hereafter?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَمَا تَخَيَّرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. That you shall therein have all that you choose?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that you will indeed have in it whatever you choose?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَمَا تَخَيَّرُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 38. That you shall therein have all that you choose?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or have ye a covenant) pledges (on oath from Us) on firm oaths from Us (that reacheth to the Day of Judgement, that yours shall be all that ye ordain) that you shall have all that you judge for yourselves in Paradise in the Hereafter?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. Or have you oaths from Us, reaching to the Day of Resurrection, that yours will be what you judge?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or do you have oaths pledges binding secured on Us until the Day of Resurrection ilā yawmi’l-qiyāmati is semantically connected to ‘alaynā ‘on Us’; these words ‘alaynā bālighatun ‘binding on Us’ contain the sense of an oath given in other words ‘Did We swear to you?’ the response to which is what follows that you will indeed have whatever you decide? to have for yourselves.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 39. Or have you oaths from Us, reaching to the Day of Resurrection, that yours will be what you judge?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ask them) O Muhammad (which of them will vouch for that) that they say!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. Ask them, which of them will stand surety for that!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Ask them which of them will aver will guarantee for them that? that decision which they have made for themselves namely that they will be given better reward than the believers in the Hereafter?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 40. Ask them, which of them will stand surety for that!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or have they other gods? Then let them bring their other gods if they are truthful) that they will have that which they claim.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأتُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ إِن كَانُواْ صَادِقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. Or have they “partners”? Then let them bring their “partners”, if they are truthful!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or do they have partners? who agree with them in this claim of theirs and able to guarantee it for them; if that is the case Then let them produce their partners those who will guarantee this for them if they are truthful.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأتُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ إِن كَانُواْ صَادِقِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 41. Or have they “partners”? Then let them bring their “partners”, if they are truthful!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (On the day when it befalleth in earnest) a matter to which they were blind in the life of the world; it is also said this means: when a severe, horrific matter is revealed; and it is also said that this means: when a sign between them and their Lord is revealed, (and they are ordered to prostrate themselves) this is because they said: By Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters or hypocrites (but are not able) to prostrate, their bodies remaining erect like solid fortresses,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. (Remember) the Day when the Shin(2) shall be laid bare (i.e. the Day (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Mention the day when the shank is bared an expression denoting the severity of the predicament during the reckoning and the requital on the Day of Resurrection one says kashafati’l-harbu ‘an sāqin ‘the war has bared its shank’ to mean that it has intensified and they are summoned to prostrate themselves as a test of their faith but they will not be able to do so — their backs will become as stiff as a brick wall.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 42. (Remember) the Day when the Shin(2) shall be laid bare (i.e. the Day (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (With eyes downcast) not able to see any good, (abasement stupefying them) humiliation and darkness appear on their faces. (And they had been summoned) in the life of the world (to prostrate themselves) to submit themselves through the profession of Allah's divine Oneness but did not submit to Allah's divine Oneness (while they were yet unhurt) while they were strong and sound of bodies.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ وَقَدْ كَانُواْ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَٰلِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: Their eyes will be cast down and ignominy will cover them; they used to be called (for the congregational prayer in the mosque) to prostrate themselves (offer prayers), while they were healthy and good (in the life of the world, but they did not come to the mosque).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: With humbled khāshi‘atan is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the verb yud‘awna ‘they are summoned’ that is to say with abject gazes which they do not raise they will be overcast enveloped by abasement; for they had indeed been summoned in this world to prostrate themselves while they were yet sound but they never used to do it by the fact that they never performed prayer.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ وَقَدْ كَانُواْ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَٰلِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: Their eyes will be cast down and ignominy will cover them; they used to be called (for the congregational prayer in the mosque) to prostrate themselves (offer prayers), while they were healthy and good (in the life of the world, but they did not come to the mosque).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Leave Me) O Muhammad ((to deal) with those who give the lie to this pronouncement) to this Scripture. (We shall lead them on) i.e. those who mock the Qur'an (by steps from whence they know not) from whence they perceive not. And Allah did indeed destroy them-they were five people-in one night and one day.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَذَرْنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِّنْ حَيْثُ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. Then leave Me Alone with such as deny this Qur’ān. We shall punish them gradually from directions they perceive not..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So leave Me to deal with those who deny this discourse — the Qur’ān. We will draw them on by degrees We will seize them little by little whence they do not know.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَذَرْنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِّنْ حَيْثُ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 44. Then leave Me Alone with such as deny this Qur’ān. We shall punish them gradually from directions they perceive not..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Yet I bear with them) I give them a reprieve, (for lo! My scheme is firm) My punishment is severe.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And I will grant them a respite. Verily, My Plan is strong..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And I will grant them respite; for assuredly My devising is firm My devising is severe and cannot be withstood.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 45. And I will grant them a respite. Verily, My Plan is strong..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or dost thou (Muhammad) ask a fee) or provision in exchange for faith (from them) from the people of Mecca (so that they are heavily taxed) they are too much indebted by accepting your invitation to accept faith?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Or is it that you (O Muḥammad ) ask them a wage, so that they are heavily burdened with debt?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or are you asking them a fee in return for delivering the Message so that they are weighed down with debt? so that they are weighed down with what they will have to give you and that is why they do not believe.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 46. Or is it that you (O Muḥammad ) ask them a wage, so that they are heavily burdened with debt?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or is the Unseen) the Guarded Tablet (theirs that they can write (thereof)) that with which they argue against you?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. Or that the Ghaib (the Unseen — here in this Verse it means Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ) is in their hands, so that they can write it down?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Or do they possess access to the Unseen that is access to the Preserved Tablet which contains knowledge of the Unseen so that they are writing down? from it what they say.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 47. Or that the Ghaib (the Unseen — here in this Verse it means Al-Lauḥ Al-Maḥfūẓ) is in their hands, so that they can write it down?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But wait thou for your Lord's decree) be patient in conveying the message of your Lord; it is also said this means: be pleased with the decree of your Lord, (and be not) fed up and heart constricted with regard to Allah's command (like him of the fish) like Jonah the son of Mathew (Matta), (who cried out) to his Lord in the belly of the fish (in despair) tired and aggrieved.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلاَ تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. So, wait with patience for the Decision of your Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish — when he cried out (to Us) while he was in deep sorrow (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So await patiently the judgement of your Lord regarding them in the way that He wills and do not be like the one of the whale in terms of impatience and haste — this is Jonah peace be upon him — who called out who supplicated his Lord choking with grief filled with anguish inside the belly of the whale.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلاَ تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 48. So, wait with patience for the Decision of your Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish — when he cried out (to Us) while he was in deep sorrow (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Had it not been that favour) mercy (from his Lord had reached him he surely had been cast into the wilderness while he was reprobate) and guilty.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّوْلاَ أَن تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Had not a Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been (left in the stomach of the fish, but We forgave him): so he was cast off on the naked shore, while he was to be blamed..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Had it not been for a grace a mercy from his Lord that reached him he would have surely been cast out of the belly of the whale onto a wilderness a desolate land while he was blameworthy — but he was shown mercy and was therefore cast out blameless.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَّوْلاَ أَن تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 49. Had not a Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been (left in the stomach of the fish, but We forgave him): so he was cast off on the naked shore, while he was to be blamed..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But his Lord chose him) to make repentance (and placed him among the righteous) among the messengers.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. Then his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But his Lord chose him for prophethood and made him one of the righteous the prophets.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 50. Then his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! those who disbelieve) the disbelievers of Mecca (would fain disconcert thee) would kill you (with their eyes) and it is said this means: they would give you the evil eye (when they hear the Reminder) when they hear you recite the Qur'an, (and they) i.e. the people of Mecca (say: Lo! he is) i.e. Muhammad (indeed mad) bewitched;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And verily, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes (through hatred) when they hear the Reminder (the Qur’ān), and they say: “Verily, he (Muḥammad ) is a madman!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed those who disbelieve would almost throw you down to the ground read la-yuzliqūnaka or la-yazliqūnaka with their looks looking at you in a severe way almost hurling you to the ground or making you fall from your place when they hear the Reminder the Qur’ān and they say out of envy ‘He is truly a madman!’ on account of the Qur’ān that he has brought.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 51. And verily, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes (through hatred) when they hear the Reminder (the Qur’ān), and they say: “Verily, he (Muḥammad ) is a madman!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (When it is) i.e. the Qur'an (naught else than a Reminder to creation) to the jinn and humankind'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. But it is nothing else but a Reminder to all the ‘Ālamīn (mankind and jinn)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Yet it namely the Qur’ān is just a Reminder an admonition for all the worlds of both humans and jinn and cannot be the cause of any dementia.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 52. But it is nothing else but a Reminder to all the ‘Ālamīn (mankind and jinn)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (The Reality. What is the Reality): '(The Reality

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلْحَاقَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The Inevitable (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The Reality the Resurrection in which is realised the truth of all that was rejected in the way of the raising from the graves the reckoning and the requital or it means the Resurrection which will manifest all of that.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلْحَاقَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The Inevitable (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: What is the Reality) He says: the Hour. What is the Hour? He said this in amazement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. What is the Inevitable?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: What is the Reality? ma’l-hāqqa an interrogative to emphasise its enormity; this is the subject as well as the predicate of the previous al-hāqqa ‘the Reality’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. What is the Inevitable?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the reality is!) it is called the Reality because of the reality of things which will entitle the believer to enter the Garden due to his faith and the disbeliever to enter the Fire because of his disbelief.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْحَاقَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And what will make you know what the Inevitable is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And how would you know what the Reality is? repeated as an extra emphasis of its enormity; the first mā of the previous verse is the subject the second one its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function as the second direct object of the verb ‘knowing’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْحَاقَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And what will make you know what the Inevitable is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((The tribes of) Thamud) the people of Salih (and 'Aad) the people of Hud (disbelieved in the judgement to come) in the coming of the Hour.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Thamūd and ‘Ād people denied the Qāri‘ah (the striking Hour of Judgement)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thamūd and ‘Ād denied the Clatterer the Resurrection because its terrors cause the hearts to clatter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Thamūd and ‘Ād people denied the Qāri‘ah (the striking Hour of Judgement)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning) they were destroyed because of their transgression and idolatry; and it is said that their transgression drove them to disbelieve until they were destroyed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُواْ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the awful cry!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: As for Thamūd they were destroyed by the overwhelming Roar an excessively severe cry.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُواْ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the awful cry!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And as for 'Aad) the people of Hud, (they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind) cold wind that disobeyed and rebelled against its wardens,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُواْ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And as for ‘Ād, they were destroyed by a furious violent wind!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And as for ‘Ād they were destroyed by a deafening intensely clamorous violent wind that was powerful and severe in its assault upon ‘Ād despite their power and might.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُواْ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And as for ‘Ād, they were destroyed by a furious violent wind!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Which He imposed on them) uninterruptedly (for seven long nights and eight long days) with the same force (so that thou mightest have seen men) the people of Hud (lying) destroyed and (overthrown) in these days and nights; and it is said: in the wind, (as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Which Allāh imposed on them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so that you could see men lying overthrown (destroyed), as if they were hollow trunks of date-palms!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He forced it upon them for seven nights and eight days the first of which was the morning of Wednesday eight days before the end of the month of Shawwāl and this was at the height of winter successively one after the next husūman it the action of the wind is likened to the repeated actions of a hāsim ‘one cauterizing a wound’ time and again until it the blood has been cut off inhsama so that you might have seen the people therein lying prostrate lying dead on the ground as if they were the hollow collapsed trunks of palm-trees.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Which Allāh imposed on them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so that you could see men lying overthrown (destroyed), as if they were hollow trunks of date-palms!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them?) He says: every single one of them was destroyed by the wind.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّن بَاقِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Do you see any remnants of them?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So do you see any remnant of them? min bāqiyatin this is either the adjectival qualification of an implicit nafs ‘soul’ or the final suffixed tā’ is for hyperbole in other words understand it as fa-hal tarā lahum min bāqin ‘any one remaining?’ No!.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّن بَاقِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Do you see any remnants of them?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Pharaoh and those before him) and Pharaoh and his army came to the sea and were drowned in it; it is also said this means: Pharaoh also uttered the words of idolatry as did the nations before him, (and the communities that were destroyed) and also the townships of Lot swallowed by the earth, (brought error) they uttered the words of idolatry,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and those before him, and the cities overthrown [the towns of the people of Lūṭ (Lot)] committed sin..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And Pharaoh and those of his followers man qibalahu a variant reading has man qablahu that is to say those disbelieving communities who came before him and the Deviant cities that is their inhabitants — these being the cities of the people of Lot — brought iniquity they committed deeds that were iniquitous.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and those before him, and the cities overthrown [the towns of the people of Lūṭ (Lot)] committed sin..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord) Moses, (therefore did He grip them with a tightening grip) therefore He punished them with a severe punishment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَعَصَوْاْ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And they disobeyed their Lord’s Messenger, so He seized them with a strong punishment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord namely Lot and others so He seized them with a devastating blow one surpassing others in its severity.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَعَصَوْاْ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And they disobeyed their Lord’s Messenger, so He seized them with a strong punishment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! when the waters rose) at the time of Noah, (We carried you) O community of Muhammad (pbuh) as well as all created beings in the loins of your fathers (upon the ship) in the ship of Noah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Verily, when the water rose beyond its limits [Nūḥ’s (Noah) Flood], We carried you (mankind) in the floating [ship that was constructed by Nūḥ (Noah)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly when the waters rose high when they rose above all things including mountains and otherwise at the time of the Flood We carried you meaning your forefathers you being in their loins in the sailing vessel the ark which Noah built and by which he and those with him were saved while all the others drowned

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Verily, when the water rose beyond its limits [Nūḥ’s (Noah) Flood], We carried you (mankind) in the floating [ship that was constructed by Nūḥ (Noah)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That We might make it) i.e. the ship of Noah; and it is said: this story (a memorial for you) an admonition so that you might learn a lesson, (and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember) might benefit from it; and it is also said that this means: so that a retentive heart might remember it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. That We might make it (Noah’s ship) an admonition for you and that it might be retained by the retaining ears..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: so that We might make it namely this act the saving of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers a reminder a lesson for you and that receptive ears ears which remember what they hear might remember it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. That We might make it (Noah’s ship) an admonition for you and that it might be retained by the retaining ears..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And when the trumpet shall sound one blast) which will not be repeated; this is the blast of the Resurrection.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Then, when the Trumpet will be blown with one blowing (the first one)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thus when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast to announce the passing of judgement upon all creatures — this being the second blast —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And no friend will ask a friend (about his condition),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And no friend will inquire about his friend no relative will inquire about his relative each being preoccupied with his own predicament.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And no friend will ask a friend (about his condition),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Though they will be given sight of them) but will not recognise them as a result of their preoccupation with their own selves. (The guilty man) the idolater, i.e. Abu Jahl and his host; and it is said: al-Nadr Ibn al-Harith and his host (will long be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day) the Day of Judgement (at the price of his children

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Though they shall be made to see one another [(i.e. on the Day of Resurrection), there will be none but.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: They will however be made to see them that is friends will catch sight of one another recognising one another but refraining from speaking to one another the sentence yubassarūnahum is a new independent one. The guilty one will desire the disbeliever will yearn to ransom himself from the chastisement of that day read min ‘adhābi yawmi’dhin or min ‘adhābin yawma’idhin at the price of his children

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Though they shall be made to see one another [(i.e. on the Day of Resurrection), there will be none but.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And his spouse and his brother) his full brother

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And his wife and his brother,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and his companion his wife and his brother

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And his wife and his brother,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And his kin) and his clan and relatives (that harboured him) to whom he belongs

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَصِيلَتِهِ ٱلَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And his kindred who sheltered him,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and his kin his clan expressed as fasīla because he is a detached part fasl of it that had sheltered him embraced him

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفَصِيلَتِهِ ٱلَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And his kindred who sheltered him,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And all that are in the earth) and at the price of all that which is in the earth, (if then it might deliver him) if Allah might deliver him from the punishment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And all that are in the earth, so that it might save him (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and all who are on earth if it that ransom might then deliver him thumma yunjīhi is a supplement to yaftadī ‘to ransom himself’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. And all that are in the earth, so that it might save him (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But nay!) truly this will not deliver him from the punishment-this is an answer to him-(for lo! it is the fire of hell

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. By no means! Verily, it will be the Fire of Hell,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay! — a refutation of his wish. Lo! for him it namely the Fire will be the Churning Fire lazā — a name for Hell so called because it churns its flames tatalazzā against the disbelievers

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. By no means! Verily, it will be the Fire of Hell,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Eager to roast) the entire body; it is also said that this means: it will pluck out the hands and feet as well as all the other members of the body;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Taking away (burning completely) the head skin!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ripping out the scalp shawā is the plural of shawāt the skin of the head;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Taking away (burning completely) the head skin!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (It calleth) to itself: “come to me, O disbeliever!”, “come to me, O hypocrite” (him who turned) from Allah's divine Oneness (and fled) from faith and did not repent of disbelief,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَدْعُواْ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Calling(2) (all) such as turn their backs and turn away their faces (from Faith) [picking and swallowing them up from that great gathering of mankind on the Day of Resurrection just as a bird picks up a food-grain from the earth with its beak and swallows it up] (Tafsīr Al-Qurṭubī).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: it will call him who turned his back and ignored faith saying to him ‘To me! to me come hither!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَدْعُواْ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Calling(2) (all) such as turn their backs and turn away their faces (from Faith) [picking and swallowing them up from that great gathering of mankind on the Day of Resurrection just as a bird picks up a food-grain from the earth with its beak and swallows it up] (Tafsīr Al-Qurṭubī).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And hoarded (wealth)) in the life of the world (and withheld it) he put it in a container and refused to give the right of Allah which is due from it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. And collect (wealth) and hide it (from spending it in the Cause of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and amassed wealth then hoarded keeping it in containers and refraining from paying from it what is God’s due.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. And collect (wealth) and hide it (from spending it in the Cause of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Man) i.e. the disbelieving person (was created anxious) miserly, too attached and tight-fisted,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Verily, man was created very impatient;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Indeed man was created restless halū‘an is an implied circumstantial qualifier the explanation of which follows

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Verily, man was created very impatient;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Fretful) he is not patient (when evil befalleth him) when poverty and hardship befall him

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Irritable (discontented) when evil touches him;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: when evil befalls him he is anxious at the point of that evil befalling him

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Irritable (discontented) when evil touches him;.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And, when good) wealth and abundance (befalleth him, grudging) he does not give thanks and withholds the right of Allah which is due from it;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And niggardly when good touches him. (1) *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and when good befalls him he is grudging at the point of that good befalling him that is to say when wealth befalls him he is grudging to give of it what is due to God;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. And niggardly when good touches him. (1) *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save worshippers) those who pray the five daily prayers for they are not like this.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. Except those who are devoted to Ṣalāt (prayers)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except those who perform prayers that is the believers

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. Except those who are devoted to Ṣalāt (prayers)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then explained the traits of the latter, saying: (Who are constant at their worship) they constantly perform their prescribed daily prayers, whether it is at night or in the day, and they never fail to perform them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلاَتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Those who remain con stant in their Ṣalāt (prayers);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: those who maintain those who regularly observe their prayers

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلاَتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. Those who remain con stant in their Ṣalāt (prayers);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And in whose wealth there is a right acknowledged) they acknowledge that there is in their wealth a right other than the prescribed poor-due,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ فِيۤ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَّعْلُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. And those in whose wealth there is a recognised right.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and in whose wealth there is an acknowledged due namely alms

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ فِيۤ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَّعْلُومٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. And those in whose wealth there is a recognised right.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (For the beggar) who ask you to give him from your wealth (and the destitute) who is denied his wage or booty; it is also said that this refers to the artisan whose skill does not earn him enough for him to subsist; it is also said that this refers to the poor who does not beg from others and as a result no one gives or knows about him;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. For the beggar who asks, and for the unlucky who has lost his property and wealth, (and his means of living has been straitened)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: for the beggar and the deprived the latter being the one who refrains from begging and thus becomes deprived

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. For the beggar who asks, and for the unlucky who has lost his property and wealth, (and his means of living has been straitened)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who believe in the Day of Judgement) and those who believe in the Day of Reckoning and all that which is in it,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And those who believe in the Day of Recompense..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and who affirm the truth of the Day of Judgement of Requital

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And those who believe in the Day of Recompense..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who are fearful of their Lord's doom

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And those who fear the torment of their Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and who are apprehensive of the chastisement of their Lord —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. And those who fear the torment of their Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure) no guarantee of security has come to them from their Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Verily, the torment of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure. —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: lo! there is no security from the chastisement of their Lord from its being sent down —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. Verily, the torment of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure. —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who preserve their chastity) they are chaste as far as what is unlawful is concerned

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. And those who guard their chastity (i.e. private parts from illegal sexual acts) (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and those who guard their private parts

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. And those who guard their chastity (i.e. private parts from illegal sexual acts) (2)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save with their) four (wives and those whom their right hands possess) of slaves without limitation, (for thus they are not blameworthy) nor sinful; they are not reproached for indulging in that which is lawful;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Except from their wives or the (women slaves) whom their right hands possess — for (then) they are not blameworthy. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except from their wives and those whom their right hands own in the way of slavegirls for in that case they are not blameworthy;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. Except from their wives or the (women slaves) whom their right hands possess — for (then) they are not blameworthy. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But whoso seeketh more than that) whoever seeks more than what I have mentioned of wives and slaves, (those are they who are transgressors) from that which is lawful to that which is unlawful;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَلِكَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. But whosoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are trespassers (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: but whoever seeks beyond that those are the infringers who transgress the bounds of what is lawful stepping into what is unlawful;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَلِكَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 31. But whosoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are trespassers (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And those who keep) and those who honour, and keep to the time agreed upon regarding (their pledges) that with which they have been entrusted whether it relates to religion or other things (and their covenant) with their Lord or with other people; and it is also said this means: and their oaths.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 32. And those who keep their trusts and covenants..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās
