meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُواْ ٱلصَّخْرَ بِٱلْوَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And (with) Thamūd (people), who hewed out rocks in the valley (to make dwellings)?(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Thamūd who hollowed hewed the rocks sakhr is the plural of sakhra in the valley the Wādī al-Qurā rocks which they used as dwellings

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُواْ ٱلصَّخْرَ بِٱلْوَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And (with) Thamūd (people), who hewed out rocks in the valley (to make dwellings)?(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And with Pharaoh) and how He destroyed Pharaoh, (firm of right) Pharaoh erected four pillars to which he tied and tortured anyone with whom he was angry until the latter died, as he did with his wife Asiyah Bint Muzahim,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِى ٱلأَوْتَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And (with) Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) who had the stakes (to torture men by binding them to the stakes)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Pharaoh the one of the tent-pegs he used to fasten four pegs and tie to these the hands and feet of those whom he tortured —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِى ٱلأَوْتَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And (with) Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) who had the stakes (to torture men by binding them to the stakes)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who (all) were rebellious (to Allah) in these lands) they rebelled and declared their disbelief in the land of Egypt; it is also said that their transgression led them to this,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ طَغَوْاْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Who did transgress beyond bounds in the lands (in the disobedience of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: those who were rebellious became tyrannical in the land

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ طَغَوْاْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Who did transgress beyond bounds in the lands (in the disobedience of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And multiplied iniquity) and multiplied killing innocent people and spread their idol worship (therein) in the land of Egypt?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَكْثَرُواْ فِيهَا ٱلْفَسَادَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And made therein much mischief..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and caused much corruption therein? by way of slaying and otherwise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَكْثَرُواْ فِيهَا ٱلْفَسَادَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And made therein much mischief..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Therefore thy Lord poured on them the disaster of His punishment) your Lord sent on them a severe punishment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. So your Lord poured on them different kinds of severe torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So your Lord poured on them a scourge of chastisement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. So your Lord poured on them different kinds of severe torment..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! thy Lord) O Muhammad (is ever watchful) He says: they, as well as all created beings, will have to go through Him; it is also said that this means: the angels of your Lord will be on the Bridge over hell stopping people at seven different stopping positions at which they will ask them about seven traits.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Verily, your Lord is Ever Watchful (over them)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly your Lord is ever on the watch watching over the deeds of servants nothing of which escapes Him that He may then requite them for these deeds.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Verily, your Lord is Ever Watchful (over them)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (As for man) the disbelieving man, in reference here to Ubayy Ibn Khalaf; and it is also said: Umayyah Ibn Khalaf, (whenever his Lord trieth him) whenever his Lord tests him with wealth, richness or means of living (by honouring him) by giving him abundant wealth, (and is gracious unto him) and expands for him his means of living, (he saith: My Lord honoureth me) by giving me wealth and means of living.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلإِنسَانُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلاَهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيۤ أَكْرَمَنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. As for man, when his Lord tries him by giving him honour and bounties, then he says (in exultation): “My Lord has honoured me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And as for man the disbeliever whenever his Lord tests him and honours him with wealth and other things and is gracious to him he says ‘My Lord has honoured me’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلإِنسَانُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلاَهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيۤ أَكْرَمَنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. As for man, when his Lord tries him by giving him honour and bounties, then he says (in exultation): “My Lord has honoured me.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But whenever He trieth him) whenever He tests him with poverty (by straitening his means of life) by tightening his means of living, (he saith: My Lord despiseth me) by giving me poverty and tightening my means of living.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلاَهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيۤ أَهَانَنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. But, when He tries him by straitening his means of life, he says: “My Lord has humiliated me!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But when he tests him and restricts his provision for him he says ‘My Lord has humiliated me’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلاَهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيۤ أَهَانَنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. But, when He tries him by straitening his means of life, he says: “My Lord has humiliated me!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay) this is a reply to them: No, but the honour I bestow is due to My acknowledgment of some My servants and the success I give to them, while My despising is because I turn away from some servants and completely forsake them, (but ye (for your part) honour not the orphan) you do not acknowledge the right of the orphan when he is under your care.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ بَل لاَّ تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Nay! But you treat not the orphans with kindness and generosity (i.e. you neither treat them well, nor give them their exact right of inheritance)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: No indeed! — a disavowal of this notion in other words honour is not about wealth nor is there any humiliation in poverty rather it has to do with obedience and disobedience respectively; but the disbelievers of Mecca unmindful of this. Rather they do not honour the orphan they do not treat him with kindness despite their wealth or it means that they do not give him what is his due from an inheritance

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ بَل لاَّ تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Nay! But you treat not the orphans with kindness and generosity (i.e. you neither treat them well, nor give them their exact right of inheritance)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And urge not) yourselves or others (on the feeding of the poor) giving alms to the poor,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ تَحَآضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. And urge not one another on the feeding of Al-Miskīn (the needy)! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and they do not urge neither themselves nor others the feeding of the needy;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ تَحَآضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. And urge not one another on the feeding of Al-Miskīn (the needy)! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And ye devour heritages) inheritances (with devouring greed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَأْكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكْلاً لَّمّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And you devour the inheritance all with greed..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and they devour inheritance turāth means mīrāth greedily lamman that is to say voraciously when they appropriate lammuhum the women’s and the young ones’ share of the inheritance together with their own share of it or to their own wealth;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَأْكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكْلاً لَّمّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And you devour the inheritance all with greed..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And love wealth with abounding love.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبّاً جَمّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And you love wealth with much love..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and they love wealth with abounding love that is to say greatly and so they do not expend any of it a variant reading in the case of all four verbs has the second person plural.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبّاً جَمّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. And you love wealth with much love..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Nay) this is also a reply to them, (but when the earth is ground to atoms, grinding, grinding) He says: when the earth is quaked again and again,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ دَكّاً دَكّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Nay! When the earth is ground to powder..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: No indeed! — a deterrent for them from such conduct. When the earth is pulverised repeatedly when it is shaken until every edifice has collapsed and is destroyed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ دَكّاً دَكّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. Nay! When the earth is ground to powder..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And thy Lord shall come) a coming without any modality (with angels, rank on rank) like the ranks of the people of the life of the world when praying,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلْمَلَكُ صَفّاً صَفّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And your Lord comes with the angels in rows..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and your Lord that is to say His command and the angels arrive rank on rank saffan saffan is a circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘standing in rows’ or ‘made up of many ranks’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلْمَلَكُ صَفّاً صَفّاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 22. And your Lord comes with the angels in rows..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And hell is brought near) with 70,000 registers, with each register 70,000 angels leading it to the place of mustering, and then they reveal them (that day) the Day of Judgement; (on that day man) the disbelieving man; i.e. Ubayy Ibn Khalaf and Umayyah Ibn Khalaf (will remember) will be admonished, (but how will the remembrance (then avail him)) when the time for being admonished has passed?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجِيۤءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلإِنسَانُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance (then) avail him?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and Hell on that day is brought near pulled by seventy thousand sets of reins each set of reins pulled by the hands of seventy thousand angels as it groans and seethes in fury; on that day yawma’idhin is a substitution for idhā ‘when’ the response to which is the following man that is to say the disbeliever will remember his prodigal conduct in it but how will remembering avail him now? the interrogative is meant as a denial in other words his remembering that will not be of any use to him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَجِيۤءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلإِنسَانُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 23. And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance (then) avail him?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He will say: Ah, would that) wishing: if only (I had sent before me (some provision) for my life!) if only I have worked in my previous perishing life to this everlasting life.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَقُولُ يٰلَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. He will say: “Alas! Would that I had sent forth (good deeds) for (this) my life!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He will say as he remembers ‘O yā is for calling attention to something would that I had sent ahead good deeds and faith for my life!’ for a good life in the Hereafter or it means ‘during my life’ in the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَقُولُ يٰلَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي
meta_data.ayah_translation: 24. He will say: “Alas! Would that I had sent forth (good deeds) for (this) my life!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (None punisheth as He will punish on that day) on the Day of Judgement!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. So, on that Day none will punish as He will punish..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then on that day none shall mete out read yu‘adhdhibu His God’s chastisement that is to say He shall not delegate it to any other;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 25. So, on that Day none will punish as He will punish..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (None bindeth as He then will bind) this can also be understood to mean: none punishes like this and none will inflict that kind of punishment except Allah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And none will bind (the wicked, disbelievers and poly theists) as He will bind..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and likewise none shall bind read yūthiqu His bind a variant reading has yu‘adhdhabu ‘none shall be chastised’ and yūthaqu ‘none shall be bound’ so that the suffixed pronoun of ‘adhābahu and wathāqahu refers to the chastisement and the binds of the disbeliever the meaning then being ‘none shall be chastised as he shall and none shall be bound as he shall be bound’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 26. And none will bind (the wicked, disbelievers and poly theists) as He will bind..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But ah! thou soul at peace) which is safe from Allah's chastisement, true in its profession of Allah's divine Oneness, grateful for the blessings Allah bestowed upon it, patient with the trials of Allah, pleased with things decreed by Allah, and content with that which Allah gives!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يٰأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. (It will be said to the pious — believers of Islamic Monotheism): “O (you) the one in (complete) rest and satisfaction!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: ‘O soul at peace! the one secure namely the believing one.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يٰأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 27. (It will be said to the pious — believers of Islamic Monotheism): “O (you) the one in (complete) rest and satisfaction!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Return unto thy Lord) return to that which Allah has prepared for you in the Garden; and it is also said this means: return to your master: the body, (content) with Allah's reward (in His good pleasure) because of its belief in Allah's divine Oneness!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱرْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. “Come back to your Lord — well-pleased (yourself) and well-pleasing (to Him)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Return — this is said to it upon death — to your Lord that is to say return to His command and to His will pleased with the reward pleasing in God’s sight with your deeds; in other words return O soul combining both descriptions both of which are circumstantial qualifiers. And it will be said to it at the Resurrection

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱرْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 28. “Come back to your Lord — well-pleased (yourself) and well-pleasing (to Him)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Enter thou among My bondmen) enter you among My friends!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱدْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. “Enter you then among My (honoured) slaves,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then enter among My righteous servants!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱدْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي
meta_data.ayah_translation: 29. “Enter you then among My (honoured) slaves,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Enter thou My Garden) which I have prepared for you!'

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱدْخُلِي جَنَّتِي
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. “And enter you My Paradise!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And enter My Paradise!’ with them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱدْخُلِي جَنَّتِي
meta_data.ayah_translation: 30. “And enter you My Paradise!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Nay, I swear by this city): '(Nay, I swear by this city) He says: I swear by the city of Mecca

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَ أُقْسِمُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. I swear by this city (Makkah);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: I swear lā is extra by this land of Mecca

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لاَ أُقْسِمُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. I swear by this city (Makkah);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And thou art an indweller of this city) and it is also said that this means: Allah has made lawful for you in this city that which he did not make lawful to anyone before or after you; and it is also said that this means: you are excused regarding that which you do in this city.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And you are free (from sin, and to punish the enemies of Islām on the Day of the conquest) in this city (Makkah) (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and you O Muhammad (s) have free disposal of sanction for this land in that you will be given permission to fight in it — and indeed God fulfilled this promise to him on the day of the Conquest of Mecca thus this is a parenthetical statement intervening between that by which the oath has been sworn and that which is a supplement thereto.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And you are free (from sin, and to punish the enemies of Islām on the Day of the conquest) in this city (Makkah) (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the begetter and that which he begat) the begetter is Adam and that which his sons begat; and it is also said this means: the begetter refers to the person who can have children, whether this person is a man or a woman, while that which he begat refers to the men or women who cannot have children; Allah swore by all these,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And by the begetter (i.e. Adam S) and that which he begot (i.e. his progeny)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And by the begetter that is Adam and that which he begat that is his descendants mā ‘that which’ actually means man ‘whom’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And by the begetter (i.e. Adam S) and that which he begot (i.e. his progeny)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (We verily have created man) i.e. Kildah Ibn Usayd (in an atmosphere) in an erect form; it is also said that this means: in strife with the matter of the life of this world and of the Hereafter; and it is also said this means: with strength and force:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Verily, We have created man in toil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We certainly created man al-insān the generic noun in travail in a state of toil and hardship struggling with the tribulations of this world and the calamities of the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Verily, We have created man in toil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thinketh he) does the disbelieving man think (that) because of his strength and force (none hath power over him?) i.e. Allah cannot seize and punish him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Does he think that none can overcome him?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Does he suppose does the strong man of Quraysh namely Abū’l-Ashadd b. Kalada presume on account of his strength that an softened in place of the hardened form its subject omitted that is to say annahu no one will have power over him? Yet God has power over him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Does he think that none can overcome him?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he) Kildah Ibn Usayd; and it is also said: al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah (saith: I have destroyed vast wealth) I have spent abundant wealth in enmity towards Muhammad, Allah bless him, and this did not benefit me:

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. He says (boastfully): “I have wasted wealth in abundance!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He says ‘I have exhausted in enmity of Muhammad (s) vast wealth!’ great wealth piles and piles of it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. He says (boastfully): “I have wasted wealth in abundance!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thinketh he) does the disbelieving man deem (that none beholdeth him) that Allah does not see his deeds whether he spends money or not?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Does he think that none sees him?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Does he suppose that an in other words annahu no one has seen him? with regard to what he has expended to know the quantity thereof; God knows the quantity thereof; but it is not in reality that much so as to be considered a great amount and in any case He will requite him for his evil conduct.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Does he think that none sees him?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon him, saying: (Did We not assign unto him two eyes) with which he sees

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Have We not made for him two eyes,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have We not given an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words ‘We have certainly given’ him two eyes

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Have We not made for him two eyes,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And a tongue) with which he speaks (and two lips) which he can join together or separate,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلِسَاناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And a tongue and two lips? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and a tongue and two lips

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلِسَاناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And a tongue and two lips? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And guide him to the parting of the mountain ways?) And We showed him the way of goodness and the way of evil; and it is also that this means: the way to the two breasts.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And shown him the two ways (good and evil)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and guided him to the two paths? did We not point out to him the path of good and that of evil?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And shown him the two ways (good and evil)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But he hath not attempted the Ascent) He says: but did he go beyond that hurdle which is the Bridge over hell?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. But, he has not attempted to pass on the path that is steep (i.e. the path which will lead to goodness and success)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Yet why does he not assault the obstacle? why does he not surmount it?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. But, he has not attempted to pass on the path that is steep (i.e. the path which will lead to goodness and success)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Ascent is!) it is a smooth hurdle between Paradise and hell. Allah said this to arouse the Prophet's astonishment.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْعَقَبَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And what will make you know the path that is steep?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you what the obstacle is? that he is to surmount — intended to emphasise its enormity this statement is a parenthetical one. He explains the way to surmount it by saying

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْعَقَبَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. And what will make you know the path that is steep?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: ((It is) to free a slave) He says: its crossing requires the freeing of a slave; and it is also said this means: none will cross it save he who has freed a slave,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. (It is) freeing a neck (slave)(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. (It is) freeing a neck (slave)(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And to feed in the day of hunger) and hardship

meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Or giving food on a day of hunger (famine),.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (An orphan near of kin,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَتِيماً ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. To an orphan near of kin..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: to an orphan near of kin maqraba means qarāba

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَتِيماً ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. To an orphan near of kin..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Or some poor wretch in misery) and who has nothing,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Or to a Miskīn (a needy person) cleaving to dust (out of misery)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: or a needy person in misery matraba literally means ‘clinging to the dust turāb’ because of his poverty; a variant reading has two verbal nouns in place of the two verbs fakka ‘he freed’ and at‘ama ‘he fed’ the first being in a genitive construction fakku raqabatin ‘the freeing of a slave’ and the second with nunation it‘āmun ‘to give food’ in which case there is an implied iqtihāmu before al-‘aqaba of which the said reading becomes the explication;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Or to a Miskīn (a needy person) cleaving to dust (out of misery)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And to be) in addition to this (of those who believe) in private between themselves and their Lord, in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and exhort one another to perseverance) in fulfilling the obligations (and export one another to pity) towards the poor and needy.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْمَرْحَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Then he became one of those who believed (in the Islamic Monotheism) and recommended one another to perseverance and patience, and (also) recom mended one another to pity and compassion..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: while being thumma kāna is a supplement to iqtahama ‘he assaulted’; thumma is for the ordering of things to be mentioned in other words what is meant is that at the point of the assault he was one of those who believe and enjoin one another to steadfastness in pursuing obedience and in refraining from disobedience and enjoin one another to compassion marhama means rahma towards creatures.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْمَرْحَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Then he became one of those who believed (in the Islamic Monotheism) and recommended one another to perseverance and patience, and (also) recom mended one another to pity and compassion..

meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. They are those on the Right Hand (i.e. the dwellers of Paradise),.

tafsir: (But those who disbelieve Our revelations) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, i.e. Kildah and his host, (their place will be on the left hand) those who are given their register in their left hand are the inhabitants of the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا هُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. But those who disbelieved in Our Āyāt (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), they are those on the Left Hand (the dwellers of Hell). (1).

meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. But those who disbelieved in Our Āyāt (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), they are those on the Left Hand (the dwellers of Hell). (1).

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And he is indeed a failure) he is in loss (who stunteth it) who leads to sin, error and forsakenness.

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Thamūd denied their messenger Sālih because of their rebellious nature

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَآ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Thamūd (people) denied (their Prophet) through their transgression ..

tafsir: (When the basest of them broke forth) when the most wretched of the folk, Qudar Ibn Salif and Masda', hamstrung the she-camel.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذِ ٱنبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. When the most wicked man among them went forth (to kill the she-camel)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: when the most wretched of them whose name was Qudār was dispatched when he hastened in order to hamstring the she-camel with their approval.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذِ ٱنبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. When the most wicked man among them went forth (to kill the she-camel)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the messenger of Allah) Salih (said) that is before they hamstrung the she-camel: (It is the she-camel of Allah) leave the she-camel of Allah alone, (so let her drink!) i.e. and let her drink in peace!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. But the Messenger of Allāh (Ṣāliḥ S) said to them: [“Be cautious! (Fear the evil end)]. That is the she-camel of Allāh! (Do not harm it) and (bar it not from having) its drink!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But then the messenger of God Sālih said to them ‘This is the she-camel of God so let her have her drink!’ her drink on her day — one day was hers the next theirs.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. But the Messenger of Allāh (Ṣāliḥ S) said to them: [“Be cautious! (Fear the evil end)]. That is the she-camel of Allāh! (Do not harm it) and (bar it not from having) its drink!”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But they denied him) they denied the message brought by Salih, (and they hamstrung her) they hamstrung the she-camel, (so Allah doomed them for their sin) so Allah destroyed them because of killing the she-camel and disbelieving in Salih (and razed (their dwellings)) killing the old and the young among them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Then, they denied him and they killed it. So their Lord destroyed them because of their sin, and made them equal in destruction (i.e. all grades of people, rich and poor, strong and weak, etc.)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But they denied him with regard to his saying this as being a command from God — which if they contravened would immediately result in chastisement being sent down on them — then hamstrung her they slew it in order to appropriate her share of the drinking water. So their Lord closed in on them the chastisement because of their sin and meted it equally among them that is the closing in on them in other words He subsumed them all by it so that not one of them escaped.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Then, they denied him and they killed it. So their Lord destroyed them because of their sin, and made them equal in destruction (i.e. all grades of people, rich and poor, strong and weak, etc.)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He dreadeth not the sequel (of events)) and it is also said this means: and He dreads not the one who instigated it'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلاَ يَخَافُ عُقْبَاهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. And He (Allāh) feared not the consequences thereof..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And He does not read wa-lā or fa-lā fear the consequence of it.

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying: (By the night enshrouding): '(By the night enshrouding) He says: Allah swears by the night when it enshrouds the light of day.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the night as it envelops..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By the night as it enshrouds with its darkness all that is between the heaven and the earth

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the night as it envelops..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And the day resplendent) and the day when it clears the darkness of night.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By the day as it appears in brightness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and by the day as it unveils as it is revealed and becomes manifest idhā ‘as’ in both instances is an absolute adverbial operated by the verbal action of the oath

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By the day as it appears in brightness..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Him Who hath created) and by Him Who has created the (male and female,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. By Him Who created male and female..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and by the One Who mā either functions as man ‘the One Who’ or it is related to a verbal action created the male and the female Adam and Eve or every male and female — the hermaphrodite although problematic for us is in fact either male or female according to God and therefore a person actually commits perjury if he speaks with one thinking that because he has sworn not to speak with a male or a female; he may do so with a hermaphrodite.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. By Him Who created male and female..

tafsir: Lo! your effort) your work (is dispersed (towards diverse ends)) there are those who oppose and disbelieve in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an and there are those who believe in Muhammad (pbuh); there are those who strive for Paradise and there are those who strive for hell. This is why Allah made the oath.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Certainly, your efforts and deeds are diverse (different in aims and purposes);.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Assuredly your efforts your deeds are dissimilar with some working towards Paradise by means of obedience while others in effect are working towards the Fire through acts of disobedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Certainly, your efforts and deeds are diverse (different in aims and purposes);.

tafsir: (As for him who giveth) to charity from his wealth for the sake of Allah and bought nine believers who were in the hands of the disbelievers who tortured them to renounce their religion; this person bought them and then freed them (and is dutiful (towards Allah)) and wards off disbelief, idolatry and indecencies

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allāh and fears Him,.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allāh and fears Him,.

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and affirms the truth of the best word that is the truth of ‘there is no god but God’ in both places here and below verse 9

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. And believes in Al-Ḥusnā(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Surely We will ease his way unto the state of ease) We shall make easy for him acts of obedience and give him success, time and again, to perform acts of obedience; and it is also said this means: We shall give him success, time and again, to give alms for the sake of Allah; this refers to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. We will make smooth for him the path of ease (goodness)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We shall surely ease his way to the abode of ease to Paradise.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. We will make smooth for him the path of ease (goodness)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But as for him who hoardeth) his wealth and is too stingy to give for the sake of Allah, in reference here to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah and it is said: Abu Sufyan Ibn Harb who was not a believer at that time (and deemeth himself independent) of Allah,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. But he who is a greedy miser and thinks himself self-sufficient (2). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: But as for him who is niggardly with what is due to God and deems himself self-sufficient without need for His reward 929 and denies the best word

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. But he who is a greedy miser and thinks himself self-sufficient (2). (1).

meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. And denies Al-Ḥusnā (See the footnote of Verse No. 6)..

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. We will make smooth for him the path for evil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We shall surely ease his way We shall pave for him the way to hardship to the Fire;

meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. We will make smooth for him the path for evil..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (His riches) which he amasses in the life of the world (will not save him when he perisheth) when he dies; and it is also said this means: when he is cast in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And what will his wealth avail him when he goes down (in destruction)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And his wealth shall not mā is or negation avail him when he perishes in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And what will his wealth avail him when he goes down (in destruction)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Ours it is (to give) the guidance) it is for Us to show what is good and what is evil

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Truly! On Us is (to give) guidance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly with Us lies all guidance the pointing out of the path of guidance from that of error so that Our command may be followed by adhering to the former manner of conduct and that Our prohibition may also be heeded by refraining from falling into the latter manner of conduct.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Truly! On Us is (to give) guidance..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! unto Us belong the latter portion and the former) and to Us belong the reward of the life of the world and that of the Hereafter; it is also said that this means: to Us belong the life of the world in which We bestow knowledge and success and also the Hereafter in which We bestow reward and honour.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And truly, to Us (belong) the last (Hereafter) and the first (this world)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And truly to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life that is to say that of this world and so whoever seeks either of the two from anyone other than Us has erred.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. And truly, to Us (belong) the last (Hereafter) and the first (this world)..

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَاراً تَلَظَّىٰ

meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. None shall enter it except the most wretched..

meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. None shall enter it except the most wretched..

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. Who denies and turns away..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. And Al-Muttaqūn (the pious)(1) will be far removed from it (Hell)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَتْقَى
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. And Al-Muttaqūn (the pious)(1) will be far removed from it (Hell)..

tafsir: Who giveth his wealth) in the way of Allah, i.e. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (that he may grow (in goodness)) intending by that Allah's Countenance alone,

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: he who gives his wealth to purify himself offering it as a means of self purification before God exalted be He by making this payment for the sake of God exalted be He and not for show or the sake of reputation so that he or the offering stands purified in the sight of God. This verse was revealed regarding the truthful one al-siddīq Abū Bakr may God be pleased with him when he purchased Bilāl the Ethiopian who was being tortured on account of his faith and then freed him whereat the disbelievers said ‘He only did this in return for a favour which he must have owed him’ and so the following was revealed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. He who spends his wealth for increase in self-purification,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And none hath with him any favour for reward,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا لأَحَدٍ عِندَهُ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And who has (in mind) no favour from anyone to be paid back,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and no one has any favour outstanding with him that must be requited;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا لأَحَدٍ عِندَهُ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. And who has (in mind) no favour from anyone to be paid back,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Except as seeking (to fulfil) the purpose of his Lord Most High) except seeking the good pleasure of his Lord the Most High, Who is higher than everything.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Except to seek the Countenance of his Lord, the Most High..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: but he did this only seeking the pleasure of his Lord the Most High that is to say only seeking to secure God’s reward;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 20. Except to seek the Countenance of his Lord, the Most High..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He verily will be content) he will be given of reward and honour until he is pleased, i.e. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his fellow believers'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. He surely will be pleased (when he will enter Paradise). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and verily soon he shall himself be pleased with the reward he will be given in Paradise. The verse applies equally to anyone who may do as he Abū Bakr did may God be pleased with him and such a person will thereby be removed far from the Fire and rewarded.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 21. He surely will be pleased (when he will enter Paradise). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the morning hours): '(By the morning hours) He says: Allah swears by the whole day

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلضُّحَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the forenoon (after sunrise)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By the forenoon that is to say the first part of the day or all of it

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلضُّحَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the forenoon (after sunrise)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And by the night when it is stillest) and by the night when it becomes dark,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By the night when it darkens (and stands still)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and by the night when it is still — or sajā can mean ‘when it envelops all in its darkness’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By the night when it darkens (and stands still)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee) your Lord has not left you since He inspired you (nor doth He hate thee) since He loved you; this is the reason for Allah's oath, this was revealed after the revelations from Allah stopped for 15 nights because the Prophet (pbuh) forgot to say " if Allah wills " when he promised the idolaters to answer their questions. And because the revelations stopped for this period of time the idolaters said: the Lord of Prophet has forsaken him and He hates him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Your Lord (O Muḥammad ) has neither forsaken you nor hates you..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Your Lord has neither forsaken you He has not abandoned you O Muhammad (s) nor does He hate you this was revealed when after the revelation had not come to him for fifteen days the disbelievers said ‘His Lord has parted with him and hates him’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Your Lord (O Muḥammad ) has neither forsaken you nor hates you..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former) He says: the reward of the Hereafter is better for you than the reward of the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَلآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And indeed the Hereafter is better for you than the present (life of this world)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily the Hereafter shall be better for you by virtue of the honours awaiting you thereat than the first life this world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَلآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلأُولَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And indeed the Hereafter is better for you than the present (life of this world)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And verily thy Lord will give unto thee) in the Hereafter of intercession (so that thou wilt be content) until you are content.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And verily, your Lord will give you (all good) so that you shall be well-pleased..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily your Lord shall give you in the Hereafter of good things a bounteous gift and you shall be satisfied with it — and so the Prophet s said ‘In that case I shall not be satisfied if a single person from among my community remains in the Fire’ the response to the oath terminates here with two affirmations and two negations.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And verily, your Lord will give you (all good) so that you shall be well-pleased..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then mentioned His blessings upon the Prophet (pbuh) saying (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (an orphan) without a father or mother (and protect (thee)) and joined you to your uncle Abu Talib and sufficed you your provision? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Did He not find you (O Muḥammad ) an orphan and gave you refuge? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Did He not find you an orphan an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words He did indeed find you an orphan having lost your father before you were born or shortly thereafter and shelter you? by having your uncle Abū Tālib embrace you as part of his household.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Did He not find you (O Muḥammad ) an orphan and gave you refuge? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Gabriel then said: (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (wandering) among people in error (and direct (thee)) and guided you by means of prophethood? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلاًّ فَهَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And He found you unaware (of the Qur’ān, its laws and Prophethood) and guided you..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And did He not find you erring from the revealed Law which you now follow and guided you? that is and then guided you to it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلاًّ فَهَدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And He found you unaware (of the Qur’ān, its laws and Prophethood) and guided you..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And he also said: (Did He not find thee) O Muhammad (destitute) poor (and enrich (thee)) with the wealth of Khadijah; and it is also said this means: and made you content with that which He gave you? The Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, O Gabriel! "

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلاً فَأَغْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And He found you poor and made you rich (self-sufficient with self-contentment)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And did He not find you needy poor and enrich you? and made you content with the spoils and other things which He gave you — in a hadīth it is stated ‘Wealth comes not from the proliferation of transient worldly goods but wealth comes from the contentedness of the soul’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلاً فَأَغْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And He found you poor and made you rich (self-sufficient with self-contentment)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: So he also said: (Therefore the orphan oppress not) do not transgress on him nor deride him,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Therefore, treat not the orphan with oppression..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So as for the orphan do not oppress him by appropriating his wealth or otherwise

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Therefore, treat not the orphan with oppression..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Therefore the beggar drive not away) nor rebuke,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And repulse not the beggar..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and as for the beggar do not drive him away do not repel him on account of his poverty

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And repulse not the beggar..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Therefore of the bounty of thy Lord) through prophethood and Islam (be thy discourse) speak to people and let them know about it'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And proclaim the Grace of your Lord (i.e. the Prophethood and all other Graces)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and as for your Lord’s grace to you by way of prophethood and otherwise proclaim it make it known. The omission in certain instances of the suffixed pronoun referring to the Prophet s from the end of the verbs is intended to sustain the end-rhyme of the verses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. And proclaim the Grace of your Lord (i.e. the Prophethood and all other Graces)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said concerning the interpretation of Allah's saying (Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate): '(Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate) this is in conjunction with His saying (Did He not find thee destitute and enrich (thee)?), and so Allah says: did We not open your heart for Islam? i.e. did We not soften your heart on the Day of the Covenant through knowledge, understanding, help, reason and certainty, as well as with other things? It is also said this means: did We not expand your heart through prophethood? And the Prophet (pbuh) said: “Yes, indeed!”

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Have We not opened your breast for you (O Muḥammad )?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Did We not expand an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words ‘We did indeed expand’ your breast for you O Muhammad (s) by means of prophethood and otherwise

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Have We not opened your breast for you (O Muḥammad )?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: He said again: (And eased thee of the burden) We lifted your sins from you

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And removed from you your burden..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and relieve you of your burden

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And removed from you your burden..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Which weighed down thy back?) It is also said: prophethood weighed down your back; And the Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, indeed! "

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Which weighed down your back?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: that which weighed down your back? — this is similar to where God says that God may forgive you what is past of your sin Q. 482.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Which weighed down your back?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And exalted thy fame) and raised your voice with the call to prayer, supplication and testification of faith, such that you are mentioned just as I am? And the Prophet (pbuh) said: " Yes, indeed! "

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And have We not raised high your fame?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Did We not exalt your mention? For you are mentioned where I God am mentioned in the call announcing the time for prayer adhān in the second call to perform the prayer iqāma in the witnessing ‘there is no god but God Muhammad is His Messenger’ tashahhud in the Friday sermon and in other instances.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And have We not raised high your fame?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then said to comfort His prophet about his poverty and the hardships he faced, saying: (But lo! with hardship goeth ease,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Verily, along with every hardship is relief,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: For truly with hardship comes ease.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Verily, along with every hardship is relief,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Lo! with hardship goeth ease;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, along with every hardship is relief (i.e. there is one hardship with two reliefs, so one hardship cannot overcome two reliefs)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly with hardship comes ease the Prophet s suffered much hardship at the hands of the disbelievers but then he enjoyed ease when he was assisted to victory by God over them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْراً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, along with every hardship is relief (i.e. there is one hardship with two reliefs, so one hardship cannot overcome two reliefs)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: So when thou art relieved) when you finish from military expeditions, jihad and fighting, (still toil) in worship; and it is also said this means: when you finish from the prescribed prayers, make supplications

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. So, when you have finished (your occupation), devote yourself to Allāh’s worship..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So when you are finished from performing prayer toil exert yourself in supplication to God

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. So, when you have finished (your occupation), devote yourself to Allāh’s worship..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And strive to please thy Lord) and ask your needs from your Lord'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَبْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And to your Lord (Alone) turn (all your) intentions and hopes..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and seek devote yourself humbly to your Lord.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَبْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And to your Lord (Alone) turn (all your) intentions and hopes..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the fig and the olive): '(By the fig and the olive) He says: Allah swears by the fig, this fig of yours, and the olive, this olive of yours; it is also said the fig and the olive refer to two mountains in Historic Syria; it is also said that the fig refers to the hill upon which Jerusalem is built while the olive refers to the mountain upon which Damascus is built,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the fig, and the olive..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By the fig and the olive that is the two edible foods — or these denote the names of two mountains in Syria on which these two foods grow —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the fig, and the olive..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (By Mount Sinai) and He swears by the mountain of Thubayr which is the mountain of Midian where Allah spoke to Moses (pbuh),

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَطُورِ سِينِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By Mount Sinai..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and by the Mount Sinai the mountain on which God exalted be He spoke to Moses sīnīn means ‘the one blessed’ or ‘the fair one with fruitful trees’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَطُورِ سِينِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. By Mount Sinai..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And by this land made safe) and He swears by Mecca which is made safe in that whoever enters it is safe;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ ٱلأَمِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. By this city of security (Makkah)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and by this secure land Mecca as people were secure in it in the time of pagandom and are still secure in it in Islam.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ ٱلأَمِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. By this city of security (Makkah)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Surely We created man) the disbelieving man, referring here to al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah, and it is also said it refers to Kildah Ibn Usayd (of the best stature) in the best of forms; and this is the reason why the oath was made.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِيۤ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Verily, We created man in the best stature (mould)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily We created man al-insān the generic in the best of forms in the best proportioning of his shape.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِيۤ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Verily, We created man in the best stature (mould)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then We reduced him) in the Hereafter (to the lowest of the low) i.e. the Fire; it is also said that the above means: We have created the children of Adam in the best of forms when they are in the pick of their youth, then We reduce them to abject old age whereby no good deed is recorded in their favour except that which they used to do in their youth and prime,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Then, We reduced him to the lowest of the low..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then in the case of certain individuals of his species We reduced him to the lowest of the low — a metaphor for old age and weakness at which point a believer’s deeds are fewer than when he was young; but he will still have his reward as God exalted be He says

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Then, We reduced him to the lowest of the low..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and do good works) and do acts of obedience in private between themselves and their Lord, (and theirs is a reward unfailing) their reward is undiminished and unspoilt, good deeds will still be written for them even in old age and after they die.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Except those who believe (in Islāmic Monotheism) and do right eous deeds. Then they shall have a reward without end (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds for they shall have an unfailing reward one unending — in a hadīth it is stated ‘When a believer reaches that stage of old age which prevents him from performing good deeds then what he used to do is recorded in his favour instead’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Except those who believe (in Islāmic Monotheism) and do right eous deeds. Then they shall have a reward without end (Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (So who henceforth) i.e. after what I have mentioned to you of the transformation of youth and old age, life and death (will give the lie to thee) O Muhammad (about the judgement) about the Day of Reckoning? It is also said this means: what has driven you, O Kildah Ibn Usayd and Walid Ibn al-Mughirah, to deny the Day of Judgement?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Then what (or who) causes you (O disbelievers) to deny the Recompense (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So what makes you deny O disbeliever thereafter — after the mention of man being created in the best of forms and his being reduced to the vilest of age all of which indicates the power of God to resurrect — the Judgement? the Requital that will be preceded by the Resurrection and the Reckoning. In other words what makes you disbelieve in all this? Nothing does!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِٱلدِّينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Then what (or who) causes you (O disbelievers) to deny the Recompense (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Is not Allah the most conclusive of all judges?) Is not Allah the most just of those who are just and the best of those who are best and is, therefore, able to bring you back to life, O Walid!'

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ ٱلْحَاكِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. 8.Is not Allāh the Best of judges? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Is not God the fairest of all judges? the most just of all judges. His passing judgement by means of the process of requital is one such example. In a hadīth it is stated ‘Whoever recites sūrat wa’l-tīni ‘By the fig’ to the end of it let him then say “Yes Indeed! And I am of those who bear witness to this!” ’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ ٱلْحَاكِمِينَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. 8.Is not Allāh the Best of judges? (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Read): '(Read) He says: Read, O Muhammad, the Qur'an; this is the first revelation that Gabriel brought down: (In the name of thy Lord) by the command of your Lord (Who createth) the created beings,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Read! In the Name of your Lord Who has created (all that exists)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Recite bring recitation into existence beginning with In the Name of your Lord Who created all creatures;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Read! In the Name of your Lord Who has created (all that exists)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Createth man) i.e. the son of Adam (from a clot) and the Prophet (pbuh) said: “what shall I read?” And Gabriel read to him the first four verses of this surah.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. He has created man from a clot (a piece of thick coagulated blood)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: created man al-insān the generic from a blood-clot ‘alaq is the plural of ‘alaqa which is a small quantity of congealing blood.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. He has created man from a clot (a piece of thick coagulated blood)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: He said to him: (Read) the Qur'an, O Muhammad: (And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous) and your Lord is Clement and forgives the ignorance of the servants,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلأَكْرَمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Recite reiterating the first one and your Lord is the Most Generous having no counterpart in terms of His generosity wa-rabbuka’l-akram is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb iqra’ ‘recite’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلأَكْرَمُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who teacheth by the pen) Who teaches writing by the pen,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Who has taught (the writing) by the pen..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Who taught the art of script by the pen — the first to write with it was the prophet Enoch Idrīs peace be upon him —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Who has taught (the writing) by the pen..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Teacheth man) writing with the pen (that which be knew not) before this; it is also said: He taught man the names of all things which he previously did not know.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. He has taught man that which he knew not..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: taught man al-insān the generic what he did not know before he was taught in the way of guidance the art of writing crafts and so on.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. He has taught man that which he knew not..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but verily) O Muhammad (man) i.e. the disbeliever (is rebellious) is a wanton, he moves from one position to another with regard to his food, drink, clothing and mount

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Nay! Verily, man does transgress (in disbelief and evil deed)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay but verily man is wont to be rebellious

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Nay! Verily, man does transgress (in disbelief and evil deed)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That he thinketh himself independent) of Allah because of his wealth!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Because he considers himself self-sufficient..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: when he sees it that is to say his own soul to be self-sufficient in terms of wealth — this was revealed regarding Abū Jahl ra’ā ‘sees’ means to see mentally; istaghnā ‘self-sufficient’ is the second direct object; an ra’āhu ‘when he sees it’ is an object denoting reason.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Because he considers himself self-sufficient..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! unto thy Lord) O Muhammad (is the return) of all created beings in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Surely, to your Lord is the return..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Surely to your Lord O man is the return — meant as a threat for him — and so He will requite the rebellious one with what he deserves.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Surely, to your Lord is the return..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then it was revealed about Abu Jahl Ibn Hisham when he wanted to step on the neck of the Prophet (pbuh) while he was in prayer: (Hast thou seen him) O Muhammad (who dissuadeth

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Have you (O Muḥammad ) seen him (i.e. Abū Jahl) who prevents..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have you seen a-ra’ayta in all three instances here and below is an exclamation of wonder him namely Abū Jahl who forbids

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Have you (O Muḥammad ) seen him (i.e. Abū Jahl) who prevents..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: A slave) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) (when he prayeth) to Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. A slave (Muḥammad ) when he prays?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: a servant namely Muhammad (s) when he prays?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. A slave (Muḥammad ) when he prays?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hast thou seen if he (relieth) on the guidance (of Allah)) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) is following the guidance: prophethood and Islam

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَىٰ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Have you seen if he (Muḥammad ) is on the guidance (of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have you considered what if he the one forbidden should be upon a path of guidance

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَىٰ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Have you seen if he (Muḥammad ) is on the guidance (of Allāh)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Or enjoineth piety) and enjoins belief in Allah's divine Oneness?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Or enjoins piety?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: or aw is for division be bidding others to fear of God?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 12. Or enjoins piety?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Hast thou seen if he denieth (Allah's guidance)) and Abu Jahl disbelieved in Allah's divine Oneness (and is froward) and turned away from faith?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Have you seen if he (Abū Jahl) denies (the truth, i.e. this Qur’ān) and turns away?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have you considered what if he the one forbidding the Prophet should be denying God’s guidance and turning away? from faith.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 13. Have you seen if he (Abū Jahl) denies (the truth, i.e. this Qur’ān) and turns away?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Is he) Abu Jahl (then unaware that Allah seeth) what he did to the Prophet (pbuh)?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Knows he not that Allāh sees (what he does)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Is he not aware that God sees? what has issued from him that is to say He does indeed know it and will requite him for it. In other words ‘Marvel O you being addressed at the way in which he forbids prayer and at the fact that the one being forbidden is actually the one upon guidance bidding to fear of God while the one forbidding is a denier disregarding faith’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 14. Knows he not that Allāh sees (what he does)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn
