tafsir: (Nay) truly, O Muhammad, (but if he cease not) if Abu Jahl does not repent of harming the Prophet (pbuh). (We will seize him by the forelock

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Nay! If he (Abū Jahl) ceases not, We will catch him by the forelock —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Assuredly if la-in the lām is for oaths he does not desist from the disbelief that he is upon We shall seize him by the forelock We shall drag him to the Fire by his forelock

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 15. Nay! If he (Abū Jahl) ceases not, We will catch him by the forelock —.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: The lying) about Allah, (sinful forelock) that ascribes partners to Allah

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. A lying, sinful forelock!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: a lying iniquitous forelock! nāsiyatin an indefinite noun substituting for a definite — the description of this forelock in such terms is meant figuratively and what is actually meant is that individual.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 16. A lying, sinful forelock!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then let him call upon his henchmen) his folk and companions!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Then let him call upon his council (of helpers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Let him then call upon the henchmen of his council the members of his council nādin — a place of assembly where people gather to talk. He Abū Jahl had said to the Prophet s in reproof having forbidden him from prayer ‘You are well aware that there is none in this town who has recourse to as large a council of men as I do. Verily I shall fill this entire valley with mature steeds and young men in battle against you if you so wish!’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 17. Then let him call upon his council (of helpers)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (We will call the guards of hell) i.e. the keepers of hell.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. We will call out the guards of Hell (to deal with him)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: We shall call the Zabāniya the grim stern angels to destroy him as stated in the hadīth ‘Had he called his council of henchmen together the Zabāniya would have seized him right before his own eyes!’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 18. We will call out the guards of Hell (to deal with him)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay) truly, O Muhammad! (Obey not thou him) i.e. obey not Abu Jahl when he wants you not to pray to your Lord. (But prostrate thyself) to your Lord, (and draw near (unto Allah)) through prostration.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لاَ تُطِعْهُ وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Nay! (O Muḥammad )! Do not obey him (Abū Jahl). Fall prostrate and draw near (to Allāh)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Do not obey him O Muhammad (s) and abandon prayer and prostrate yourself perform prayer to God and draw near to Him through obedience to Him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لاَ تُطِعْهُ وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب
meta_data.ayah_translation: 19. Nay! (O Muḥammad )! Do not obey him (Abū Jahl). Fall prostrate and draw near (to Allāh)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Lo! We revealed it): '(Lo! We revealed it) He says: We sent Gabriel with the entire Qur'an to the scribes of the nether heaven (on the Night of Power) on the night of judgement and decree; it is also said this means: on a night blessed with forgiveness and mercy, and then it was revealed to the Prophet (pbuh) in instalments.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Verily, We have sent it (this Qur’ān) down in the night of Al-Qadr (Decree)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lo! We revealed it that is the Qur’ān in its entirety sending it down from the Preserved Tablet to the heaven of this world on the Night of Ordainment that is the Night of great eminence.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Verily, We have sent it (this Qur’ān) down in the night of Al-Qadr (Decree)(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad-this is said out of glorification of this night-(what the Night of Power is) what the merit of the Night of Power is!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And what will make you know what the night of Al-Qadr (Decree) is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you O Muhammad (s) what the Night of Ordainment is? — intended to emphasise its great status and to provoke marvel at it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And what will make you know what the night of Al-Qadr (Decree) is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: He then explained its merit by saying: (The Night of Power is better than a thousand months) He says: works in this night are better than works performed in 1,000 months which do not include such a night.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. The night of Al-Qadr (Decree) is better than a thousand months ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The Night of Ordainment is better than a thousand months in which there is no Night of Ordainment for a righteous deed on that Night is better than one performed for a thousand months without it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. The night of Al-Qadr (Decree) is better than a thousand months ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The angels and the Spirit) Gabriel with them (descend therein) at the beginning of the Night of Power, (by the permission of their Lord) by the command of their Lord, (with all decrees.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Therein descend the angels and the Rūḥ [Jibrā’īl (Gabriel)] by Allāh’s Permission with all Decrees,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The angels and the Spirit namely Gabriel descend tanazzalu one of the two original tā’ letters of tatanazzalu has been omitted in it on that night by the leave of their Lord by His command with every command that God has decreed from that year to the following one min is causative functioning as bi ‘with’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Therein descend the angels and the Rūḥ [Jibrā’īl (Gabriel)] by Allāh’s Permission with all Decrees,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That night is) Peace) He says: they greet the greeting of peace those who fast and those who pray, on that day, from among the nation of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) (until the rising of the dawn) He says: its merit and grace lasts until the rise of dawn'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَلاَمٌ هِيَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. (All that night), there is Peace (and Goodness from Allāh to His believing slaves) until the appearance of dawn (2). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is peaceful salāmun hiya a predicate preceding the subject until the rising of the dawn read matla‘ or matli‘ until the time it rises it is peaceful because of the numerous salutations of peace salām spoken in it by the angels who every time they come across a believing man or believing woman bid him peace.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَلاَمٌ هِيَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. (All that night), there is Peace (and Goodness from Allāh to His believing slaves) until the appearance of dawn (2). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture): '(Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture) i.e. the Jews and Christians (and the idolaters) the Arab idolaters (could not have left off (erring)) could not have remained in their denial of Muhammad (pbuh) the Qur'an and Islam (till the clear proof came unto them) until clarification of what is in their Scriptures, the Scriptures of the Jews and Christians, came to them. There is another way of understanding the above: those who disbelieve among the people of the Scripture, before the advent Muhammad (pbuh) such as 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers, and those who ascribed partners to Allah before the advent of Muhammad (pbuh) such as Abu Bakr and his fellow Arabs, would not have desisted from their disbelief and idolatry until the clear proof came to them, i.e. until Muhammad (pbuh) came to them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikūn, (1) were not going to leave (their disbelief) until there came to them the clear evidence..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The disbelievers from among min explicative the People of the Scripture and the idolaters that is the idol-worshippers wa’l-mushrikīna is a supplement to ahl ‘the People of’ were not going to leave off munfakkīna is the predicate of yakun ‘were’ that is to say they were not going to abandon their ways until the clear proof namely Muhammad (s) should come to them that is until it came to them;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Those who disbelieve from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikūn, (1) were not going to leave (their disbelief) until there came to them the clear evidence..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (A messenger from Allah) i.e. Muhammad (pbuh) (reading) to them (purified pages) pages purified from idolatry

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتْلُواْ صُحُفاً مُّطَهَّرَةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. A Messenger (Muḥammad ) from Allāh, reciting (the Qur’ān) purified pages [purified from Al-Bāṭil (falsehood)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: a messenger from God rasūlun mina’Llāhi substitutes for al-bayyinatu ‘the clear proof’ namely the Prophet s reciting pages purified of all falsehood

meta_data.ayah_arabic: رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتْلُواْ صُحُفاً مُّطَهَّرَةً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. A Messenger (Muḥammad ) from Allāh, reciting (the Qur’ān) purified pages [purified from Al-Bāṭil (falsehood)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Containing) i.e. the page of Muhammad (pbuh) contains (correct scriptures) a religion and a straight and just way that contains no crookedness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Wherein are correct and straight laws from Allāh..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: wherein are upright precepts written rulings that are upright that is to say one who recites what contains all that and that is the Qur’ān. Thus some of them believed in it while others disbelieved.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Wherein are correct and straight laws from Allāh..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nor were the People of the Scripture divided) those who were given the Torah, i.e. Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf and his host, did not differ about Muhammad (pbuh) the Qur'an and Islam (until after the clear proof came unto them) until the clarification of what is in their Scripture regarding the traits and description of Muhammad (pbuh) came to them.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) differed not until after there came to them the clear evidence (i.e. Prophet Muḥammad  and whatever was revealed to him)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided regarding belief in him the Prophet s except after the clear proof had come to them namely the Prophet s — or the Qur’ān which he brought as his miracle. Before his s arrival they had all agreed to believe in him when he would come; then those who disbelieved in him from among them became envious of him.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) differed not until after there came to them the clear evidence (i.e. Prophet Muḥammad  and whatever was revealed to him)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And they are ordered) in all the Scriptures (naught else than to serve Allah) nothing else but to profess Allah's divine Oneness, (keeping religion pure for Him) through the profession of Allah's divine Oneness, (as men by nature upright) as ones surrendered unto Him, (and to establish worship) and perform the five daily prayers after declaring their profession in Allah's divine Oneness (and to pay the poor-due) from their wealth after that. Allah then mentioned belief in Allah's divine Oneness, saying: (That) i.e. belief in Allah's divine Oneness (is true religion) the religion of truth, straight without any crookedness; it is also said that this means: that, i.e. belief in Allah's divine Oneness, is the religion of the angels; and it is also said this means: it is the religion of those who are by nature upright; and it is also said this means: the religion of Abraham.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أُمِرُوۤاْ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَيُؤْتُواْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ ٱلقَيِّمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And they were commanded not, but that they should worship Allāh, and worship none but Him Alone (abstaining from ascribing partners to Him), and perform Aṣ-Ṣalāt (Iqāmat-aṣ-Ṣalāt) and give Zakāt, and that is the right religion. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And they were only commanded in their Scripture the Torah and the Gospel to worship God illā li-ya‘budū means illā an ya‘budū an having been omitted and the lām added devoting religion purely to Him free of any idolatry as hanīfs upright in following the religion of Abraham and the religion of Muhammad (s) when he would come — so how is it that they disbelieved in him? and to establish prayer and pay the alms. That is the upright religion the upright creed.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أُمِرُوۤاْ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَيُؤْتُواْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ ٱلقَيِّمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And they were commanded not, but that they should worship Allāh, and worship none but Him Alone (abstaining from ascribing partners to Him), and perform Aṣ-Ṣalāt (Iqāmat-aṣ-Ṣalāt) and give Zakāt, and that is the right religion. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! those who disbelieve) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, (among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters) i.e. the idolaters among the people of Mecca, (will abide in fire of hell) never to die therein or leave it. (They are the worst of created beings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, those who disbelieve (in the religion of Islām, the Qur’ān and Prophet Muḥammad ) from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikūn will abide forever in the Fire of Hell. They are the worst of creatures (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly the disbelievers from among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters shall be in the fire of Hell to abide therein khālidīna an implied circumstantial qualifier in other words it will be decreed for them by God exalted be He to abide therein — those are the worst of creatures.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, those who disbelieve (in the religion of Islām, the Qur’ān and Prophet Muḥammad ) from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikūn will abide forever in the Fire of Hell. They are the worst of creatures (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And) lo! those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an, such as 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his companions (and do good works) acts of obedience privately between themselves and their Lord (are the best of created beings.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Verily, those who believe [in the Oneness of Allāh, and in His Messenger Muḥammad ) including all obligations ordered by Islām] and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Truly those who believe and perform righteous deeds — they are the best of creatures al-bariyya means al-khalīqa.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Verily, those who believe [in the Oneness of Allāh, and in His Messenger Muḥammad ) including all obligations ordered by Islām] and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Their reward is with their Lord: Gardens of Eden) the chamber of the Beneficent, the source of the prophets and those near to Him (beneath which) beneath whose trees, habitations and rooms (rivers flow) rivers of wine, water, honey and milk, (wherein they dwell forever) they remain in Paradise for ever never to die or leave it. (Allah hath pleasure in them) i.e. in their faith and works (and they have pleasure in Him) in His reward and bestowal of honour upon Him. (This) i.e. the Gardens and good pleasure (is (in store) for him who feareth his Lord) is for him who believes in Allah's divine Oneness such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his companions and 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِنْ تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَداً رِّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُواْ عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Their reward with their Lord is ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (Gardens of Eternity), underneath which rivers flow. They will abide therein forever, Allāh will be pleased with them, and they with Him. That is for him who fears his Lord. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eden as a residence underneath which rivers flow wherein they shall abide forever. God is pleased with them because of their obedience of Him and they are pleased with Him because of His reward. That is the reward for him who fears his Lord for him who fears His punishment and hence desists from disobeying Him exalted be He.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِنْ تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَداً رِّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُواْ عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Their reward with their Lord is ‘Adn (Eden) Paradise (Gardens of Eternity), underneath which rivers flow. They will abide therein forever, Allāh will be pleased with them, and they with Him. That is for him who fears his Lord. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (When Earth is shaken with her (final) earthquake): '(When Earth is shaken with her (final) earthquake) He says: the earth is shaken and quaking and all that which is on it of trees, mountains and building is crumbling down

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: When earth is shaken when it is rocked for the rising of the Hour with its final quake with its most violent rocking one that befits its magnitude

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And Earth yieldeth up her burdens) and the Earth brings out her dead and treasures,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And when the earth throws out its burdens..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the earth brings forth its burdens its hidden treasures and its dead casting them onto its surface

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And when the earth throws out its burdens..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And man) i.e. the disbeliever (saith: What aileth her?) He says this in astonishment from the horror he sees

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَا لَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And man will say: “What is the matter with it?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and man the disbeliever in resurrection says ‘What is wrong with it?’ — in denial of that situation.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَا لَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And man will say: “What is the matter with it?”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That day) when the earth is shaken (she will relate her chronicles) the earth will inform about the good and evil that were done on its surface,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. That Day it will declare its information (about all that happened over it of good or evil)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: On that day yawma’idhin substitutes for and is the response to idhā ‘when’ it shall relate its chronicles it shall inform of the good and evil deeds committed in it

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. That Day it will declare its information (about all that happened over it of good or evil)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Because thy Lord inspires her) because your Lord gives her leave to talk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Because your Lord will inspire it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: for its Lord will have inspired it that is He will have commanded her to do this — in a hadīth it is stated ‘It the earth shall testify to every single deed committed by every servant and handmaiden upon its surface’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Because your Lord will inspire it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (That day) when the earth speaks (mankind will issue forth in scattered groups) a group will go to Paradise, these are the believers, and a group will go to hell, and these are the disbelievers (to be shown their deeds) what they have done of good or evil when they were in the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتاً لِّيُرَوْاْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. That Day mankind will proceed in scattered groups that they may be shown their deeds (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: On that day mankind shall issue forth they will depart from the site of the Reckoning in separate groups divided up so that those taking it their book by the right hand will go to Paradise while those taking it by the left hand will go to the Fire to be shown their deeds that is the requital for them in either Paradise or the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتاً لِّيُرَوْاْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. That Day mankind will proceed in scattered groups that they may be shown their deeds (1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then revealed the following verse about a group of people who thought that they are not rewarded for any small goodness they do nor punished for any small evil they commit, and so Allah urged them to do acts of goodness even if they are small and warned them against acts of evil even if they are small acts: (And whoso doeth good an atom's weight) the weight of the smallest ant (will see it then) in his register and then will be happy with it; it is also said: the believer sees his works in the Hereafter while the disbeliever sees his works in the life of the world,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. So, whosoever does good equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant) shall see it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good shall see it he shall see its reward

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. So, whosoever does good equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant) shall see it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight) the weight of a small atom (will see it then) is written in his register and will displease him; and it is also said: the believer sees it in the life of the world while the disbeliever sees it in the Hereafter'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن يَعْـمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرّاً يَرَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And whosoever does evil equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant) shall see it. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil shall see it he shall see its requital.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَن يَعْـمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرّاً يَرَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And whosoever does evil equal to the weight of an atom (or a small ant) shall see it. (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the snorting courses): '(By the snorting courses) the Prophet (pbuh) had sent a military expedition to Banu Kinanah and was quite aggrieved because he did not hear their news for a while. Allah therefore informed His Prophet about this expedition in the form of an oath, saying (By the snorting courses) He says: Allah swears by the horses of the conquerors, whose breaths are audible because of the enemies,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the (steeds) that run, with panting..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By the chargers the steeds that charge in attack and snort with a snorting — this being the name of the sound which they emit from inside them when they charge;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By the (steeds) that run, with panting..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Striking sparks of fire) with their hooves, but this fire is as beneficial as the Fire of Abu Hubahib. The latter was one of the stingiest Arabs in camp. He never lit any fire to make bread for himself or for anyone else until everybody went to sleep, and whenever someone woke up he hurried to put the Fire out so that no one would benefit from it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Striking sparks of fire (by their hooves)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: by the strikers the steeds that strike fire by way of sparks with their hoofs when they gallop across rocky terrain by night;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Striking sparks of fire (by their hooves)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And scouring to the raid at dawn,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And scouring to the raid at dawn..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: by the dawn-raiders the steeds that make raids against the enemy at dawn at the hands of their riders

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَٱلْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And scouring to the raid at dawn..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then, therewith, with their trail of dust,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And stirring clouds of dust..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: raising stirring up therein in the place of their charge or at that time of dawn a trail of dust by the power of their movement

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And stirring clouds of dust..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Cleaving, as one, the centre (of the foe)) the above can also be understood as follow: Allah swears by the pilgrims' horses and camels when they return from 'Arafah to Muzdalifah snorting and striking sparks of fire; it is also said the latter means: performing acts which leads them to safety, i.e. the pilgrimage. And He swears by these when they go at dawn from Muzdalifah to Mina in the evening, leaving trails of dust and surrounding their enemies. Allah swore by all these.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And penetrating forthwith as one into the midst (of the foe)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: cleaving therewith with the dust a host of the enemy that is to say cutting right into their centre! the verb is supplemented to the noun in the above instances because it serves to explain the verbal action in other words wa’llātī ‘adawna fa-awrayna fa-agharna ‘by those that charge then strike sparks then raid’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And penetrating forthwith as one into the midst (of the foe)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Man) i.e. the disbelieving man: Qurt Ibn 'Abdullah Ibn 'Amr; and it is also said it refers to Abu Hubahib (is an ingrate unto his Lord) He says: he is ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord; it is also said this means: He is disobedient of his Lord; and it is also said this means: he is stingy; and it is also said this means: he denies those who are dependent on him, starves his slaves, eats alone and does not give those who are his relatives among his folk.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, man (disbeliever) is ungrateful to his Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily man the disbeliever is ungrateful to his Lord thankless denying the reality of His graces exalted be He

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, man (disbeliever) is ungrateful to his Lord..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! he is a witness unto that) and Allah records His doing;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And to that he bears witness (by his deeds)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and verily to that ingratitude of his he is a witness bearing witness against himself to his own actions.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And to that he bears witness (by his deeds)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And lo! in the love of wealth) abundant wealth (he) i.e. Qurt (is violent) is extreme.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ ٱلْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And verily, he is violent in the love of wealth..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And verily in the love of wealth he is avid and is therefore niggardly with it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ ٱلْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. And verily, he is violent in the love of wealth..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Knoweth he not) i.e. Abu Hubahib; and it is also said: Qurt (that, when the contents of the graves) the dead (are poured forth

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَلاَ يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلْقُبُورِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Knows he not that when the contents of the graves are poured forth (all mankind is resurrected)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Does he not know that when that which is in the graves in the way of the dead is strewn when it is turned over and brought out that is to say that when they are raised

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَفَلاَ يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلْقُبُورِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. Knows he not that when the contents of the graves are poured forth (all mankind is resurrected)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And the secrets of the breasts) what is in the hearts of good and evil, miserliness and generosity (are made known.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And that which is in the breasts (of men) shall be made known?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and that which is in the breasts the hearts of disbelief or faith is obtained when it is revealed and examined

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And that which is in the breasts (of men) shall be made known?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: On that day) the Day of Judgement (will their Lord be perfectly informed concerning them) their Lord is perfectly Aware'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Verily, that Day (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) their Lord will be Well-Acquainted with them (as to their deeds and will reward them for their deeds). *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: on that day their Lord will indeed be Aware of them Knower of them and will requite them for their disbelief the pronoun reverts to the plural because of the collective import of the term ‘man’; this sentence indicates the direct object of the verb ya‘lamu ‘does he not know’ that is to say ‘We will requite him at the time mentioned’; khabīrun ‘Aware’ is semantically connected to yawma’idhin ‘on that day’ even though in fact God is ever Aware because that is the Day of Requital.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. Verily, that Day (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) their Lord will be Well-Acquainted with them (as to their deeds and will reward them for their deeds). *.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Calamity! What is the Calamity?): '(Calamity!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Al-Qāri‘ah (the striking Hour i.e. the Day of Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The Clattering Blow the Resurrection that will make hearts clatter by its terrors.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Al-Qāri‘ah (the striking Hour i.e. the Day of Resurrection)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: What is the Calamity?) He says: the Hour! What is the Hour? He said this to arouse his wonder; the Hour is called Calamity because it shakes people's hearts.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. What is the striking (Hour)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: What is the Clattering Blow? — intended to emphasise its awesomeness mā’l-qāri‘a both of these elements constitute a subject and a predicate and together the predicate of the first al-qāri‘a.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. What is the striking (Hour)?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Calamity is!) he said this to show its tremendousness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And what will make you know what the striking (Hour) is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you what the Clattering Blow is? — additional emphasis of its awesomeness the first mā is a subject and what follows it is its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function together as the second direct object of the verb adrā ‘show’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And what will make you know what the striking (Hour) is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Allah then gave more details about it, saying: (A day wherein mankind will be) a day when people will fall on each other (as thickly scattered moths

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. It is a Day whereon mankind will be like moths scattered about..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: The day yawma that which renders it accusative is the verb indicated by al-qāri‘a in other words by the implied taqra‘u ‘it clatters’ mankind will be like scattered moths like a throng of scattered locusts surging into each other in confusion until they are summoned to the Reckoning

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. It is a Day whereon mankind will be like moths scattered about..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And the mountains will become as carded wool.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And the mountains will be like carded wool..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and the mountains will be like tufts of wool like carded wool in terms of the lightness with which it floats in the air until it comes to settle upon the earth.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And the mountains will be like carded wool..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then, as for him whose scales are heavy (with good works)) as for him whose good works weigh heavy on his scale; this refers to the believer,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Then, as for him whose balance (of good deeds) will be heavy, (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then as for him whose scales weigh heavy in that his good deeds outweigh his misdeeds

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Then, as for him whose balance (of good deeds) will be heavy, (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He will live a pleasant life) He will be in a pleasant Paradise, pleasing to himself.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. He will live a pleasant life (in Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: he will enjoy a pleasant life in Paradise that is to say a pleasing one for he will be pleased with it that is it will be pleasing to him;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. He will live a pleasant life (in Paradise)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (But as for him whose scales are light) i.e. the disbeliever,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. But, as for him whose balance (of good deeds) will be light,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: but as for him whose scales weigh light in that his evil deeds outweigh his good ones

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. But, as for him whose balance (of good deeds) will be light,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (The Bereft and Hungry One will be his mother) his abode and destination will be the Fire; it is also said this means: he will be thrown in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. He will have his home in Hāwiyah (pit, i.e. Hell)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: his home will be the Abyss.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. He will have his home in Hāwiyah (pit, i.e. Hell)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what she is!) this is to show how tremendous she is,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And what will make you know what it is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And what will show you what it is? that is to say what the Abyss is.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 10. And what will make you know what it is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Raging fire) extremely hot'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. (It is) a fiercely blazing Fire! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is A scorching fire of extremely hot temperature the hā’ of hiya is for consonantal quiescence and is retained when reciting without a subsequent pause or with; some omit it when reciting without a pause.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 11. (It is) a fiercely blazing Fire! (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Rivalry in worldly increase distracteth you): '(Rivalry in worldly increase distracteth you) He says: bragging about your status and lineage has distracted you

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Rivalry in worldly things mutual vainglory about wealth children and men distracts you preoccupies you diverting you from obedience to God

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Until ye come to the graves) this is because the Banu Sahm and Banu 'Abd Manaf were bragging to each other about which tribe is larger as concerns the number of its population, and found out that the Banu 'Abd Manaf were more numerous. The Banu Sahm said at that point: “We were rooted out by injustice in the pagan era; go and count the living and the dead of our people and the living and the dead of your people”. When they did so they found out that the Banu Sahm were more numerous. Therefore the above verses were revealed about them: bragging about status and lineage distracted you to the extent that you visited the graveyards to count the dead; it is also said that this means: increase in wealth and children distracts you until you die and be put in the graves.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Until you visit the graves (i.e. till you die)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: until you visit the graves either in that you have died and then been buried in them or it means to the extent that you actually count the dead as a something to rival one another by.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Until you visit the graves (i.e. till you die)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay) this is a reply and threat to them, (but ye will come to know) what will be done to you in the graves!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Nay! You shall come to know!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: No indeed! — a disavowal. You will come to know!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Nay! You shall come to know!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, but ye will come to know!) what will be done to you when you die!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Again nay! You shall come to know!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Again no indeed! You will come to know the evil consequences of your mutual vainglory at the moment of the extraction of the soul then you will come to know in the grave.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Again nay! You shall come to know!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay, would that ye knew (now)) what will be done to you on the Day of Judgement (with a sure knowledge!) what you bragged about in the life of the world!

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Nay! If you knew with a sure knowledge (the end result of piling up, you would not have been occupied yourselves in worldly things)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: No indeed! — verily — Were you to know with certain knowledge the consequences of your vainglory you would not preoccupy yourselves with it for

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Nay! If you knew with a sure knowledge (the end result of piling up, you would not have been occupied yourselves in worldly things)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (For ye will behold hellfire) on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, You shall see the blazing Fire (Hell)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: you would surely see hell-fire the Fire la-tarawunna’l-jahīma this is the response to an omitted oath; the third consonant of the root of the verb r-’-y together with the second have been omitted and its vowel has been transposed onto the rā’.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Verily, You shall see the blazing Fire (Hell)!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Aye, ye will behold it with sure vision) which cannot be missed on the Day of Judgement.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And again, you shall see it with the eye of certainty!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Again you will surely see it — repeated for emphasis — with the eye of certainty ‘ayna is a verbal noun as both ra’ā and ‘āyana have the same meaning.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. And again, you shall see it with the eye of certainty!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then, on that day) on the Day of Judgement, (ye will be asked concerning pleasure) you will be asked about whether you gave thanks for all the bounties you enjoyed, of food, drink, clothing, etc'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Then, on that Day you shall be asked about the delights(1) (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Then on that day the day you see it you will assuredly be questioned la-tus’alunna the nūn of the indicative has been omitted because of one nūn coming after the other; likewise omitted is the wāw indicating the plural person of the verb because of two unvocalised consonants coming together about the comforts of the world the health leisure security food drink and other things which one enjoys in this world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Then, on that Day you shall be asked about the delights(1) (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (By the declining day): (By the declining day) Allah swears by the 'Asr prayer; and it is also said by the hardships of time,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By Al-‘Aṣr (the time)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: By Time! — or it ‘asr can mean the period from the declining of the sun to sunset or it may denote the afternoon prayer.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. By Al-‘Aṣr (the time)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! Man) i.e. the disbelieving man (is in a state of loss) and torment because of losing his family and position in Paradise; it is also said this means: he is in a state of loss because of decrease in his works in old age and its cessation after death,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Verily, man is in loss,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Verily man al-insān the generic is in a state of loss in all his bargaining

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Verily, man is in loss,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Save those who believe) in Muhammad (pbuh) and the Qur'an (and do good works) and do acts of obedience privately between them and their Lord, (and exhort one another to truth) to belief in Allah's divine Oneness; and it is said to the Qur'an (and exhort one another to endurance) in performing the obligations imposed by Allah and in avoiding transgressions and also in enduring misfortunes and calamities, because the believers are unlike the disbelievers'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Except those who believe (in Islāmic Monotheism) and do righteous good deeds, and exhort one another to the truth [i.e. exhort one another to perform all kinds of good deeds (Al-Ma‘rūf) which Allāh has ordained, and to abstain from all kinds of sins and evil deeds (Al-Munkar) which Allāh has forbidden], and exhort one another to patience ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds they are not in a state of loss and enjoin one another to follow the truth faith and enjoin one another to patience in maintaining obedience and in refraining from acts of disobedience.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. Except those who believe (in Islāmic Monotheism) and do righteous good deeds, and exhort one another to the truth [i.e. exhort one another to perform all kinds of good deeds (Al-Ma‘rūf) which Allāh has ordained, and to abstain from all kinds of sins and evil deeds (Al-Munkar) which Allāh has forbidden], and exhort one another to patience ..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Woe): '(Woe) severe punishment; and it is also said that this refers to a valley in Gehenna which is full of blood and puss; and it is also said that it refers to a well in the Fire (unto every slandering) who backbites people (traducer) and slanders and abuses them in their face. This verses was revealed about Akhnas Ibn Shurayq, or al-Walid Ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who used to backbite the Prophet (pbuh) and also abuse him when in his presence.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Woe to every slanderer and backbiter(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Woe waylun an expression implying chastisement to every backbiter who is a slanderer frequently engaging in backbiting and slander that is to say defamation — this was revealed regarding those who slandered the Prophet s and the believers the likes of Umayya b. Khalaf al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra and others —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Woe to every slanderer and backbiter(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who hath gathered wealth (of this world) and arranged it) and counted it; and it is also said: counted his camels.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالاً وَعَدَّدَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Who has gathered wealth and counted it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: who amasses read jama‘a or jamma‘a wealth and counts it over keeping count of it and stores it aside as a provision against the unforeseeable calamities of time.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالاً وَعَدَّدَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Who has gathered wealth and counted it..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He) the disbeliever (thinketh that his wealth will render him immortal) in the life of the world.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He thinks that his wealth will make him last forever!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He thinks in his ignorance that his wealth will make him immortal never to die.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He thinks that his wealth will make him last forever!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Nay) this is a reply to him: it will not render him immortal in the life of the world, (but verily he will be flung to the Consuming One.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Nay! Verily, he will be thrown into the crushing Fire..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nay! — a repudiation — He will surely be flung la-yunbadhanna is the response to an omitted oath that is he will be hurled down into the Crusher that crushes everything that is thrown into it.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: كَلاَّ لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. Nay! Verily, he will be thrown into the crushing Fire..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Ah, what will convey unto thee) O Muhammad (what the Consuming One is!) He said this to show its tremendousness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْحُطَمَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And what will make you know what the crushing Fire is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you what the Crusher is?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْحُطَمَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And what will make you know what the crushing Fire is?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: Then He explained, saying: ((It is) the Fire of Allah, kindled) for the disbelievers,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. The fire of Allāh kindled,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: It is the fire of God kindled set ablaze

meta_data.ayah_arabic: نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. The fire of Allāh kindled,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Which leapeth up over the hearts (of men)) which consumes everything until it reaches the hearts.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلأَفْئِدَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Which leaps up over the hearts,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: which peers over the hearts to burn them — the pain of which is much more severe than any other because of the delicate nature of the heart.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلأَفْئِدَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 7. Which leaps up over the hearts,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Lo! It) i.e. the Fire (is closed in on them) on the disbelievers

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Verily, it shall be closed upon them,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Lo! it will be closed in mu’sada or mūsada on them ‘alayhim ‘on them’ the plural pronoun takes into account the plural import of kull ‘every’

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 8. Verily, it shall be closed upon them,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (In outstretched columns) it is also said that this means: its bottom is very deep'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. In pillars stretched forth (i.e. they will be punished in the Fire with pillars). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: in outstretched mumaddadatin is an adjective qualifying the preceding noun ‘amadin columns read ‘umudin or ‘amadin and will therefore be inside the columns.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 9. In pillars stretched forth (i.e. they will be punished in the Fire with pillars). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said about the interpretation of Allah's saying (Hast thou not seen): '(Hast thou not seen) i.e. have you not been informed, O Muhammad, in the Qur'an (how thy Lord dealt with) how your Lord punished and destroyed (the owners of the Elephant) the people of the Negus who intended to destroy the House of Allah?

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ ٱلْفِيلِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Have you (O Muḥammad ) not seen how your Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant? [The Elephant army which came from Yemen under the command of Abrahah Al‑Ashram intending to destroy the Ka‘bah in Makkah]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Have you not considered an interrogative meant to provoke marvel in other words ‘marvel at’ the way in which your Lord dealt with the Men of the Elephant? who was named Mahmūd and the men were Abraha King of Yemen and his troops. He had built a church in San‘ā’ in order to divert pilgrims away from Mecca to it. A man from among the Banū Kināna defecated in it and stained its prayer niche with a deflowered virgin’s blood in contempt of it. Abraha then swore that he would knock down the Ka‘ba. So he approached Mecca with his troops riding Yemeni elephants with Mahmūd at the vanguard. But when they turned to destroy the Ka‘ba God unleashed upon them what He relates in His words

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ ٱلْفِيلِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Have you (O Muḥammad ) not seen how your Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant? [The Elephant army which came from Yemen under the command of Abrahah Al‑Ashram intending to destroy the Ka‘bah in Makkah]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Did He not bring their stratagem) their scheming (to naught) to utter loss,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Did He not make their plot go astray?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Did He not make — that is to say He did indeed make — their stratagem to destroy the Ka‘ba go astray ending up in failure and destruction

meta_data.ayah_arabic: أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Did He not make their plot go astray?.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And send against them) and set on them (swarms of flying creatures) in succession,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْراً أَبَابِيلَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And He sent against them birds, in flocks,.

tafsir: And thou seest mankind) the people of Yemen and others (entering the religion of Allah) Islam (in troops) entire groups at a time, when this happens, know that you will die.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And you see that the people enter Allāh’s religion (Islām) in crowds..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and you see people entering God’s religion that is to say Islam in throngs in large droves after they had been entering one by one — this was after the conquest of Mecca when the Arabs from all corners of the land came to him willingly in obedience to his command —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. And you see that the people enter Allāh’s religion (Islām) in crowds..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Then hymn the praises of thy Lord) pray by the command of your Lord in gratitude for this, (and seek forgiveness of Him) from sins. (Lo! He is ever ready to show mercy) and forgiving. The Prophet (pbuh) was therefore informed in this surah that he was to die soon'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّاباً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. So, glorify the Praises of your Lord, and ask His Forgiveness. Verily, He is the One Who Ever accepts the repentance and Who forgives..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: then glorify with praise of your Lord that is continuously praising Him and seek forgiveness from Him; for verily He is ever ready to relent. The Prophet s after this sūra had been revealed would frequently repeat the words subhāna’Llāhi wa bi-hamdihi ‘Glory and praise be to God’ and astaghfiru’Llāha wa-atūbu ilayhi ‘I seek forgiveness from God and I repent to Him’; with the revelation of this final sūra he realised that his end was near. The victory over Mecca was in Ramadān of year 8; the Prophet s passed away in Rabī‘ I of the year 10.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّاباً
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. So, glorify the Praises of your Lord, and ask His Forgiveness. Verily, He is the One Who Ever accepts the repentance and Who forgives..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (The power of Abu Lahab will perish): '(The power of Abu Lahab will perish) this is because when Allah said to His Prophet (pbuh) (And warn your tribe of near kindred [26: 214]) he called them and said: “Say: there is no god but Allah” and his uncle-the brother of his father from their mother's side-'Abd al-'Uzza whose agnomen was Abu Lahab said: “May you perish! Is this why you summoned us?” Allah then revealed His saying (The power of Abu Lahab will perish) He says: the hand of Abu Lahab is deprived of all good (and he will perish) he lost himself by rejecting belief in Allah's divine Oneness.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Perish the two hands of Abū Lahab (an uncle of the Prophet) and perish he!(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Perish ruined be the hands of Abū Lahab in other words all of him — the use of ‘hands’ here to denote all of him is figurative and is because most actions are performed by them; the statement is an invocation — and perish he! may he be ruined! this tabba is a predicate as where one says ahlakahu’Llāhu wa-qad halak ‘God destroyed him and he indeed is destroyed’. When the Prophet threatened him with the chastisement he said ‘If what my brother’s son says is true then I shall ransom myself from it with my wealth and sons!’; so the following was revealed

meta_data.ayah_arabic: تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Perish the two hands of Abū Lahab (an uncle of the Prophet) and perish he!(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (His wealth) his abundant wealth (and gains) many children (will not exempt him) in the Hereafter.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. His wealth and his children will not benefit him!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: His wealth will not avail him nor what he has earned wa-kasab means wa-kasbihi that is to say his sons; mā aghnā means mā yughnī.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. His wealth and his children will not benefit him!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (He will be plunged) in the Hereafter (in flaming fire) which will kindle and rage with flames,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَاراً ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He will be burnt in a Fire of blazing flames!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He will soon enter a Fire of flames that is to say a fire that is flaming and ignited this statement is the source of his nickname which was given to him on account of his flaming reddish fair face

meta_data.ayah_arabic: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَاراً ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He will be burnt in a Fire of blazing flames!.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And his wife) Umm Jamilah Bint Harth Ibn Umayyah with him, (the wood carrier) the talebearer who used to go between the Muslims and disbelievers and spread lies among them about each other; it is also said that she used to throw thorns in the way of the mosque whenever she saw the Prophet (pbuh) heading that way.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱمْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And his wife, too, who carries wood (thorns of Sa‘dān which she used to put on the way of the Prophet , or used to slander him) (2). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and his wife wa’mra’atuhu is a supplement to the person of the verb yaslā ‘he will enter’ separated by the clause of the direct object and its qualification — and this was Umm Jamīl — the carrier read hammālatu or hammālata of firewood cactus and thorns which she used to fling into the path of the Prophet s.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَٱمْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And his wife, too, who carries wood (thorns of Sa‘dān which she used to put on the way of the Prophet , or used to slander him) (2). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Will have upon her neck a halter of palm fibre) and this halter strangulated her and she died as a result; it is also said that this means: she will have an iron chain on her neck'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Around her neck is a twisted rope of Masad (palm fibre)(1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: with a rope of palm-fibre around her neck fī jīdihā hablun min masadin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to hammālata’l-hatab which in turn is either a description of imra’atahu ‘his wife’ or the predicate of an implied subject.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Around her neck is a twisted rope of Masad (palm fibre)(1). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Say: He is Allah, the One!): '(Say: He is Allah, the One!) the people of Quraysh asked the Prophet (pbuh): “O Muhammad! Describe for us your Lord; is He made of gold or silver?” And so Allah revealed this surah to describe His attributes and traits, saying: say to Quraysh, O Muhammad: He is Allah, the One, He has no son or partner.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Say (O Muḥammad ): “He is Allāh, (the) One..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Say ‘He is God One Allāhu is the predicate of huwa ‘He is’ and ahadun is its substitution or a second predicate.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Say (O Muḥammad ): “He is Allāh, (the) One..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Allah, the eternally Besought of all!) the Master whose glory is at its peak and for Whom all created beings are in need; it is also said that (al-Samad) means: He Who does not eat or drink; it is also said that this means: He Who does not have an interior; it is also said that this means: the Everlasting; and it is also said this means: the Sufficient; and it is also said this means: He who does not have an entrance or exit.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Allāh-uṣ-Ṣamad ( [Allāh — the Self-Sufficient Master, Whom all creatures need, (He neither eats nor drinks)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: God the Self-Sufficient Besought of all Allāhu’l-samad constitute a subject and a predicate al-samad means the One Who is always sought at times of need

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. Allāh-uṣ-Ṣamad ( [Allāh — the Self-Sufficient Master, Whom all creatures need, (He neither eats nor drinks)]..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And it is also said that al-Samad means:(He begetteth not nor was begotten) He says: He did not inherit and will not be inherited; and it is also said this means: He does not have a son who will inherit His dominion and He was not begotten, which means that He did not inherit His dominion.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He begets not, nor was He begotten(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: He neither begot for no likeness of Him can exist nor was begotten since createdness is precluded in His case.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. He begets not, nor was He begotten(1)..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (And there is none comparable unto Him) He says: He does not have an opposite, peer, or equal nor anyone who may resemble or begin to resemble Him; and it is also said this means: He does not have any co-equal who would compete with Him about dominion and sovereignty'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And there is none co-equal or comparable to Him.” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: Nor is there anyone equal to Him’ neither match nor comparison lahu ‘to Him’ is semantically connected to kufuwan ‘equal’ but precedes it because it is the object of the intended negation; ahadun ‘anyone’ which is the subject of yakun ‘is there’ has been placed after the predicate of the latter kufuwan ‘equal’ in order to retain the harmony of the end-rhyme of the verses.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And there is none co-equal or comparable to Him.” (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: And from his narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of Allah's saying (Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of Daybreak): '(Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of Daybreak) He says: Say, O Muhammad, I seek protection, and it is said: I seek refuge, in the Lord of daybreak; and it is also said that al-falaq refers to a well in the Fire; and it is also said that al-falaq is a valley in the Fire.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Say: “I seek refuge with (Allāh), the Lord of the daybreak,.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. And from the evil of the darkening (night) as it comes with its darkness; (or the moon as it sets or goes away),.

tafsir: And from the evil of malignant witchcraft,

meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And from the evil of those who practise witchcraft when they blow in the knots,.

tafsir: and from the evil of the women-blowers sorceresses who blow on knots which they knot into strings blowing into them certain words but without spittle; however al-Zamakhsharī says ‘with this spittle’ — sorceresses such as the daughters of the said Labīd —

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي ٱلْعُقَدِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. And from the evil of those who practise witchcraft when they blow in the knots,.

tafsir: And from the evil of the envier when he envieth) this refers to Labid Ibn al-A'sam, the Jew, who was envious of the Prophet (pbuh) and used black magic to separate him from 'A'ishah'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: and from the evil of an envier when he envies’ when he manifests his envy and behaves in accordance with it — such as the mentioned Labīd from among the Jews who were envious of the Prophet s; the mention of these three elements of evil which are already subsumed by the statement ‘of what He has created’ is because of the severity of their evil.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. And from the evil of the envier when he envies.”.

tafsir: Say ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind their Creator and their Possessor they mankind have been singled out for mention here in order to honour them and a preface to seeking refuge from the evil of the one who whispers in their hearts;

meta_data.ayah_arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 1. Say: “I seek refuge with (Allāh) the Lord of mankind,(1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. The King of mankind —(2).

meta_data.ayah_translation: 2. The King of mankind —(2).

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. The Ilāh (God) of mankind,.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 3. The Ilāh (God) of mankind,.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (From the evil of the sneaking whisperer) i.e. Satan who runs away and hides himself whenever Allah is mentioned,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. From the evil of the whisperer (devil who whispers evil in the hearts of men) who withdraws (from his whispering in one’s heart after one remembers Allāh) (3). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: from the evil of the slinking whisperer Satan — he is referred to by the name of the action waswasa on account of his repeated engaging in it — who slinks away and recoils from the heart whenever God is mentioned

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 4. From the evil of the whisperer (devil who whispers evil in the hearts of men) who withdraws (from his whispering in one’s heart after one remembers Allāh) (3). (1).
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind) and when Allah is not mentioned, he whispers in the hearts of created beings,

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Who whispers in the breasts of mankind..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: who whispers in the breasts of mankind in their hearts — whenever they neglect to remember God

meta_data.ayah_arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 5. Who whispers in the breasts of mankind..
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn

tafsir: (Of the jinn and of mankind) He says: Satan whispers in the hearts of the jinn just as he whispers in the hearts of mankind. The last two surah were revealed about Labid Ibn al-A'sam, the Jew, who used black magic on the Prophet (pbuh) and when the Prophet (pbuh) read these two surahs on Labid's black magic, Allah relieved him from it and it was as if he was untied from his fetters'.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Of jinn and men.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tanwīr al-Miqbās min Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās

tafsir: of the jinn and mankind’ mina’l-jinnati wa’l-nāsi an explication for the whispering Satan being of the jinn and also of the humans similar to God’s saying the devils of humans and jinn Q. 6112; or mina’l-jinnati ‘of the jinn’ is an explication for him Satan wa’l-nāsi ‘and of mankind’ being a supplement to al-waswās ‘the whisperer’. Both explanations apply to the evil of the mentioned Labīd and his daughters; the objection to the first opinion is that humans do not ‘whisper’ in the hearts of other humans but that it is the jinn who whisper in their hearts I would respond by saying that human beings also ‘whisper’ in a manner appropriate to them beginning externally whereafter their whispers reach the heart and establish themselves in it in the way in which this customarily happens. But God knows best what is correct and to Him shall be the return and the final destination and may God bless our Master Muhammad and his family and Companions and grant them all much peace forever and always. God suffices for us and what an excellent guardian is He! And there is no power or might except in God the Sublime the Tremendous.

meta_data.ayah_arabic: مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
meta_data.ayah_translation: 6. Of jinn and men.”.
meta_data.En_tafsir_source: Tafsir al-Jalalayn
